source: species_system_dynamics, teaser fields only, joined to published SEO species pages
note: Newly generated rows do not appear on the page until this snapshot is refreshed and deployed. The production build consumes this file only and never fetches Supabase.

entries.name: Aardvark

waveform.description: A night of heavy repeated digging bouts with short moves between.

entries.closingLine: Continuous heavy night work makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Aardwolf
entries.archetype: Immune to a Chemical Nobody Tolerates

modes.label: Walking the grassland • Licking termites off the surface • Leaving the mound intact

waveform.description: A steady patient nightly foraging rhythm with no bursts.

entries.closingLine: This is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Abyssinian Ground Hornbill

waveform.description: A long level walking band with sharp, short strikes rising out of it — the work is the walking, not the peaks.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts steady all-day walking into a modest continuous return, rather than storing reserves or hunting in bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ackie Monitor
entries.archetype: A Tail That Plugs the Hole Behind It

waveform.description: An active foraging rhythm dropping into a held wedged state.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: active foraging and a wedged defensive plug.

entries.name: Acorn Barnacle

waveform.description: Even, repeating mid-height waves: each crest is a feeding tide, each trough a quieter interval while the barnacle remains fixed.

entries.closingLine: Because the barnacle’s entire architecture is built for repeated, tide-synchronized bouts of filtering from a fixed point, its operating rhythm is a steady, mid-frequency system tied to environmental pulses rather than long dormancy or explosive bursts.

entries.name: Acorn Weevil

waveform.description: A low, gently descending line showing steady, sustained effort with no sudden bursts: long, focused work on a single hidden target.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a low-frequency system: dense specialization and slow, targeted action focused on a few well-chosen, future-yielding sites rather than many quick attempts.

entries.name: Acorn Woodpecker
entries.archetype: A Tree Drilled Into a Group Pantry

waveform.description: A steady line of granary upkeep broken by one sharp spike when a breeding vacancy is contested.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady shared maintenance of a store and brief, violent contests over who inherits it.

entries.name: Addax

waveform.description: A shallow steady line — an animal moving continuously and slowly across ground that offers very little.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at a very low rate across a very large area, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Adelie Penguin
entries.archetype: Needing Ice and Bare Rock at Once

modes.label: Walking to the sea • Diving for krill • Carrying stones back

waveform.description: A repeating cycle of walking out, diving, and returning to nest.

entries.closingLine: Repeated daily foraging trips make this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: African Bullfrog

waveform.description: A long sealed flat line broken by a short violent burst.

entries.closingLine: That makes it an adaptive system: a sealed dormant state and a total, hurried exploitation of water that is already going.

entries.name: African Bush Elephant

waveform.description: Two long feeding periods across the day on a steady baseline — continuous demand rather than episodes.

entries.closingLine: Because a very large continuous demand is met by steady informed movement rather than by reserves or bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: African Civet

waveform.description: A steady nightly circuit of marking and searching.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady nightly searching organised by marks left on the ground.

entries.name: African Clawed Frog
entries.archetype: A Lateral Line Kept Into Adulthood

waveform.description: A low patient line with small steady variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: patient, economical and entirely tactile.

entries.name: African Fish Eagle
entries.archetype: A Call That Marks the Shoreline

waveform.description: A patient perched line with brief sharp descents.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a patient vocal baseline and a brief efficient strike.

entries.name: African Forest Buffalo
entries.archetype: A Compact Grazer Tied to Forest Clearings

waveform.description: Grazing at dawn, dusk and night with a deep midday trough of shaded rest.

entries.closingLine: Because the system alternates between grazing in the openings and resting together in cover, it is bimodal.

entries.name: African Forest Elephant

waveform.description: A slow steady line — an animal whose effect comes from persistence rather than from any single event.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: African Grey Hornbill

waveform.description: A low, steady baseline with gentle, even mid-sized pulses, showing a protected sealed state with repeated, moderate provisioning and contact events.

entries.closingLine: That dependence on a protected baseline plus ongoing, moderate-intensity exchange makes the hornbill a bimodal LOW–MID frequency system.

entries.name: African Grey Parrot

waveform.description: Loud coordinated exchanges at each end of the day with a long social working period between — a rhythm set by the flock, not by food.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on continuous social coordination and repeated daily exchange, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: African Harrier-Hawk

waveform.description: A patient working rhythm: slow repeated probing rather than fast strikes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, patient and defined by access rather than speed.

entries.name: African Jacana

waveform.description: A steady walking rhythm across a floating surface.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady walking feeding on a surface nothing else can stand on.

entries.name: African Openbill
entries.archetype: A Gap That Holds the Shell Still

waveform.description: A steady repeated handling rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: a steady repeated handling cycle in which each item is processed the same way.

entries.name: African Palm Civet

waveform.description: A quiet low rhythm with small variations: an unhurried circuit repeated each night.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: quiet, economical and built on repeating a known low-competition round.

entries.name: African Penguin

modes.label: Excavating a burrow in deep guano • Shading eggs and chicks from direct sun • Returning to the same burrow with the same partner each year

waveform.description: A regular alternation of similar magnitude, because the year is built from repeated foraging trips and nest reliefs.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging trips repeat, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: African Pygmy Hedgehog

modes.label: Nosing the litter • Rolling when touched • Anointing what is new

waveform.description: A low pottering rhythm interrupted twice by short flat troughs, because the animal's response to danger is to stop entirely rather than to accelerate.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs slowly and cheaply through the night, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: African Pygmy Kingfisher
entries.archetype: Low Perch, Long Watch, Short Strike

waveform.description: A long flat watch broken by brief, sharp strikes and quick returns.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: patient perch-watching and sudden short strikes.

entries.name: African Rock Python
entries.archetype: Pressure Held Until the Heart Stops

modes.label: Strike • Coil • Tighten on every exhale

waveform.description: Months of flat line with two very short, very high events in it.

entries.closingLine: That is a bimodal system of low-frequency waiting and a high-frequency kill.

entries.name: African Sharptooth Catfish

modes.label: A pair of branched tree-like structures above the gill chambers, densely supplied with blood and open to the air • Air gulped at the surface held against that huge folded surface for oxygen uptake • The fish surviving in water with almost no oxygen and crossing wet ground between pools when one dries

waveform.description: A steady repeating rhythm of surfacing, because the fish must return to the air at regular intervals.

entries.closingLine: Because surfacing is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: African Wild Dog

modes.label: Resting • Social • Most of the day

waveform.description: Two long flat rests separated by sustained plateaus rather than spikes — the hunt is long as well as intense.

entries.closingLine: Because the system needs both the long social rest and the sustained pursuit, it is bimodal.

entries.name: Agile Wallaby
entries.archetype: Tendons That Give Back What They Take

waveform.description: An even bouncing rhythm at constant amplitude.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, rhythmic and unusually economical.

entries.name: Agrarian Sac Spider

modes.label: Building a closed silk sac in a rolled leaf, a corner or a fold of cloth • Spending the day sealed inside it • Hunting on foot at night with no web at all

waveform.description: Long sealed stretches alternating with an active period, because the animal is either shut inside the sac or out hunting.

entries.closingLine: Since hunting recurs nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Aldabra Giant Tortoise

waveform.description: Two short grazing windows either side of a deep midday trough — a day shaped by temperature rather than by appetite.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on short daily windows inside a very long life, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Alderfly

modes.label: An aquatic larva with lateral abdominal gills, hunting small invertebrates in the silt of slow water for one to two years
A terrestrial adult living a few days with non-functional mouthparts, flying weakly near the water and doing nothing but mating and laying

waveform.description: A long flat aquatic stretch breaking into a brief agitated burst, because the two stages are different animals in effect.

entries.closingLine: The division is architectural rather than behavioural, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Alligator Gar

modes.label: Hanging motionless • Grabbing sideways • Rarely moving far

waveform.description: Long motionless stretches in slow water with rare movement.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Alligator Snapping Turtle

waveform.description: The flattest possible baseline with one vertical event — hours of gaping against a fraction of a second.

entries.closingLine: Because a near-zero cost lure supports one instantaneous capture, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Alpaca

waveform.description: A soft even rhythm with small amplitude: continuous low-level contact rather than alarm.

entries.closingLine: That makes the alpaca a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, social and organised around keeping a group aligned at very low cost.

entries.name: Alpine Chough

waveform.description: Even rolling waves showing repeated bouts of active, social flight and foraging with no long flat waits or extreme spikes.

entries.closingLine: Because their survival depends on this ongoing, shared exploration rather than on rare ambushes or long fasting, their system runs as a mid-frequency rhythm: continuous, social, and cyclic rather than slow-reserve or single-burst based.

entries.name: Alpine Ibex
entries.archetype: Climbing a Dam Wall for Salt

waveform.description: A steady grazing line rising into a sustained climbing phase.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady high-altitude grazing and a distinct mineral-seeking climb.

entries.name: Alpine Marmot

modes.label: Grazing alpine meadow through a short summer • Building fat and maintaining a shared burrow • Posting sentries and whistling at raptors
The whole group sealed in one chamber • Bodies packed together to share heat • Adults rousing in synchrony and warming the young

waveform.description: A brief active section against a very long depressed one, because more than half the year is spent in the second state.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two physiologies, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Alpine Musk Deer

modes.label: Browsing • Scent-marking • Keeping the same weapon

waveform.description: A flat, unvarying trace with no annual spike anywhere in it.

entries.closingLine: Solitary, secretive and slow, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Alpine Newt

waveform.description: A working aquatic rhythm alternating with a long low held state.

entries.closingLine: That makes it an adaptive system: the operating state is selected by conditions rather than fixed.

entries.name: Alpine Salamander
entries.archetype: Years of Pregnancy, No Pond Needed

modes.label: Emerging in damp weather • Feeding slowly • Carrying young for years

waveform.description: An extraordinarily slow trace across years rather than seasons.

entries.closingLine: Everything about this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Alpine Swift

waveform.description: A sustained mid-level airborne line dipping into a quieter breeding phase.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: continuous aerial feeding and a crevice-bound breeding phase.

entries.name: Amano Shrimp

modes.label: Living and breeding as adults in fresh water • Releasing larvae that drift downstream into brackish water • Producing postlarvae that migrate back upstream months later

waveform.description: A long even line rising into one broad seasonal event, because the reproductive movement is the only large feature of the year.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Amazon Milk Frog

waveform.description: A quiet, patient signature with regular calling pulses.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: patient, cheap to run, and built entirely around one small hidden container.

entries.name: Amazon River Dolphin

waveform.description: A slow, winding high-water phase giving way to a busier low-water hunting phase in the channels.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-change system: slow flooded-forest weaving and low-water channel hunting.

entries.name: Amazon Sailfin Catfish

modes.label: The whole body covered in overlapping bony plates rather than scales • Rigid spines in the pectoral and dorsal fins that lock outward when the fish is seized • Predators and birds unable to swallow or process it, so the fish survives attacks that would kill an unarmoured one

waveform.description: A very flat placid line, because the fish grazes slowly and relies on armour rather than on any response.

entries.closingLine: Because the defence is passive and continuous, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Amazonian Giant Centipede

modes.label: The animal climbing a cave wall and anchoring its rear legs to the ceiling • The body held hanging free in the air below, in the flight path bats use to leave the roost • Bats struck in flight and held by the forcipules, the whole capture happening with nothing beneath the centipede at all

waveform.description: A long motionless wait broken by sudden strikes, because the animal hangs still until something passes.

entries.closingLine: Because the hunt is occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Amazonian Manatee

waveform.description: High-water grazing that falls into a long, low dry-season fast and recovers with the flood.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: flood-season grazing on floating meadows and a long dry-season fast in deep water.

entries.name: Amber Snail

modes.label: Ingesting flatworm eggs from bird droppings on vegetation • The parasite growing broodsacs that push into the snail's eye stalks and pulsate there • The snail moving into open sunlight and exposed leaves instead of hiding, until a bird takes it

waveform.description: A slow rise and fall over the whole line, because the infection develops gradually and then takes the animal.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs across seasons, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Amboina Sailfin Lizard

modes.label: Basking on the branch • Carrying the sail • Dropping into the river

waveform.description: A moderate even rhythm of basking and moving, with nothing abrupt because the escape route is always a step away.

entries.closingLine: Because the basking, feeding and moving proceed at one steady daily tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Alligator

waveform.description: A very long still baseline interrupted by a single narrow explosive spike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an extremely cheap wait, in a place it engineered, punctuated by brief total commitment.

entries.name: American Avocet

waveform.description: A metronomic side-to-side sweep that never changes amplitude.

entries.closingLine: Continuous rhythmic coverage rather than any single strike makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Badger

modes.label: Digging the prey out • Sealing the exits first • Moving to the next colony

waveform.description: A heavy working rhythm of deep regular efforts, because the whole hunt is sustained digging rather than any moment of speed.

entries.closingLine: Since the digging runs at one sustained heavy tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Bison

waveform.description: A heavy unvarying working rhythm that continues through weather.

entries.closingLine: Continuous grazing and steady movement through a hard season makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Black Bear

modes.label: An active bear feeding heavily, excreting normally and laying down fat through the autumn
A denning bear neither eating, drinking, urinating nor defecating for months, with heart rate and metabolism sharply reduced but body temperature only slightly lowered

waveform.description: A vigorous active rhythm collapsing into a flat suppressed line, because the two states are physiologically different systems.

entries.closingLine: This is a different operating architecture rather than a slowed version of the same one, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: American Bullfrog

waveform.description: Deep evenly spaced calls with quiet intervals between them.

entries.closingLine: That makes the bullfrog a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and repeatable, built on converting a small input into a large signal.

entries.name: American Crocodile

waveform.description: A near-motionless line broken by one explosive event.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: prolonged stillness and a rare violent strike.

entries.name: American Crow

modes.label: Learning the face of a person who threatened it • Scolding that face on sight for years • Passing the association to birds that never saw the event

waveform.description: Ordinary activity broken by strong sustained reactions that decay slowly, because a recognition event produces a prolonged response rather than a reflex.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Dipper
entries.archetype: A Songbird That Walks on the Riverbed

waveform.description: A regular rhythm of entering and leaving the water.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady repeated work in a medium its whole family avoids.

entries.name: American Eel
entries.archetype: One Ocean-Born Stock Spread Along a Continent

waveform.description: An early surge of young eels moving inland, then a long, flat growing phase.

entries.closingLine: Because the system switches from a mass inland invasion to a long settled growth phase, it is a phase-change system.

entries.name: American Giant Millipede

modes.label: Coiling tightly when disturbed • Releasing benzoquinones from pores along each body segment • Staining and repelling whatever is handling it, and remaining coiled until the threat leaves

waveform.description: A slow line interrupted by a discharge and then a long flat raised stretch, because the animal coils and stays coiled.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: American Kestrel

modes.label: Perching in the open on wires and posts with the back exposed • Carrying two black ocelli on the nape that read as a face • Hunting small prey from that perch and from a hover

waveform.description: A watchful baseline broken by regular decisive drops, because the bird perches and then strikes at intervals.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Lobster

modes.label: Moulting throughout life rather than reaching a final size • Continuing to grow, feed and reproduce at ages of many decades • Showing little of the decline in fertility or survival that age normally brings

waveform.description: A long slow line with widely spaced small steps, because growth happens only at moults and those become rarer with age.

entries.closingLine: Since moults are years apart, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: American Marten

waveform.description: Relentless searching with no settled stretch long enough to rest in.

entries.closingLine: Constant expensive searching makes this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: American Paddlefish

waveform.description: A gentle continuous rhythm — the fish neither waits nor sprints, it simply keeps moving through the water it is filtering.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is a continuous steady process, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Pika

waveform.description: Low winter activity under snow, a surge of summer haying, then a return to stored food.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: MID haying in summer and LOW sheltering that relies on the store.

entries.name: American Red Squirrel

modes.label: Cutting conifer cones green and dropping them before they open • Piling all of them into a single damp midden where the scales stay shut • Defending that one heap year-round with rattle calls and chases

waveform.description: One concentrated autumn surge followed by a long level winter, because the whole year is built around a single harvest.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual with constant defence, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Robin

modes.label: Head cocked sideways • Listening for movement below • Pulling

waveform.description: Flat runs broken by short identical strikes, because the bird alternates between holding still and pulling.

entries.closingLine: Because the hunting runs continuously through daylight, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Toad

modes.label: Gathering in huge numbers at temporary water • Calling and spawning within days • Producing tadpoles that develop fast enough to leave before it dries

waveform.description: A flat line interrupted by one narrow block of activity, because the entire reproductive year happens in a single short window.

entries.closingLine: Since the whole cycle runs once a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: American White Pelican

modes.label: Birds forming a line or arc on the water and swimming forward together • Beating wings and feet to drive fish ahead of them into shallows • Dipping in unison once the fish are concentrated against the shore or against each other

waveform.description: A steady coordinated rhythm, because the herding and dipping cycle repeats through the day as a group.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle repeats daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: American Woodcock

waveform.description: Long low, flat stretches of stillness and slow probing with a few moderate, evenly spaced crepuscular rises for display and active foraging.

entries.closingLine: This creates a bimodal pattern: a dominant low-frequency mode of quiet, soil-focused probing and rest, and a necessary mid-frequency mode of repeated crepuscular flights and patrols that keep feeding and breeding working across seasons.

entries.name: Amur Leopard

waveform.description: A low steady rhythm — a solitary cat covering large distances slowly through a landscape that offers little.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs slowly across a wide area, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Andean Cock-of-the-rock

modes.label: Feeding on fruit • Returning to the same court • Displaying

waveform.description: Repeated bursts of display returning to the same baseline.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daily feeding and display makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Andean Condor

waveform.description: An almost unbroken line — hours of flight in which the animal barely changes its output at all.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs continuously at almost no cost, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Andean Goose

waveform.description: An unremarkable steady grazing rhythm held at an unusual altitude.

entries.closingLine: Steady, repeated, unhurried foraging through the day makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Andean Lapwing

waveform.description: The even run-stop-pick cadence of a plover on open ground.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady walking and picking in a medium that charges more for every wingbeat.

entries.name: Andean Mountain Cat
entries.archetype: A Hunter Tied to Viscacha Rocks

waveform.description: A long, low searching line broken by one brief spike of attack.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long solitary searching and brief, fast attacks.

entries.name: Andean Sparrow

waveform.description: Evenly spaced moderate peaks showing regular bouts of vocal activity separated by short rests.

entries.closingLine: That pattern of ongoing, coordinated signalling makes this a mid-frequency system built around a sustained broadcast rhythm.

entries.name: Anegada Rock Iguana

waveform.description: Two shallow warming humps tied to the sun's height, riding on a floor that never drops far — a day governed by temperature rather than by hunger.

entries.closingLine: Because a low-cost body converts poor food into size over very long periods, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Angoumois Grain Moth

modes.label: An egg laid on the surface of a single grain of wheat, maize or rice • The hatched larva boring in and sealing the entry behind it, then eating out the inside while the husk stays intact • The whole of development and pupation completed inside that one kernel, with the adult cutting a circular exit hole on emergence

waveform.description: A slow internal development cycle, because everything happens inside the grain over weeks with nothing visible.

entries.closingLine: Because development runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Anhinga

waveform.description: A consistently low submerged line with very little variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: quiet, submerged and built around a single release.

entries.name: Ankole-Watusi Cattle

waveform.description: Two grazing peaks in the cool of morning and late afternoon, separated by a midday trough of cud-chewing.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady heat-managed grazing and slow cud-chewing rest.

entries.name: Annam Pond Turtle

modes.label: A wild population reduced to almost nothing by collection for trade • Managed breeding groups held in Vietnam and abroad carrying nearly the whole gene pool • Offspring produced under management rather than in the marshes the species came from

waveform.description: A long decline levelling into a flat low line, because the wild collapse ended in a small managed population held steady.

entries.closingLine: Because the timescale is generational, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ant Mimic Mantis

modes.label: An early nymph black, narrow-waisted and ant-sized, moving in the rapid jerky manner of an ant with the front legs held forward like antennae
A later nymph and adult green and mantis-shaped, too large to pass as an ant, relying on stillness and foliage crypsis instead

waveform.description: A quick jerky early rhythm settling into a slow still one, because the animal switches from imitating movement to avoiding it.

entries.closingLine: The switch happens because the first stops being available rather than because the second is better, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Ant-mimicking Spider

waveform.description: A gently undulating mid-level line showing continuous, moderate activity: always moving, always maintaining the disguise, without long waits or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: That produces a mid-frequency system: not a slow reserve engine or a single dramatic switch, but a steady, ongoing rhythm of deceptive signaling woven into daily activity.

entries.name: Antarctic Petrel
entries.archetype: Commuting From Nunataks to the Ice Edge

waveform.description: Long foraging trips alternating with sustained incubation shifts at the colony.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long-range ocean foraging and enduring colony incubation.

entries.name: Apostlebird

modes.label: Living permanently in a group of about a dozen • Building one mud nest that all members attend • Foraging, roosting and moving as a single unit year round

waveform.description: A very even line with one broad gentle rise, because the group's life is continuous and the breeding season is a raised phase rather than an event.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle turns over annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Apple Snail

modes.label: Breathing through a gill while submerged • Grazing plant material underwater • Sealing the shell with an operculum when disturbed
Extending a long siphon to the surface or leaving the water entirely • Breathing air through a lung in the left mantle cavity • Sealing up and waiting out a dry season in mud

waveform.description: Ordinary variation alternating with long flat depressed stretches, because the animal genuinely alternates between two respiratory regimes.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two respiratory architectures, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Arabian Oryx
entries.archetype: Letting Body Heat Rise to Save Water

waveform.description: A low midday rest with gentle rises for feeding in the cool hours.

entries.closingLine: Because it is built on slow, water-saving movement and rest, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Arabian Sand Boa

waveform.description: A nearly unbroken floor with the smallest possible perturbations — the profile of an animal that is almost never doing anything.

entries.closingLine: Because the system replaces activity with burial in a medium that provides both shelter and concealment, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Arapaima

waveform.description: Evenly spaced surfacing events on a steady baseline — a rhythm imposed by physiology rather than by hunger.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs on a regular obligatory cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Archerfish

waveform.description: Watchful stretches broken by paired spikes of shot and interception.

entries.closingLine: Fast, committed, repeated attempts make this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Arctic Char

waveform.description: A low resident level and a raised migratory one in the same trace — the same fish running at a different setting.

entries.closingLine: Because the same system reconfigures itself to its context rather than running one way, it is an adaptive system.

entries.name: Arctic Fox

waveform.description: A mostly low, steady line with gentle repeating mid-height waves, showing long periods of background concealment with regular, moderate foraging activity layered on top.

entries.closingLine: That combination of a slow seasonal molt and ongoing, season-tuned activity makes the Arctic fox a bimodal LOW-plus-MID frequency system.

entries.name: Arctic Ground Squirrel

waveform.description: A long low flat segment representing deep hibernation, rising to a moderate, rolling plateau for the active season before returning to low, showing a system that spends most of its cycle in frozen minimal output with a defined preparation window.

entries.closingLine: The result is a bimodal rhythm: long stretches of ultra-low activity in a prepared place, anchored by a shorter, moderate, repeatable season of foraging and rebuilding that reloads the system for the next freeze.

entries.name: Arctic Hare

waveform.description: Long flat low-activity periods of still camouflage with a single sharp dip representing a brief high-activity escape burst before returning to quiet.

entries.closingLine: Because the body is built around a contrast between extended stillness and brief, intense escape runs, the Arctic hare operates as a bimodal system: a low-frequency camouflage-and-rest mode anchored to the snow, and a high-frequency sprint mode that is triggered only when danger forces it to spend.

entries.name: Arctic Tern
entries.archetype: The Long Way Round Is Cheaper

modes.label: Leaving the Arctic • Tracing an S down the Atlantic • Arriving south

waveform.description: A long sustained travelling rhythm carried across a year.

entries.closingLine: Sustained travel and feeding makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Argali

waveform.description: Steady grazing through most of the year, with clustered spikes of rutting clashes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: vigilant open-country grazing and violent rutting clashes.

entries.name: Argentine Black and White Tegu

waveform.description: An active warmed rhythm falling away into a long dormant floor.

entries.closingLine: That makes it an adaptive system: the operating state is selected by the season rather than fixed.

entries.name: Argus Monitor
entries.archetype: Standing Up on a Tripod of Tail

waveform.description: An active ranging rhythm with brief stationary raised pauses.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: continuous ranging with brief deliberate elevated pauses.

entries.name: Armadillo Girdled Lizard

waveform.description: An almost unbroken low line with one small perturbation — an animal whose answer to disturbance is to change shape, not level.

entries.closingLine: Because everything is invested in durable structure and almost nothing in activity or turnover, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Artichoke Plume Moth

modes.label: Wings divided along their length into narrow feather-like lobes rather than forming continuous surfaces • Those lobes rolled tightly together at rest and held out at right angles to the body • The whole insect reduced to a thin T-shape that reads as a dry grass stem

waveform.description: A very flat quiet line, because the insect rests immobile and flies only weakly at dusk.

entries.closingLine: Because the posture is held through the day, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Arowana

modes.label: Taking the fertilised eggs into the mouth • Holding developing young there for weeks without feeding • Releasing free-swimming fry and taking them back in when threatened

waveform.description: A steady line that drops to a sustained lower level and returns, because the brooding period is a long enforced pause in normal life.

entries.closingLine: Since breeding runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Box Turtle
entries.archetype: A Shell That Latches From Below

waveform.description: Steady foraging interrupted by quiet sealed spells when danger appears.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: steady foraging with a sealed, waiting refuge.

entries.name: Asian Common Toad

modes.label: Sitting under a streetlight • Swelling and tilting • Secreting from behind the eyes

waveform.description: A slow low line with two small lifts, because a toad that cannot run has almost nothing that registers as activity.

entries.closingLine: Since everything else runs slowly through the night, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Elephant

waveform.description: Two long feeding periods over a steady baseline — continuous demand rather than episodes of effort.

entries.closingLine: Because a vast continuous demand is met by steady precise gathering, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Fairy-bluebird

modes.label: Feather barbs containing a spongy keratin structure with air spaces of a consistent size but no regular arrangement • Light scattered by that structure reinforcing one wavelength regardless of the direction it is viewed from • A deep even blue that does not shift or flash with angle, unlike the iridescence of a starling or a sunbird

waveform.description: A very even rhythm with little variation, because the property does not change with circumstance.

entries.closingLine: Because the property is constant, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Forest Tortoise

modes.label: Raking leaf litter backwards with the forelimbs into a large mound • Laying the eggs inside the pile where decomposition generates heat • Remaining on the mound for days or weeks driving off anything that approaches

waveform.description: A flat line with one raised episode, because nest building and guarding is a single concentrated event in an otherwise slow year.

entries.closingLine: Because the sequence runs once a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Glossy Starling

modes.label: Taking small fruit whole in large flocks • Passing seeds through the gut intact within minutes • Voiding them under a roost or a perch elsewhere

waveform.description: A busy repeated pattern of similar events, because the flock feeds and moves in continuous bouts through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding bouts repeat, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Honey Bee

modes.label: Detecting a scouting hornet at the nest entrance • Engulfing it in a ball of hundreds of workers • Vibrating flight muscles until the centre reaches a temperature the hornet cannot survive and the bees can

waveform.description: A calm line rising into a sustained intense event and returning, because the response builds, holds for minutes and then ends.

entries.closingLine: Since the response is measured in minutes, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Hornet

modes.label: A hornet hovering in front of a hive entrance rather than entering it, facing the returning foragers • Bees taken in flight as they arrive loaded and slow, one at a time and repeatedly through the day • The colony inside eventually ceasing to forage at all, so the damage comes from the foragers stopping rather than from the number of bees killed

waveform.description: A steady repeating rhythm of hovering and striking, because the hornet works the entrance continuously through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the attacks recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Leaf Turtle

modes.label: A juvenile with a rigid plastron joined solidly to the shell and a serrated rear margin • Relying on running, hiding in leaf litter and dropping into water when threatened • Defence through movement because the shell cannot be shut

An adult in which the plastral sutures have loosened into a flexible ligament • Drawing the front lobe up against the carapace to close the shell on the head and forelimbs • Defence through sealing rather than fleeing

waveform.description: An active early phase settling into a slower later one, because the animal changes from a runner into a closer as it matures.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal operates one defensive architecture as a juvenile and a different one as an adult, it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Asian Palm Civet

modes.label: Moving the canopy • Taking only ripe fruit • Depositing the seed elsewhere

waveform.description: A flat daytime floor with a raised active block dropped into the middle of it, because the animal's operating day is a bounded night shift.

entries.closingLine: Because that nightly search is continuous, unhurried and repeated year-round, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Small-clawed Otter

modes.label: Feeling under stones • Crushing • Passing it on

waveform.description: A close-packed busy chatter of small movements, none of them large, because the work is done in many quick touches rather than in strokes.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole animal is one continuous close-range tactile search, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Swamp Eel

modes.label: Gulping air into a mouth and throat richly supplied with blood vessels • Crossing wet ground and burrowing into mud • Surviving in water with almost no oxygen at all

waveform.description: A steady moderate rhythm with no dramatic features, because the animal breathes and moves at an even unhurried rate.

entries.closingLine: Since breathing recurs continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Tramp Snail

modes.label: Circling a partner for an extended courtship • Driving a calcareous dart through the body wall of the other • Mating reciprocally with the dart's secretion already acting inside the recipient

waveform.description: A long slow line with brief sharp interruptions, because a very slow animal's life contains one abrupt event.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a season, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Vine Snake

modes.label: A horizontal keyhole-shaped pupil, unique among snakes, giving a wide field with acute resolution along one axis • A groove running along each side of the elongated snout, clearing the line of sight from each eye forward • Both eyes able to see the same point ahead, giving the binocular overlap needed to judge distance for a strike

waveform.description: A long motionless line with brief strikes, because the snake holds position for long periods and moves suddenly.

entries.closingLine: Because the snake waits and strikes occasionally, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Weaver Ant

modes.label: Chaining across gaps • Holding leaves together • Squeezing a larva along the seam

waveform.description: A tight busy chatter of small even peaks with no gaps, the trace of thousands of small simultaneous actions.

entries.closingLine: Because thousands of small actions run simultaneously and never stop, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Asian Woolly-necked Stork

waveform.description: Two walking-foraging plateaus separated by a midday rest and bookended by high roosts.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: walking patch-foraging and low-cost soaring and rest.

entries.name: Asiatic Black Bear

waveform.description: A rising feeding rhythm settling into a long low winter floor.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: concentrated accumulation and a long slow drawdown.

entries.name: Asiatic Rhinoceros Beetle

modes.label: Adults boring into the unopened crown of a coconut or oil palm • Cutting through the folded fronds before they have expanded • Leaving a single tunnel that becomes a row of V-shaped cuts across every leaf as it unfurls

waveform.description: A flat line with one damaging excursion, because a single boring event produces consequences that unfold slowly afterwards.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is generational, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Assassin Spider

waveform.description: A series of sharp, frequent peaks near the top of the range, representing a system built around repeated poised tension and rapid, precise strikes.

entries.closingLine: Because the system stays in a state of poised tension, committing energy in quick, accurate bursts whenever a narrow opportunity appears, this is a single-mode, high-frequency hunting architecture.

entries.name: Atlantic Blue Marlin

modes.label: Cruising blue water • Diving cold • Explosive pursuit

waveform.description: Repeated explosive surges separated by fast cruising.

entries.closingLine: Fast, volatile and short-horizon in every pursuit, this is a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Atlantic Cod

modes.label: Growing large over many years • Producing egg numbers that rise steeply with body size • Releasing them into the water column and providing nothing further

waveform.description: A quiet line rising to one broad annual event, because spawning is a concentrated season inside an otherwise steady year.

entries.closingLine: Since generations take years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Atlantic Herring

waveform.description: An even, tightly repeating wave: many identical small movements staying in step.

entries.closingLine: That makes the herring a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, networked and powerful only as a coordinated group.

entries.name: Atlantic Mackerel

modes.label: Swimming continuously from hatching to death • Driving water over the gills by forward motion rather than by pumping • Having no swim bladder, so stopping means sinking

waveform.description: A shallow perfectly regular oscillation with no interruption at all, because the animal never stops for any reason.

entries.closingLine: Since the tailbeat continues every second of life, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Atlantic Puffin

waveform.description: A day of alternating flights and dives with no settled stretch.

entries.closingLine: Repeated diving and provisioning makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Atlantic Sailfish

waveform.description: A fast climb to a short peak followed by a slower settle: one committed burst, then recovery.

entries.closingLine: That makes the sailfish a high-frequency system: explosive, short-horizon and dependent on recovery between attacks.

entries.name: Atlantic Salmon

waveform.description: A long, low river phase followed by sea growth, a return, and sometimes a second cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because the system switches from a patient river phase to a sea-going phase, it is a phase-change system.

entries.name: Atlantic Tarpon
entries.archetype: A Lung That Buys Dead Water

modes.label: Cruising • Rolling to gulp air • Running hard

waveform.description: A steady cruising rhythm broken by one very large surge.

entries.closingLine: Continuous cruising and feeding makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Atlantic Trumpetfish

waveform.description: Even mid-height oscillations: long hovering plateaus with small, regular dips where short ambush darts occur, reflecting steady stalking around coral lines.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system built on rhythmic, repeated ambushes and constant micro-adjustments around coral cover, rather than rare huge efforts or continuous high-speed motion.

entries.name: Atlantic Wolffish

modes.label: Crushing urchins, whelks and crabs with conical front teeth and molar plates • Grinding the shell fragments on a toothed palate • Feeding steadily on armoured prey nothing else takes
Ceasing to feed for several weeks after spawning • Shedding the entire dentition at once • Regrowing every tooth before feeding resumes

waveform.description: Steady feeding activity interrupted by a long flat depressed stretch, because the animal genuinely stops eating while the teeth are replaced.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, a weeks-long toothless non-feeding state is a distinct architecture, making it bimodal.

entries.name: Atlantic Yellow-nosed Albatross

waveform.description: A shallow soaring oscillation that drops away before it climbs — the mollymawk arc run out over deep water and back to one island.

entries.closingLine: Because enormous cheap movement is anchored to a very small fixed point on a slow reproductive clock, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Atlas Beetle
entries.archetype: Three Horns Closing as One Caliper

waveform.description: A long hidden accumulation, then short decisive grapples.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long hidden accumulation and a brief contest only some are built to enter.

entries.name: Atlas Moth

waveform.description: A long quiet accumulation, then a burn that decays to nothing.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long feeding accumulation and a short sealed burn with no income at all.

entries.name: Australasian Swamphen

modes.label: Pulling up a reed stem or a rhizome • Holding it in one foot raised to the bill • Stripping and chewing the soft base and discarding the rest

waveform.description: A steady deliberate rhythm of moderate excursions, because each item is handled individually and takes comparable effort.

entries.closingLine: Since items are processed continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Australian Box Jellyfish

waveform.description: A mostly low, gently undulating line showing quiet drifting, interrupted by one sharp narrow spike for the sudden, intense stinging event before returning to the low baseline.

entries.closingLine: This makes the box jellyfish a bimodal system: a low-frequency, drifting invisible boundary punctuated by rare, high-frequency bursts of intense, localized attack the moment that boundary is crossed.

entries.name: Australian Brush-turkey

waveform.description: A busy daily rhythm of raking and adjustment beside a long flat period of unattended development.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: daily mound management and long incubation with no parent sitting on the eggs.

entries.name: Australian Funnel-web Spider

modes.label: A silk-lined burrow with a collapsed funnel entrance under a log or in a bank • Irregular silk trip lines radiating outward across the ground from that entrance • The spider waiting just inside, striking outward the instant a line is disturbed

waveform.description: A long flat waiting line with sudden brief strikes, because the spider sits motionless inside until a line moves.

entries.closingLine: Because strikes are infrequent, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Australian Green Tree Frog

modes.label: Secreting a mixture of peptides across the whole skin surface • Killing bacteria and fungi on contact with it • Depending on that chemistry because a permeable skin cannot be sealed

waveform.description: A very even line with a single small disturbance, because the defence is continuous rather than triggered.

entries.closingLine: Since secretion is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Australian Magpie

waveform.description: Even, rolling pulses representing regular bouts of song and patrol across the day, without long dormancy or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because their survival comes from this steady rhythm of calling, listening, and patrolling—neither slow-hoarding nor pure bursts—the magpie is best understood as a mid-frequency system built on ongoing acoustic neighborhood maintenance.

entries.name: Australian Pelican

modes.label: Waiting through years in coastal and inland waters without breeding • Detecting and travelling hundreds of kilometres inland when monsoon rain fills Lake Eyre • Breeding in enormous colonies on the temporary lake and leaving as it dries

waveform.description: A very long flat stretch with one large irregular event, because breeding waits years for a flood and then happens all at once.

entries.closingLine: Because the trigger is irregular and rare, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Australian Pineapplefish

modes.label: A pair of light organs on the lower jaw housing dense colonies of luminous bacteria • The bacteria supplied with nutrients and oxygen by the fish and producing continuous light in return • That light shuttered and directed by the fish to illuminate small shrimp in the dark

waveform.description: A single nocturnal plateau, because the fish is inactive by day and hunts through the dark hours.

entries.closingLine: Because hunting is nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Australian Sea Lion
entries.archetype: Seabed Commuter on an Odd Calendar

waveform.description: Rest ashore alternating with long trips made of many repeated seabed dives.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long rest and lactation ashore and repeated seabed diving at sea.

entries.name: Axolotl

waveform.description: A quiet unvarying line — an animal whose remarkable property is chemical rather than behavioural.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at a slow steady rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Aye-aye

waveform.description: Rapid tapping runs punctuated by a deeper extraction — the animal's night is a repeated search-and-open cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because that cycle repeats steadily through every night, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Azure-winged Magpie
entries.archetype: A Flock Moving Tree by Tree

waveform.description: A steady rolling line of group foraging with occasional sharp collective mobbing peaks.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: steady social foraging and short, intense bouts of collective defence.

entries.name: Babirusa

waveform.description: A shallow repeating pattern with no large excursions — steady rooting and feeding through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding and moving run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bactrian Camel

modes.label: Losing a quarter of body water without failing • Drinking a hundred litres or more in a few minutes • Having oval red cells with membranes that stretch rather than burst as the blood dilutes

waveform.description: A long slow decline repeatedly reset by abrupt recoveries, because water is lost gradually and replaced all at once.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs over days, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Baird's Tapir

waveform.description: A steady nightly rhythm of feeding and moving between forest and water, with no peak and no dormancy.

entries.closingLine: Since browsing and moving run as a steady nightly cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bala Shark

modes.label: Shoaling in fast-flowing river channels in Southeast Asia • Being farmed in enormous numbers for the aquarium trade • Having the wild population collapse over the same period without anyone noticing

waveform.description: A steady shoaling rhythm without extremes, because a schooling river fish's day is continuous and even.

entries.closingLine: Since shoaling and feeding are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bald Eagle

waveform.description: A patient low line with very little movement.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: patient, stationary and almost entirely sensory.

entries.name: Bald Uakari

waveform.description: A steady troop-level rhythm across the day, with no single event standing out — foraging spread across many trees.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on continuous troop foraging and a continuously visible signal, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bald-faced Hornet

modes.label: One mated queen • Overwintering alone • Starting the first cells herself
Hundreds of workers • Envelope enlarged outward • Defended as a unit

waveform.description: A long flat floor rising into a single broad hump and collapsing back to it, because the colony is built from nothing each year and does not survive the winter.

entries.closingLine: Because a solitary founding state and a large defended collective state are both indispensable, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Bali Myna

waveform.description: A brisk even rhythm — a small bird feeding and calling continuously through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding and calling run steadily through the day, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ball Python

waveform.description: A long flat wait, one sharp strike, then a sustained elevated hold that eases back down.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an extremely cheap waiting state and a short, fully committed application of force.

entries.name: Ballan Wrasse

modes.label: Pulling molluscs and barnacles from rock with strong front teeth • Crushing them on paired pharyngeal plates in the throat • Working the same stretch of reef for years

waveform.description: A slow steady line with occasional modest rises, because a long-lived reef fish working the same ground has an even routine.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Baluchistan Pygmy Jerboa

waveform.description: Active bounding through the night, a long flat daytime trough in the burrow, then activity again after dusk.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: sheltered daytime conservation and a night of bounding forage.

entries.name: Banana Slug

modes.label: Laying trail • Rasping • Paying in water

waveform.description: A near-flat drift with a single slow undulation, the trace of an animal whose fastest state is still barely movement.

entries.closingLine: Because every process is slow and metered against a water budget, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Banana Stalk Fly

modes.label: Males reared on rich or poor larval diets developing into large or small adults respectively • Those males transferring more than sperm at mating, including material that affects how the offspring develop • Offspring of well-fed fathers growing larger than offspring of poorly fed fathers, with no genetic difference between the two

waveform.description: A slow generational cycle, because the effect is transmitted once per generation and appears in the next.

entries.closingLine: Because the effect passes once per generation, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Band-eyed Drone Fly

modes.label: Hovering at flowers • Passing for a bee • Larva breathing through a tube

waveform.description: A quick hovering flutter of even peaks, because the animal holds position at flowers rather than travelling between them.

entries.closingLine: Because the adult's hovering and feeding run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Banded Humbug Damselfish

modes.label: Living as a group in a single coral head with a strict size hierarchy • Each fish maintaining a size just below the one above it • Every fish moving up one place when a larger one is removed

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm with no extremes, because a group in one coral head does much the same thing all day.

entries.closingLine: Since interactions recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Banded Linsang

waveform.description: A light, quick, repeated rhythm — many small movements at low amplitude, none of them heavy.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from repeated small captures across a night, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Banded Mongoose
entries.archetype: Forage, Breed and Fight as One Pack

waveform.description: A steady foraging line broken by sudden collective spikes of alarm or defence.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: dispersed, chattering group foraging and sudden collective alarm or defence.

entries.name: Banded Palm Civet

waveform.description: A fine even rhythm of small finds through the night — many modest returns rather than any single capture.

entries.closingLine: Because returns accumulate from many small finds repeated nightly, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bank Swallow

waveform.description: A mostly low, steady line with gentle repeating mid-level rises, showing a stable shared burrow base with regular foraging commutes.

entries.closingLine: This produces a bimodal system: a low-frequency anchored burrow grid that persists across seasons, overlaid with mid-frequency, rhythmic foraging flights tied tightly to that common sandbank base.

entries.name: Bank Vole

modes.label: Breeding rapidly when seed and berry crops are good • Building to high density across a whole region • Collapsing within a season as food fails and predators concentrate

waveform.description: A large slow oscillation repeating across the span, because the population itself rises and falls on a multi-year cycle.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs over years while the animals live months, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Banner-tailed Kangaroo Rat
entries.archetype: One Mound, One Owner, One Larder

waveform.description: A flat daytime line inside the sealed mound, rising into a night of seed harvesting.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: night harvesting and a sealed, stocked home.

entries.name: Banteng

waveform.description: Two feeding peaks at dawn and late afternoon separated by a long shaded rest.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: productive edge grazing alternating with sheltered rumination.

entries.name: Bar-headed Goose

modes.label: Crossing high passes on migration • Loading oxygen from air a third as dense • Beating continuously with no soaring

waveform.description: A working rhythm that climbs into a sustained elevated section and returns, because the crossing is a prolonged extreme effort within an ordinary year.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle repeats seasonally within a working year, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bar-tailed Godwit
entries.archetype: Rebuilt Body for the Nonstop Crossing

waveform.description: Tide-timed feeding cycles give way to a long flat plateau of nonstop flight, then drop.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: tide-timed fuelling and a nonstop ocean crossing.

entries.name: Barbary Macaque

waveform.description: Two daily activity periods over a steady baseline — a troop rhythm with no individual events standing out.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on continuous social maintenance paying off in a seasonal physical return, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Barbary Sheep

waveform.description: Feeding peaks at the cool ends of the day, a midday lull, and a sharp climbing escape.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: cool-hours foraging and bursts of climbing escape.

entries.name: Barbel

modes.label: Holding position on gravel in fast water with a flat belly and large pectoral fins • Using the current's own force to press itself down • Feeling for invertebrates in the gravel with four barbels

waveform.description: A steady shallow rhythm sustained without large events, because the fish holds position and works the bed continuously.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bare-necked Umbrellabird

waveform.description: A mostly low, flat line with one tall, narrow dip upward toward high activity, showing long quiet periods punctuated by a brief, intense display bout.

entries.closingLine: That clear separation between an energy-thrifty, cryptic foraging mode and a short, high-intensity resonant display mode makes this a bimodal system with low and high frequencies.

entries.name: Bare-throated Bellbird

waveform.description: Repeated extreme peaks separated by quiet perching — the calls are the only large events in the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on repeated high-output signalling from a fixed position, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Barn Funnel Weaver

waveform.description: A low, mostly flat line with small, narrow dips for brief ambush sorties, showing a stable retreat with short activity bursts.

entries.closingLine: This anchored, shelter-first architecture makes the barn funnel weaver a low-frequency system: dense, patient and retreat-led.

entries.name: Barn Owl

waveform.description: A steady low quartering rhythm back and forth across open ground.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: a steady searching pattern in which the sensor rather than the speed does the work.

entries.name: Barn Swallow

waveform.description: A continuous rolling line with no rests: every part of the trace is working flight.

entries.closingLine: That makes the swallow a mid-frequency system: steady, repeatable and built to gather small amounts without ever pausing the process.

entries.name: Barnacle Goose

modes.label: Grazing the flush • Flying as a family • Returning to the same ledge

waveform.description: A grazing baseline lifting twice into long flat elevated plateaus, because the two journeys are sustained crossings rather than events.

entries.closingLine: Because a single continuous grazing operation is maintained across a moving geography, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Barramundi
entries.archetype: A Mouth That Opens Into a Vacuum

waveform.description: A still holding line broken by one instantaneous expansion.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: patient holding and one instantaneous engulfment.

entries.name: Barred Eagle-Owl

modes.label: Still in the mid-storey • Ear tufts level • Listening down

waveform.description: A high quiet line with three narrow downward strikes, each returning immediately to the same level.

entries.closingLine: Because hours of near-costless listening fund a movement lasting a second, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Barreleye
entries.archetype: Rotating Tubular Eyes Under a Dome

waveform.description: A long still searching state and a raised tracking one — the same instrument pointed two different ways.

entries.closingLine: Because the same system is reconfigured for the situation rather than running one way, it is an adaptive system.

entries.name: Basking Shark

waveform.description: An unhurried near-flat rhythm — the trace of an animal whose feeding requires no change of pace at all.

entries.closingLine: Because enormous scale is carried by continuous low-intensity intake, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bat-eared Fox

waveform.description: A steady pacing and listening rhythm across open ground.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, continuous acoustic searching.

entries.name: Bateleur

waveform.description: A long high plateau with a continuous side-to-side roll written into it — hours aloft with the rocking never stopping.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts continuous cheap coverage into a steady return, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bawean Deer

waveform.description: A quiet day and a raised night — the whole active period sits in the hours when nobody is about.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding runs as a steady nightly cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bay Duiker

waveform.description: Frequent modest feeding movements through the dark hours, falling away sharply before light.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on quiet continuous foraging with short committed escapes, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Baya Weaver

modes.label: Weaving a hanging shell from torn grass strips • Pausing at the helmet stage for inspection • Completing only the nests a female accepts

waveform.description: Repeated climbs that reach different heights before dropping back, because each nest is built up and only some are carried through.

entries.closingLine: Since nests are built within weeks, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bearded Reedling

waveform.description: An active insect-feeding rhythm settling into a lower winter level.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a soft-food active season and a hard-food conserving one.

entries.name: Bearded Seal
entries.archetype: Built to Probe, Not to Track

modes.label: Diving to the bottom • Sweeping the sediment • Back to the ice

waveform.description: A repeating dive to the bottom, a long sweep, and a return.

entries.closingLine: Steady repeated bottom foraging makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bearded Vulture
entries.archetype: Bones Dropped Onto a Known Rock

waveform.description: A slow, low-cost search cycle with rare deliberate efforts.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: patient, cheap, and aimed at a resource with no queue.

entries.name: Bee Hummingbird

waveform.description: A dense band at the top of the frame collapsing to a deep floor at dusk — two levels with almost nothing in between.

entries.closingLine: Because a maximum-rate daytime state alternates with a genuinely suppressed nocturnal one, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Beira

waveform.description: A steady modest rhythm — browsing and moving across rock at an unvarying pace through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because browsing and moving run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Belted Kingfisher

waveform.description: A regular patrolling rhythm repeated along the same line.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, repetitive patrolling of a fixed line rather than concentrated effort at a point.

entries.name: Beluga Sturgeon

waveform.description: A very low line with occasional slight lifts — a life measured in decades, in which a year shows almost nothing.

entries.closingLine: Because the entire cycle runs on a scale of decades, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Beluga Whale
entries.archetype: A Forehead That Aims the Sound

modes.label: Clicking • Reshaping the melon • Turning the head

waveform.description: A dense continuous stream of clicks and calls.

entries.closingLine: Continuous social and navigational calling makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bengal Monitor

waveform.description: Broad low plateaus of inactivity with moderate, rounded rises representing each measured foraging circuit before returning to a cooler, resting state.

entries.closingLine: The result is a bimodal system: a low-frequency, shelter-based recharge mode coupled to a mid-frequency, rhythmic patrol mode that systematically samples their habitat.

entries.name: Bengal Tiger

waveform.description: Long quiet ranging lines broken by two narrow full-height rushes, with no chase phase on either side of them.

entries.closingLine: Because a long patient low-cost approach exists to deliver one brief total commitment, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Bharal

modes.label: Grazing steep slopes • Watching • Moving onto broken rock

waveform.description: A slow, even trace: grazing steep ground with few events.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bicolor Angelfish

modes.label: Living as one of several females in a harem held by a single male • Feeding on algae and detritus across a small area of reef • Being ranked by size within the group
Changing sex within days of the male being lost • Taking over the harem and defending it • Producing sperm from tissue that was producing eggs weeks before

waveform.description: One level held, a single transition, and a different level afterwards, because the change happens once and does not reverse.

entries.closingLine: Because the change happens once and irreversibly, it operates as a phase-change system.

entries.name: Bicolor Parrotfish

modes.label: An initial-phase female, white with a broad orange band across the head and a dark eye patch, feeding within a harem on a defended stretch of reef
A terminal-phase male, green and pink with heavy scale outlines and a yellow spot behind the pectoral, holding a territory and displaying to a group of females

waveform.description: A subdued early rhythm giving way to a bolder later one, because the animal changes its whole role partway through life.

entries.closingLine: Parrotfish of both phases scrape algae and coral with fused beak-like teeth and produce large quantities of sand, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Big-headed Ant

modes.label: Minor workers making up the great majority of the colony, small and numerous, doing the foraging, brood care and nest work
Major workers with enormously enlarged heads and mandibles, far fewer, used for milling hard seeds and for defence

waveform.description: A rapid dense rhythm interrupted by a slower heavier one, because the two castes operate at completely different rates.

entries.closingLine: The two castes are different bodies for different jobs, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Bigclaw Snapping Shrimp

waveform.description: Long flat low activity punctuated by one sharp, narrow spike representing a single cavitation snap before returning to stillness.

entries.closingLine: Because the shrimp’s structure and habitat are built around extended low-output waiting punctuated by rare, explosive snaps, it operates as a bimodal system with a low-frequency resting/aiming mode and a high-frequency discharge mode.

entries.name: Bighorn Sheep

waveform.description: A mostly mid-level, gently undulating line with one sharp, narrow peak for a rutting clash, then a return to steady activity.

entries.closingLine: Most of life runs in the surefooted mid mode, but the system is incomplete without those short, explosive contests that decide breeding and status, making this a bimodal mid-and-high-frequency system.

entries.name: Binturong

waveform.description: A shallow unhurried rhythm — nothing in this animal's day has a sharp edge.

entries.closingLine: Because a slow-moving low-cost animal produces its main effect through digestion rather than activity, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bivalve

modes.label: Adding shell material in daily and seasonal increments throughout life • Locking the chemistry of the surrounding water into each increment as it forms • Producing a banded record in which temperature, salinity and productivity at the time are readable decades or centuries later

waveform.description: A regular seasonal oscillation repeated without variation, because growth follows the same annual cycle every year.

entries.closingLine: Because the record accumulates over years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black and Yellow Mud Dauber

modes.label: Building a mud cell • Stocking it with spiders stung into paralysis • Sealing one egg in with food that stays alive

waveform.description: A long series of near-identical working cycles, because the wasp repeats the same build-hunt-seal sequence cell after cell.

entries.closingLine: Since cells are completed within days, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Ant

modes.label: Laying pheromone on the return from food • Reinforcing the trail only while the source lasts • Letting it evaporate when the food runs out

waveform.description: Gradual build-ups and equally gradual declines, because a trail is reinforced into existence and then allowed to fade.

entries.closingLine: Since trails build and fade within minutes, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Caiman

waveform.description: An extremely flat floating line broken by a single vertical event — the proportion is the profile.

entries.closingLine: Because an almost costless concealed baseline supports a rare, total commitment, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Black Dragonfish

waveform.description: A deep daytime trough between night-time rises toward the surface to feed.

entries.closingLine: The adult female routine is bimodal: concealed daytime waiting at depth and a nightly hunting ascent.

entries.name: Black Giant Squirrel

modes.label: Hooking the hind feet over a branch and hanging out into space • Using both forefeet to handle large hard fruit while suspended • Feeding at the ends of branches that will not carry its weight

waveform.description: A steady moderate rhythm, because the animal moves and feeds continuously at an even pace.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding bouts recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Ground Beetle

modes.label: Running down prey and predators alike on the ground at night • Turning the tip of the abdomen toward an attacker • Discharging formic acid, quinones or other compounds from paired glands directly onto it

waveform.description: Steady running broken by extremely brief sharp discharges, because the animal moves constantly and fires rarely.

entries.closingLine: Since discharges are over in milliseconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Horse Fly

modes.label: Blade-like mandibles that cut and scissor through skin rather than piercing it • Blood welling into the resulting wound and pooling at the surface • The fly lapping that pool with a spongy mouthpart while anticoagulants in the saliva keep it flowing

waveform.description: A rapid persistent rhythm of approach and retreat, because the fly returns repeatedly after each disturbance.

entries.closingLine: Because approaches repeat constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Howler Monkey

waveform.description: A low settled line with two small dawn and dusk disturbances.

entries.closingLine: A large cheap signal standing in for expensive movement, on top of a slow gut, makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Lechwe

waveform.description: A regular bounding rhythm — every stride is the same leap through resisting water.

entries.closingLine: Because the daily cycle of grazing and moving through the floodplain is steady, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Mamba

waveform.description: Long ordinary hours broken by very short, total commitments.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: short, decisive, expensive episodes separated by long uneventful hours.

entries.name: Black Planthopper

modes.label: Glands on the abdomen of the nymph extruding long threads of white wax • Those threads held in a fan behind the insect, breaking its outline completely • The threads detaching in a predator's mouth or grip while the nymph jumps clear

waveform.description: A quiet feeding line with abrupt escapes, because the nymph sits still on a stem and jumps when disturbed.

entries.closingLine: Because the wax accumulates over days, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Rat
entries.archetype: Climbing to Nests Nothing Else Reaches

modes.label: Climbing rigging and branches • Breeding fast • Emptying a seabird colony

waveform.description: A fast volatile rhythm of rapid breeding and constant movement.

entries.closingLine: Short lives and rapid breeding make this a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Rhinoceros
