waveform.description: A steady selective rhythm — many small deliberate pulls rather than any bulk feeding.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding runs as a steady daily selection, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Sea Bass

modes.label: Occupying wrecks, reefs and hard structure on the shelf • Moving inshore and offshore with the seasons • Shifting the whole distribution northward as bottom water has warmed

waveform.description: A varying line whose whole level drifts steadily upward across the span, because the baseline itself is moving.

entries.closingLine: Since the shift runs across decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Sicklebill

waveform.description: Even mid-height waves showing repeated bouts of foraging and display using the specialized curved bill rather than long waits or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: That makes the Black Sicklebill a mid-frequency system: a rhythm of ongoing, shaped interactions where its curved advantage pays off every day.

entries.name: Black Skimmer

modes.label: Flying low • Blade in the water • Snapping shut on contact

waveform.description: Long low passes with sharp downward catches through them.

entries.closingLine: Continuous low-tide foraging makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Skirt Tetra

modes.label: Shoaling loosely while feeding • Releasing alarm chemical when skin is torn • Contracting the whole shoal within seconds

waveform.description: A long calm line broken by one abrupt vertical drop with a slow recovery, because the alarm is instantaneous while the return to normal is not.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding and shoaling run through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Spiny-tailed Iguana

modes.label: Basking in the open where escape distance is long • Running on the hind legs at speeds recorded above thirty kilometres an hour • Reaching a burrow, a crevice or a tree before anything can close

waveform.description: A still basking line broken by extremely sharp brief events, because the animal is motionless and then running flat out.

entries.closingLine: Since escape runs are brief and repeated, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Swallower

waveform.description: A flat, low-activity line showing a deep-sea fish built for long, steady digestion with no separate high-frequency operating mode.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a single-mode, low-frequency system: sparse opportunities, massive one-off intake, and long, steady processing between events.

entries.name: Black Swallowtail

modes.label: A silk pad spun at the tail end and gripped by the cremaster, holding the base of the pupa to a stem • A loop of silk spun across the thorax and anchored at both ends, forming a girdle • The pupa held upright against the stem rather than hanging, so it sits in the posture and position of a broken twig or a leaf base

waveform.description: A long sustained motionless period, because the pupa is fixed in place for weeks or months.

entries.closingLine: Because pupation runs across months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black Swan

waveform.description: A smooth even rhythm with very little visible variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, rhythmic and organised around sustained reach rather than bursts.

entries.name: Black Vulture

waveform.description: A long low soaring line with gentle undulation and no spikes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: patient, cheap soaring in which the expensive work of searching is done by someone else.

entries.name: Black-and-rufous Elephant Shrew

waveform.description: Low continuous housekeeping along the trails, punctuated by two near-vertical escape sprints that end as abruptly as they start.

entries.closingLine: Because an animal built on daily upkeep also depends on an all-out run that the upkeep exists to enable, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Black-and-white Colobus
entries.archetype: A Thumb Removed to Move Faster

modes.label: Leaping between crowns • Hooking with four fingers • Sitting to digest

waveform.description: A leaping rhythm interrupted by long sedentary digestion.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-and-white Ruffed Lemur

waveform.description: Dense chorus bursts at either end of a steadier middle — the day is bracketed by calling and filled with feeding.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding and calling run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-and-yellow Garden Spider

waveform.description: A gently undulating mid-line, representing ongoing cycles of web use and repair with a consistently visible structure.

entries.closingLine: Because the spider’s foraging depends on this standing, signposted structure, its whole system runs as a rhythmic, mid-frequency operation: build, signal, intercept, repair, rather than slow stockpiling or brief explosive bursts.

entries.name: Black-bellied Whistling Duck

modes.label: Females laying eggs in the nests of other females of the same species as well as in their own • Dump nests accumulating far more eggs than one bird laid or can cover, sometimes over fifty • Some of those nests abandoned because the clutch is uncoverable, while others hatch broods containing the young of several mothers

waveform.description: A single seasonal accumulation and decline, because eggs pile up over weeks and the outcome resolves at once.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-billed Magpie

waveform.description: A steady foraging line with repeated slower dips as surplus is cached and recovered.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: steady opportunistic foraging and a slower cycle of caching and recovery.

entries.name: Black-breasted Leaf Turtle

waveform.description: Almost no variation at all — a small animal moving slowly through litter and doing nothing else.

entries.closingLine: Because activity and intake both run very low, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-browed Albatross

waveform.description: A tight shallow soaring oscillation — the same repeated arc that converts wind gradient into distance, run on a shorter shelf-edge circuit.

entries.closingLine: Because enormous distances are covered on borrowed energy under a slow reproductive clock, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-capped Bulbul

modes.label: A single widespread species recognised for a century across South and Southeast Asia, differing between regions in the colour of the throat and head • Genetic work finding those regional forms to be deeply divergent lineages rather than variants of one bird • The species split into several, each with a much smaller range and a conservation status that had never been assessed

waveform.description: A steady line with a stepped drift, because the change is in how the population is counted rather than in the birds.

entries.closingLine: Because the reassessment runs across decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-crested Coquette

modes.label: The wing tracing a horizontal figure of eight rather than beating up and down • The shoulder joint rotating so the wing inverts at the end of each stroke • Lift generated on the backstroke as well as the forward stroke, holding the body still in the air

waveform.description: An extremely fast even oscillation with no variation, because both halves of every stroke do the same work.

entries.closingLine: Because wingbeats run dozens per second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-crowned Night Heron
entries.archetype: The Same Marsh, Eight Hours Later

waveform.description: A low daytime floor rising into a sustained night level.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an inactive day and a productive uncontested night.

entries.name: Black-faced Ibis
entries.archetype: An Ibis That Left the Water

waveform.description: A steady walking and probing rhythm across open grassland.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, methodical, tactile ground-working.

entries.name: Black-footed Albatross

waveform.description: A shallow continuous S-curve that never stops and never spikes — the shape of energy taken from the wind rather than spent from the body.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal moves enormous distances on borrowed energy and reproduces on a decade-scale clock, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-footed Cat
entries.archetype: A Kill Every Half Hour, All Night

waveform.description: Dense unbroken hunting activity across a whole night.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: continuous, unbanked and running with no margin.

entries.name: Black-footed Ferret

waveform.description: A regular nightly rhythm of entries and returns — the same move repeated through the dark hours.

entries.closingLine: Because hunting runs as a steady nightly cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-headed Gull

modes.label: Nesting on open ground in a dense colony • Picking up the shell within minutes of a chick hatching • Flying it away from the nest before returning

waveform.description: A colony baseline broken by regular brief events, because the removals are short deliberate actions within continuous activity.

entries.closingLine: Since removals recur through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-headed Ibis

waveform.description: A metronomic sequence of identical probes — the rhythm of a bird that works by coverage rather than by selection.

entries.closingLine: Because returns accumulate from many identical low-cost probes repeated for hours, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-legged Kittiwake

waveform.description: Long flat stretches on the ledge broken by repeated rises for foraging trips out to sea.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: patient, shared attendance on the ledge and repeated foraging trips out to sea.

entries.name: Black-naped Oriole

modes.label: A horizontal fork selected near the end of a slender outer branch rather than against the trunk • Fibre, bark strips and grass woven and bound around both arms of the fork to form a deep hanging cup • The nest suspended beyond the reach of anything that cannot fly, on branches too thin to bear a climbing animal

waveform.description: A single seasonal build and decline, because the construction and the brood run once through the year.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-naped Tern

waveform.description: A steady searching line with short repeated drops cut into it.

entries.closingLine: Many cheap repeated attempts across a long day make this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-necked Crane

waveform.description: A shallow annual dip and recovery — a movement down and back rather than a long journey out and in.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle repeats steadily each year, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Black-necked Stilt

waveform.description: A steady deliberate wading rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady deliberate feeding in a zone it has largely to itself.

entries.name: Black-necked Swan
entries.archetype: A Neck Visible Across a Lagoon

waveform.description: Calm continuous surface feeding on open water.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady surface feeding organised around reach and recognition at range.

entries.name: Black-shouldered Kite

waveform.description: A costly hovering rhythm dropping into a slow controlled descent.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: expensive hovering and a slow controlled drop.

entries.name: Black-tailed Jackrabbit

waveform.description: Long stretches of low, steady activity punctuated by a single sharp, narrow spike representing an explosive sprint and rapid return to stillness.

entries.closingLine: Because its survival depends on conserving energy in a vulnerable landscape and then converting that reserve into short, intense escape runs, the jackrabbit operates as a bimodal system with a low-frequency watchful baseline and a high-frequency burst-escape mode.

entries.name: Black-winged Stilt

modes.label: Wading in water deeper than any comparable wader can enter • Picking invertebrates from the surface and just below with a fine straight bill • Feeding on ground that shorter-legged species have to leave

waveform.description: A steady deliberate rhythm of similar events, because the bird picks continuously at an unhurried pace.

entries.closingLine: Since picking recurs constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blackbuck

modes.label: Grazing open plain • Holding a small patch • Darkening with rank

waveform.description: A steady grazing rhythm with a concentrated breeding pulse.

entries.closingLine: This is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blacktip Reef Shark

modes.label: Never stopping • Reading electrical fields • Working a small known patch

waveform.description: A continuous unbroken swell that never touches a baseline, because this animal has no resting state to return to.

entries.closingLine: Because the swimming and the sensing run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blakiston's Fish Owl

waveform.description: A low, steady line with tiny undulations, showing long quiet watching with only slight adjustments rather than big bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is organized around long stretches of stillness and careful signal filtering, with energy spent only on select high-probability lunges, this owl is a distinctly low-frequency, patience-led hunter.

entries.name: Blanket Octopus

modes.label: Drifting in open water • Carrying stolen tentacles • Unfurling when pressed

waveform.description: A loose drifting swell with no sharp edges, because an animal with nowhere to hide never accelerates to hide in it.

entries.closingLine: Because the drifting and hunting run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blesbok
entries.archetype: Each Extra Head Buys Grazing Time

modes.label: Grazing • Lifting the head • Grazing again

waveform.description: A regular graze-and-scan pulse repeated across the day.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daytime grazing makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blind Cave Tetra
entries.archetype: Eyeless Forager Reading the Water Itself

waveform.description: A nearly continuous line of foraging with no clear rest trough.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a continuous sensory search, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blister Beetle

waveform.description: A steady, low, slightly undulating line showing a constant background cost of maintaining chemical defenses rather than sharp bursts of activity.

entries.closingLine: That makes blister beetles a low-frequency system built around a durable, always-on chemical boundary that shapes interactions long before a physical fight begins.

entries.name: Blobfish

waveform.description: A nearly flat line with almost imperceptible movement — an animal that spends less than almost anything with a backbone.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole body plan replaces effort with density matching, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blood Parrot Cichlid

modes.label: Drawing food in by suction through a permanently open beak-like mouth • Failing to grip or tear anything • Feeding slowly on small sinking items

waveform.description: A shallow repetitive pattern with no strong events at all, because every feeding action is weak and nothing about the routine varies.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding attempts repeat through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blossom-headed Parakeet

modes.label: A bill built for cracking seed and climbing, not for excavating sound timber • Nest sites limited to existing holes cut by woodpeckers and barbets or produced by decay • Competition with other cavity nesters for a supply the parakeet has no way to increase

waveform.description: A steady annual rhythm with a raised breeding period, because the constraint applies once a year.

entries.closingLine: Because breeding is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blow Fly

waveform.description: A sharp arrival spike at the carcass, then a sustained larval feeding plateau that fades as larvae leave to pupate.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a fast arrival race and a steady collective feeding phase.

entries.name: Blue Bird-of-paradise
entries.archetype: Upside-Down Plume Fan and Mechanical Song

waveform.description: Steady fruit foraging with a single sustained peak of inverted display.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: canopy fruit-feeding and short, inverted display.

entries.name: Blue Button Jelly
entries.archetype: A Wind-Driven Disc of Divided Labour

waveform.description: A near-constant line of passive drifting and feeding with no rest cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because the system drifts and feeds continuously without any rest cycle or active travel, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Crane

modes.label: Nesting on open dry grassland and cropland rather than in marsh • Laying directly on bare ground with no built nest and no surrounding water • Defending the site by long sightlines and aggressive approach instead of by inaccessibility

waveform.description: A flat line with one long raised breeding season, because the whole commitment falls in a single annual period.

entries.closingLine: Because breeding is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Duiker
entries.archetype: Living on What the Canopy Drops

modes.label: Working the forest floor • Taking fallen fruit • Eating things a ruminant should not

waveform.description: A quiet, careful foraging rhythm close to cover.

entries.closingLine: Quiet, careful and small-scale, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Glaucus

modes.label: Floating upside down • Eating the stinger • Storing its cells intact

waveform.description: A slow surface drift with no propulsion in it, because the animal does not swim and the current supplies the movement.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at the speed of a current, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Morpho
entries.archetype: Blue Made of Shape, Not Pigment

waveform.description: A hard on-off flicker repeating several times a second.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: a fast intermittent signal that beats pursuit instead of outrunning it.

entries.name: Blue Mud Dauber

modes.label: Carrying water • Remodelling somebody else's mud • Stocking one cell at a time

waveform.description: A measured repeating rhythm of separate errands, each one similar to the last because each cell is filled the same way.

entries.closingLine: Because that cycle runs steadily through the warm months, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Parrotfish

modes.label: Biting algae and its rock substrate with fused beak-like teeth • Crushing the whole mouthful in a pharyngeal mill • Voiding the rock as fine carbonate sand

waveform.description: A very dense and completely regular series of identical bites, because the animal works the substrate continuously all day.

entries.closingLine: Since bites recur every few seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Tang
entries.archetype: A Folding Blade at the Tail

modes.label: Grazing algae across the reef in loose groups • Keeping a hinged spine folded flat in a groove at the tail base • Flicking the tail sideways to cut anything that presses too close

waveform.description: An even grazing rhythm broken by occasional sharp events, because the blade is deployed rarely against a background of ordinary feeding.

entries.closingLine: Since grazing is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Tit
entries.archetype: A Brood Timed to a Peak

modes.label: Reading spring temperature and vegetation to set laying date • Incubating so hatching meets the caterpillar peak • Feeding a large brood through a window of about a fortnight

waveform.description: A long ordinary line rising to one concentrated peak and falling back, because everything in the year converges on a single short window.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding trips recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Tree Monitor

waveform.description: An active searching rhythm — an alert lizard covering bark continuously rather than waiting anywhere.

entries.closingLine: Because searching runs as a steady daily activity, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue Whale

waveform.description: A long low cruising line broken by two enormous lunges — the most expensive event in the animal kingdom, twice.

entries.closingLine: Because a cheap oceanic baseline funds a rare extreme commitment, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Blue Wildebeest

modes.label: Walking the green edge • Cropping short grass • Never settling
Calving together • Standing within minutes • Swamping the predators

waveform.description: A long even walking rhythm interrupted by one short raised block, because the calving is a narrow window rather than a spike or a season.

entries.closingLine: Because a continuous movement funds one narrow synchronised release, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Blue-and-yellow Macaw

modes.label: Flying wingtip to wingtip • Calling continuously • Landing at the same clay bank

waveform.description: A loud regular exchange of similar peaks, because the calling is continuous and answered rather than occasional.

entries.closingLine: Because the calling and flying run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-crowned Hanging Parrot

modes.label: The female cutting strips of leaf and bark with her bill • Tucking those strips among the feathers of her rump and flanks rather than carrying them in the bill • Flying to the nest hole with both bill and feet free and unloading the strips there

waveform.description: A brisk repeating rhythm of trips, because the bird makes many short journeys carrying material.

entries.closingLine: Because nest building is seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-footed Booby

waveform.description: A working day of repeated dives with the display renewed between them.

entries.closingLine: Repeated diving and daily upkeep of the display make this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-fronted Amazon

modes.label: A thick muscular tongue with its own skeletal support and fine motor control • Food rotated and positioned against the bill by the tongue while the bill does the cutting • The same tongue shaping the airflow from the syrinx to produce consonant-like sounds without lips or teeth

waveform.description: A busy continuous rhythm, because the tongue is working constantly during both feeding and calling.

entries.closingLine: Because both activities are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-headed Macaw

modes.label: Feeding on unripe seeds and fruit protected by tannins and alkaloids that most animals cannot process • Gathering at exposed riverbank clay faces and eating the clay itself • Clay minerals binding those compounds in the gut so the toxins pass through without being absorbed

waveform.description: A regular daily rhythm with a recurring dip, because the birds feed steadily and gather at the clay at a predictable time.

entries.closingLine: Because the visits are daily and the diet steady, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-naped Parrot

modes.label: Birds feeding scattered through dense canopy where none can see any other • Loud contact calls exchanged constantly to establish who is where • The flock held together as a structure in sound rather than in sight

waveform.description: A rapid call-and-answer rhythm, because the exchange continues constantly while the birds feed.

entries.closingLine: Because calling is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-ringed Octopus

waveform.description: A low hidden baseline with one pulsing cluster — the display flashes repeatedly within a single event rather than once.

entries.closingLine: Because a cheap concealed baseline is paired with an instant unmistakable display, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Blue-rumped Parrot

modes.label: Two toes forward and two back on each foot, giving an opposed grip rather than a perching one • Food lifted to the bill in one foot while the bird stands on the other • The bill acting as a third point of contact so climbing and manipulation use the same three limbs

waveform.description: A steady busy rhythm of handling, because the bird works continuously at food with feet and bill.

entries.closingLine: Because handling is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-spotted Mudskipper
entries.archetype: Grazing the Mud Surface Between Tides

waveform.description: Two low-tide grazing windows a day, each with short bursts of display.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: MID grazing and HIGH display, both timed by the tides.

entries.name: Blue-spotted Salamander

waveform.description: A quiet buried line lifted briefly by one thaw and settling again.

entries.closingLine: A long cheap buried life and one short return make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Blue-tongued Skink

waveform.description: A slow low line interrupted by one loud held display.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a slow, cheap ordinary life and a brief, very loud defensive display.

entries.name: Blue-winged Macaw

modes.label: Flocks that on close inspection consist of pairs flying side by side rather than a uniform mass • Each pair maintaining position relative to one another rather than to the flock as a whole • The bond persisting across years and outside the breeding season entirely

waveform.description: A close paired rhythm in which two elements track each other, because the unit of the flock is two birds rather than one.

entries.closingLine: Because the coordination is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bluebottle Fly

modes.label: Detecting sulphur compounds from decomposition at long range • Flying upwind to the source • Laying within hours of death

waveform.description: A fast continuous oscillation with no structure at a larger scale, because the animal is searching constantly and everything happens within hours.

entries.closingLine: Since the whole search-and-lay cycle runs within hours, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Blueface Angelfish

modes.label: Grazing sponges and tunicates loaded with toxins and glass spicules • Processing those compounds rather than avoiding them • Feeding on a resource left almost untouched by other reef fish

waveform.description: A very even line, because the food supply is constant and requires no timing or pursuit at all.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is steady, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bluefin Tuna

waveform.description: Sustained high activity with no floor — a fish that cannot stop swimming and rarely drops out of its working band.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole architecture is held at a high rate all the time, it is a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Bluespine Unicornfish

modes.label: Ranging the reef • Cropping tough weed • Blades always out

waveform.description: A steady rolling browse with even peaks, because the animal works its way across reef without stopping or hurrying.

entries.closingLine: Because the browsing is continuous and unhurried across a large area, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bluestreak Cleaner Wrasse

waveform.description: A steady working rhythm: client after client handled at the same pace through the day.

entries.closingLine: That makes the wrasse a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, networked and built on repeated exchange rather than any single event.

entries.name: Boa Constrictor

waveform.description: A long still line broken by one sustained tightening.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: near-total stillness and one intense, monitored, expensive event.

entries.name: Boat-billed Heron
entries.archetype: A Scoop Where Others Have a Spear

modes.label: Waiting in mangrove shade • Scooping • Feeling with bristles

waveform.description: Long motionless waits in shade with occasional quick scoops.

entries.closingLine: Slow and mostly stationary, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bobbit Worm

waveform.description: A low, almost flat line with only tiny ripples, showing long buried stillness with minimal visible change even when striking.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole biology is built around long periods of still concealment punctuated by very short, localized actions rather than ongoing activity or roaming bursts, the bobbit worm is best understood as a single-mode, low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bobcat

waveform.description: A long quiet approach line ending in one brief committed burst.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long patient approach and a very brief commitment.

entries.name: Bocage's Wall Lizard

modes.label: Dorsal patterning of green, brown and black reticulation matching lichen-mottled granite • Populations differing in ground colour and pattern density according to the rock they occupy • Individuals remaining on the substrate their pattern matches rather than moving between rock types

waveform.description: A brisk regular rhythm of basking and darting, because the lizard alternates between stillness and short sprints.

entries.closingLine: Because basking and darting alternate constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Boelen's Python

waveform.description: A long low trace with one shallow lift — warming is continuous and cheap, while feeding is a rare, brief commitment.

entries.closingLine: Since the system earns its heat passively and spends its energy only at rare intervals, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Boeseman's Rainbowfish

modes.label: A species confined to a small group of connected lakes in the Vogelkop peninsula of West Papua and nowhere else on earth • Males carrying a striking split colouring, blue-grey at the front and orange at the rear, that made them highly desirable in the aquarium trade • Enormous numbers exported from those lakes through the 1980s and 1990s, from a total range of a few square kilometres

waveform.description: A decline flattening at a low level, because the population fell under collection and has stayed reduced.

entries.closingLine: Because the decline runs across decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bog Turtle
entries.archetype: A Turtle Kept Alive by Spring Seepage

waveform.description: A long dormant winter line and a steady raised plateau through the active season.

entries.closingLine: The system switches between a dormant winter phase and a steady active season of basking, foraging and burrowing.

entries.name: Bolas Spider
entries.archetype: A Borrowed Scent on a Swinging Thread

waveform.description: A long, flat luring line broken by a few brief swings when moths arrive.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long patient lure and a brief swing.

entries.name: Bold Jumper

modes.label: Attaching a dragline before every leap • Paying it out during the jump and using tension to control pitch and rotation • Braking on it if the landing fails, and climbing back up the same line

waveform.description: Steady movement broken by very brief full-depth events, because the animal stalks constantly and jumps occasionally.

entries.closingLine: Since jumps recur through the day, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Bolivian Squirrel Monkey

waveform.description: A gently oscillating mid-level line showing ongoing, regular social and movement activity without extreme peaks or deep troughs.

entries.closingLine: The result is a mid-frequency system built on rhythmic, ongoing social and spatial coordination: operational, networked and continuously maintained.

entries.name: Bombardier Beetle

waveform.description: A flat ordinary baseline interrupted by a tight cluster of very tall pulses.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a cheap ordinary baseline holding one violent, briefly available response.

entries.name: Bongo

waveform.description: Two long feeding periods bracketing the darkest hours, on a baseline that never rises far — a big animal keeping its activity low and steady.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts steady quiet browsing inside cover into a living, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bonobo

waveform.description: A busy even rhythm with no large peaks — tension is released constantly rather than allowed to build.

entries.closingLine: Because that regulation runs steadily through every day, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bontebok

waveform.description: An even grazing baseline with regular small lifts — heads coming up to check and dropping back, all day long.

entries.closingLine: Because grazing, watching and responding proceed as a steady daily rhythm, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Boobook Owl
entries.archetype: An Owl That Hunts by Eye

waveform.description: A watchful perched line broken by short agile sallies.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a watchful perched baseline and short agile aerial captures.

entries.name: Book Scorpion

waveform.description: Long, quiet hunting in crevices with a rare, sudden ride on another insect.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: a LOW mode of concealed, patient hunting and a rare HIGH mode of hitchhiking dispersal.

entries.name: Boomslang

waveform.description: A sustained searching rhythm with modest rises where prey is approached — effort spread across the hunt.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on sustained searching with delayed chemical resolution, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bootlace Worm

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line with small, regular downward dips representing repeated, moderate-intensity reach-and-retract feeding actions from concealment.

entries.closingLine: That produces a mid-frequency pattern: a stable base of concealment punctuated by repeated, moderate, tool-based strikes whenever food and safety briefly overlap.

entries.name: Bornean Bearded Pig

waveform.description: Steady foraging interrupted by one large irregular surge of movement and breeding.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady opportunistic foraging with irregular bursts of movement and breeding.

entries.name: Bornean Bristlehead

waveform.description: A gently undulating midline showing steady, ongoing activity within a single, consistent operating pattern.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system: ongoing, rhythmic activity expressed through one enduring, singular lineage pattern rather than multiple modes or bursts.

entries.name: Bornean Orangutan

waveform.description: One modest lift each cycle and nothing else — a single repeated task performed once a day for a lifetime.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bornean Pygmy Elephant

modes.label: Walking river valleys • Opening paths • Remembering routes for decades

waveform.description: A slow steady rhythm of travel measured in decades.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bornean Slow Loris
entries.archetype: Venom Mixed From Arm Gland and Saliva

waveform.description: A slow, quiet line with one sharp defensive spike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: quiet deliberate climbing backed by a rare, costly bite.

entries.name: Bowfin

waveform.description: Long flat low-activity baseline with one sharp, narrow spike representing a brief ambush strike before returning to the same low level.

entries.closingLine: This architecture—air breathing that supports long, low-cost hiding punctuated by short, explosive ambush—makes the bowfin a bimodal system with a dominant low-frequency survival mode and a high-frequency capture burst.

entries.name: Bowhead Whale

waveform.description: A single very long slow swell repeated across the whole frame — the tempo of an animal whose life is measured in centuries.

entries.closingLine: Because everything is arranged around insulation, endurance and very slow continuous intake, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bowmouth Guitarfish

waveform.description: A smooth even trace — continuous unhurried movement along the bottom with nothing abrupt in it.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding and moving both run at a steady low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Boxer Crab

waveform.description: A tiny steady pattern of waving and picking, never rising far.

entries.closingLine: Minimal movement and constant upkeep make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Brahminy Kite

modes.label: Soaring low over harbours, estuaries and fishing grounds watching other birds rather than the water • Harrying terns, gulls and other raptors until they release or drop what they are carrying • Catching the dropped item in the air or taking it from the surface before the owner recovers it

waveform.description: A steady patrolling rhythm with repeated chases, because the bird soars continuously and harries whenever an opportunity appears.

entries.closingLine: Because chases recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Brazilian Lava Lizard

modes.label: Moving between sun and shade many times an hour • Changing posture and orientation to the sun to control heat gain • Holding body temperature within a narrow band by position alone

waveform.description: A rapid regular alternation maintained throughout, because the animal is moving between sun and shade continuously.

entries.closingLine: Since the shuttling recurs constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Brazilian Treehopper

waveform.description: A gently undulating mid-level line, showing a constant, built-in structural effect that is always present rather than spiking only at rare moments.

entries.closingLine: Because the structure is always present and passively working whenever anything looks at the insect, its system is a steady, mid-frequency pattern: a constant architectural rewrite of how observers parse its form rather than a rare burst or deep reserve play.

entries.name: Brazilian Wandering Spider

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line of movement with a single sharp narrow dip upward representing an explosive pounce before returning to roaming search.

entries.closingLine: The spider’s survival depends on both modes working together — systematic ground search to find opportunities, then brief explosive attacks to convert them — which makes it a bimodal system with a mid-frequency roaming baseline and a high-frequency strike burst layered on top.

entries.name: Brill

modes.label: Settling onto a new substrate and comparing it against the eyes' input • Redistributing pigment within chromatophores under nervous control • Reproducing the tone, contrast and coarseness of the ground within minutes

waveform.description: A smooth slow oscillation with no sharp features, because the change is gradual and continuous rather than a switch.

entries.closingLine: Since matching happens over minutes, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Brilliant Blue

modes.label: A male occupying a sunlit opening in vegetation and perching on a prominent leaf within it • Any passing insect intercepted and pursued, with rival males driven out and females approached • The same gap held for days, so the male is defending a position rather than a resource, because females passing through are what the position delivers

waveform.description: A repeating pattern of perching and sallying, because the male returns to the same leaf after every interception.

entries.closingLine: Because interceptions recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Brimstone Butterfly

modes.label: Flying from early spring through summer • Feeding at flowers and searching for buckthorn to lay on • Living as an active adult for weeks at a time
Hanging among ivy or bramble with wings closed and leaf-shaped • Accumulating glycerol and other cryoprotectants in the tissues • Surviving frost, snow and rain without shelter for months

waveform.description: Long flat depressed stretches alternating with an extended active period, because the year is genuinely divided into two different states.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two physiologies, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Bristle-tail Filefish

waveform.description: A gentle, regular undulation around a midline, showing steady, small-amplitude motion that never fully stops or spikes.

entries.closingLine: Because its safety, feeding and recovery all rely on the same ongoing, low-amplitude motion that tracks the reef’s rhythm, this is a mid-frequency system built on continuous, believable drift rather than long stillness or sudden bursts.

entries.name: Bristlenose Pleco

modes.label: Males developing branched fleshy tentacles across the snout that resemble a mass of wriggling larvae • Occupying and defending a cave or crevice into which a female is invited to lay • The male remaining alone in the cave fanning and guarding the eggs until they hatch and the fry disperse

waveform.description: A long sustained raised commitment, because the male holds the cave and tends the clutch continuously for days.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Broad-bodied Chaser

modes.label: Watching from a perch with an upward-facing eye region • Launching on an intercept course • Taking the prey from beneath in flight

waveform.description: Very frequent near-vertical spikes from a constant baseline, because each attack is a brief, violent excursion from a motionless perch.

entries.closingLine: Since attacks recur within seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Brolga
entries.archetype: Dancing and Duetting to Hold a Pair

waveform.description: Steady wetland foraging broken by short, sharp bursts of display.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady wetland foraging punctuated by short, intense displays.

entries.name: Bronze Ground Beetle

modes.label: Seizing a slug or caterpillar with curved mandibles • Regurgitating digestive fluid onto it • Sucking up the liquefied tissue and leaving the rest

waveform.description: A quiet line with occasional broad raised sections, because feeding is a slow process rather than a rapid strike.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding bouts recur nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bronze-winged Jacana

waveform.description: A steady walking rhythm across a floating surface.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady surface feeding within an inverted and actively defended breeding structure.

entries.name: Brown Anole

modes.label: Holding a low perch and watching • Snapping the dewlap open on a hinged cartilage • Folding it away again immediately

waveform.description: A dense train of very sharp identical spikes, because each display is a brief full-amplitude event repeated many times an hour.

entries.closingLine: Since displays repeat within minutes, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown Bear

modes.label: Digging, fishing and grazing across a huge range • Converting everything into fat • Feeding almost continuously before winter
Lying in a den for months • Not eating, drinking, urinating or defecating • Recycling urea back into protein • Giving birth and nursing inside it

waveform.description: An active jagged section giving way to a long flat depressed line and back again, because the animal genuinely runs two different physiologies across the year.

entries.closingLine: Since the two regimes alternate once a year, this runs as a bimodal system with a low-frequency winter state.

entries.name: Brown Crab

modes.label: Feeding on molluscs and crustaceans with heavy black-tipped claws • Buried in sediment or wedged into rock by day • Carrying a hard shell that grows not at all
Withdrawing from the old shell over hours • Lying soft, swollen with water and unable to feed or defend itself • Hardening over days to weeks before returning to normal life

waveform.description: Normal activity interrupted by a long flat depressed section, because the animal genuinely stops being capable of anything while it is soft.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two different states, making this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Brown Greater Galago
entries.archetype: Night Gum-Forager With Shared Day Beds

waveform.description: A quiet shared rest by day rising into a long night of foraging.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: daytime rest in shared sleeping sites and solitary nocturnal foraging for gum, fruit and insects.

entries.name: Brown Pelican

waveform.description: A smooth gliding line punctuated by a steep committed drop.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: economical travel and a violent committed strike.

entries.name: Brown Rat

modes.label: Avoiding the new • Taking a trace • Coming back if nothing happened

waveform.description: A cautious baseline with small probes that grow steadily taller, because each successful test licenses a larger one.

entries.closingLine: Because the sampling routine runs continuously every night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown Recluse

modes.label: Flat against a hidden surface • Irregular sheet web • Months without food if needed

waveform.description: A near-flat line with almost no movement at all, because an animal built around not being found does very little that would reveal it.

entries.closingLine: Since everything runs slowly and continuously, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown Shrike

modes.label: Feet built for perching rather than for gripping and tearing, unlike a raptor's • Prey carried to a thorn, barbed wire or a sharp twig and pushed onto it • The spike holding the carcass while the hooked bill tears it, and the same larder storing surplus for later

waveform.description: A patrolling rhythm with repeated captures, because the bird hunts from perches through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because captures recur through the day, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown Shrimp

modes.label: Settling onto sand and beating the pleopods to throw grains over the back • Working the body down until only the eyes and antennae remain clear • Emerging at night to hunt across the same sediment

waveform.description: Long buried stretches alternating with an active period, because the animal is either inside the sediment or hunting over it.

entries.closingLine: Since burial and emergence recur daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown Sicklebill

waveform.description: A long low baseline of concealed activity interrupted by a single sharp, brief spike representing an intense display, then a return to concealment.

entries.closingLine: That combination of a long, hidden baseline and short, high-intensity display bursts makes the Brown Sicklebill a bimodal system with a low-frequency concealment mode and a high-frequency flourish mode.

entries.name: Brown Widow Spider

modes.label: Colonising urban structures far more densely and rapidly than the native widow it replaces • Juveniles preying on black widow spiders where the two meet, rather than merely competing for space • A venom of comparable potency delivered in far smaller quantity and with a far lower tendency to bite

waveform.description: A steady expansion levelling off, because the spread is continuous and eventually saturates the available structures.

entries.closingLine: Because the spread runs across seasons, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown Wood Owl

modes.label: A comb of stiff serrations along the leading edge of the outer primary feathers, breaking up the air before it passes over the wing • A velvety pile covering the upper surface, damping the sound of feathers sliding across each other • A soft fringed trailing edge preventing the sharp turbulence that normally generates noise where the airflow leaves the wing

waveform.description: An almost featureless line, because the whole point of the system is the absence of any disturbance.

entries.closingLine: Because flight is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Brown-throated Sunbird

modes.label: A bird that perches beside a flower rather than hovering in front of it • A decurved bill and tubular tongue reaching into the corolla from that fixed position • Flowers selected partly for whether there is something to stand on, so the plant's structure determines which birds can use it

waveform.description: A busy rhythm of short flights between perches, because the bird moves constantly but never hovers for long.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Brownbanded Bamboo Shark

modes.label: Suppressing metabolic rate and brain activity when oxygen in a tide pool falls away • Surviving hours with almost none rather than attempting to leave • Walking between pools on the pectoral and pelvic fins when it does move

waveform.description: A slow trough rather than a peak, because the animal responds to stress by dropping activity down and then recovering.

entries.closingLine: Because tidal cycles govern the pattern, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Brush-tailed Mulgara

waveform.description: Even, repeating night-time pulses rising from a low daytime baseline, showing regular foraging bouts anchored by rest.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole animal is organized around this steady, cyclical pattern rather than long storage or explosive bursts, the Mulgara expresses a mid-frequency, rhythmically active Night-Heat Economy.

entries.name: Budgerigar

modes.label: Calling constantly • Matching the flock • Following the rain

waveform.description: A dense rapid chatter of near-identical peaks, because the flock's sound is a continuous overlapping exchange.

entries.closingLine: Because the calling and matching run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Budgett's Frog
entries.archetype: Sealed in Layers of Its Own Skin

modes.label: Buried • Wrapped in shed skin • Months without water
Water arrives • Eat everything • Breed at once

waveform.description: Long flat buried months and a short violent wet-season burst.

entries.closingLine: This is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Buff-necked Ibis

waveform.description: Even mid-height ripples showing steady, repeated bouts of foraging effort as conditions shift but never become fully extreme.

entries.closingLine: That steady, environment-tracking search pattern makes it a mid-frequency system built on rhythmic, ongoing activity.

entries.name: Buff-tip Moth

modes.label: Wings rolled tightly around the body into a cylinder rather than held flat • Silvery grey wing surfaces and buff patches at the head and wingtips reproducing bark and the pale exposed wood of a break • The insect resting in the open as a broken twig rather than hiding against a surface

waveform.description: An almost perfectly level line, because the animal rests without moving for the whole of the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the posture is held all day, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bufflehead

waveform.description: Alternating mid-level activity plateaus with drops into low, sheltered periods, representing repeated returns to cavities between active bouts.

entries.closingLine: Because the bird’s life is organized around cycling between these two structurally different operating states—mobile foraging and stationary cavity use—this is a bimodal system with a mid-frequency commuting mode anchored by a low-frequency shelter-return mode.

entries.name: Buffy Fish Owl

modes.label: Low perch • Bare legs over water • Reading the surface

waveform.description: A high quiet line dropping three times to the floor and returning, because the action in this system goes downward rather than upward.

entries.closingLine: Because hours of almost costless watching fund a movement measured in seconds, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Bull Shark

waveform.description: Continuous cruising with continuous internal regulation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: one continuously regulated body running the same hunting strategy across water that should exclude it.

entries.name: Bullet Ant
entries.archetype: Pain With No Damage Behind It

modes.label: Foraging up the trunk • Defending the nest • One sting that lasts hours

waveform.description: A steady foraging rhythm with occasional defensive events.

entries.closingLine: Foraging continuously up and down one tree, this is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bumblebee

modes.label: Decoupling the flight muscles from the wings and contracting them against each other • Generating heat until the thorax reaches around thirty degrees regardless of the air temperature • Flying in cold, wet and early-morning conditions that ground other bees entirely

waveform.description: A steep initial climb settling into a busy sustained rhythm, because warming precedes a long working day.

entries.closingLine: Because warming and foraging repeat constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Burbot

modes.label: Gathering on gravel shoals in the coldest weeks of the year • Forming a writhing ball of dozens of fish beneath the ice • Releasing eggs and milt into the middle of it and dispersing

waveform.description: One deep sustained excursion at the start of the span with a long flat remainder, because the single event falls in midwinter.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Burgundy Goliath Birdeater

modes.label: Turning the abdomen towards a threat and rubbing the hind legs across it • Releasing a cloud of barbed urticating hairs into the air • Producing a hissing stridulation with the leg bristles at the same time

waveform.description: A flat line with a short burst of sharp activity, because the spider does nothing for long periods and then defends violently.

entries.closingLine: Because episodes are rare, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Burmese Python
entries.archetype: Organs That Grow for the Meal

waveform.description: A flat idle floor rising into a sustained digestive peak and falling back.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a near-dormant idle state and an intense constructed digestive one.

entries.name: Burrowing Owl

modes.label: Standing at the entrance • Scattering dung • Eating what comes

waveform.description: A watchful daytime rhythm with frequent short feeding events.

entries.closingLine: Steady daytime activity makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Burrowing Parakeet
entries.archetype: A Rock Soft Enough, Hard Enough

modes.label: Digging tunnels • Flying out to feed • Returning to the wall

waveform.description: A daily cycle of leaving the cliff, feeding, and returning.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daily foraging flights make this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Bush Dog

waveform.description: Steady travelling broken by short clusters of intense activity — a hunt is a burst of several animals acting at once.

entries.closingLine: Because the system requires both cohesive travel and the coordinated drive, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Bush Hyrax
entries.archetype: Sharing a Kopje and Not the Food

waveform.description: A steady browsing rhythm alongside a shared colony.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady browsing within a shared and jointly defended colony.

entries.name: Bushbuck

waveform.description: A quiet browsing line that flattens further rather than spiking.

entries.closingLine: Quiet low-expenditure browsing in cover makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Bushmaster

waveform.description: The flattest possible floor with a single spike — weeks of one posture against a fraction of a second.

entries.closingLine: Because near-total inactivity supports one committed strike, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Bushy-tailed Mongoose

modes.label: Working leaf litter alone • Digging for insects • Moving only after dark

waveform.description: A quiet solitary nocturnal foraging rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Slow, quiet and solitary, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Butterfly Peacock Bass

modes.label: A large visual daytime predator introduced into a lake whose fish had never encountered one • Native species showing no avoidance because nothing in their history selected for it • Whole guilds of small fish removed within a few years, and the effects propagating upward to birds and outward to mosquito numbers

waveform.description: A normal rhythm collapsing into a flat depleted line, because the change is one-directional and does not recover.

entries.closingLine: Because the collapse runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: By-the-wind Sailor

waveform.description: Gentle, even undulations showing a steady, wind-driven rhythm of drift and feeding with no sharp bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because the entire organism is built for ongoing, externally powered movement and steady capture rather than long storage or explosive bursts, its operating rhythm is a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, repeatable, and synchronized to the changing wind and waves.

entries.name: Cabbage Cluster Moth

modes.label: Eggs laid in clusters on the undersides of leaves near the centre of the plant • Larvae moving inward to the growing point and feeding within the folded heart leaves • The tissue around them shielding them from any spray applied to the outside of the plant

waveform.description: A gradual build to a peak and decline, because the infestation develops inside the plant over weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because generations run over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cacomistle
entries.archetype: Hind Feet Turned All the Way Round

modes.label: Climbing after dark • Reversing the ankles • Coming down head first

waveform.description: A quick repeating climb-and-descend rhythm through the night.

entries.closingLine: Continuous nightly movement and feeding makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cactus Mouse
entries.archetype: Torpid by Day Among Rocks and Cactus

waveform.description: A torpid, flat day rising to a peak early in the night and tailing off toward dawn.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: early-night foraging and daytime or seasonal torpor.

entries.name: Cactus Wren
entries.archetype: Roost Nests Built Among Cholla Spines

waveform.description: Morning and late-afternoon foraging peaks around a midday lull in shade, with nights spent in roost nests.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: territorial foraging and building, and sheltered rest in shade and roost nests.

entries.name: Caiman Lizard

modes.label: Diving • Collecting • Crushing at the back of the jaw

waveform.description: A repeating dive, crush and sort cycle through the day.

entries.closingLine: Steady daily foraging makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cairo Spiny Mouse
entries.archetype: Skin That Tears Away and Regrows

waveform.description: A steady night of foraging broken by one sharp escape spike and a gradual recovery.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady nocturnal foraging and rare, violent escapes followed by regrowth.

entries.name: California Condor

waveform.description: A low line with small regular lifts — each one an intervention rather than anything the bird does.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs on a very slow cycle, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: California Quail

waveform.description: A steady group rhythm of feeding and checking, repeated all day.

entries.closingLine: That makes the quail a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and coordinated, where safety comes from shared attention and from the geometry of staying near cover.

entries.name: California Scrub-Jay
entries.archetype: Remembering What Was Buried Where and When

waveform.description: An autumn caching peak with recovery running alongside it, then a long, steady recovery phase.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: intensive autumn caching and a long, memory-driven recovery that continues for months.

entries.name: California Sea Lion

waveform.description: A continuously curving line that never settles into one direction.

entries.closingLine: That makes the sea lion a mid-frequency system: continuous, agile and organised around changing direction rather than sustaining one.

entries.name: California Spiny Lobster

modes.label: Sheltering in rock crevices by day with antennae outward • Drawing a soft plectrum at the antenna base across a file on the head • Producing a rasping noise that continues even immediately after a moult

waveform.description: A rapid regular rasping pattern held throughout, because the sound is produced by a repeated slipping motion rather than by discrete strikes.

entries.closingLine: Since the rasp repeats many times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Camel Spider

waveform.description: Repeated violent sprints with almost no settled ground between them.

entries.closingLine: A short life, a direct attack and an expensive engine make this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Campbell's Dwarf Hamster

modes.label: A male remaining with the female through gestation rather than leaving after mating • That male present at the birth, pulling the pups free, clearing the membranes and licking them dry • Continued warming, grooming and retrieval of the pups afterwards, so two animals rather than one raise the litter

waveform.description: A single sustained episode of intense involvement, because the whole arrangement centres on one birth and its aftermath.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is per litter, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Canada Goose

waveform.description: An even alternating rhythm: the same load passed back and forth without the total changing.

entries.closingLine: That makes the goose a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, coordinated and built around distributing a cost.

entries.name: Canada Lynx

waveform.description: An even hunting rhythm with no dominant peak — a system whose real oscillation runs over years rather than hours.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on steady hunting effort tied to one resource, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Candy-striped Leafhopper

modes.label: Specialised gland cells producing protein granules a few hundred nanometres across, secreted in liquid and dried onto the surface • The insect combing that powder over its whole body with brushes on its legs • A microscopically rough coating that water and sticky plant sap cannot wet or adhere to

waveform.description: A steady maintenance rhythm, because the insect grooms and recoats itself continuously while feeding.

entries.closingLine: Because the maintenance is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cane Toad

waveform.description: A flat, unhurried low line: a body that never needs to accelerate.

entries.closingLine: That makes the cane toad a low-frequency system: slow, cheap to run and protected by chemistry rather than by movement.

entries.name: Cape Buffalo
entries.archetype: A Herd That Votes by Gaze

modes.label: Resting as a herd before a move • Having individual females stand, gaze in a direction and lie down again • Moving off in the average of the directions gazed in rather than following any leader

waveform.description: A long steady line with periodic broad rises, because the herd is at rest and then moves as a single event.

entries.closingLine: Since moves occur daily within a slow annual cycle, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cape Golden Mole
entries.archetype: Blind Digger Feeling for Footsteps in the Soil

waveform.description: Two foraging bouts of shallow tunnelling separated by troughs of rest in the nest.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: shallow vibration-guided foraging and low-energy rest.

entries.name: Cape Ground Squirrel
entries.archetype: A Tail Held Up as a Parasol

waveform.description: Daytime foraging held at a steady level, broken by a sharp alarm spike and a dash below ground.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long periods of shaded, social foraging and short sprints to cover.

entries.name: Cape Teal

modes.label: Supraorbital salt glands excreting concentrated brine through the nostrils • Feeding on brine shrimp and invertebrates in saline and alkaline pans other ducks avoid • Moving between scattered temporary pans as they fill and dry across the interior

waveform.description: A steady moderate rhythm, because the bird works shallow water continuously and moves between pans as they change.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding and movement are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Capuchin Monkey

modes.label: Juveniles sitting close to adults cracking nuts and watching the whole sequence repeatedly • Handling the discarded hammers and anvils afterwards without producing a strike • Acquiring a technique over years that no individual works out alone

waveform.description: A busy repeating rhythm of attempts and observation, because learning happens through constant repetition.

entries.closingLine: Because learning and use are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Capuchinbird

waveform.description: Evenly spaced tall spikes rising from a steady baseline, representing repeated powerful calls separated by short pauses.

entries.closingLine: This creates a system built around rhythmic, high-impact signaling at regular intervals, which makes the capuchinbird a mid-frequency system organized around repeated broadcast rather than continuous output or single bursts.

entries.name: Capybara
entries.archetype: Water at the Edge of the Grass

waveform.description: A low unhurried line with small even variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: unhurried, tolerant and dependent on position rather than on speed.

entries.name: Caracal
entries.archetype: Swatting at the Top of the Jump

modes.label: Creeping in • Launching vertically • Batting birds down

waveform.description: Sharp vertical spikes against a low resting baseline.

entries.closingLine: Volatile, explosive and short-horizon, this is a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Caribbean Cleaner Goby

waveform.description: Gentle, even waves showing repeated bouts of activity at the same station with short rests between, rather than long dormancy or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: This creates a mid-frequency system built on steady, rhythmic service at a stable location rather than slow reserve hoarding or short, explosive bursts.

entries.name: Caribbean Spiny Lobster

modes.label: Sheltering communally in crevices with others • Detecting a chemical cue from an infected individual in the urine • Refusing to share a den with it and moving elsewhere

waveform.description: A social baseline broken by decisive avoidance events, because ordinary communal life is interrupted by rejections.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Carmine Bee-eater

waveform.description: A steady flocked rhythm following a moving front.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuously active and organised entirely around somebody else's movement.

entries.name: Carolina Wolf Spider

modes.label: A female attaching the egg sac to her spinnerets and dragging it everywhere she goes • Opening it when the spiderlings are ready and letting them climb onto her abdomen • Carrying dozens of young on her back for days while continuing to hunt

waveform.description: A long flat line with one extended raised period, because the burden of carrying is sustained over weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Carolina Wren

waveform.description: A gently undulating mid-level line showing steady, repeated investment in nest concealment and upkeep without extreme peaks or troughs.

entries.closingLine: The system’s rhythm is a repeatable cycle of searching, building, lining, and guarding a protected interior space, which makes this a mid-frequency, rhythmic cavity-nesting strategy rather than a slow hoarding or explosive burst pattern.

entries.name: Carp

waveform.description: Quiet bottom sifting rises into turbidity pulses that reset the lake.

entries.closingLine: Quiet sifting and turbidity pulses are one engine with two tempos, not separate strategies.

entries.name: Carpenter Ant

modes.label: Cutting galleries through dead and damp wood with the mandibles • Carrying the shavings out and discarding them rather than eating them • Feeding instead on honeydew from sap-feeding insects and on other insects entirely outside the nest

waveform.description: A long nocturnal build and decline, because this is a night-foraging ant whose activity rises and falls with darkness.

entries.closingLine: Because colony cycles run across seasons, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Carpenter Bee

modes.label: Landing on the outside of a long tubular flower rather than at its opening • Slitting the base of the corolla with sharp mandibles • Drinking nectar directly through that hole without contacting the anthers or stigma at all

waveform.description: A brisk repeating rhythm of visits, because the bee works flower after flower steadily through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because visits are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Carrion Beetle

waveform.description: A long even searching rhythm interrupted by the occasional find.

entries.closingLine: The searching never stops and rarely pays, which makes this a mid-frequency system whose entire return is concentrated into a handful of finds.

entries.name: Carrion Crow

waveform.description: A mostly low, steady line for ongoing caching and memory, with a sharp dip upward (high activity) for a brief tool-use burst before returning to the low baseline.

entries.closingLine: Because their biology is organized around long-horizon storage and memory with intermittent, opportunistic tool-use bursts, this is a bimodal system with a low-frequency caching base and a high-frequency problem-solving spike.

entries.name: Cat Flea

modes.label: A fully formed adult remaining inside its silk cocoon rather than emerging when development finishes • That adult waiting for weeks or months, resistant to insecticide and to drying while sealed • Emergence triggered by vibration, warmth and carbon dioxide, so it appears only when something is present to feed on

waveform.description: A long flat dormant line with one abrupt emergence, because nothing happens until a host arrives and then everything does.

entries.closingLine: Because the wait runs across months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cattle Egret

waveform.description: A steady stream of small strikes, one after another, at a walking pace.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and continuous, built on many small captures created by something else's movement.

entries.name: Cayenne Caecilian

waveform.description: A slow undulation entirely within the low band — the trace of an animal that moves continuously and never accelerates.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs on low expenditure inside a medium nothing else exploits, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cayenne Tick

modes.label: The tick climbing a grass stem and holding position with the front pair of legs extended into the air • Haller's organ on those forelegs detecting carbon dioxide, heat, vibration and odour from a passing animal • That pose held for weeks or months without feeding, until something brushes past and is grasped

waveform.description: An almost completely flat line with one brief interruption, because nothing happens at all until a host arrives.

entries.closingLine: Because the wait runs across months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cecropia Moth
entries.archetype: Antennae That Detect a Few Molecules

waveform.description: A still calling line and a rising tracking response.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a stationary signalling half and a searching half.

entries.name: Cedar Waxwing

waveform.description: A steady social feeding rhythm, broken by flights on to the next fruit crop.

entries.closingLine: It is a mid-frequency system: steady, social and governed by where the fruit is.

entries.name: Celebes Crested Macaque

modes.label: Crowding in close • Bared teeth as greeting • Copying what worked

waveform.description: A varied social rhythm of unequal peaks, because each is a different interaction rather than a repeat of the last.

entries.closingLine: Because the watching and copying run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Centipede

modes.label: Running down prey on many pairs of legs • Seizing it with the first pair of legs converted into hollow fangs • Injecting venom through them before anything can be lost

waveform.description: Rapid movement broken by extremely narrow full-depth strikes, because the animal runs constantly and the seizure is instantaneous.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes occur in a fraction of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Central American Agouti

waveform.description: A steady repeated caching rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady repeated burying in which the losses do the work.

entries.name: Central Bearded Dragon

waveform.description: A low line drifting gently up and down as the animal corrects its temperature.

entries.closingLine: That makes the dragon a low-frequency system: economical, unhurried and regulated by position instead of by expenditure.

entries.name: Cetti's Warbler

waveform.description: A quiet hidden baseline punctuated by two extremely tall, very narrow bursts.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a quiet concealed baseline and a short, very high-output broadcast.

entries.name: Chaco Golden Knee Tarantula

modes.label: A metabolic rate far below that of comparable active invertebrates • Long periods motionless in a burrow with no feeding at all, sometimes months • A lifespan reaching two decades or more in females, with growth measured in years

waveform.description: An almost completely level line, because the animal's activity barely varies from one month to the next.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs on a timescale of months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Chain Catshark

waveform.description: A low, gently rippling line showing steady, ongoing but modest activity: continuous background concealment rather than sharp bursts.

entries.closingLine: This creates a single, low-frequency system built around constant, passive camouflage rather than rapid, high-cost changes.

entries.name: Chain Pickerel

modes.label: The body drawn into an S shape while hanging motionless among weed • The whole trunk musculature contracting along one side to straighten it in a single stroke • Acceleration produced by the body itself rather than by any fin, covering the strike distance in a fraction of a second

waveform.description: A quiet waiting baseline with extremely abrupt vertical strikes, because the attack is a single explosive event.

entries.closingLine: Because the strike itself takes hundredths of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Chambered Nautilus

waveform.description: A deep flat day and a raised night — one vertical journey up and back, repeated every twenty-four hours.

entries.closingLine: Because both the deep resting phase and the shallow feeding phase are essential, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Chamois

waveform.description: A steady climbing rhythm with regular changes of level.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuously active on terrain that is itself the defence.

entries.name: Cheetah

waveform.description: A rapid climb to peak output followed by a fast decline and recovery.

entries.closingLine: That makes the cheetah a strongly high-frequency system: explosive, short-horizon and dependent on recovery after the burst.

entries.name: Cherry Shrimp

modes.label: A wild form that is drab translucent brown with no bright colour at all • Selectively bred lines fixed for red, yellow, blue, green and black over many generations • Any two colour lines crossed producing offspring that revert towards the wild brown within a few generations

waveform.description: A steady rhythm drifting back upward, because the colour lines revert whenever selection stops.

entries.closingLine: Because reversion runs across generations, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Chicken

modes.label: Releasing a yolk most mornings • Building the shell overnight • Reading daylength to keep going

waveform.description: An almost metronomic repetition of identical cycles, because the animal completes the same twenty-five-hour process over and over.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle repeats daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Chicken Mite

modes.label: Feeding on roosting birds for under an hour at night and then leaving them entirely • Spending the day in cracks, perch joints and structural crevices away from any bird • Surviving months in those crevices without feeding if the birds are removed

waveform.description: A flat daytime line with a single nocturnal feeding episode, because the mite is on the bird only briefly each night.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is nightly and development takes days, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Chickweed Geometer Moth

modes.label: Carrying feathered antennae with an enormous surface area of receptors • Detecting female pheromone at concentrations of a few molecules • Flying upwind along the plume until the source is reached
