waveform.description: A rapid fine oscillation with no strong features, because the searching flight is continuous small adjustment.

entries.closingLine: Since the flight is continuous adjustment, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Chihuahuan Raven
entries.archetype: Late Nest Timed to Summer Rain

waveform.description: Restless flocking for much of the year, then a quieter nesting phase in the rainy summer.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-change system: wandering flock foraging and a late, rain-timed nesting season.

entries.name: Chilean Swallow

modes.label: A bird catching insects exclusively in flight, with a wide gape, short bill and long pointed wings and no ability to glean from surfaces • That food supply consisting entirely of insects that are airborne at the time, which is a small and variable fraction of the total • Aerial insectivores declining as a guild across several continents, faster than birds that can take insects from vegetation as well

waveform.description: A fast continuous rhythm of sallies, because the bird feeds on the wing throughout the day without settling.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Chimpanzee

waveform.description: A rhythm that climbs slowly across the trace — each generation starts from what the last one had rather than from nothing.

entries.closingLine: Because learning and using run as a steady daily process across long periods, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Chinese Alligator

waveform.description: Half a year near the floor and half raised — a clean seasonal division rather than a daily rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because both the dormant winter and the active summer are essential, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Chinese Cobra

modes.label: Rearing up and spreading elongated ribs to flare a hood • Presenting a broad marked surface toward the threat • Striking or spraying venom only if the display is ignored

waveform.description: A calm line rising into a sustained raised display and subsiding, because the hood is held for as long as the threat is present.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Chinese Crocodile Lizard

waveform.description: A near-flat trace with two small lifts — the only events in a day are drops into the water below.

entries.closingLine: Because nothing about the animal happens at speed, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Chinese Giant Salamander

waveform.description: An almost unbroken line near the floor — a wild population reduced to a trace of what the farms contain.

entries.closingLine: Because everything about the animal runs slowly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Chinese Hwamei

modes.label: Learning and incorporating phrases from other species heard in the surrounding scrub • Assembling them into long varied sequences rather than repeating a fixed species song • Continuing to add new material through life so no two individuals sing the same thing

waveform.description: An irregular varied rhythm that never repeats exactly, because the song is assembled rather than fixed.

entries.closingLine: Because learning and singing are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Chinese Mantis

modes.label: Waiting motionless on vegetation and increasingly at garden feeders • Striking with raptorial forelegs in a few hundredths of a second • Taking prey up to and including small birds

waveform.description: A long motionless line broken by extremely brief full-depth strikes, because nothing happens and then the capture is over.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes are sudden and rare, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Chinese Pond Heron

modes.label: Standing folded and drab • Striking • Opening into white

waveform.description: A patient wading rhythm of small regular dips, because the strikes are frequent and the animal rarely stops moving.

entries.closingLine: Because the stalking and striking run together through the workable hours, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Chinese Rice Grasshopper

modes.label: A rice pest occurring in very large numbers in the same fields as the crop it damages • Collected, farmed and sold as food across parts of China, where it is a valued seasonal item • Harvesting operating simultaneously as pest control and as production, so the insect is both the problem and a product

waveform.description: A seasonal build and collapse, because the population rises through the crop season and is then harvested.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Chinese Softshell Turtle

waveform.description: A buried still line with brief surfacing intervals.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: prolonged burial and brief surfacing to rinse and breathe.

entries.name: Chinese Water Dragon

waveform.description: Alert perching, one sharp drop, then a long motionless hold.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: alert perching directly above a refuge, and a long still submerged hold that outlasts attention.

entries.name: Chinook Salmon
entries.archetype: Upstream on a Fixed Fat Budget

waveform.description: Repeated bursts of upstream effort separated by flat resting spells in slack water.

entries.closingLine: Because the run alternates between hard bursts of travel and spells of holding in slack water, the system is bimodal.

entries.name: Chiru

waveform.description: A long flat plateau raised into one broad seasonal arc — the migration is a season, not an event.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal cannot survive without both the insulation and the migration, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Chital

modes.label: Grazing under the troop • Taking what is dropped • Barking what it smells

waveform.description: A steady grazing rhythm with two brief sharp lifts, because the alarm is an interruption rather than a state.

entries.closingLine: Because the grazing and the listening run together through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Chocolate Chip Sea Star

waveform.description: A single almost imperceptible swell across the whole span, the flattest trace a working animal can produce.

entries.closingLine: Because every process it runs is measured in months and costs close to nothing per hour, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Christmas Island Red Crab

modes.label: Waiting in forest burrows through the dry season • Moving to the coast en masse when the wet season rains begin • Releasing larvae into the sea at the turn of the high tide on a specific lunar day

waveform.description: A long flat line rising into one concentrated event and falling back, because everything happens in a few weeks of one month.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cicada

modes.label: Nymphs underground piercing xylem vessels and drinking sap that is almost entirely water • Filtering enormous volumes to extract traces of amino acids at very low concentration • Taking years rather than months to accumulate enough to complete development

waveform.description: A very long flat stretch ending in one sudden peak, because almost the whole life happens underground and unseen.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cicada Killer Wasp

waveform.description: A repeated cycle of hunt and delivery at a steady summer pace.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and repetitive, organised around preserving and stocking rather than around the kill.

entries.name: Cichlid

modes.label: Oral jaws at the front used only for catching and holding • A second set of jaws in the throat, formed from modified gill arches, used for processing • Each set free to specialise because neither has to do the other's job

waveform.description: A busy varied rhythm without a single dominant pattern, because the family does many different things at once.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cinereous Vulture

waveform.description: Long shallow searching with one substantial feeding event — the rare meal is the only structure in the line.

entries.closingLine: Because the system pairs very cheap search with rare, large, heavily banked returns, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Citrus Flatid Planthopper
entries.archetype: Wax Colonies on Any Woody Stem

waveform.description: A steady feeding baseline with sudden, brief spikes of jumping or flight.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: sedentary sap feeding and sudden escape.

entries.name: Citrus Mealybug

waveform.description: An almost unchanging low line: a settled feeder that barely moves at all.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, settled and protected by what it builds over itself.

entries.name: Clark's Nutcracker

waveform.description: Even mid-height waves showing repeated bouts of caching and later retrieval rather than long idling or single bursts.

entries.closingLine: This steady, spatially organized pattern of activity makes Clark’s Nutcracker a mid-frequency system built around ongoing, coordinated work rather than rare bursts or deep torpor.

entries.name: Click Beetle
entries.archetype: Years Underground, Then a Latched Snap

waveform.description: A long flat larval line, then a brief loaded rise released as sharp snapping spikes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: years of slow subterranean growth and a brief latched snap.

entries.name: Cliff Chipmunk

waveform.description: A mid-level baseline with repeated sharp, narrow spikes, showing steady route-based caching punctuated by brief high-intensity dashes.

entries.closingLine: This makes the cliff chipmunk a bimodal system: a mid-frequency, route-based caching rhythm structurally supported by short, high-frequency dash-and-evade bursts.

entries.name: Cliff Swallow

waveform.description: Even mid-level oscillations for repeated foraging-and-return flights, with a cluster of sharp high spikes representing brief intense construction or alarm activity at the colony wall.

entries.closingLine: This creates a bimodal pattern: a mid-frequency commuting circuit anchored to a remembered wall, punctuated by high-frequency construction and defense bursts that keep the mud-cup village usable and safe.

entries.name: Clothes & House Moth

modes.label: Feeding as a larva on wool, fur, feathers and horn • Running a highly alkaline gut with strongly reducing conditions • Breaking the disulphide bonds that make keratin indigestible to almost everything else

waveform.description: A long slow even line with a small rise, because the larva feeds quietly for months and the adult stage is brief.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Clouded Leopard

waveform.description: An irregular climbing rhythm of different heights — movement through a canopy is never the same twice.

entries.closingLine: Because hunting and moving run as a steady nocturnal cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Clown Knifefish

modes.label: Holding the body rigid and driving with a long undulating anal fin • Reversing direction by reversing the wave • Manoeuvring through submerged roots without turning around

waveform.description: A smooth continuous wave of constant amplitude, because propulsion itself is a travelling wave rather than a series of strokes.

entries.closingLine: Since fin waves run many times a second, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Clown Loach
entries.archetype: A Blade That Flicks Out Below the Eye

modes.label: Working the substrate • Clicking • Locking out the spine

waveform.description: An active pulsing rhythm of group foraging and movement.

entries.closingLine: Continuous active foraging makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Clown Triggerfish
entries.archetype: A Second Spine That Locks the First

waveform.description: Active territorial daylight, then a long locked hold.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: assertive open foraging, and a locked state a predator cannot mechanically undo.

entries.name: Clownfish

waveform.description: A small steady rhythm held within a very short radius all day.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, continuous and defined by maintaining one relationship rather than by ranging.

entries.name: Coal Tit

modes.label: Taking one seed at a time and hiding each in a separate place • Distributing caches over a wide area of bark, moss and needles • Returning to specific sites over weeks using spatial memory

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying repetition of identical small actions, because the bird makes the same short trip over and over.

entries.closingLine: Since caching trips recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cobweb Spider

modes.label: Vertical silk lines running from a tangled web down to the ground, glued at the bottom and held under tension • An insect walking into one sticking to the glue and snapping the line free • The prey hauled up off the surface as the line contracts, leaving it hanging and helpless

waveform.description: A long flat line with sudden sharp releases, because the web sits loaded until something triggers it.

entries.closingLine: Because triggering is occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cockatiel

modes.label: Raising and lowering a mobile crest • Signalling alarm, interest or calm continuously • Reading the same signal in others

waveform.description: Sharp rises returning quickly to a variable baseline, because the crest snaps up with arousal and settles again.

entries.closingLine: Since crest movements occur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cockroach

modes.label: A pair of cerci at the rear covered in fine hairs, each hair deflected by the slightest air movement • The air pushed ahead of an approaching object detected before the object itself arrives • Giant interneurons carrying that signal to the legs so the insect is running within a few thousandths of a second

waveform.description: A quiet baseline broken by instantaneous departures, because the escape is among the fastest reactions in any animal.

entries.closingLine: Because the response is measured in milliseconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Cocoa Tussock Moth

modes.label: A winged male flying at night, tracking female pheromone across distance and mating with whatever he finds
A wingless female emerging from her cocoon, remaining on it, releasing pheromone and laying her entire clutch on the cocoon she emerged from

waveform.description: A mobile varied rhythm giving way to a flat stationary one, because the two sexes are doing entirely different things.

entries.closingLine: The two sexes run different architectures, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Coconut Crab

waveform.description: A heavy flat baseline with slow shallow working rises — force applied over hours rather than delivered in a strike.

entries.closingLine: Because value comes from long structural accumulation spent patiently rather than from speed, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Coconut Octopus

waveform.description: A laboured working pace lifted where the shells are pulled shut.

entries.closingLine: Continuous transport and deployment of its own cover makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Coelacanth

waveform.description: A deep resting trough and a raised drifting section — the day and the night are different animals.

entries.closingLine: Because both the cave day and the drifting night are essential, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Coffee hawk-moth

waveform.description: Tight, repeated high spikes around a midline, showing continuous rapid output with small oscillations rather than long rests.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a single, high-frequency system built around fast, continuous stabilization rather than slow conservation.

entries.name: Coho Salmon
entries.archetype: A Creek Year, Then a Rain-Timed Run

waveform.description: A long quiet stream year, then surges upstream on autumn freshets before the end.

entries.closingLine: Because the system switches from a sheltered stream year to a rain-timed run, it is a phase-change system.

entries.name: Collared Falconet
entries.archetype: A Falcon Living in a Woodpecker's Hole

modes.label: Perched in the open • Dashing after insects • Nesting in a borrowed cavity

waveform.description: Frequent short dashes from a fixed perch and straight back.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daylight perch-hunting makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Collared Peccary

modes.label: A gland on the lower back releasing a strong musky secretion • Animals rubbing head and flank against each other's glands repeatedly through the day • The whole herd converging on one blended odour that marks membership

waveform.description: A continuous even rhythm, because the rubbing and reinforcement happens throughout every day without episodes.

entries.closingLine: Because the reinforcement is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Collared Pratincole
entries.archetype: A Wader That Hunts Like a Swallow

waveform.description: Rest on open ground broken by sustained flocking flights, peaking towards dusk.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: aerial insect hawking and a colonial ground-nesting phase.

entries.name: Collector Urchin

modes.label: Tube feet extended above the body and used to grip fragments of algae, seagrass, shell and coral rubble • That material held over the upper surface as a continuous cover, replaced as pieces are lost • Ultraviolet light blocked and the outline broken, so the urchin is shaded and also does not read as an urchin

waveform.description: A very slow steady rhythm, because the animal moves and adjusts its covering gradually and continuously.

entries.closingLine: Because the adjustment is continuous but slow, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Comet Moth

waveform.description: A short shallow arc that declines toward the end — a life of a few days spending a balance that is never topped up.

entries.closingLine: Because a fixed reserve is spent evenly across a few days, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Commerson's Dolphin
entries.archetype: Small Fast Body in Cold Shallow Water

waveform.description: Steady inshore foraging broken by quick bursts of speed at the surface.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: MID coastal foraging and HIGH bursts of speed.

entries.name: Commerson's Frogfish

modes.label: A modified first dorsal spine forming a rod with a fleshy lure at the tip • That lure worked in front of the mouth so it moves like a small worm or shrimp • The mouth expanding explosively when a fish comes to investigate, drawing it in faster than any strike can be seen

waveform.description: A near-motionless line broken by two extremely brief events, because nothing happens until the strike.

entries.closingLine: Because strikes are rare, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Backswimmer

waveform.description: Long stretches of level, low activity just under the surface, punctuated by brief sharp dips representing fast upside-down rowing strikes.

entries.closingLine: That combination of extended poised suspension and brief, high-output oar strokes makes the backswimmer a bimodal system with a low-frequency baseline and a high-frequency strike-and-escape mode.

entries.name: Common Basilisk
entries.archetype: Outrunning the Cavity Before It Closes

waveform.description: A still perched line broken by a very rapid burst.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: relaxed riverside perching and a brief burst that cannot be sustained.

entries.name: Common Bed Bug

waveform.description: Long flat low-activity stretches with two short, sharp spikes, showing extended sheltering punctuated by brief feeding excursions.

entries.closingLine: This makes the bed bug a bimodal wait-then-strike system whose core is Patient Shelter around a necessary but risky resource.

entries.name: Common Blackbird

modes.label: Flicking leaves aside • Running and stopping • Listening down

waveform.description: Flat runs broken by short identical flicks, because the bird alternates between holding still and turning something over.

entries.closingLine: Since the searching and listening run together through every daylight hour, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Bluetail

waveform.description: Even, mid-height oscillations showing repeated patrol passes along reeds with steady activity and no extreme bursts.

entries.closingLine: This creates a mid-frequency operating pattern: rhythmic patrols, regular short bursts of movement and capture, and continuous but moderate expenditure anchored to the same reed structures.

entries.name: Common Bream

modes.label: Tilting head down over soft mud • Shooting the jaws forward and downward into a tube • Sucking sediment in, sorting the invertebrates and blowing the rest back out

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm of similar events, because the fish works the bottom at a constant deliberate pace.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding actions repeat constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Brittle Star

waveform.description: A mostly low, steady line with a modest, smoother rise in the middle, showing a stable hidden state with occasional coordinated activity when moving, shedding or regenerating.

entries.closingLine: This creates a bimodal rhythm: long stretches of low-frequency, anchored reaching and feeding punctuated by coordinated mid-frequency episodes of crawling escape and the slower cycle of arm loss and regeneration that keeps the system working after damage.

entries.name: Common Buzzard

modes.label: Circling in rising air with broad wings and splayed primary feathers • Gaining height at almost no metabolic cost • Covering ground and scanning it from a height nothing else can hold for hours

waveform.description: A slow smooth drifting line with very little structure, because the animal is being carried rather than driving itself.

entries.closingLine: Since soaring is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Carpet Beetle

modes.label: A larva with gut conditions and enzymes capable of breaking the disulphide bonds that make keratin indigestible to almost everything • Wool, hair, feather, horn and dried skin therefore usable as food, in a world where those materials are otherwise effectively inert • Museum collections, textiles, carpets and stored specimens consumed as a result, because they are made of exactly that material

waveform.description: A slow steady larval progression, because feeding continues over months at a constant low rate.

entries.closingLine: Because larval development runs over months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Carpet Moth

modes.label: Settling flat against a surface with wings spread rather than folded • Carrying dark bands that run continuously across fore and hind wing • Having the outline of a moth replaced by a pattern of stripes on a flat plane

waveform.description: A quiet even line with small occasional disturbances, because the animal is motionless for long periods and flies briefly.

entries.closingLine: Since resting bouts alternate with flight through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Chiffchaff

modes.label: Singing a simple two-note phrase repeated from high in a tree • Recognising and responding only to that pattern • Ignoring the near-identical bird singing something else

waveform.description: A strict alternation of two levels repeated without variation, because the song is literally two notes traded back and forth.

entries.closingLine: Since song bouts recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Chuckwalla
entries.archetype: Lungs Inflated to Lock the Crevice

waveform.description: A slow warm-up and feeding plateau with a sharp spike of escape and wedging, then retreat to the crevice.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long low-frequency basking and grazing, and short explosive episodes of escape.

entries.name: Common Cuckoo

waveform.description: A mostly steady mid-level line of watchful activity with a single sharp, narrow dip upward representing a brief, intense timing-critical nest intrusion.

entries.closingLine: This makes the cuckoo a bimodal system: a steady, observant mid-frequency search-and-shadow mode punctuated by rare, high-frequency timing strikes where the entire reproductive payoff is decided in moments.

entries.name: Common Cusimanse

waveform.description: A dense, unbroken chatter rhythm with no long pauses in it.

entries.closingLine: Continuous, unhurried ground searching makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Darter

modes.label: Basking flat on a warm surface to raise thoracic temperature • Flying only once the flight muscles are warm enough • Angling the abdomen to the sun to control the temperature

waveform.description: Repeated short flights from a returning baseline, because the animal alternates between perching and brief sorties all day.

entries.closingLine: Since sorties recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Dwarf Mongoose
entries.archetype: Rotating Lookouts Over a Digging Pack

waveform.description: A steady foraging rhythm broken by short sharp spikes when an alarm sends the pack to cover.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady cooperative foraging under guard, and short explosive responses when danger is called.

entries.name: Common Earthworm

waveform.description: A steady mid-frequency rhythm: the same modest amount of work repeated without pause.

entries.closingLine: That makes the earthworm a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, continuous and defined by steady throughput rather than any decisive event.

entries.name: Common Eastern Firefly

modes.label: Flying a rising J-shaped flash at dusk • Waiting a fixed interval for a reply • Answering only a response with the correct delay

waveform.description: Alternating tall and short spikes separated by even gaps, because the exchange is a call and a reply with a fixed interval between them.

entries.closingLine: Since flashes repeat every few seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Eland

waveform.description: A gently undulating low line, showing steady, unhurried output with small fluctuations rather than sharp bursts.

entries.closingLine: That architecture makes them a low-frequency system: slow, steady, reserve-conscious movement built to reuse the same calm, powerful pace again and again rather than living in constant high-speed bursts.

entries.name: Common European Harvestman

modes.label: Taking small prey, carrion and plant material directly into the mouth • Swallowing particles rather than liquefying them outside the body • Feeding on things no spider could process at all

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm with no dramatic features, because the animal forages continuously and slowly.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Evening Brown

waveform.description: A long low plateau for daylight rest with a single moderate rise and fall in the middle, representing the brief, rhythmic dusk activity window.

entries.closingLine: The system therefore runs as a bimodal pattern: a low-frequency, concealment-led day state coupled to a mid-frequency, time-windowed movement and feeding state.

entries.name: Common Fangtooth
entries.archetype: Jaws Oversized for Rare Meals in the Dark

waveform.description: A steady juvenile feeding rhythm giving way to a low adult baseline with rare, sudden strikes.

entries.closingLine: That is a phase-change system from steady juvenile feeding to a low-frequency adult regime of long waits and rare strikes.

entries.name: Common Field Grasshopper

modes.label: Males stridulating by drawing a row of pegs on the hind femur across a vein on the forewing • Each species producing a characteristic pattern of pulses and pauses rather than a distinctive appearance • Females responding only to their own species' pattern, so the song rather than any structure decides who mates with whom

waveform.description: A patterned sequence of pulses and gaps repeated exactly, because the rhythm rather than the pitch carries the information.

entries.closingLine: Because the song cycles many times a second, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Flameback

modes.label: Repeated strikes delivered at high speed with the bill, decelerating the head very sharply at each impact • A thickened spongy region of skull bone, an unequal upper and lower bill, and a hyoid apparatus wrapping around the skull, together spreading and absorbing the force • The brain small, tightly enclosed and oriented so the force passes across rather than through it, so almost none of the energy reaches it as damaging motion

waveform.description: An extremely rapid regular percussion, because the bird delivers strikes in fast repeated bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because strikes come in fast bursts, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Flesh Fly

waveform.description: Repeated short bursts of finding and depositing.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: brief contested opportunities captured by deleting the slowest step.

entries.name: Common Frog

modes.label: Feeding on land through spring and summer • Breathing with lungs and skin together • Hunting invertebrates in damp vegetation
Lying at the bottom of a pond through winter • Taking up oxygen entirely through the skin from the water • Not surfacing, not feeding and barely moving for months

waveform.description: Active variation alternating with a long flat depressed stretch, because the animal genuinely switches between two ways of breathing.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two respiratory regimes, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Common Fruit-piercing Moth

modes.label: Flying into orchards after dark • Driving a stiffened barbed proboscis through intact fruit skin • Drinking juice from inside and leaving a puncture that rots

waveform.description: A flat nocturnal baseline with isolated deep punctures, because each feeding event is a discrete penetration rather than a continuous draw.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding visits recur nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Genet

waveform.description: A steady careful nocturnal rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, careful and continuously mobile in three dimensions.

entries.name: Common Grass Blue

modes.label: Completing a generation in a few weeks on low-growing legumes • Producing overlapping broods all year in warm climates • Colonising any patch of clover, medick or lucerne that appears

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying repetition across the whole span, because generations follow one another with no seasonal break at all.

entries.closingLine: Since generations turn over in weeks, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Green Darner

modes.label: Intercepting • Turning on the wing • Covering ground

waveform.description: A dense fast oscillation running the full height of the frame with almost no gaps, because this animal is either flying hard or not operating.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal's operating existence is fast and short-horizon, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Green Forest Lizard

waveform.description: Long stretches of low, flat activity for background matching, punctuated by short, sharp peaks representing rapid colour-display bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because its system is built around long, low-visibility periods punctuated by short, high-intensity visual signals, this lizard operates as a bimodal low–high frequency system.

entries.name: Common Green Magpie

modes.label: Brilliant green plumage produced by a yellow carotenoid pigment laid over blue structural colour • That carotenoid obtained entirely from the diet, principally from invertebrate prey • The green fading to turquoise and then blue when the diet lacks it or when sunlight degrades it faster than it is replaced

waveform.description: A steady rhythm drifting gradually downward, because the colour is maintained continuously and declines when it is not.

entries.closingLine: Because the turnover runs over weeks, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Gundi

waveform.description: A low quiet line lifted slightly by short warm-hour outings.

entries.closingLine: Imported heat, minimal expenditure and short trips from cover make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Hill Myna

modes.label: Young birds learning calls from same-sex neighbours in their own small area rather than from their parents • Distinct local dialects forming across distances of a few kilometres • No imitation of other species in the wild at all, despite a famous capacity for it in captivity

waveform.description: A varied local rhythm, because the material is specific to one place and exchanged constantly within it.

entries.closingLine: Because calling is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Hippopotamus

modes.label: Walking out • Cropping short grass • Returning before dawn

waveform.description: A deep flat floor with a raised plateau lifted out of it once, because the animal changes medium rather than intensity.

entries.closingLine: Because one low-cost aquatic state and one nightly terrestrial one are each indispensable, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Common House Gecko

waveform.description: Repeated short strikes from a held position through the night — many small events, none of them dominant.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from repeated small captures at a held position, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common House Spider

modes.label: Building a tangle above with taut silk lines running down to the ground • Gluing the lower ends and leaving them under tension • Having a walking insect stick, snap the line and be lifted off its feet

waveform.description: A still line broken by isolated sharp events, because nothing happens until a line is triggered and then the capture is immediate.

entries.closingLine: Since triggers occur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Hoverfly

waveform.description: A fine continuous tremor with occasional violent departures.

entries.closingLine: Continuous heavy expenditure and millisecond reactions make this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Hydra

waveform.description: A gently undulating mid-level line showing steady, continuous cycles of cellular renewal rather than long flat conservation or sharp bursts.

entries.closingLine: The defining rhythm is a steady, repeating cycle of growth, sloughing, and regrowth across the whole body, making this a mid-frequency, single-mode renewal system.

entries.name: Common Kingfisher
entries.archetype: Correcting for Where the Fish Is Not

waveform.description: A still perched line broken by one steep committed drop.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long still calculation and one committed blind strike.

entries.name: Common Limpet

waveform.description: Long clamped stillness broken by two tidal grazing excursions.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: clamped rest and tidal grazing.

entries.name: Common Loon

waveform.description: A working rhythm of descents and returns repeated through a day.

entries.closingLine: Repeated diving through a long day makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Marble

waveform.description: A low, steady line showing long periods of protected, low-movement living once the leaf shelter is built.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a low-frequency system built around one protective build and long, frugal use of that shelter.

entries.name: Common Marmoset

waveform.description: Even, mid-height oscillations showing repeated bouts of coordinated group movement and watchfulness across the day.

entries.closingLine: That makes the marmoset a mid-frequency system: not a slow hoarder or a pure sprinter, but a steady, coordinated pattern of repeated, shared actions that keep both food intake and infant protection going together.

entries.name: Common Midwife Toad

waveform.description: A long steady loaded line ending in one short release.

entries.closingLine: Few eggs, long investment and very high survival per egg make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Minke Whale

waveform.description: A steady searching line broken by sharp bursts of lunging and sprinting.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady travelling and searching between prey patches and explosive lunges and sprints.

entries.name: Common Molly

modes.label: Internal fertilisation through a modified anal fin acting as a gonopodium • Storing viable sperm in folds of the female's reproductive tract for months • Producing several successive broods of live young from that one stored supply

waveform.description: A repeating cycle of broods at regular intervals, because each stored batch is released on the same rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because broods recur on a cycle of weeks, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Murre
entries.archetype: An Egg That Rolls in a Circle

waveform.description: Sharp costly flights bracketing long sustained dives.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: costly marginal flight and deep sustained wing-powered diving.

entries.name: Common Musk Turtle

waveform.description: A long, low, steady line of quiet bottom-walking with a single sharp, narrow spike representing a short, intense musk event when the boundary is breached.

entries.closingLine: This produces a bimodal system: a low-frequency, place-bound routine that minimizes contact, backed by a high-frequency, short-lived but very memorable chemical boundary when that quiet perimeter is breached.

entries.name: Common Myna

modes.label: Locating an occupied nest hole • Evicting the residents and destroying eggs or chicks • Holding the cavity and breeding in it

waveform.description: A working rhythm punctuated by regular deep events, because ordinary foraging is broken by decisive takeovers.

entries.closingLine: Since takeovers and foraging recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Nighthawk

waveform.description: A mostly low, flat line of rest with two narrow high spikes, showing quiet roosting punctuated by brief, intense dusk and dawn feeding flights.

entries.closingLine: That architecture—long periods of camouflaged waiting anchored around ground cover and open perches, punctuated by brief, high-intensity twilight feeding—makes the common nighthawk a bimodal system with a low-frequency resting mode and a high-frequency burst-feeding mode.

entries.name: Common Octopus
entries.archetype: Neurons in the Arms, Colour in the Skin

waveform.description: Quiet den time broken by repeated foraging excursions.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: sheltered den time and exploratory foraging.

entries.name: Common Opossum

modes.label: Hissing and baring fifty teeth at a threat • Collapsing involuntarily into a rigid open-mouthed state if that fails • Remaining unresponsive for minutes to hours while producing a foul anal secretion

waveform.description: Ordinary activity rising into a sharp event and then dropping to a sustained flat depressed state, because the collapse is not a return to normal.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur through the night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Pheasant

modes.label: Tens of millions of birds reared in pens each year and released into the countryside before the shooting season • That release adding a very large seasonal mass of birds to the landscape at one time • Predator and scavenger populations, plant communities and invertebrates all responding to a food supply that appears and disappears on a calendar set by people

waveform.description: A sharp annual pulse and decline, because the population is created in a few weeks and consumed through the winter.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Pill Woodlouse

modes.label: Curling into a closed ball • Plates interlocking • Losing nothing from inside

waveform.description: A slow crawl interrupted by two flat troughs, because the response to trouble is to stop being an animal shape at all.

entries.closingLine: Since everything runs slowly in the damp dark, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Poorwill

waveform.description: Long low stretches of torpor punctuated by narrow sharp peaks of active insect-hawking when conditions are briefly favorable.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole system alternates between deep, extended torpor and tightly timed bursts of foraging, the Common Poorwill operates as a bimodal low-and-high frequency system built around torpor timing.

entries.name: Common Potoo

modes.label: Upright on a stump • Eyes shut • Watching anyway
Dusk • Sallying out • Back to the same perch

waveform.description: A long flat day followed by a cluster of brief night sallies.

entries.closingLine: That is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Common Prawn

modes.label: Holding among weed and in rockpools with a shell that transmits light • Being visible only as thin lines and two dark eyes • Flicking the abdomen to shoot backwards when detected

waveform.description: Quiet movement interrupted by extremely sharp escape events, because the animal drifts and grooms until something triggers the tail flick.

entries.closingLine: Since escape responses recur in fractions of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Quail

modes.label: Breeding in one crop and moving on as it is cut • Crossing the Sahara twice a year • Following green cereal northward across a season

waveform.description: A restless irregular pattern that never settles at one level, because the bird keeps relocating rather than holding a place.

entries.closingLine: Since breeding attempts shift within a season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Rat Snake

waveform.description: A moderate, repeating rhythm with small oscillations and occasional higher bumps representing each shed cycle rising in activity and then returning to baseline.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system built on recurring, whole-body renewal pulses rather than constant micro-adjustment or rare one-time transformations: a steady rhythm of operate–accumulate–shed–resume that lets the animal keep extending beyond previous physical limits.

entries.name: Common Raven

waveform.description: An irregular rhythm that keeps changing shape, with occasional sharp committed peaks.

entries.closingLine: Because the behaviour is selected to match the context rather than fixed to one tempo, the raven is best described as an adaptive system: a steady watching-and-storing baseline that can switch into fast opportunistic action.

entries.name: Common Roach

modes.label: Shoaling in open water and among weed • Growing deeper-bodied where predators are abundant • Becoming too tall for a pike's gape to close on

waveform.description: A regular unremarkable rhythm without extremes, because a shoaling fish's day is a continuous even routine.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding and shoaling are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Rose

modes.label: Larvae feeding on Aristolochia vines and sequestering aristolochic acids that make the adult genuinely unpalatable • A slow deliberate flight and a conspicuous red body advertising that fact clearly • Several unrelated butterflies converging on the same appearance, so the model bears the cost of the education while the mimics do not

waveform.description: A slow unhurried rhythm with little variation, because a protected butterfly has no reason to fly evasively.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs generationally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Rotifer

waveform.description: A mid-level gentle oscillation for steady feeding, a sharp high spike for rapid renewal, then a sagging low plateau for dormancy before rising back toward mid activity.

entries.closingLine: The result is a multimodal rhythm: mid-frequency ongoing wheel-feeding, punctuated by high-frequency renewal bursts and underpinned by low-frequency dormancy that lets the cycle repeat across changing freshwater conditions.

entries.name: Common Rough Woodlouse

modes.label: Walking fast and turning often while the air is dry • Slowing and turning less as soon as the air becomes humid • Accumulating in damp places without ever steering towards them

waveform.description: A fast agitated start settling into a slow steady line, because activity falls as the animal reaches humid air.

entries.closingLine: Because the response is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Sand Dollar

waveform.description: A low, gently rippling line showing continuous, modest activity as the sand dollar stays buried and filters passing food.

entries.closingLine: This architecture of staying put, staying hidden, and letting the environment bring resources defines a low-frequency system built on quiet, continuous intake.

entries.name: Common Sandpiper

waveform.description: Steady mid-height bobbing pulses along a continuous patrol line.

entries.closingLine: Success is measured in uninterrupted scanning loops, not in rare decisive events.

entries.name: Common Sawshark

waveform.description: A gently oscillating mid-level line, representing repeated sweeps along the seafloor with small, regular bursts when prey is contacted.

entries.closingLine: Its life is built from many such passes—resting near the bottom, then resuming this patterned search when food and safety coincide—so its operating rhythm is a coordinated, ongoing mid-frequency system driven by repeated rostrum sweeps rather than rare huge bursts or deep, static conservation.

entries.name: Common Scorpionfly
entries.archetype: A Long Beak Robbing Spider Webs

waveform.description: A steady scavenging line with occasional sharp spikes of web raiding.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady scavenging in low cover and brief raids on webs.

entries.name: Common Seahorse

modes.label: Gripping a stem • Eyes moving separately • Snapping the head upward

waveform.description: A held line pricked by very narrow spikes at short intervals, because the strike is frequent and the body never moves.

entries.closingLine: Because that rhythm never pauses, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Snapping Turtle

waveform.description: A buried flat line broken twice by a reach that goes all the way.

entries.closingLine: Long cheap concealment paying for one committed reach makes this a bimodal system, low-frequency in the mud and high-frequency at the strike.

entries.name: Common Sole

modes.label: Lying buried in soft sediment through the day • Emerging after dark and pressing the blind side of the head to the bottom • Locating buried worms with dense sensory papillae and taking them without seeing anything

waveform.description: Long buried stretches alternating with a raised active period, because the animal is either in the sediment or working over it.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding actions repeat through the night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Stingray

modes.label: A serrated spine mounted on the upper surface of the tail, pointing backwards • Backward-facing barbs along both edges so the spine enters cleanly and resists being pulled out • A venom-bearing sheath rupturing on entry and delivering its contents into the wound

waveform.description: A flat buried line with rare sharp defensive events, because the animal lies still and strikes only when trodden on.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are rare, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Sun Skink

modes.label: Retaining developing embryos inside the body for weeks • Supplying them through a placental connection rather than a yolk alone • Giving birth to fully formed young that can run immediately

waveform.description: A very slow even line with a single modest rise, because the cycle is annual and nothing about it is abrupt.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Swift
entries.archetype: Roosting on the Air After Dusk

waveform.description: A steady daytime feeding line easing into a quiet nocturnal glide aloft.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: daytime aerial feeding and nocturnal high-altitude resting.

entries.name: Common Tailorbird

waveform.description: A gentle, even ripple showing repeated, moderate activity cycles around a stable stitched nest site.

entries.closingLine: This creates a mid-frequency system: not a slow reserve hoarder or a pure burst hunter, but a steady, site-bound rhythm of sewing, foraging, and returning to the same stitched canopy.

entries.name: Common Tenrec

waveform.description: Gentle mid-level oscillations for regular foraging, a low stable segment for torpor, and one sharp brief spike for defensive bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because its survival depends on moving between concealed torpor, routine flexible foraging, and brief defensive bursts rather than living in a single operating tempo, the common tenrec is best understood as a multimodal system spanning low, mid and high frequencies.

entries.name: Common Treeshrew
entries.archetype: Snout-First Forager of the Forest Floor

waveform.description: A busy daytime line of short foraging bursts, quiet from dusk to dawn.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a steady daytime routine of rapid, probing searches rather than either long rest or explosive action, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common True Katydid

modes.label: Males calling in an alternating pattern so that each song falls into the gap left by a neighbour • Each individual adjusting its timing within a fraction of a second to avoid overlapping the one before • The result an interleaved chorus in which every call remains separately audible rather than merging into noise

waveform.description: A precisely alternating rhythm with no overlap, because each call is fitted into the gap left by the last.

entries.closingLine: Because the alternation runs several times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Vampire Bat
entries.archetype: Blood Debts Repaid in the Roost

waveform.description: A slow night of patient feeding giving way to a busier social period back in the roost.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: patient nocturnal feeding and a social exchange phase in the roost.

entries.name: Common Wall Gecko

waveform.description: Even mid-level oscillations showing a repeating cycle of gripping and stepping while overall activity stays continuous and controlled.

entries.closingLine: That produces a mid-frequency system: continuous, stepwise movement built from tightly controlled, repeating contact cycles rather than slow reserve use or explosive sprinting.

entries.name: Common Wall Lizard

modes.label: Basking on stone until warm enough to move • Foraging across vertical rock and wall faces • Shifting diet to whatever the site actually supplies

waveform.description: A brisk repeating pattern of similar events, because the animal alternates basking and activity through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging bouts recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Wanderer

modes.label: A male in plain bluish white with black veining, flying fast and erratically, unprotected and behaving accordingly
A female patterned in pale blue and black closely resembling the distasteful Parantica tigers she flies among, moving slowly and openly like them

waveform.description: A fast erratic rhythm giving way to a slow steady one, because the two sexes fly in entirely different ways.

entries.closingLine: This is sex-limited Batesian mimicry, and the two sexes therefore run genuinely different defensive systems in the same species, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Common Warthog

waveform.description: A steady daytime grazing rhythm with regular returns.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, practical and organised around borrowed structure.

entries.name: Common Water Flea

modes.label: An animal in water with no predator present, smooth-headed and without spines, putting everything into growth and reproduction
An animal detecting chemical traces released by predators and growing a helmet, neck teeth and an elongated tail spine within one moult

waveform.description: An active fast rhythm dropping into a slower heavier one, because the defended animal grows and reproduces less.

entries.closingLine: The system is one of the standard demonstrations that an organism can carry the genes for two quite different bodies and construct whichever the environment calls for, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Common Wolf Snake

modes.label: A pattern of pale bands on a dark body closely resembling that of the kraits it shares its range with • No venom of consequence and no capacity to back the warning up • Predators and people treating it as dangerous on the strength of the pattern alone

waveform.description: A quiet nocturnal line with a broad gentle rise, because the animal moves steadily through the night without bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because activity is nightly, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Common Wombat

waveform.description: A very flat low line with almost no variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, retentive and built around a place rather than a behaviour.

entries.name: Common Wood Pigeon

waveform.description: Even, repeating peaks of activity between flat segments, representing regular flights out to feed and back to woodland cover each day.

entries.closingLine: That pattern makes the wood pigeon a single mid-frequency system, organized around rhythmic commuting between woodland shelter and open feeding grounds.

entries.name: Cone-headed Grasshopper

waveform.description: Long stretches of low visible activity on a support, punctuated by sharp, narrow spikes of intense effort when jumping.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal’s structure is built around holding a prepared state and then spending energy in brief, forceful jumps whenever a route or threat appears, this is a high-frequency burst system rather than a steady, moderate one.

entries.name: Convict Tang

waveform.description: Even, medium-amplitude ripples showing ongoing, rhythmic group activity without long dormancy or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: That makes the convict tang a mid-frequency system, defined by steady, rhythmic group activity anchored by always-on visual cohesion.

entries.name: Coppery Titi Monkey

waveform.description: A gently undulating midline showing ongoing, steady, shared activity with small, regular fluctuations that never fully separate.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency pattern: rhythmic, coordinated and networked, where intertwined bodies and behaviours keep the group supported and connected in real time.

entries.name: Coquerel's Sifaka

waveform.description: Periods of stillness against a trunk broken by identical launches — each leap is the same movement repeated.

entries.closingLine: Since the day is a repeating cycle of clinging, feeding and leaping, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Corkwing Wrasse
entries.archetype: Males That Build, Males That Do Not

modes.label: Building a nest of algae in a rock crevice • Displaying in bright breeding colours • Courting and then guarding and fanning the eggs
Wearing female colouring and shape • Slipping into another male's nest during spawning • Releasing sperm and leaving without building or guarding anything

waveform.description: Two clearly different levels alternating irregularly, because the two strategies coexist and neither replaces the other.

entries.closingLine: Since the two run side by side through the season, this is an adaptive system.

entries.name: Corn Snake

waveform.description: A flat, economical line: steady slow searching with almost no variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: patient, cheap to run and organised around following information rather than chasing prey.

entries.name: Corsac Fox
entries.archetype: A Fox That Does Not Hold Ground

modes.label: Ranging without a territory • Taking over marmot burrows • Moving south from snow

waveform.description: A continuous travelling rhythm with no fixed centre.

entries.closingLine: This is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Coscoroba Swan

waveform.description: Calm surface feeding punctuated by a repeated call.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady surface feeding organised by one repeated signal rather than by elaborate display.

entries.name: Cotton Bud Moth

modes.label: Males locating females by following a plume of pheromone released in very small quantities • Synthetic pheromone released from dispensers across a whole field at far higher concentration • Males unable to follow any single plume because the entire air carries the signal, so mating rates collapse without anything being killed

waveform.description: A continuous searching rhythm, because the males are flying and sampling the air throughout the night.

entries.closingLine: Because the search is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cotton Pygmy Goose

waveform.description: Feeding in the morning and afternoon, with a quiet rest through the midday heat.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: surface feeding among lilies and rest in cover.

entries.name: Cotton-top Tamarin

waveform.description: A dense varied rhythm of different heights — many distinct signals rather than one repeated over and over.

entries.closingLine: Because calling runs continuously through the day, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Couch's Spadefoot

waveform.description: A buried flat line broken by one very narrow burst of everything.

entries.closingLine: Enormous dormancy punctuated by an explosive window makes this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Cougar

waveform.description: A long even travelling line broken twice by a very narrow strike.

entries.closingLine: Those two unlike parts make this a bimodal system, a mid-frequency patrol that exists to set up a rare high-frequency strike.

entries.name: Cow

waveform.description: An unvarying moderate rhythm with every cycle the same height, because the vat inside is never allowed to stop.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is one continuous conversion at a steady rate, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cownose Ray

waveform.description: A mostly level mid-line for steady schooling sweep, with a single sharp dip-and-rise spike showing a brief high-frequency burst for strike or evasion before returning to coordinated travel.

entries.closingLine: That makes the cownose ray a bimodal system: a dominant mid-frequency, coordinated sweep mode, with essential but brief high-frequency bursts for capture and escape layered on top.

entries.name: Coyote

waveform.description: A low quiet line that lifts into a sustained grouped rhythm and settles back.

entries.closingLine: That makes it an adaptive system: the operating state is selected by context rather than fixed.

entries.name: Coypu

modes.label: Mammary glands positioned along the upper sides of the body rather than on the belly • Young able to reach them while the mother floats with her back at the surface • Suckling continuing during swimming so the litter is never separated from water

waveform.description: A steady aquatic rhythm, because the animal moves and feeds continuously in and around water.

entries.closingLine: Because nursing recurs continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cozumel Coati

waveform.description: A busy continuous searching rhythm across a small area of ground.

entries.closingLine: Continuous social searching over bounded ground makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cozumel Raccoon
entries.archetype: A Dwarfed Crab-Hunter in Mangrove Roots

waveform.description: A steady night of shoreline foraging rising and settling each evening.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a steady nightly foraging routine along one kind of shoreline, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Crab Spider

waveform.description: Long, near-flat stillness with rare, very brief spikes of capture.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: long, cryptic waiting punctuated by a very brief seizure.

entries.name: Crab-eating Fox
entries.archetype: Diet Set by Whatever the Season Left

waveform.description: A rhythm alternating between two sustained levels across the year.

entries.closingLine: That makes it an adaptive system: the operating state is set by the season rather than by the species.

entries.name: Crane Fly

modes.label: Flying weakly on long trailing legs that catch on everything • Shedding a leg at a fracture point when it is grasped • Continuing to fly and mate with several legs missing

waveform.description: A loose irregular drift broken by occasional sharp events, because the flight is erratic and the shedding is sudden.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Crest-tailed Mulgara

waveform.description: Long low stretches of burrowed conservation with brief, sharp dips upward in activity representing nocturnal hunting bursts.

entries.closingLine: This creates a bimodal rhythm: a dominant low-frequency, reserve-and-shelter mode punctuated by necessary high-frequency nocturnal foraging bursts.

entries.name: Crested Auklet

waveform.description: Even, repeating mid-height waves showing continuous cycles of display, calls, and scent use in colony life.

entries.closingLine: That makes the Crested Auklet a mid-frequency system: it runs on steady, rhythmic, multi-sensory communication woven through everyday colony activity.

entries.name: Crested Berrypecker

waveform.description: A gently undulating midline showing steady, modest oscillations that represent continuous, precise activity without big bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because its survival depends on this ongoing, well-matched rhythm of movement and feeding instead of extreme endurance or explosive bursts, its system expresses a single, mid-frequency pattern of niche-precise activity.

entries.name: Crested Coua

waveform.description: A still, sunlit start rising into steady clambering through the day, easing off before roosting.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: close canopy gleaning and brief morning sunning.

entries.name: Crested Fireback

modes.label: Bare blue facial skin with lappets that can be engorged with blood within seconds • Those wattles swelling and intensifying in colour during display and deflating afterwards • Colour and size depending directly on circulation and condition rather than on a fixed structure

waveform.description: A calm line with sharp swelling episodes, because the wattles inflate suddenly during display and subside afterwards.

entries.closingLine: Because displays are seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Crested Gecko

modes.label: Climbing on adhesive toe pads and a gripping tail tip • Shedding the tail to escape a grip • Living the rest of its life without one

waveform.description: A steady line interrupted once, after which it settles at a different level, because the loss is permanent rather than temporary.

entries.closingLine: Since climbing and foraging recur nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Crested Oropendola
entries.archetype: Hanging Colony on an Isolated Tree

waveform.description: A steady building rhythm sustained across a colony.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady construction and communal occupation rather than any individual response.

entries.name: Crested Pigeon

waveform.description: A quiet ground line breaking into a rapid whistling flush.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: quiet ground feeding and an automatic broadcast generated the instant the bird leaves.

entries.name: Crested Porcupine
entries.archetype: Hollow Quills Rattled as a Warning

waveform.description: A slow quiet line breaking into a noisy escalating display.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: quiet nocturnal foraging and a loud staged deterrent.

entries.name: Crested Serpent Eagle

waveform.description: A shaded perched line broken by a short committed drop.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a patient shaded watch and a brief armoured strike.

entries.name: Crimson Sunbird

modes.label: Landing on a stem beside a flower rather than hovering in front of it • Inserting a decurved bill and tubular tongue into the corolla • Drawing nectar up capillary grooves while the body is supported

waveform.description: A rapid even rhythm sustained throughout, because visits follow one another continuously through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since visits recur constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Crimson-fronted Barbet

modes.label: A stout bill used to excavate a nest hole in soft dead or decaying wood, which most cavity nesters cannot do • A new hole cut most years rather than an old one reused, so the number of cavities in a wood accumulates • Those abandoned holes taken over by parakeets, mynas, owlets, bats and bees, none of which can make one

waveform.description: A single seasonal excavation and occupation, because a hole is cut and used once through a breeding cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Crocodile Icefish

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing continuous but subdued circulation and activity in stable cold conditions.

entries.closingLine: This makes them a strongly low-frequency system: built for continuous, economical flow in stable cold rather than fast, wasteful spikes of activity.

entries.name: Crocodile Monitor

waveform.description: Steady climbing and searching effort across the day — sustained work rather than waiting.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts continuous searching effort into a steady return, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Crown-of-thorns Starfish

waveform.description: A mostly low, slightly rising band for slow pressure feeding, with a return to low shelter at the end, showing alternating rest and sustained but moderate activity.

entries.closingLine: This creates a bimodal rhythm: low-frequency sheltering and digestion anchored in the reef, and medium-frequency, sustained feeding movements that steadily reshape the habitat when their hunger is applied.

entries.name: Crowned Eagle

modes.label: One chick • Fed for a year • Biennial

waveform.description: One broad shallow rise spread across many months, then a year close to the baseline — a two-year cycle rather than an annual one.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole reproductive system runs on a two-year cycle, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Crystal Red Shrimp
entries.archetype: A Colour Form Bred Into Place

modes.label: Grazing biofilm and algae from surfaces continuously • Carrying a fixed red and white pattern produced by selective breeding • Depending on soft acidic water held within a narrow range

waveform.description: A gentle unvarying rhythm with no strong features, because the animal grazes steadily and nothing about its day changes.

entries.closingLine: Since grazing is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cuban Crocodile

waveform.description: An uneven rhythm with sharp lifts — a crocodile that moves on land in bursts rather than gliding in water.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding and moving run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cuban Hutia
entries.archetype: Generalist Browser Sheltering in Rock and Hollow

waveform.description: Feeding bouts through the day separated by rest in shared shelters.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: daytime browsing and long communal sheltering.

entries.name: Cuban Rock Iguana

waveform.description: Two warming humps tracking the sun with a floor that never drops far — a day governed by temperature rather than by hunger.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs on cheap solar heat converted patiently into size and status, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cuban Solenodon

waveform.description: A modest repeating rhythm close to the baseline — steady nocturnal rooting rather than any decisive event.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding runs as a steady unhurried nocturnal search, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Cuban Tody
entries.archetype: Upward Sally to the Leaf Underside

waveform.description: An even rhythm of still scanning punctuated by short, regular upward sallies.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a single-mode system: an unbroken rhythm of watching and upward sallies.

entries.name: Cuckoo Wasp

modes.label: Entering the nest of a solitary bee or wasp to lay in it • Being attacked by the owner on the way in or out • Rolling into a ball with the concave underside enclosing the legs, inside a cuticle thick enough that stings do not penetrate

waveform.description: Ordinary activity alternating with sustained defensive states, because the animal is either moving or curled and immobile.

entries.closingLine: Since nest entries recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Cuckoo Wrasse

modes.label: Living as a reddish-orange female with dark marks near the tail • Spawning in a group over rocky ground • Being one of many similar fish
Turning blue and yellow with an intense head pattern • Holding and defending a territory • Building a nest of algae and courting visiting females

waveform.description: One level held, a single transition, and a different level afterwards, because the change happens once and does not reverse.

entries.closingLine: Because the change happens once and cannot reverse, it operates as a phase-change system.

entries.name: Culpeo
entries.archetype: A Wild Dog Spanning the Whole Andes

waveform.description: Quiet daytime rest rising into sustained hunting and travel through dusk and night.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal, sheltered rest and a sustained, opportunistic roaming mode.

entries.name: Cunner

modes.label: Foraging over rocky reef and wrecks through the warm months • Picking mussels, barnacles and crustaceans from hard surfaces • Defending small areas and cleaning other fish
Wedging into a rock crevice as water temperature falls • Ceasing to feed for months • Dropping heart rate and metabolism far enough to survive on almost nothing

waveform.description: Ordinary activity alternating with a long flat depressed stretch, because the animal genuinely alternates between two physiological states.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two physiologies, making this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Curl-crested Aracari

waveform.description: A gently undulating mid-level line, showing a steady, ongoing signal that never drops to invisibility and does not spike into brief extremes.

entries.closingLine: That makes the curl-crested aracari a mid-frequency system: a steady, repeating signal woven into regular activity instead of a single slow reserve or a brief high-speed burst.

entries.name: Cyclodes Moth

modes.label: A proboscis stiffened and armed at the tip with barbs and cutting ridges rather than built only for sucking • That tip worked through the intact skin of a ripening fruit by twisting and pressing • Juice drawn out from inside a fruit that no ordinary nectar-feeding moth could open at all

waveform.description: A slow nocturnal build and decline, because the moth works at a single fruit for a long period.

entries.closingLine: Because the feeding is nightly, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Daddy Long-Legs Spider

modes.label: Hanging inverted in a loose tangle • Entering a resident spider's web and vibrating the silk • Killing from beyond reach with very long legs

waveform.description: A flat line disturbed by a short accelerating flutter before one sharp spike, because the deception builds before the strike.

entries.closingLine: Since hunting recurs nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Dall Sheep

modes.label: Growing horn continuously in summer and almost not at all in winter • Leaving a visible constriction at each winter • Carrying a readable record of age and of every hard year on the head

waveform.description: A regular annual oscillation of diminishing amplitude, because growth repeats each year and slows as the animal ages.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Dama Gazelle
entries.archetype: Long Legs Tracking the Sahel Rains

waveform.description: Browsing rises in the cool hours around a low midday rest.

entries.closingLine: Because it is built on slow browsing and seasonal movement, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Damaraland Mole-rat

waveform.description: A mostly low, steady line for sheltered colony maintenance with a few rounded mid-height humps for coordinated digging and foraging bouts.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system depends on a stable, low-risk base overlaid with coordinated work pulses in the same hidden network, this is a bimodal system with a low-frequency shelter core and a mid-frequency labor rhythm.

entries.name: Damsel Bug

modes.label: Front legs thickened and held folded, used to seize rather than to walk • A dense pad of fine adhesive hairs on the underside of the tibia gripping the prey's surface directly • The captured insect held by adhesion rather than by force while the beak is inserted

waveform.description: A steady searching rhythm with brief captures, because the bug moves continuously and seizes what it meets.

entries.closingLine: Because captures recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Damselfly

modes.label: Fluttering between stems • Hanging in the air • Picking prey off a leaf

waveform.description: A light continuous hovering wave with no sharp attack in it, because the flight is a hold rather than a chase.

entries.closingLine: Because the flying and gleaning run continuously through warm daylight, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Danube River Snail

modes.label: Retaining developing embryos in a brood pouch for months • Releasing fully formed shelled young a few millimetres across • Producing few offspring, each of them already viable

waveform.description: A long low even line with a single small rise, because a slow-moving animal releasing a few young a year has almost no variation in its year.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Dark Fishing Spider

modes.label: Resting at the edge with front legs touching the water film • Reading the ripples that a struggling insect makes • Running across the surface to reach it and diving beneath when threatened

waveform.description: A still line broken by a short build of small disturbances leading to a sharp event, because the ripples arrive before the run.

entries.closingLine: Since ripple events recur through the night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Dark-eyed Junco

modes.label: A population establishing on a coastal campus where winters are mild and irrigation keeps food available • Selection there favouring a longer breeding season, more parental effort and less white in the tail • Measurable change in those traits within decades rather than over evolutionary time

waveform.description: A steady rhythm with a persistent drift in one direction, because the change accumulates while daily life continues.

entries.closingLine: Because the change accumulates over generations, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Darkling Beetle

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing mostly steady, frugal activity with small rises when recurring dry-ground resources appear.

entries.closingLine: This makes Tenebrionidae a low-frequency system: dense-bodied, conservative with water and energy, and tuned to a slow, recurring dry-ground economy rather than rapid, volatile bursts.

entries.name: Darwin’s Bark Spider

waveform.description: Even, medium-height oscillations showing repeated cycles of web construction, maintenance and reuse rather than long dormancy or frantic bursts.

entries.closingLine: That rhythm of ongoing structural investment and maintenance around a giant web makes this a mid-frequency, rhythmic system.

entries.name: Darwin's Fox

waveform.description: A steady working rhythm — small foraging bouts repeated through the day and into the night.

entries.closingLine: Because foraging runs as a steady daily round rather than in bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Darwin's Frog

waveform.description: A low, nearly flat line with tiny undulations, showing long stretches of quiet shelter with only small, timed movements.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole reproductive strategy depends on steady, cautious, body-based shelter rather than bursts of activity or constant ranging, Darwin’s frog operates as a single, low-frequency system built around patient, carried protection.

entries.name: De Brazza's Monkey
entries.archetype: A Face Readable Only Up Close

modes.label: Foraging near water • Freezing • Moving only when unwatched

waveform.description: A deliberately quiet trace with long motionless stretches.

entries.closingLine: Slow, secretive and largely stationary, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Death's-head Hawkmoth

waveform.description: Rapid tall spikes with almost no settled baseline between them.

entries.closingLine: A few weeks of life, an expensive engine and a sugar-rich raid make this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Decorator Crab
