waveform.description: A gently undulating mid-level line showing steady, rhythmic activity with small rises when disguise and movement align, rather than long dormancy or sharp bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because the crab’s survival depends on this ongoing, context-matched maintenance of a borrowed coat plus well-timed movement, its system runs as a coordinated, rhythmic mid-frequency pattern rather than a single slow reserve or a pure speed burst.

entries.name: Degu

waveform.description: A steady sociable daytime rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, social and continuously coordinated.

entries.name: Demoiselle Crane

waveform.description: A level steppe rhythm rising into one long seasonal climb and back.

entries.closingLine: Sustained walking and long seasonal travel make this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Denison Barb

waveform.description: Even, rolling mid-height waves showing a school’s steady, shared-direction swimming with repeated coordinated effort.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, coordinated, and based on ongoing shared movement rather than extremes of stillness or sudden sprinting.

entries.name: Desert Cottontail

modes.label: Fermenting plant material in a large caecum where bacteria break down cellulose • Passing soft nutrient-rich caecotrophs and re-ingesting them directly • Digesting those a second time in the stomach and small intestine where the released nutrients can be absorbed

waveform.description: A regular alternating rhythm, because the animal cycles between feeding and re-ingestion through the day and night.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Desert Hedgehog

waveform.description: Even, moderate spikes rising from a safe baseline, showing repeated nightly foraging trips out from shelter and back.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: a rhythmic, place-anchored operating pattern built on steady, repeatable activity rather than deep dormancy or explosive sprinting.

entries.name: Desert Horned Viper
entries.archetype: A Warning Made by Rubbing Scales

modes.label: Shuffling into sand • Waiting • Rasping if approached

waveform.description: Near-total stillness beneath the sand across long nights.

entries.closingLine: Motionless waiting throughout makes this a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Desert Iguana
entries.archetype: Foraging in Heat That Excludes Rivals

waveform.description: Burrowed low periods framing a sustained hot-day activity plateau.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: hot-day foraging and a seasonal retreat underground.

entries.name: Desert Kangaroo Rat
entries.archetype: A Water Budget Balanced Without Drinking

waveform.description: A flat, conserving day in the burrow and a night of foraging with a sudden evasive leap.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a daytime water-saving retreat and nocturnal foraging.

entries.name: Desert Locust

waveform.description: A moderate, gently wavering baseline that bends sharply downward at a threshold, after which the line breaks into rapid, higher-amplitude oscillations representing the shift into intense swarm activity.

entries.closingLine: Because crossing this density threshold rewrites how the entire system is built and how it spends energy, this is best understood as a phase-change system with a mid-frequency solitary baseline and a high-frequency gregarious swarm state.

entries.name: Desert Pocket Mouse
entries.archetype: Dry Seeds Carried Outside the Mouth

waveform.description: Night foraging bouts rising out of long, flat days spent in a sealed burrow.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: nightly seed collection and long sealed rest below ground.

entries.name: Desert Rain Frog

waveform.description: An almost unbroken floor with the smallest night-time excursions — an animal that spends nearly nothing.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs on minimal expenditure inside a narrow band of damp sand, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Desert Woodrat
entries.archetype: A House Cemented by Its Builder

waveform.description: A flat, sheltered daytime gives way to a moderate night of foraging near the house.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long sheltered days inside and short nightly gathering runs.

entries.name: Devil's Coach Horse Beetle

modes.label: The abdomen curved up over the back in a posture that reads immediately as a scorpion
Paired glands at the tip of that raised abdomen releasing a foul-smelling secretion into the air and onto anything close

waveform.description: A quiet line with paired sharp episodes, because the display and the discharge happen together and briefly.

entries.closingLine: The beetle is a fast ground predator of other invertebrates, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Devil's Flower Mantis

waveform.description: Almost unbroken stillness with two instantaneous full-height events — the same shape whether the trigger is prey or a predator.

entries.closingLine: Because near-zero waiting alternates with two different instantaneous commitments, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Dhole

waveform.description: A dense regular rhythm of returns to the den — many trips a day, none of them large.

entries.closingLine: Because provisioning runs as a steady repeated daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Diamondback Terrapin

waveform.description: A slow tidal rhythm of modest amplitude sliding into a deeper winter floor — a year with two speeds, both of them low.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal trades speed and turnover for durable occupation of a chemically difficult niche, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Diana Monkey
entries.archetype: Alarm Calls That Name the Predator

waveform.description: A steady canopy foraging line broken by sharp alarm spikes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: canopy foraging and brief alarm events.

entries.name: Dibatag

waveform.description: A repeating rise and settle — each browsing stand lifts the animal and returns it, all day long.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is a steady repeated cycle of standing, taking and settling, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Dibbler

waveform.description: A fine dense rhythm of small captures across the night, falling away before dawn.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from many small captures repeated nightly, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Differential Grasshopper

modes.label: Chewing through the season • Laying pods in soil • Surviving as numbers

waveform.description: A steady chewing rhythm of even peaks, because the animal itself does one thing all season regardless of how many of it there are.

entries.closingLine: Because the individual chews steadily through a season at one unvarying tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Dingy Bushbrown

waveform.description: A low, gently wavering line showing mostly steady, subdued activity in the shade with only small fluctuations.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a single-mode, low-frequency system built around living in the calm shade beneath busier movement above.

entries.name: Discus Fish

waveform.description: An almost flat held line with only the smallest corrections in it.

entries.closingLine: Minimal movement and very high parental cost make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Diving Bell Spider

waveform.description: Even, moderate oscillations showing repeated cycles of leaving and refilling the bell while maintaining a steady underwater routine.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system: a stable underwater base sustained by rhythmic maintenance and ongoing, repeatable cycles rather than rare deep reserves or explosive bursts.

entries.name: Dobsonfly
entries.archetype: Mandibles Too Long to Bite With

waveform.description: A long active larval rhythm dropping to a brief low adult stage.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long capable aquatic stage and a short ornamental terrestrial one.

entries.name: Domestic Canary

modes.label: Singing through the breeding season • Growing the brain regions that produce it • Shedding them again after

waveform.description: A rising and falling rhythm whose peaks grow through the middle and subside, because the capacity itself expands and contracts across the year.

entries.closingLine: Since singing and feeding run together through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Cat

waveform.description: A controlled mid-frequency rhythm interrupted by a precise high-frequency pounce.

entries.closingLine: The cat is therefore a bimodal system: cruise quietly, then act fast when the opening is right.

entries.name: Domestic Dog

modes.label: Watching the face • Following the point • Checking back

waveform.description: An irregular attentive ripple whose peaks do not repeat evenly, because the rhythm belongs to the household rather than to the animal.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a continuous, cheap and unbroken reading of another species' attention, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Donkey

modes.label: Walking under load • Stopping to assess • Refusing to bolt

waveform.description: A long shallow line with two brief flat holds in it, because the only interruption this animal offers is stopping.

entries.closingLine: Since every process is slow, economical and built for a long horizon, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Duck

modes.label: Barbules along each feather barb carrying hooks that interlock with the barbs beside them • The bird drawing each feather through the bill to re-zip separated barbs and spread oil from the preen gland • The plumage forming a continuous surface that water cannot pass through, with dry insulating down beneath

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm of preening and paddling, because maintenance is continuous rather than occasional.

entries.closingLine: Because preening is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Ferret
entries.archetype: Long Spine, Fast Gut, Deep Sleep

waveform.description: Long stretches of deep sleep punctuated by short, intense bursts of activity.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long, deep sleep and short, intense active bursts.

entries.name: Domestic Goat

waveform.description: A restless uneven flutter where no two peaks match, because the animal never works the same item twice in a row.

entries.closingLine: Because the sampling is continuous and repeated all day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Goose

modes.label: Gripping grass between serrated bill edges and tearing with a head movement • Passing it through a short gut very quickly • Feeding for most of the daylight hours to compensate

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying rhythm sustained across the whole span, because grazing continues with almost no pause through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since bites recur every few seconds, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Horse

modes.label: Grazing most of the day • Fermenting behind the small intestine • Dozing on locked legs

waveform.description: An almost unvarying rhythm with no peaks or gaps, because the animal is designed never to stop taking food in.

entries.closingLine: Since intake and fermentation run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Pig

modes.label: Driving the snout disc into ground • Reading what is turned up • Wallowing to shed heat

waveform.description: A busy rooting rhythm with one flat trough dropped into the middle, because the day is built around hours spent lying in mud.

entries.closingLine: Since rooting runs through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Pigeon

modes.label: Reading the sun's position against an internal clock • Sensing magnetic field and low-frequency sound • Following remembered landmarks near home

waveform.description: A steady repeating pattern of moderate depth, because navigation is a continuous correcting process rather than a series of decisions.

entries.closingLine: Since orientation is corrected continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Rabbit

modes.label: Rotating each ear independently • Scanning almost the full circle by eye at the same time • Shedding heat through the same ear surface

waveform.description: Constant small movements with one much larger excursion, because scanning never stops and a genuine alarm is a different order of event.

entries.closingLine: Since scanning runs continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Sheep

modes.label: Grazing head-down • Watching sideways • Moving as one

waveform.description: A smooth low-amplitude wave with no sharp edges anywhere, because the alertness is continuous rather than episodic.

entries.closingLine: Because the watching and the feeding happen simultaneously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Domestic Turkey

waveform.description: A steady foraging line with regular small lifts, broken once by a sharp alarm spike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady vigilant foraging broken by brief flock-wide alarms.

entries.name: Double-crested Cormorant

waveform.description: A working diving rhythm followed by a long flat drying plateau.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: productive underwater work and a mandatory recovery period.

entries.name: Downy Woodpecker

modes.label: Working thin stems • Drumming a resonant branch • Listening for the reply

waveform.description: Tight bursts of identical strokes separated by flat gaps, because a drum roll is a discrete message rather than a continuous rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because that day is steady and repeated, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Dragon Moray
entries.archetype: Curved Fangs Waiting in a Reef Hole

waveform.description: Long, still waiting in a crevice broken by sudden strikes.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: LOW waiting in shelter and HIGH strikes.

entries.name: Dragonface Pipefish

waveform.description: A long, low creeping line broken by needle-thin spikes where the strike happens.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: slow, concealed creeping and a single explosive strike.

entries.name: Dragonfly

modes.label: Waiting motionless on the bed of a pond as a nymph • Firing a hinged labium forward on hydraulic pressure • Pulling the prey back to the mouth in a fraction of a second

waveform.description: A still baseline broken by extremely narrow full-depth strikes, because the nymph waits motionless and the strike is over in milliseconds.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes recur in milliseconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Drain Fly

modes.label: Developing as larvae inside the gelatinous biofilm on the inside of drains • Breathing through a siphon that reaches the surface of that film • Grazing the bacteria and organic matter the film is made of

waveform.description: A rapid shallow rhythm with no larger structure, because the whole life cycle turns over in weeks and nothing about it varies.

entries.closingLine: Since generations turn over in weeks, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Drill

waveform.description: A steady collective rhythm — a large group moving and feeding together at one unvarying pace.

entries.closingLine: Because movement and feeding run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Driver Ant

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line for organized column activity with a single sharp dip upward (higher activity) representing a brief mass recruitment surge before returning to the marching baseline.

entries.closingLine: The system therefore has a mid-frequency backbone of coordinated marching, with high-frequency surges layered on top when cues demand concentrated force, making it a bimodal pattern of steady organization plus triggered swarm bursts.

entries.name: Dromedary Camel

waveform.description: A slow low line drifting gently without sharp changes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, tolerant and built to let conditions swing rather than to resist them.

entries.name: Dugong

waveform.description: A shallow steady rhythm — the grazing pass of an animal that never hurries and never stops for long.

entries.closingLine: Because a large animal is supported by continuous low-intensity grazing on a long horizon, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Dumbo Octopus

modes.label: Flapping two ear-like fins • Hovering above the mud • Swallowing prey entire

waveform.description: A gentle continuous swell with no floor and no peak, because there is nothing in this environment to react to.

entries.closingLine: Because every process is slow, continuous and shaped by an environment that never changes, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Dung Beetle

modes.label: Cutting a ball from a fresh dung pat within minutes of it falling • Rolling it away backwards while navigating by the sky • Burying it before any of the competitors arriving at the pat can take it

waveform.description: A brisk repetitive pattern of similar efforts, because rolling is continuous physical work at a steady rate.

entries.closingLine: Since rolling is continuous work, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Dusky Dolphin
entries.archetype: Leaping to Bring Others to the Ball

waveform.description: A working herding rhythm interleaved with sharp leaping peaks.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: coordinated herding and a loud signalling behaviour that supports it.

entries.name: Dusky Gopher Frog

modes.label: Sheltered • Borrowed • Most of the year

waveform.description: A long underground trough with one raised section — the year's activity compressed into the weeks after rain.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal runs a long sheltered state and a brief aggregated one and requires both, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Dusky Leaf Monkey

waveform.description: A shallow, slow, almost unvarying rhythm across the day.

entries.closingLine: The cost is a diet that releases energy slowly, which is why the days are long, still and quiet: a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Dusky Lory

modes.label: Flocks of hundreds and occasionally thousands moving together between flowering trees • The whole group arriving, stripping a tree of blossom and leaving together rather than dispersing • Individuals gaining nothing by staying behind because a stripped tree offers nothing and the next is found collectively

waveform.description: A repeating pattern of mass arrivals and departures, because the flock moves as a unit between concentrated resources.

entries.closingLine: Because arrivals and departures recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Dusky Pademelon

waveform.description: A cautious repeating rhythm of coming out and going back in.

entries.closingLine: Repeated short excursions from cover makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Dwarf Caiman

waveform.description: A flat submerged line broken twice by a movement that goes fully.

entries.closingLine: A long cheap wait paying for one committed snap makes this a bimodal system, low-frequency in the water and high-frequency at the strike.

entries.name: Dwarf Cassowary

waveform.description: Two steady foraging periods over broken ground — a routine set by where fruit has fallen rather than by any event.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts steady walking and continuous modest intake into dispersal, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eared Dove

modes.label: Colonies forming in dense scrub where nests are packed at extraordinary density across large areas • Millions of birds breeding within a single colony, with several nests in a single bush • Predators present in numbers but taking a small fraction, because the total is far beyond what any of them can consume

waveform.description: A single enormous seasonal event, because the whole colony forms, breeds and disperses together.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Earless Monitor Lizard

waveform.description: A nearly motionless line — one of the slowest lizards there is, doing very little very deliberately.

entries.closingLine: Because nothing about the animal happens at any speed, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Earwig

modes.label: Laying a clutch in a chamber under cover • Turning and licking each egg repeatedly through weeks of incubation • Guarding the young through their first instar

waveform.description: A long steady low line with a single small rise, because the work is continuous, unspectacular and sustained over weeks.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs once a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: East African Oryx

modes.label: Storing heat by day • Grazing • Dumping it at night

waveform.description: A slow rise across the day and a slow fall overnight.

entries.closingLine: Conservative and reserve-based, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Bettong

waveform.description: A busy, evenly distributed night of digging and carrying, with no dominant event and a clean drop at dawn.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole night is spent on steady digging and upkeep rather than on reserves or bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Box Turtle

waveform.description: A long, slow foraging baseline broken by one abrupt closure.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a slow, long-lived foraging routine punctuated by brief, complete closure.

entries.name: Eastern Boxelder Bug

modes.label: Feeding on seed • Scattered across the tree • Breeding through summer
Packed into a wall cavity • Reproduction shut down • Months without feeding

waveform.description: A busy feeding rhythm falling away to a long flat shelf, because the winter state has no activity in it at all.

entries.closingLine: Because a dispersed feeding season and a hormonally distinct aggregated winter are both necessary and neither is a version of the other, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Eastern Chipmunk

modes.label: Filling pouches • Carrying • Stacking one chamber
Torpid • Cooled to the burrow • Waking to eat

waveform.description: A working rhythm that falls to a deep floor and then ticks upward at intervals, because the animal keeps waking inside its own dormancy.

entries.closingLine: Because a season of accumulation and a season of metered drawdown are each indispensable to the other, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Eastern Collared Lizard

waveform.description: A long warming watch with one short violent sprint raised out of it.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long low-cost basking watch and a brief, temperature-limited burst.

entries.name: Eastern Cottontail

waveform.description: A long still line breaking into a short series of sharp turns.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: near-total stillness and a short, sharp, pre-mapped run.

entries.name: Eastern Emerald Elysia

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing continuous but modest energy use from stored chloroplasts, with no sharp bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole design favors slow acquisition, internal storage, and gentle ongoing use of a borrowed energy system, Elysia chlorotica operates as a single, strongly low-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Glass Lizard

waveform.description: A steady gliding search rhythm with one sharp discontinuity in it.

entries.closingLine: Continuous low searching through cover makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Gray Squirrel

modes.label: Burying one nut per hole • Faking caches when watched • Recovering by memory and smell

waveform.description: A rapid repeating rhythm of identical small efforts, because the whole strategy is one action performed thousands of times.

entries.closingLine: Since the caching and recovery run continuously at one tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Indigo Snake

waveform.description: A sustained searching rhythm across the day — an active hunter rather than an ambusher.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts continuous searching effort into a steady return, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Lesser Bamboo Lemur
entries.archetype: Living on the Grass Other Primates Refuse

waveform.description: Long flat stretches of feeding and rest broken by short twilight bursts of group movement through the stems.

entries.closingLine: The system is therefore bimodal, dominated by slow processing and rest, with a smaller mode of vertical clinging and leaping through upright stems around dawn and dusk.

entries.name: Eastern Lubber Grasshopper

modes.label: Walking rather than flying or jumping, on wings too small to use • Advertising with bright yellow, red and black • Hissing, spreading the wings and producing a foul froth from the thorax when handled

waveform.description: A slow even line with a broad raised event, because the animal moves very little and the display is sustained when it happens.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Newt
entries.archetype: A Land Stage Between Two Water Stages

waveform.description: A long low terrestrial floor stepping up to a sustained aquatic level.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: two genuinely different bodies, each suited to a medium the other could not use.

entries.name: Eastern Phoebe

modes.label: Watching from a low exposed perch • Launching to take an insect in the air • Returning to the same perch and pumping the tail

waveform.description: A metronomic run of identical short excursions, because every sally is the same length and returns to the same point.

entries.closingLine: Since sallies recur within seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Quoll

waveform.description: Many modest captures spread evenly across the dark hours — a night of small finds rather than a hunt.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from many small finds repeated nightly, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Rat Snake

modes.label: Wedging against bark • Gripping with belly scales • Reaching nests nothing else can
Balled underground with others • Metabolism at a fraction • Months without moving

waveform.description: A climbing season lifted out of a long flat winter floor, because the brumating months register nothing at all.

entries.closingLine: Since a climbing season and a physiologically suppressed winter are both obligatory and neither is a slowed version of the other, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Eastern Red-backed Salamander

waveform.description: A very low steady line with minimal variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: small, slow and defined entirely by a constraint.

entries.name: Eastern Screech Owl

waveform.description: Busy night hunting at each end, with a long, quiet daytime roost between.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: concealed daytime roosting and night-time perch-and-pounce hunting.

entries.name: Eastern Spiny Lizard

modes.label: Carrying brilliant blue patches on the belly and throat that are invisible from above • Doing push-ups on a rock to flash them sideways and downward • Being a mottled grey-brown animal the rest of the time

waveform.description: A calm line broken by sharp bursts, because the displays are short and repeated against an otherwise still background.

entries.closingLine: Since displays recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Tiger Swallowtail

modes.label: Passing as a dropping • Swelling into eyespots • Everting a forked gland

waveform.description: A rising rhythm whose peaks climb through the trace, because each stage of the animal is larger and louder than the last.

entries.closingLine: Because the feeding and growing run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eastern Yellowjacket

modes.label: A single mated queen emerging from hibernation in spring and building the first cells and raising the first workers entirely alone
A colony of thousands of workers expanding rapidly through summer, then producing new queens and males and dying entirely at the first hard frost

waveform.description: A completely flat solitary line that breaks into a violent oscillation and then stops dead, because the two phases are different systems and the end is abrupt.

entries.closingLine: The two states are structurally different systems rather than stages of one, separated by a threshold the colony crosses, so it operates as a phase-change system.

entries.name: Eciton Army Ant

waveform.description: A flat low segment for bivouac rest, a sharp rise into a high, uneven plateau for the raid, then a drop back to low as the colony re-forms its bivouac.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system alternates between a compact, protective low-output bivouac and a high-output, high-mobility raid, the Eciton army ant is a bimodal system with a low-frequency rest core and a defining high-frequency marching appetite.

entries.name: Eclectus Parrot

modes.label: Female at the hollow • Male ranging • Both running at once

waveform.description: Two separate traces running at once, one almost flat and one rolling, because the system is a division rather than an alternation.

entries.closingLine: Because the provisioning and the guarding proceed together through most of the year, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Edible-nest Swiftlet

modes.label: Producing thick salivary secretion from enlarged glands during the breeding season • Drawing it out in strands against a vertical cave wall • Letting it harden into a shelf of cemented saliva with nothing else in it

waveform.description: A steady repeated rhythm of similar small efforts, because the nest is built from many identical strands over weeks.

entries.closingLine: Since building continues over weeks, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Egyptian Cobra

waveform.description: A ranging hunting rhythm with the body rising at intervals.

entries.closingLine: Continuous wide-ranging hunting makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Egyptian Fruit Bat

waveform.description: Evenly spaced mid-height pulses showing repeated bouts of coordinated calling and movement across a night of foraging.

entries.closingLine: That pattern makes them a mid-frequency system: steady, coordinated activity maintained by regular communication pulses through the active period.

entries.name: Egyptian Goose

modes.label: Locating an occupied nest in a tree hole, a cliff ledge or another bird's stick nest • Driving out the residents by direct attack • Laying and raising a brood in the site without building anything

waveform.description: A working rhythm broken by regular decisive events, because ordinary activity is punctuated by takeovers and fights.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Egyptian Grasshopper

modes.label: Sitting still on bark and stems with vertically striped eyes • Having the dark pseudopupil broken up by those stripes • Feeding on foliage at a slow deliberate pace without gathering into swarms

waveform.description: A very flat unvarying line with one small rise, because the animal moves slowly and almost nothing about it changes.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Egyptian Mongoose
entries.archetype: Feint, Dodge and a Toxin-Blind Receptor

waveform.description: Steady daytime foraging through cover broken by two brief, sharp confrontations.

entries.closingLine: The result is a bimodal system: steady foraging through cover and short, explosive confrontations when prey fights back.

entries.name: Egyptian Plover

waveform.description: A mostly mid-level, gently undulating line with occasional sharp dips upward representing brief, high-intensity bursts of movement and protection emerging from steady vigilance.

entries.closingLine: Because their structure is built around a steady, shared watch punctuated by short, decisive reactions, the Egyptian Plover operates as a bimodal system with a mid-frequency cooperative vigilance mode and a high-frequency reactive burst mode.

entries.name: Egyptian Tortoise
entries.archetype: Small Enough to Shelter Under a Shrub

waveform.description: A flat summer line with one sustained rise through the cool rainy season.

entries.closingLine: The system switches between a low sheltering phase and a productive rainy-season phase.

entries.name: Electric Catfish

modes.label: Lying still in murky water • Spending almost nothing • Waiting
One command • Every cell at once • A stunned fish

waveform.description: A long flat baseline broken by two very tall narrow spikes.

entries.closingLine: That is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Electric Eel

modes.label: Low pulses running continuously • Reading the field • Breathing air
A pair of high-voltage pulses • Involuntary twitch • The volley

waveform.description: A low continuous ripple with occasional enormous spikes.

entries.closingLine: That is a bimodal system: constant quiet sensing, and very brief enormous output.

entries.name: Elephant Beetle

waveform.description: Heavy slow activity punctuated by sustained maximum-force pushing.

entries.closingLine: A fixed body, a short season and contests decided by pushing make this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Elephantnose Fish
entries.archetype: Reading Distortions in a Self-Made Field

waveform.description: Low daytime pulsing rises into a sustained night of active sensing, then settles again at dawn.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: active nocturnal electrolocation and a quieter daytime rest in which the field is never switched off.

entries.name: Elf Owl

waveform.description: A low baseline with evenly spaced, moderate peaks, showing long anchored shelter periods punctuated by regular foraging flights.

entries.closingLine: This makes the Elf Owl a bimodal system with a low-frequency shelter mode and a mid-frequency nocturnal hunting mode built around precise use of tiny refuges.

entries.name: Elk
entries.archetype: A Whistle From a Body That Size

waveform.description: An even herd rhythm broken by a sustained high-pitched passage.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady herd life and a short exhausting vocal contest.

entries.name: Elongated Tortoise

waveform.description: Months near the baseline with one broad seasonal lift — activity follows the rain rather than the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal moves slowly and is active for only part of the year, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Emerald Cockroach Wasp
entries.archetype: Two Stings, the Second Into the Brain

waveform.description: A searching line broken by two sharp precisely placed events.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: unremarkable searching and two surgically exact interventions.

entries.name: Emerald Moth

modes.label: A green produced by a pigment in the wing scales rather than by structure, unlike most green in insects • That pigment chemically unstable, breaking down with exposure to light and with time after death • Museum specimens fading to yellow, cream or white within years, so the preserved animal no longer matches the living one

waveform.description: A steady line drifting downward, because the colour declines continuously from the moment the animal dies.

entries.closingLine: Because the fading runs over years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Emerald Toucanet
entries.archetype: A Bill That Works as a Radiator

modes.label: Working canopy fruit • Reaching from a perch • Dumping heat through the bill

waveform.description: A steady canopy foraging rhythm through the day.

entries.closingLine: This is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Emerald Tree Boa

waveform.description: Long horizontal rest interrupted by two downward-launched spikes — the shape of an animal that does nothing and then does everything.

entries.closingLine: Because near-zero maintenance alternates with brief total commitment, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Emerald Tree Skink

waveform.description: An active daytime rhythm sustained on vertical surfaces.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: active, exposed and sociable within a vertical space.

entries.name: Emperor Goose
entries.archetype: A Pair Working the Bering Tideline

waveform.description: A tidal feeding rhythm that flattens into a long still nesting stretch.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a tide-timed coastal feeding routine and a still, concealed breeding phase.

entries.name: Emperor Newt

waveform.description: A near-flat line — an animal that relies on being left alone rather than on doing anything.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Emperor Penguin

waveform.description: A regular mid-frequency wave representing continuous rotation and coordinated burden sharing.

entries.closingLine: That makes the emperor penguin a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, collective and organized around rotating risk.

entries.name: Emperor Scorpion

modes.label: Waiting in a burrow • Grasping • Rarely stinging

waveform.description: An almost motionless trace across a long slow life.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Emperor Tamarin

waveform.description: A steady coordinated group rhythm with constant small exchanges.

entries.closingLine: Continuous coordinated group operation makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Emu

waveform.description: A steady travelling rhythm dropping to a long still floor.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: continuous travelling and a long stationary fast.

entries.name: Epaulette Shark

waveform.description: A low tolerant line with small slow variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, tolerant and built to persist through what cannot be escaped.

entries.name: Ethiopian Wolf

waveform.description: Steady daily solitary foraging on a shared territory.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady daily solitary foraging inside a collectively defended patch of one very particular habitat.

entries.name: Eupterote Fabia Moth

waveform.description: A long, low band of activity for larval and pupal growth that rises sharply into a short, higher adult reproductive burst near the end.

entries.closingLine: Because the organism uses one long, low-intensity growth-and-build phase and one short, high-intensity dispersal-and-reproduce phase, its life history forms a bimodal system built around a decisive stage change.

entries.name: Eupterote Moth

modes.label: Larvae covered in dense fine hairs that are brittle and detach at the slightest contact • Those hairs barbed and hollow, carrying irritant compounds, and small enough to be carried on air • Contact producing intense itching and dermatitis in people and predators alike, hours after the encounter

waveform.description: A slow seasonal build and decline, because larval populations rise and fall over a generation.

entries.closingLine: Because outbreaks run seasonally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Bittern

waveform.description: An almost unbroken low line — an animal whose main activity is standing still in a posture that costs nothing.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on stillness and short close-range commitments, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Blackcap

modes.label: Inheriting a compass bearing rather than a route • Departing on that bearing at a genetically set time • Producing offspring that take the parents' direction

waveform.description: A working rhythm broken twice a year by sustained departures, because migration is a seasonal event inside an otherwise steady life.

entries.closingLine: Since departures and song bouts recur seasonally within a steady life, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Bullfinch

modes.label: Working along a branch stripping dormant buds • Taking hundreds a day through late winter • Switching to ash keys and seeds when those are available

waveform.description: A steady deliberate rhythm of similar small actions, because the bird works along a branch taking one bud after another.

entries.closingLine: Since bud-taking recurs constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Collared Dove

waveform.description: A steady unremarkable rhythm that simply never stops through most of the year.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, unspectacular and built on continuous reliable intake rather than on any decisive capability.

entries.name: Eurasian Eagle-Owl

waveform.description: A long resident watch broken by one heavy strike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long cheap resident watch and a brief, unusually powerful strike.

entries.name: Eurasian Harvest Mouse
entries.archetype: A Fifth Grip in the Stalk Zone

waveform.description: Activity climbs with the grass through summer and drops to a low ground-level phase in winter.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-change system: a climbing season above ground and a sheltered winter beneath the stalks.

entries.name: Eurasian Jay

waveform.description: An intense autumn burst settling into a long low winter line.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a short intense storing phase and a long patient retrieval one.

entries.name: Eurasian Lynx
entries.archetype: Guarding a Kill That Lasts Days

modes.label: Stalking • One large kill • Several days at the carcass

waveform.description: Long quiet stretches with occasional short hunting events.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Magpie

modes.label: Investigating a reflection as though it were another bird • Noticing a mark on its own throat in the mirror • Scratching at the mark on its body rather than at the glass

waveform.description: An irregular exploratory pattern with varied excursions, because the animal is investigating rather than repeating a fixed routine.

entries.closingLine: Since investigative bouts recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Oystercatcher

waveform.description: Even, repeating mid-height taps representing rhythmic, tide-synced shell-opening strikes.

entries.closingLine: That tide-linked, tool-using routine makes them a mid-frequency system: steady, rhythmic, and built around repeated skilled actions instead of extremes of conservation or explosive bursts.

entries.name: Eurasian Reed Warbler

modes.label: Weaving a deep cup slung between standing reed stems • Inspecting the clutch and comparing eggs against each other • Ejecting an egg that does not match, and reacting to a cuckoo at the nest by mobbing

waveform.description: A working rhythm broken by sharp decisive events, because ordinary nest activity is punctuated by rejection episodes.

entries.closingLine: Since nest inspections recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Sparrowhawk

modes.label: Females up to twice the mass of males • The male taking tits and finches, the female taking thrushes and pigeons • A pair working prey ranges that barely overlap

waveform.description: A watchful line broken by extremely brief full-depth strikes, because the bird waits concealed and attacks in a rush.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes recur through the day, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Spoonbill
entries.archetype: A Paddle That Moves Water, Not Mud

waveform.description: A regular sweeping rhythm at a constant rate.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: a steady sweep sampling water rather than searching it.

entries.name: Eurasian Tree Sparrow
entries.archetype: A Colony in Other People's Holes

waveform.description: A steady sociable rhythm sustained through the year.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, social and entirely dependent on structure it did not build.

entries.name: Eurasian Wolf

modes.label: Howling as a chorus at territorial boundaries • Being answered or not from kilometres away • Adjusting movement to avoid the neighbours that answered

waveform.description: A long quiet baseline interrupted by broad sustained events, because the chorus is infrequent but carries for a long time when it happens.

entries.closingLine: Since chorus events recur across weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Eurasian Woodcock

waveform.description: A low, almost flat line with small gentle ripples, showing long periods of stillness with tiny, repeated probing actions.

entries.closingLine: This combination of cryptic stillness and fine-grained sensing makes the woodcock a low-frequency system: slow, patient, and built around repeated, subtle probing from a hidden position.

entries.name: European Badger

waveform.description: A very steady low line with slight regular variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, cumulative and structural.

entries.name: European Bee-eater

waveform.description: Long low stretches of perch-based waiting punctuated by brief, sharp spikes of aerial snatch flights before returning to baseline.

entries.closingLine: This makes their system a bimodal pattern: a low-frequency, perch-and-burrow anchored waiting mode, and a high-frequency, short-burst aerial snatch mode that only activates when food and safety briefly overlap.

entries.name: European Chub

modes.label: Taking anything from insects to fruit to small fish at the surface or the bed • Crushing it with paired pharyngeal teeth in the throat • Holding station in current behind cover

waveform.description: An irregular pattern of varied excursions, because the fish takes very different items and each one demands something different.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding events recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European Eel
entries.archetype: Decades Inland, One Unseen Ocean Crossing

waveform.description: A long, flat, low line of inland years ending in a sustained ocean migration.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a long, patient growth phase ended by a single oceanic migration, it is a phase-change system.

entries.name: European Field Cricket

modes.label: A burrow dug into short turf with a widened flared entrance and a cleared platform in front of it • The male singing from that platform rather than from open ground • The flared opening coupling the sound to the air far more efficiently, so the same wing movement carries considerably further

waveform.description: A regular insistent rhythm, because the male sings in sustained chirps for long periods from a fixed place.

entries.closingLine: Because the song cycles many times a second, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European Flounder

modes.label: Lying on soft bottom in estuaries and coastal shallows • Regulating internal salt concentration actively as the water changes • Moving far upriver into fresh water and back to the sea to spawn

waveform.description: A slow steady rhythm following a tidal rather than a rapid cycle, because the animal's movements track the water.

entries.closingLine: Since movements follow the tide, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European Goldfinch
entries.archetype: Tweezer Bill in a Thistle Head

waveform.description: A steady picking rhythm of many small extractions.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, precise and repeated many times over for small returns.

entries.name: European Greenfinch
entries.archetype: A Bill That Cracks Hard Seed

modes.label: Holding a hard seed in a groove in the palate • Applying jaw force from unusually large adductor muscles • Splitting the husk and extracting the kernel

waveform.description: A steady deliberate rhythm of similar efforts, because each seed takes comparable work and they are dealt with one at a time.

entries.closingLine: Since seeds are handled continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European Hedgehog
entries.archetype: A Drawstring Muscle Round the Whole Body

waveform.description: A low foraging line rising abruptly into a held closed state.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: unbothered noisy foraging and a complete mechanical closure.

entries.name: European Hornet

modes.label: One mated queen • Overwintering in a crevice • Starting the comb alone
Several hundred workers • Hunting past dusk • Defending a cavity nest

waveform.description: A flat floor swelling into one broad season and collapsing back, because the colony is assembled from nothing each year and does not survive the winter.

entries.closingLine: Because a solitary founding state and a large hunting colony are both indispensable and neither reduces to the other, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: European Lobster

modes.label: Holding prey with a slender toothed cutter • Breaking shells with a heavy blunt crusher • Losing and regrowing either across successive moults

waveform.description: A long steady line with occasional modest rises, because the animal is slow and the moult events are rare.

entries.closingLine: Since moults are a year or more apart, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: European Mole Cricket
entries.archetype: A Burrow Shaped Into a Horn

waveform.description: A long low line of underground digging rising into a sustained evening song, then sinking back into the soil.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: slow subterranean tunnelling and a sustained evening calling phase.

entries.name: European Nightjar

waveform.description: Long flat stretches of low activity with a series of moderate, evenly spaced night-time rises representing repeated foraging sallies from still ground cover.

entries.closingLine: Because survival depends on this alternation between cryptic day stillness and rhythmic night hunting from cover, the nightjar is best understood as a bimodal system with a low-frequency hiding mode and a mid-frequency foraging mode.

entries.name: European Perch

modes.label: Holding station among reed stems and submerged branches • Carrying dark vertical bars that match the vegetation • Darting out when a small fish passes and returning to cover

waveform.description: Steady holding broken by sharp brief dashes, because the fish waits in cover and attacks in short bursts.

entries.closingLine: Since dashes recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European Plaice

waveform.description: A low, gently wavering line showing a mostly flat, low-activity pattern with small shifts rather than sharp bursts.

entries.closingLine: This architecture makes the plaice a low-frequency system: energy is spent slowly, movement is modest and close to the bottom, and the core strategy is continuous, patient camouflage rather than repeated high bursts or large-scale shifts.

entries.name: European Pond Terrapin

waveform.description: Activity drops into a long, low trough during retreat, then rises slightly as the animal recovers while still sheltered.

entries.closingLine: Because the main response to overwhelm is to withdraw, reduce output and stretch limited resources over time, its operating rhythm is a single low-frequency mode built around retreat and patient recharge.

entries.name: European Rabbit

modes.label: Out on the sward • Cropping fast • Ears turning
Underground • Passing it twice • Extracting the rest

waveform.description: A deep underground floor lifted twice into short raised blocks at either end of the day, because the exposed part is deliberately brief.

entries.closingLine: Because a brief exposed intake phase is paired with a long protected processing phase, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: European Rhinoceros Beetle

modes.label: Curled in decaying heartwood • Fermenting what it chews • Years before it surfaces

waveform.description: A near-flat line across the whole span, because a life measured in years of chewing has nothing in it that registers as an event.

entries.closingLine: Since the years that matter run at the pace of microbial digestion, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: European Robin

waveform.description: Regular song bursts on a steady baseline, repeated through the whole year.

entries.closingLine: That makes the robin a mid-frequency system, rhythmic and continuous, where the output is advertisement rather than force.

entries.name: European Roller

waveform.description: A working baseline broken by short, deliberate display tumbles.

entries.closingLine: Hunting is a steady perch-and-drop cycle over large ground insects, and that continuous working rhythm makes it a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European Serin

waveform.description: Repeated mid-height weaving loops that settle into a stable cup.

entries.closingLine: When local fibres are wrong—too stiff, too sparse, too wet—the weave fails because the system assumes proximate materials can be worked into a holding geometry through steady mid effort.

entries.name: European Spider Crab

modes.label: Walking the seabed alone through most of the year • Feeding on molluscs, echinoderms and algae • Carrying a spined carapace that is hard and adequate
Gathering into mounds of hundreds of animals • Moulting inside the heap while soft and defenceless • Relying on the bodies of the others for protection until the shell hardens

waveform.description: Even solitary activity giving way to a long flat depressed section, because the animal alternates between ordinary life and a state in which it can do nothing.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, a soft aggregated animal and a hard solitary one are two states, making this a bimodal system.

entries.name: European Spiny Lobster

modes.label: Occupying a particular cave or crevice on rocky ground • Foraging out and returning to the same shelter • Holding that site for years and remaining findable in it

waveform.description: A very steady line with small regular excursions, because a long-lived animal on a fixed site has a remarkably uniform life.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: European Starling

modes.label: Driving the closed bill into turf • Forcing it open against the soil • Looking down into the gap with forward-rotated eyes

waveform.description: A dense regular sequence of identical strikes, because the bird repeats the same probe over and over as it works across the ground.

entries.closingLine: Since probes repeat continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European Stick Insect

waveform.description: A low, almost flat line with tiny undulations, showing long stretches of near-stillness with only minimal adjustments.

entries.closingLine: Because its core survival pattern is extended, low-output stillness that blends into a stable background, this is a low-frequency system anchored in branch-like, enduring quiet.

entries.name: European Stonechat

modes.label: Holding a territory through the winter rather than migrating • Beginning to breed weeks before migrants arrive • Fitting in two or three broods before the season closes

waveform.description: A brisk repeated pattern of short excursions, because the bird hunts in the same quick drops all day and all year.

entries.closingLine: Since hunting drops recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: European Storm Petrel

waveform.description: Even, small ripples around a mid-level line, showing continuous fluttering passes with light, repeated surface contacts.

entries.closingLine: Because their whole system is built around ongoing, rhythmic interaction with the stormy surface—neither slow hoarding nor explosive bursts—the European Storm Petrel is a mid-frequency, steady-operations animal.

entries.name: European Sturgeon

modes.label: A species that once spawned in rivers from the Baltic to the Black Sea • A single naturally reproducing population remaining in the Gironde and Garonne • Every reintroduction elsewhere drawn from stock originating in that one catchment

waveform.description: A long steady decline flattening at the bottom, because a continental collapse ended in one surviving remnant.

entries.closingLine: Because the timescale runs across decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: European Wildcat

modes.label: A wild population overlapping everywhere with free-ranging domestic and feral cats • Hybridisation producing fertile offspring that backcross freely in both directions • Wild genomes progressively diluted, so animals that look and behave like wildcats increasingly carry domestic ancestry

waveform.description: A steady line drifting upward without any crisis, because the change is gradual and shows no sharp event.

entries.closingLine: Because the dilution runs across generations, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Evergreen Bagworm Moth

waveform.description: A low, gently rising line showing steady, small expenditures over time as the case is slowly built and used.

entries.closingLine: This architecture makes the system slow, conservative and reuse-focused: energy goes into one shelter that doubles as armor and camouflage, and action is timed to moments when food and cover overlap, which produces a distinctly low-frequency, case-worn patience strategy.

entries.name: Eyelash Viper
entries.archetype: Gold Morph Mistaken for a Flower

modes.label: Coiled on a branch • Waiting • One strike

waveform.description: Near-total stillness for days at a time on a single perch.

entries.closingLine: Stillness on one branch for days makes this a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Fallow Deer

waveform.description: An even grazing rhythm rising into a short sustained high block.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long low-contest grazing year and a short, total, self-consuming rut.

entries.name: False Gharial

waveform.description: Long flat waiting with two small lifts — the snap is brief and shallow against a baseline of stillness.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is rare and waiting is the default, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: False Killer Whale
entries.archetype: Spread-Out Hunters That Share the Catch

waveform.description: Wide, steady searching broken by fast chases and shared kills.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: MID spread-out travel and HIGH chases with shared prey.

entries.name: False Water Cobra
entries.archetype: A Hood Spread the Wrong Way

waveform.description: An active hunting rhythm broken by a broad flattened display.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: continuous active hunting and a broad flattened threat display with something behind it.

entries.name: Fan-horned Beetle

modes.label: Antennal segments extended into long lateral branches that fan out into a comb • Receptor cells distributed across that whole expanded surface rather than on a simple filament • A few molecules of female pheromone in a large volume of air intercepted because the sampled area is enormous relative to the insect

waveform.description: A rapid continuous sampling rhythm, because the antennae are being swept through the air constantly during search.

entries.closingLine: Because sampling is continuous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Fanaloka

waveform.description: A soft even nightly search with no spikes and no long pauses.

entries.closingLine: Continuous nightly searching makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Fat-tailed Dunnart
entries.archetype: Tiny Hunter Banking Fat in the Tail

waveform.description: Night hunting at a steady level dropping into a long daytime torpor trough.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: nightly hunting and bouts of daily torpor.

entries.name: Fat-tailed Dwarf Lemur

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing consistently reduced, steady activity and slow reserve use across the season.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is built around dense storage, low waste and long, quiet stretches of survival between pulses of intake, the fat-tailed dwarf lemur is a single-mode, strongly low-frequency system.

entries.name: Featherfin Cichlid

waveform.description: Even, medium-height ripples showing repeated bouts of sand-circle building and display with brief recoveries in between.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a mid-frequency system built around rhythmic, ongoing sand-circle maintenance and display.

entries.name: Feathertail Glider
entries.archetype: Feather-Vane Steering on a Tiny Glide

waveform.description: A busy foraging line punctuated by short, sharp glide launches between trees.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: busy nocturnal foraging among flowers and short, steered glides between trees.

entries.name: Fennec Fox

waveform.description: A flat daytime line with one gentle night-time rise: activity shifted into the cool hours.

entries.closingLine: That makes the fennec fox a low-frequency system: quiet, thrifty and organised around avoided cost rather than raw output.

entries.name: Fiddler Crab

modes.label: Emerging as the water drops • Waving one enormous claw • Plugging the burrow before it returns

waveform.description: Two raised working windows separated by flat troughs, because the animal's day is set by the water rather than by the light.

entries.closingLine: Since that window repeats on every tide, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Fieldfare

modes.label: Nesting in loose colonies rather than alone • Rising together at an approaching predator • Striking it with accurately aimed droppings

waveform.description: A social baseline broken by intense collective events, because ordinary activity gives way to whole-colony responses.

entries.closingLine: Since colony responses recur through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Fiji Banded Iguana
entries.archetype: A Green Leaf-Eater Still in the Canopy

waveform.description: A nearly flat line of slow canopy feeding and basking, with small lifts for display.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is built on stillness and slow feeding, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Fin Whale
entries.archetype: Pleated Throat Behind a Racing Hull

waveform.description: A steady cruising line broken by sharp spikes of lunge feeding at prey patches.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: sustained streamlined cruising and brief, explosive engulfment.

entries.name: Finch-billed Myna

modes.label: A short stout finch-like bill used to excavate holes in soft dead standing timber • Hundreds of pairs cutting nest chambers into the same trunk until it is honeycombed from base to crown • The whole colony breeding inside a single dead tree rather than spread across the forest

waveform.description: A concentrated seasonal build and decline, because the whole colony works to the same schedule.

entries.closingLine: Because breeding is seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Finlayson's Squirrel

waveform.description: A gently oscillating mid-level line showing repeated bouts of daytime foraging and vigilance without extreme peaks or deep troughs.

entries.closingLine: That produces a mid-frequency system: a steady, rhythmic pattern of activity and vigilance where appearance can vary widely while the core daily operating rhythm remains consistent and useful.

entries.name: Fire Salamander

waveform.description: An unvarying slow walk with nothing raised or lowered in it.

entries.closingLine: Slow movement, long life and no need for speed make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Fire-maned Bowerbird

waveform.description: Even mid-height undulations showing regular cycles of bower maintenance and display, without extreme peaks or long flat pauses.

entries.closingLine: That pattern of ongoing, crafted attraction makes the fire-maned bowerbird a mid-frequency system built on regular cycles of building, editing and showing.

entries.name: Fire-tufted Barbet

modes.label: A call consisting of a rising buzzing trill that closely resembles the sound of a cicada rather than of a bird • That call delivered from high in the canopy where the bird itself is invisible among leaves • Listeners including rivals, mates and observers frequently mistaking it for an insect, so the bird is present and unremarked

waveform.description: A rapid buzzing rhythm with little variation, because the call is a sustained trill rather than a phrase.

entries.closingLine: Because the call is a sustained trill, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Firebug

modes.label: Developing through nymphal stages under hormonal control • Requiring juvenile hormone to fall before the final moult to adult • Being stopped at that point by a compound in North American paper that mimics it

waveform.description: A slow line with periodic broad depressions, because moults are the structure of the animal's year.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Firefly

modes.label: Males flying and emitting flashes of a species-specific duration, interval and pattern • Females answering from the vegetation after a precise delay unique to their species • The exchange continuing only while both sides keep the timing, so the code itself is the species barrier

waveform.description: A precisely regular series of identical pulses, because the whole signal is carried in exact timing.

entries.closingLine: Because the exchange repeats through the evening, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Firefly Squid

waveform.description: A regular daily up-and-down rhythm ending in one bright spawning peak, then collapse.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: nightly vertical migration and a single mass spawning.

entries.name: Fischer's Lovebird
entries.archetype: A Domed Nest in a Hole

modes.label: Carrying strips of bark and grass to a tree cavity in the bill • Weaving a roofed nest with a side entrance inside it • Filling a cavity that other parrots would simply lay in

waveform.description: A quiet line rising into a sustained building period and subsiding, because the construction is days of work once a year.

entries.closingLine: Since nest building is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Fisher
entries.archetype: Attacking a Porcupine From the Front

waveform.description: An active ranging rhythm broken by a repeated attacking sequence.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: wide opportunistic ranging and a specific repeated attack sequence.

entries.name: Fishing Cat

waveform.description: Long flat watching broken by two very narrow spikes — the catch is over before the ripples have settled.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal fails without either of them, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Flamboyant Cuttlefish

waveform.description: A steady walking-and-hunting baseline broken by a sharp spike of colour display.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: slow benthic hunting and sudden conspicuous display.

entries.name: Flame Bowerbird

waveform.description: A low baseline of shelter and foraging with evenly spaced moderate rises, showing repeated returns to a prepared display site rather than continuous high activity.

entries.closingLine: The system therefore alternates between a quieter, shelter-and-feeding mode and a structured, rhythmic display mode built around a specific location, making it a bimodal pattern with low-frequency conservation anchored by a mid-frequency, site-focused arrangement and performance rhythm.

entries.name: Flamed Tigersnail

modes.label: Rasping lichen, fungi and decaying leaves from bark and litter • Gliding on a mucus trail • Working only while the air stays damp
Withdrawing into the shell • Sealing the aperture with a dried mucus epiphragm • Suspending metabolism until moisture returns

waveform.description: Active undulation alternating with long flat depressed stretches, because the animal genuinely alternates between working and being sealed shut.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, a sealed animal with suspended metabolism and no exchange with its surroundings is a different architecture rather than rest within one, which makes this a bimodal system with a low-frequency dormant state.

entries.name: Flamingo Tongue Snail

waveform.description: A gently undulating midline showing steady, repeating activity as the snail moves and feeds while keeping its warning mantle visible.

entries.closingLine: Because the same feeding act both gathers chemical defenses and powers a continuous visual warning, the snail runs as a steady, mid-frequency system: it must keep moving, grazing and displaying rather than alternating between long dormancy and rare bursts.

entries.name: Flashlight Fish

waveform.description: Even mid-height blinking pulses for routine movement, interrupted by a brief, sharper low dip representing a sudden blackout or spike in light control under threat.

entries.closingLine: This makes their system bimodal: a mid-frequency, rhythmic blink cycle that runs most of the time, and a high-frequency, sharply switched light-control mode that is triggered by immediate opportunity or danger.

entries.name: Flat Porcelain Crab
entries.archetype: Fans Out When the Tide Comes In

waveform.description: Two tidal cycles: filtering peaks while submerged and flat, still troughs while the rock is exposed.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: rhythmic filtering while submerged and still sheltering while exposed.

entries.name: Flat-backed Millipede

waveform.description: A mostly flat, low line with small bumps showing minor defensive expenditures against ongoing low-level threats.

entries.closingLine: Because their whole system is built to endure frequent minor challenges through persistent, low-cost protection rather than rapid bursts, flat-backed millipedes are a single-mode, low-frequency defence system.

entries.name: Flat-headed Cat
entries.archetype: Flattened Skull Built for the Waterline

waveform.description: Active at night along the water, with a long daytime lull.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady nocturnal hunting along the waterline.

entries.name: Flat-nosed Pit Viper

modes.label: Selecting a perch on a low branch or a trail edge where prey passes • Holding the same coiled position for days or weeks without feeding • Returning to that identical site after each excursion rather than searching new ground

waveform.description: An almost completely flat line with one small break, because the snake holds position for weeks and strikes very occasionally.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Flathead Catfish

modes.label: Holding station in cover under logs, undercut banks and rock through the day • Hunting live fish at night by ambush rather than searching for carrion or scent trails • Taking only moving prey, so bait that works for every other catfish does not work for this one

waveform.description: A flat daytime line rising into a single nocturnal hunting period, because the animal is inactive by day.

entries.closingLine: Because hunting is nightly and prey is large, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Flathead Grey Mullet

modes.label: Taking mouthfuls of sediment, algae and detritus from the bottom rather than hunting anything • Grinding it in a thick muscular pyloric stomach that works like a bird's gizzard • Passing it through a gut several times the body length to extract nutrition from very poor material

waveform.description: A steady continuous rhythm of feeding passes, because the fish grazes the bottom without pause.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Florida Scrub-Jay

waveform.description: A steady family working line with a long, lower autumn and winter caching phase.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: steady cooperative territory life and a slower caching and recovery phase.

entries.name: Flower Crab Spider

modes.label: Sitting motionless on a flower head with front legs held open • Secreting or withdrawing a yellow pigment over days to match white or yellow petals • Seizing bees and hoverflies far larger than itself

waveform.description: A long almost featureless line with a single brief disturbance, because the animal is motionless for days and the strike is the only event.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a season, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Flower Hat Jelly
entries.archetype: Glowing Tentacle Tips Luring Small Fish

waveform.description: Near-constant hovering with occasional small peaks when prey is caught.

entries.closingLine: Its hovering, luring routine makes it a SINGLE LOW system.

entries.name: Flower Wasp

modes.label: A female burrowing through soil in search of a scarab beetle larva • Stinging it where it lies to paralyse it permanently • Building a small cell around the grub in the soil and laying an egg on it there rather than moving it

waveform.description: A flat surface line with deliberate descents, because the wasp feeds above ground and works below it in episodes.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs seasonally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Flowerhorn Cichlid

modes.label: Holding and patrolling a space • Displaying a fluid-filled forehead mass laterally at anything approaching • Settling contests by size rather than by fighting

waveform.description: A continuous pattern of sharp display events at a similar level, because the animal challenges repeatedly and nothing resolves permanently.

entries.closingLine: Since displays recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Flying Dragon
entries.archetype: Wing Held in Its Own Hands

modes.label: Climbing the trunk • Launching • Landing on the next one

waveform.description: A repeating climb-and-descend pattern with no ground contact.

entries.closingLine: Steady daily foraging and crossing makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Flying Gurnard

waveform.description: Mostly low, steady activity along the bottom with a single sharp, narrow spike representing a rapid fin-flare event before returning to seafloor calm.

entries.closingLine: The system therefore runs on a low-frequency, shelter-led baseline punctuated by short, high-frequency startle displays that only appear when risk or opportunity peaks, making this a bimodal pattern.

entries.name: Forest Wagtail

modes.label: A tail swung from side to side in a horizontal arc rather than pumped up and down • That movement maintained almost continuously while the bird walks on the forest floor • Insects flushed from leaf litter by the disturbance and taken as they move

waveform.description: A regular unbroken lateral rhythm, because the movement continues without pause while the bird forages.

entries.closingLine: Because the movement is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Fork-tailed Drongo
entries.archetype: False Alarms That Make Others Drop Food

waveform.description: Steady perch-and-sally foraging punctuated by sudden sharp thefts.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady sentinel foraging and brief bursts of theft.

entries.name: Fossa

waveform.description: Repeated pursuit efforts of similar magnitude — hunting that involves genuine chases rather than single strikes.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts sustained three-dimensional pursuit into regular returns, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Four-horned Antelope

waveform.description: A repeating out-and-back rhythm through the day — the animal never ranges far, and it always returns.

entries.closingLine: Since the pattern is a steady daily circuit rather than rare bursts or long dormancy, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Four-lined Whiptail Lizard

modes.label: Moving almost continuously through vegetation and litter rather than waiting on a perch • Flicking the tongue repeatedly to collect molecules and deliver them to the vomeronasal organ • Locating hidden and buried prey by chemical trace rather than by seeing it move

waveform.description: A fast unbroken high-frequency rhythm, because the animal is moving and sampling almost constantly.

entries.closingLine: Because the sampling is nearly continuous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Fowler's Toad

modes.label: Two toad species overlapping in range, breeding in the same ponds and fully capable of producing fertile hybrids • Males giving distinctly different calls, a short nasal scream in one and a long musical trill in the other • Females responding to their own species' call and not the other, so the boundary between two species rests on an acoustic preference and nothing else

waveform.description: A single concentrated breeding season, because the whole interaction happens during a few weeks of calling.

entries.closingLine: Because breeding is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Fox Squirrel

modes.label: Handling each acorn and assessing it • Eating the ones that germinate quickly and will be worthless by winter • Burying the ones whose dormancy lets them keep

waveform.description: A rapid repeated rhythm of similar actions, because each nut is handled individually at a constant pace.

entries.closingLine: Since nuts are handled continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Foxface Rabbitfish

modes.label: A clean bright yellow body with a sharply marked black and white face, held while actively grazing in daylight
A mottled dark brown and blotchy pattern assumed within seconds at night or under threat, breaking the outline against reef structure

waveform.description: A bright active rhythm collapsing into a subdued flat one, because the fish changes state entirely between day and night.

entries.closingLine: Aquarists who see the change at lights-out routinely think the fish is sick, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Francois' Langur
