waveform.description: A day that rises from and returns to the same low point — the cave at either end of it.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle repeats steadily every day, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: French Angelfish
entries.archetype: A Paired Sponge Grazer Holding Reef Ground

waveform.description: A steady grazing line punctuated by sharp spikes of territorial chasing.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady paired grazing with bursts of territorial defence.

entries.name: Freshwater Angelfish

modes.label: A body compressed into a thin disc with greatly extended dorsal and anal fins • That shape allowing movement between vertical stems and roots that a deep-bodied fish cannot pass • Dark vertical bars continuing the lines of the surrounding stems so the outline disappears among them

waveform.description: A slow steady rhythm, because the fish hovers and moves deliberately rather than swimming quickly.

entries.closingLine: Because movement is continuous but unhurried, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Freshwater Butterflyfish

waveform.description: A held line disturbed only twice by something arriving overhead.

entries.closingLine: Minimal expenditure, a single occupied layer and long quiet waits make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Freshwater Crab

modes.label: Large yolk-rich eggs carried by the female rather than released into the water • The whole larval sequence completed inside the egg rather than in the plankton • Young hatching as miniature crabs able to walk and feed immediately, with no marine phase at all

waveform.description: A single slow annual swell, because the whole reproductive investment is carried and released once.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Freshwater Crayfish

modes.label: A giant interneuron running the length of the nerve cord carrying a single impulse • That impulse firing the abdominal flexor muscles together in a few thousandths of a second • The tail snapping under the body and driving the animal backwards away from the stimulus

waveform.description: A jittery baseline punctuated by violent instantaneous spikes, because the response is all-or-nothing and extremely fast.

entries.closingLine: Because the response is near-instantaneous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Freshwater Pearl Mussel
entries.archetype: A Riverbed Life Borrowed From Salmon Gills

waveform.description: A long, level adult life interrupted by one sharp pulse of larval release and host attachment.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-change system: a brief mass larval release onto host fish and a very long filtering adult life.

entries.name: Frilled Lizard
entries.archetype: The Jaw That Opens the Frill

waveform.description: Ordinary foraging punctuated by two instant flares.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: ordinary cryptic foraging with a single coupled action standing between it and everything else.

entries.name: Frilled Shark

waveform.description: A long flat low line of waiting, one sharp narrow spike of activity for the lunge, then a return to the low baseline.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is built around long, quiet waiting punctuated by brief, decisive strikes, the frilled shark operates as a bimodal low–high frequency hunter rather than a continuous chaser.

entries.name: Fruit Bat
entries.archetype: Night Flights That Replant the Forest

waveform.description: A long, quiet daytime hang giving way to a sustained night of foraging flight.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: nightly foraging flights and daytime hanging rest.

entries.name: Fruit Fly

modes.label: Salivary gland cells replicating their DNA repeatedly without dividing, so each chromosome becomes a bundle of a thousand aligned copies • Those giant chromosomes showing a fixed pattern of dark and light bands, each band a reproducible landmark along the DNA • Deletions, inversions and duplications visible directly as missing or reversed bands under an ordinary microscope

waveform.description: A rapid regular cycle repeated without variation, because generations turn over in about ten days indefinitely.

entries.closingLine: Because generations turn over in days, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Gaboon Viper

waveform.description: An exceptionally flat floor with a single vertical event — the proportion of stillness to action is the profile itself.

entries.closingLine: Because near-total stillness supports a single overwhelming commitment, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Galah

modes.label: Paired inside the flock • Preening each other • Returning to the same hollow

waveform.description: A lively even chatter of similar peaks, because the social contact is constant rather than occasional.

entries.closingLine: Because that contact is continuous through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Galapagos Hawk

waveform.description: Long watching periods from perches broken by short drops onto prey.

entries.closingLine: Because the system combines long watching from perches with brief drops onto prey, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Galapagos Penguin
entries.archetype: A Cold-Current Diver Hiding from Equatorial Sun

waveform.description: Daytime fishing in cool water, with hot hours and nights spent resting ashore.

entries.closingLine: Because the system alternates between fishing in cool water and managing heat on land, it is bimodal.

entries.name: Galápagos Sea Lion

modes.label: Hauling out on rock and sand directly on the equator • Holding flippers up to the air and lying in shade, surf or wet sand • Returning to cold upwelled water to shed heat when nothing else works

waveform.description: A steady moderate rhythm without extremes, because the animal alternates continuously between resting and cooling.

entries.closingLine: Since cooling behaviour recurs through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Galápagos Tortoise

waveform.description: An almost flat low line: a body that changes its output very little from day to day.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a strongly low-frequency system: heavy, economical and built for a time horizon measured in decades.

entries.name: Garden Warbler

modes.label: Laying down fat before departure • Becoming restless at night for a number of weeks that matches the journey • Stopping when the internal programme runs out rather than when the destination is reached

waveform.description: A quiet line rising into a sustained elevated period twice and returning, because migration is a long programmed state rather than an event.

entries.closingLine: Since the whole cycle runs once a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Gargoyle Gecko

waveform.description: A near-static nocturnal pattern with slow careful steps in it.

entries.closingLine: Minimal expenditure and patient climbing make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Garibaldi Fish

waveform.description: A steady mid-height waveform with small regular oscillations, representing continuous patrolling and frequent local responses rather than long quiet stretches or extreme bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because the system relies on ongoing, rhythmic activity and continuous visual signaling rather than long dormancy or rare explosive efforts, it operates as a mid-frequency pattern built around persistent territorial display and defense.

entries.name: Gaur

waveform.description: A heavy low line with slow shallow movement.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, heavy and defended by scale rather than by behaviour.

entries.name: Gee's Golden Langur
entries.archetype: Fermenting Leaves Within a River-Bound Range

waveform.description: Morning and afternoon feeding separated by a long midday rest.

entries.closingLine: A slow, digestion-paced routine makes it a SINGLE LOW system.

entries.name: Gelada
entries.archetype: A Hand That Plucks One Blade

modes.label: Seated on the grass • Plucking • Shuffling forward

waveform.description: An almost completely flat trace of continuous low-yield feeding.

entries.closingLine: All of this is one low-value food taken in enormous numbers of small identical actions, so this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Gemsbok

waveform.description: A slow daily rise and fall with nothing sharp anywhere in it.

entries.closingLine: Minimal water use and unhurried movement make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Gentoo Penguin
entries.archetype: A Waddle That Is Actually Efficient

waveform.description: Slow deliberate colony work broken by bursts of real speed.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: slow deliberate work ashore and short bursts of genuine speed below the surface.

entries.name: Geoffroy's Cat
entries.archetype: Small Enough to Live on Rodents

waveform.description: A steady repeated hunting rhythm through the night.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: repeated small captures rather than rare large ones.

entries.name: Geography Cone Snail

waveform.description: A low, almost flat line with tiny ripples, showing long, quiet periods of minimal movement and occasional small bursts when a precise strike occurs.

entries.closingLine: This creates a low-frequency system built around infrequent but highly structured, precise venom use from a largely stationary ambush platform.

entries.name: Geometer Moth

modes.label: Gripping a stem with the rear prolegs only, since the middle pairs are absent • Holding the entire body out rigid at an angle with no support at the front • Maintaining that posture for hours with silk sometimes anchoring the head end

waveform.description: An almost entirely flat line, because the animal holds one position for hours at a time and moves rarely.

entries.closingLine: Because the posture is held for long periods, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Geometric Tortoise

waveform.description: A very low line with one modest seasonal lift — activity appears briefly with the winter rains and subsides.

entries.closingLine: Because everything about the animal runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Gerenuk

waveform.description: Repeated rises to a similar height, each one a standing bout — a rhythm made of postures rather than journeys.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts a sustained posture into steady exclusive access, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: German Yellowjacket

waveform.description: A season-long climb in activity that ends abruptly rather than tapering.

entries.closingLine: Continuous building and provisioning makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ghost Ant

modes.label: Many queens distributed across many small nests rather than one queen in one place • New nests founded by a group simply walking away with a queen rather than by a mating flight • Disturbance or poisoning causing the colony to fragment further, so treatment multiplies the number of nests rather than removing them

waveform.description: A continuous busy rhythm with no dominant period, because many small nests operate independently and simultaneously.

entries.closingLine: Because the network operates continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ghost Mantis

modes.label: Hanging motionless among dry foliage with an irregular leaf-shaped body • Swaying gently as though in a breeze • Striking anything that comes within reach of the forelegs

waveform.description: A long motionless line broken by isolated full-depth strikes, because the animal does nothing at all between very brief attacks.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes are rare and the cycle runs across months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant African Land Snail

modes.label: Growing a shell up to twenty centimetres long • Rasping calcium from render, mortar, bones and other snails' shells as well as plants • Requiring a supply of calcium that vegetation alone cannot provide

waveform.description: A slow steady line with small regular excursions, because a large snail feeds continuously at an unvarying pace.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant African Millipede

waveform.description: A very low, almost featureless line.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, continuous and chemical rather than fast.

entries.name: Giant Anteater

waveform.description: Dozens of short identical visits across a day, each one brief — the shape of a system that never empties any single source.

entries.closingLine: Because value accumulates from many brief repeated visits, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Armadillo

waveform.description: A long quiet baseline with one modest lift — a night's work is a single excavation, not a series of efforts.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal feeds rarely and spends most of its time underground at very low cost, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Asian Mantis

modes.label: Rows of spines along the femur and tibia of each foreleg, offset so they interlock when the limb closes • The tibia snapping back against the femur so the prey is caught between two rows of opposed spines • The whole strike completed in a few hundredths of a second, before the prey can begin to respond

waveform.description: A long motionless line broken by extremely brief strikes, because the animal is still and then instantaneous.

entries.closingLine: Because the strike is measured in hundredths of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Barrel Sponge

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing steady, continuous filtration with only minor variation over time.

entries.closingLine: Because their whole biology is built around anchored, low-waste, long-horizon filtration of whatever flows past, the giant barrel sponge is a strongly low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Burrowing Cockroach

waveform.description: Long low underground processing interrupted by sharp surface haul spikes.

entries.closingLine: Failure appears when litter cannot be found or when the burrow climate collapses, because the animal has no alternate high-tempo foraging strategy once the cellar fails.

entries.name: Giant Burrowing Mayfly

waveform.description: A very long flat floor ending in one narrow burst.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a very long accumulation and a single unrepeatable expenditure.

entries.name: Giant Clam

waveform.description: One slow daily arc following the sun — the only rhythm in the animal's entire life.

entries.closingLine: Because growth is assembled from a continuous low-intensity input over a very long life, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Day Gecko

modes.label: A large diurnal gecko feeding on nectar and soft fruit as well as insects • Pollen picked up on the snout and throat while the animal pushes into a flower to lick nectar • That pollen carried to the next flower, so several Madagascan plants depend on a lizard rather than on an insect or a bird

waveform.description: A single daily activity arc, because the animal is diurnal and follows the sun through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because activity is daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Dead Leaf Mantis

waveform.description: A long flat low line of stillness with one narrow sharp dip upward to high activity for the strike, then an immediate return to flat stillness.

entries.closingLine: That makes the dead leaf mantis a bimodal system with a dominant low-frequency camouflage mode and a triggered high-frequency strike mode.

entries.name: Giant Eland

waveform.description: Two broad browsing plateaus divided by a midday trough, on the long slow gradient of an animal that walks between them.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts continuous movement and steady browsing into a very large body, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Forest Hog
entries.archetype: A Grazing Pig That Rarely Digs

waveform.description: A long flat daytime rest in cover rising into a night of grazing out in the glades.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: communal daytime lying-up in cover and nightly grazing out in the openings.

entries.name: Giant Forest Scorpion
entries.archetype: A Shell That May Detect Light

modes.label: Waiting in a burrow • Grasping • Emerging only in real darkness

waveform.description: An extremely slow trace with almost no variation.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Freshwater Prawn

modes.label: Staying small and fast • Sneaking matings under the dominant male • Growing quietly
Growing rapidly • Carrying orange claws • Waiting for the position above to open
Carrying long blue claws • Holding a territory • Guarding moulting females

waveform.description: A stepped profile that climbs and falls back, because a male moves up through discrete forms rather than growing smoothly.

entries.closingLine: The forms also turn over at different rates, a small male moulting and growing quickly where a blue-claw male holds one position for a season, which is why this is an adaptive system running three states rather than one rhythm.

entries.name: Giant Freshwater Stingray

waveform.description: A nearly unbroken flat trace with one shallow lift — feeding involves settling rather than striking.

entries.closingLine: Because a body of this size feeds by remaining still and spends almost nothing between meals, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Golden Orb-weaver

modes.label: Dragline silk spun from proteins that crystallise into stiff regions embedded in a flexible matrix • That combination giving high tensile strength together with the ability to stretch far before breaking • A web of it absorbing the full kinetic energy of a large flying insect without snapping or throwing the prey back out

waveform.description: A long building effort followed by a settled watch, because the web takes time to construct and then simply waits.

entries.closingLine: Because the web is rebuilt over days, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Gourami

modes.label: A chamber above the gills filled with thin bony plates folded into a maze and covered in respiratory tissue • Air gulped at the surface held in that chamber where the enormous folded surface absorbs oxygen • The fish surviving in stagnant water and rice paddies where dissolved oxygen is close to nothing

waveform.description: A steady repeating rhythm of surfacing, because the fish must return to the air at regular intervals.

entries.closingLine: Because surfacing recurs constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Grouper

waveform.description: A long hovering floor with one vertical event — the capture has no approach phase at all.

entries.closingLine: Because an almost costless hovering baseline supports a single instantaneous capture, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Giant Hatchetfish

modes.label: Hanging in the twilight zone • Sides reflecting the water • Belly lights matched to the surface

waveform.description: A quiet suspended drift with almost no variation, because an animal whose defence is not being seen does not move in ways that would give it away.

entries.closingLine: Since the hovering and watching run without interruption in a place that has no day or season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Huntsman Spider

waveform.description: Dense, repeating sharp peaks showing constant high-alert microbursts as the spider patrols and reacts across a wide surface.

entries.closingLine: Because its hunting and safety both depend on continuous scanning and rapid movement rather than stored traps or deep reserves, its system runs as a single, high-frequency pattern of ongoing readiness and quick microbursts of action.

entries.name: Giant Ibis

waveform.description: A dispersed low half-year rising into a concentrated one — the same birds at two very different densities.

entries.closingLine: Because it needs both the dispersed wet season and the concentrated dry one, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Giant Isopod

waveform.description: An almost flat floor with two barely perceptible rises — the profile of an animal whose year usually contains no events at all.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system converts extreme patience into survival on rare enormous meals, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Kangaroo Rat

waveform.description: A gently undulating low line showing steady, modest activity anchored around conserved underground stores.

entries.closingLine: That pattern of conserving resources in place, spending cautiously, and relying on built-up stores over time makes the giant kangaroo rat a low-frequency, reserve-led system.

entries.name: Giant Katydid
entries.archetype: Green Wings Veined Like a Leaf

waveform.description: A still green daytime line rising into a night of feeding among the same leaves.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: daytime leaf masquerade and nocturnal feeding.

entries.name: Giant Leaf-tailed Gecko

waveform.description: An almost unbroken floor with the smallest nocturnal excursions — an animal whose main activity is being unfindable.

entries.closingLine: Because concealment replaces both flight and defence, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Malabar Squirrel

waveform.description: A repeated leaping rhythm between levels.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuously active in three dimensions and confined to one layer.

entries.name: Giant Malaysian Katydid

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing long periods of quiet, continuous camouflage with only minor adjustments.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: a steady, concealment-led presence that relies on continuous camouflage rather than short, explosive actions.

entries.name: Giant Malaysian Leaf Insect

waveform.description: A low, gently wavy line showing long periods of near-stillness with tiny rhythmic motions that echo leaf movement.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is organized around sustained, low-output concealment that quietly tracks the background’s colour and rhythm, this insect is a low-frequency operator.

entries.name: Giant Otter
entries.archetype: A Family That Hunts as One Animal

waveform.description: Dense continuous high-rate group activity.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: loud, continuous and collectively powered.

entries.name: Giant Pacific Octopus

waveform.description: Many overlapping small actions with no single dominant rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Continuous exploratory work makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Panda

waveform.description: A long shallow line with almost no variation — twelve hours of the same low-grade work, every day of the year.

entries.closingLine: Because a low-quality input is converted by sheer duration rather than by effort, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Redeye

modes.label: A palm leaf cut and rolled into a tube fastened with silk, occupied by a single large larva • The inside and the larva itself coated in a white waxy powder secreted by the caterpillar • That powder keeping the interior dry and non-adhesive so frass and moisture do not accumulate against the animal

waveform.description: A slow build and decline over the larval period, because the whole system runs once through development.

entries.closingLine: Because development runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Scoliid Wasp

modes.label: A larva developing on a single scarab grub and receiving no more than that one grub contains • Adult body size therefore determined by the mass of the host it was laid on • The species reaching enormous size because its hosts are the largest scarab larvae in the forest

waveform.description: A single seasonal cycle of search and development, because everything happens once per generation.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is generational, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Squid

waveform.description: Long, low, steady activity in darkness with a single sharp, narrow spike representing a rapid reaching strike before returning to quiet drift.

entries.closingLine: This makes the giant squid a bimodal system with a low-frequency conceal-and-drift baseline and a high-frequency strike-and-grip burst mode that defines how it feeds, avoids danger and places its young in the dark ocean.

entries.name: Giant Stick Katydid

waveform.description: A long flat line of daytime stillness, then a modest rise of slow night-time feeding.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: daytime stillness as a twig and slow nocturnal feeding.

entries.name: Giant Stonefly

waveform.description: A very low steady line with almost no variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: still, clinging and entirely dependent on the condition of the water around it.

entries.name: Giant Trevally

waveform.description: Level patrolling torn open by charges that reach the top of the frame.

entries.closingLine: Total brief commitment between long patrols makes this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Tube Worm

waveform.description: A low, steady line with tiny undulation, showing continuous, rooted, slow energy intake with minimal fluctuation.

entries.closingLine: Because energy capture, protection, and life history are all built around long-term attachment to a narrow vent zone and steady chemical processing, this is a strongly low-frequency system: dense, rooted, conservative and designed to keep going as long as the vent does.

entries.name: Giant Water Bug

waveform.description: Long motionless waiting broken by instantaneous strikes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long still hold at almost no cost, and a brief total commitment the digestion completes afterwards.

entries.name: Giant Waxy Monkey Frog

waveform.description: A near-motionless baseline with a few small deliberate interruptions — the wiping routine and the slow climb, nothing else.

entries.closingLine: Because the system spends almost nothing and buys its freedom with structure rather than activity, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giant Whip Scorpion

modes.label: Paired glands at the base of the abdomen producing a concentrated mixture of acetic and caprylic acid • A short movable turret at the rear that can be swivelled to point in any direction • The spray directed accurately at a specific attacker rather than released in all directions

waveform.description: A flat nocturnal line with isolated sharp discharges, because the animal walks quietly and fires only when attacked.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are rare, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Gidgee Skink
entries.archetype: The Same Crack Held for Generations

waveform.description: A settled group rhythm rising abruptly into a held defensive state.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a settled social baseline and a wedged defensive posture.

entries.name: Gila Monster

waveform.description: Long buried flatlines broken by two slow, rounded feeding events — the rises are gradual, never sharp.

entries.closingLine: Because the entire system is arranged around storage, long dormancy and rare large returns, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Giraffe

modes.label: Browsing above the line • Threading thorns • Lowering the head carefully

waveform.description: A steady elevated line cut by three sharp full-depth drops, because the only violent thing this animal does is lower its head.

entries.closingLine: Because the feeding is unhurried, near-constant and spread across day and night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Giraffe Weevil

waveform.description: A sequence of small identical working strokes climbing gradually — the rhythm of a fold being made one crease at a time.

entries.closingLine: Because the system turns steady daily folding into a small number of well-protected offspring, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Glass Catfish

modes.label: Hanging at an angle in midwater in a tight shoal • Transmitting light through a body with no scales and almost no pigment • Producing flashes of colour as muscle fibres diffract the light passing through

waveform.description: An even unremarkable rhythm, because the animal hovers and adjusts continuously without abrupt events.

entries.closingLine: Since movement is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Glass Octopus

waveform.description: An almost flat line: continuous, passive concealment with nothing to punctuate it.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: continuous, passive concealment in water that offers none.

entries.name: Glasswing Butterfly

waveform.description: An even unhurried drift with no spikes to catch the eye.

entries.closingLine: It stays in motion in shaded forest all day rather than freezing, which makes this a mid-frequency system that is hard to resolve precisely while it keeps flying.

entries.name: Glaucus Marginatus
entries.archetype: Upside-Down Drifter Armed by Its Prey

waveform.description: A flat line of drifting broken by a brief rise when floating prey is met.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: passive floating in the surface film and feeding on the stinging colonies met there.

entries.name: Globular Springtail

waveform.description: Long stretches of low, steady activity with a single sharp spike representing a rapid furcula-powered escape jump, then an immediate return to the low baseline.

entries.closingLine: This architecture creates a bimodal system: a low-frequency, hidden foraging and reset mode built around safety in place, and a high-frequency, very brief release mode where stored mechanical energy is spent in one explosive escape.

entries.name: Glossy Ibis
entries.archetype: Following the Flood, Not the Map

waveform.description: A steady travelling rhythm with regular stops.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: mobile, flocked and continuously relocating.

entries.name: Goblin Shark

waveform.description: A near-flat deep drift broken by two extremely narrow spikes — the strike occupies a tiny fraction of the animal's time.

entries.closingLine: Because both states are essential and neither can be removed, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Goffin's Cockatoo

modes.label: Working at a problem with no species-typical solution • Producing a tool from whatever material is available • Making a different tool for each part of a task when one will not do

waveform.description: An irregular exploratory pattern with varied excursions, because the animal is solving rather than repeating.

entries.closingLine: Since problem-solving bouts recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Goitered Gazelle

waveform.description: Two long grazing periods at the cool ends of the day — an even rhythm with no spikes, because the escape is rare.

entries.closingLine: Because a steady watchful routine maintains the margin that keeps the animal alive, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Gold Tail Moth

modes.label: A dense tuft of golden hairs at the tip of the female's abdomen, retained from the larval stage • Those hairs brushed off deliberately onto the egg mass after laying, covering it completely • Anything attempting to reach the eggs meeting the same urticating hairs that protected the caterpillar, so the defence is transferred rather than regrown

waveform.description: A single seasonal cycle, because the transfer happens once at laying and the protection then stands.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Golden Eagle

waveform.description: Long shallow soaring broken by two committed plunges.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long cheap observing state and a short irreversible spending of stored height.

entries.name: Golden Hamster

waveform.description: Long flat rest underground broken by two short collecting runs above ground.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: brief collecting runs above ground and a long, sheltered life below it.

entries.name: Golden Jackal

waveform.description: A steady patrolling rhythm with no large peaks or troughs.

entries.closingLine: That makes the jackal a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, continuous and defined by the breadth of what it can convert into a meal.

entries.name: Golden Lancehead

waveform.description: A long quiet baseline with occasional modest lifts — the snake feeds rarely, and only when birds are passing.

entries.closingLine: Because it feeds only when birds pass and otherwise spends almost nothing, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Golden Lion Tamarin

waveform.description: A busy even family rhythm through the day — many small coordinated actions rather than any single event.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on continuous shared effort, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Golden Mantella

modes.label: Dispersed • Litter • Most of the year

waveform.description: A quiet year with one short raised section — everything reproductive compressed into a few weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal runs a dispersed low state and a brief aggregated breeding one and needs both, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Golden Pheasant

waveform.description: A quiet ground rhythm with regular bright display events raised out of it.

entries.closingLine: That makes the pheasant a mid-frequency system: a steady foraging rhythm carrying a permanent, repeatedly used signal.

entries.name: Golden Poison Frog

waveform.description: A steady daytime rhythm of short foraging moves — the animal never needs a burst because it never needs to escape.

entries.closingLine: Since the system runs as steady daytime collecting and advertising rather than in bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Golden Silk Orb-weaver
entries.archetype: A Web Left Standing for Weeks

waveform.description: A low patient line with almost no variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: patient, fixed and paid for once.

entries.name: Golden Snub-nosed Monkey

waveform.description: An active seasonal rhythm that flattens and settles into a low winter floor, then holds there — two states joined by a slope, not a switch.

entries.closingLine: Because context genuinely selects between two different operating states, this is an adaptive system.

entries.name: Golden Tortoise Beetle

modes.label: Reflecting gold from a fluid-filled multilayer cuticle • Draining the layers when disturbed • Turning red as the mirror collapses

waveform.description: Two stable levels with rapid transitions between them, because the colour is either mirrored or not and does not sit between.

entries.closingLine: Since the change occurs within minutes, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Golden-fronted Bowerbird

waveform.description: Even rolling waves showing recurring bouts of bower building and display separated by moderate lulls.

entries.closingLine: Because their biology centers on repeated, coordinated effort around a fixed display rather than on long dormancy or explosive bursts, the golden-fronted bowerbird is best understood as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Golden-headed Lion Tamarin

waveform.description: A quick repeating probe rhythm — many small searches through the day rather than any single effort.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging is a steady repeated daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Goldfish

modes.label: Working the bottom • Sifting sediment • Learning where food appears
Under ice for months • No oxygen available • Converting lactate to alcohol

waveform.description: An active season lifted out of a long flat winter floor, because the cold state produces nothing that registers.

entries.closingLine: Since both are indispensable and neither is a slowed version of the other, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Goliath Beetle

waveform.description: Heavy laboured activity with brief maximum-output episodes in it.

entries.closingLine: A fixed body, a short season and high output make this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Goliath Birdeater

waveform.description: A long flat floor with small disturbances — an animal that spends almost nothing and reacts rather than acts.

entries.closingLine: Because a very low-cost body relies on deterrence rather than activity, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Goliath Frog

waveform.description: A steady rhythm of repeated heavy effort — each lift is one stone moved, and the nest takes many of them.

entries.closingLine: Because the building and guarding run as a steady seasonal cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Goliath Tigerfish

waveform.description: Repeated full-height spikes with almost no floor between them — a system that lives near its maximum rather than visiting it.

entries.closingLine: Because the architecture is organised around power, turbulence and brief violent opportunity, it is a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Goodfellow's Tree-kangaroo

waveform.description: A slow deliberate arboreal pace with no hopping rhythm in it.

entries.closingLine: Unhurried movement on low-value leaves makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Goose Barnacle

modes.label: Attaching by the front of the head and secreting cement • Combing plankton from the water with feathery legs • Travelling wherever the object it settled on goes

waveform.description: A rapid even rhythm sustained without variation, because the feeding legs sweep continuously whenever the animal is submerged.

entries.closingLine: Since the legs sweep many times a minute, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Gopher Tortoise

waveform.description: A low steady line with two shallow surface excursions — most of the animal's life happens below the trace.

entries.closingLine: Because a long structural investment supports a very low-cost life, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Gouldian Finch

waveform.description: A quick even flocking rhythm — many small movements between seed heads and water through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding and flocking run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Grass Moth

waveform.description: Mostly flat low activity with two small, brief rises for short flights between long periods of stem shelter.

entries.closingLine: This produces a low-frequency system: long, quiet intervals of stem shelter punctuated by brief, necessary repositioning.

entries.name: Grasshopper & Locust

modes.label: Living solitary, green or brown, avoiding others • Moving little and breeding locally • Being a grasshopper nobody notices
Turning yellow and black with enlarged flight muscle and a different brain chemistry • Actively seeking others rather than avoiding them • Marching as bands and flying as swarms across continents

waveform.description: Two clearly different levels with rapid transitions between them, because the change is a switch rather than a gradient.

entries.closingLine: Because the two states are switched by density and the animal can move between them, this runs as an adaptive system.

entries.name: Gray Angelfish

modes.label: A small black juvenile with bright yellow bars, holding a cleaning station and picking parasites from larger fish that come to it
A large grey adult feeding on sponges, tunicates and algae across the reef, ignored by and ignoring the fish it once cleaned

waveform.description: A rapid high-amplitude early rhythm flattening into a slow shallow one, because an interactive juvenile becomes a solitary adult.

entries.closingLine: That is not a refinement of the same strategy but a change of trophic architecture: from a mutualist whose living depends on other animals choosing to come, to a specialist grazer whose living depends on chemistry, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Gray Four-eyed Opossum

waveform.description: A busy nightly rhythm of many small separate attempts.

entries.closingLine: Nothing here is a specialised defence; the marks are one cheap addition to a life of many small chances taken every night, which makes it a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Gray Fox
entries.archetype: A Dog That Goes Up the Tree

waveform.description: A steady active rhythm moving between levels.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steadily active across ground and canopy both.

entries.name: Gray Whale

modes.label: Rolling onto one side on shallow Arctic bottom • Sucking mouthfuls of sediment in and straining them through short coarse baleen • Leaving pits in the seafloor and plumes of mud behind

waveform.description: A slow steady line with broad regular dips, because each feeding dive is a prolonged event at an unhurried pace.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Gray Wolf

modes.label: Trotting • Approaching • Letting most of them go

waveform.description: A long even travelling rhythm punctuated twice by narrow spikes, most of the trace being movement that leads to nothing.

entries.closingLine: Because a long economical assessment phase funds a rare and hazardous commitment, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Gray's Leaf Insect

modes.label: Eggs dropped to the forest floor with a hard sculptured shell that resembles a plant seed • A fleshy structure on the shell corresponding to the elaiosome of an ant-dispersed seed • Ants carrying the eggs into their nests, eating that structure and discarding the intact egg in the refuse chamber, where it develops underground and protected

waveform.description: A slow seasonal cycle, because eggs are dropped over months and develop underground over further months.

entries.closingLine: Because development runs over months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Grayling

modes.label: Holding station low on clean gravel in fast water • Raising an outsized dorsal fin into the flow • Using it to brace, to turn and to display in the spawning season

waveform.description: A steady moderate rhythm without large events, because the fish holds position continuously and adjusts constantly.

entries.closingLine: Since station-holding adjustments are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Argus

waveform.description: Repeated display bouts of consistent height with court maintenance between them — attendance rather than a single performance.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on continuous preparation and repeated daily performance, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Blue Heron

waveform.description: A long motionless line broken by one extremely fast extension.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an extremely cheap loaded wait and a single instantaneous release.

entries.name: Great Blue Turaco
entries.archetype: Copper Pigment, Not Trick Of Light

waveform.description: A bounding, branch-to-branch rhythm rather than sustained flight.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daily foraging and travel make this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Cormorant
entries.archetype: One Long Dive at a Time

waveform.description: Long deep excursions with brief recoveries between them.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: sustained deep work in long repeated efforts.

entries.name: Great Crested Grebe

modes.label: Head-shaking face to face • Diving for weed and rising breast to breast • Repeating the whole sequence through the season

waveform.description: Paired rises that build toward a central maximum and fall away, because the sequence escalates through stages and then subsides.

entries.closingLine: Since ceremonies recur through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Crow

modes.label: Adults feeding at withered plants to take up pyrrolizidine alkaloids they cannot synthesise • Storing those compounds in the body so that the butterfly is unpalatable to birds • Converting part of the same supply into the courtship pheromone released from extrusible hairpencils

waveform.description: A slow even drift, because the butterfly moves unhurriedly and accumulates its chemistry over time.

entries.closingLine: Because acquisition runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Curassow

waveform.description: Low booming sequences at first light and again at dusk, with a long quiet foraging stretch between them.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on a repeated daily broadcast and steady walking foraging, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Eggfly

modes.label: A bacterium inherited through the egg that kills male embryos, leaving populations almost entirely female • A suppressor gene appearing that blocks the killing without removing the bacterium • That gene sweeping through the population within about ten generations as any male carrying it leaves enormous numbers of offspring

waveform.description: A long flat depressed line that rises sharply and then levels, because the recovery happened abruptly after a long suppression.

entries.closingLine: Because generations run over months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Egret

waveform.description: A slow measured walking rhythm at a low level.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, deliberate and economical.

entries.name: Great Frigatebird

waveform.description: A long shallow climb-and-glide cycle with no real expenditure in it.

entries.closingLine: Almost no expenditure, decades of life and very slow breeding make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Gray Owl

waveform.description: Long still stretches cut twice by a very narrow committed drop.

entries.closingLine: That pairing makes it a bimodal system, a low-frequency listening hold paying for a high-frequency plunge.

entries.name: Great Green Bush-cricket

modes.label: A row of fine teeth on the underside of one forewing forming a file • A hardened scraper on the edge of the other wing drawn across those teeth as the wings close • Each tooth producing a click, and a thin membrane on the wing resonating to amplify the train of clicks into a continuous song

waveform.description: A very rapid regular oscillation, because each tooth strike produces one pulse and the rate is fixed by the mechanism.

entries.closingLine: Because the mechanism cycles thousands of times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Hornbill

waveform.description: A relentless even rhythm of delivery flights — the whole breeding season is one repeated trip made hundreds of times.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on a constant repeated delivery cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Horned Owl

waveform.description: A long still perched line broken by one heavy strike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an extremely cheap listening watch and a rare, decisive strike.

entries.name: Great Kiskadee

waveform.description: Regular short sallies from a held position, repeated through the day.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and repeatable, built on holding a visible vantage point and converting whatever comes past.

entries.name: Great Mormon

modes.label: Wearing a tailed, red-bodied, white-patched pattern • Copying a distasteful Pachliopta swallowtail • Protected only where birds have learned that model
Wearing the plain dark tailless pattern shared with the males • Copying nothing • Relying on size, speed and forest shade

waveform.description: Two clearly separated stable levels joined by a single transition, because an individual is one form or the other with nothing between.

entries.closingLine: The two strategies also work on different timescales, one needing a season of predator learning and the other acting within a single encounter, which makes this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Great Plains Toad

modes.label: Hardened keratinised tubercles on the heel of each hind foot working as blades • The animal shuffling backwards into loose soil rather than digging forwards with the hands • Descending until it is well below the dry surface layer and remaining there for months

waveform.description: A long buried flat line with one abrupt surge, because the animal spends most of the year underground and emerges in a burst.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Potoo

waveform.description: A long motionless daytime line followed by a band of short night strikes.

entries.closingLine: A full day of motionless imitation and a night of short committed strikes make this a bimodal system, a low-frequency hold beside a high-frequency hunt.

entries.name: Great Skua

waveform.description: A patrolling line with sharp interceptions cut into it repeatedly.

entries.closingLine: Continuous patrol and interception makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Great Tinamou

waveform.description: A mostly low, flat line with a few evenly spaced, modest rises, showing long periods of quiet cryptic presence punctuated by occasional vocal pulses.

entries.closingLine: This combination of persistent low-motion concealment with periodic, moderate vocal signalling makes the system bimodal: a dominant low-frequency cryptic mode, with a structured mid-frequency acoustic channel layered on top.

entries.name: Great Tit

modes.label: Approaching novel objects quickly or slowly depending on individual temperament • Passing that tendency to offspring • Being favoured or penalised depending on how hard the year is

waveform.description: A varied pattern whose excursions differ in depth from one to the next, because individuals differ in how strongly they respond.

entries.closingLine: Since exploratory behaviour recurs daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Great White Pelican

waveform.description: A coordinated advancing rhythm with the group's dips lining up.

entries.closingLine: Continuous coordinated group work makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Great White Shark

waveform.description: A warm cruising band broken by two near-vertical upward strikes that fall back below the line — the drop before each charge is part of the shape.

entries.closingLine: Because a warm steady patrol supports a rare, total upward strike, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Great-tailed Grackle

modes.label: Occupying irrigated farmland, car parks, city squares and anywhere with water and waste • Nesting colonially in ornamental trees and roosting in thousands • Following irrigation and settlement north across a continent

waveform.description: A busy irregular pattern of varied excursions, because the animal is doing many different things across a day.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging and social interactions recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Adjutant

waveform.description: A steady working rhythm — repeated bouts of feeding and waiting across the day with no sharp events.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding runs as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Amberjack

modes.label: Cruising in open water above reefs and wrecks • Driving down a shoal until individuals tire • Turning on the ones that fall behind

waveform.description: A rapid sustained pattern of strong excursions with no rest between them, because the animal operates at high output continuously.

entries.closingLine: Since pursuit is continuous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Bamboo Lemur

waveform.description: A quiet steady rhythm — long feeding bouts on a food that returns little and takes time to handle.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding and processing both run slowly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Bee Fly

modes.label: A female hovering over the ground near solitary bee nest entrances rather than landing at them • Eggs coated in dust or sand picked up into an abdominal chamber to add weight • Those eggs flicked from the air towards or into the burrow entrance while the fly never touches the ground

waveform.description: A hovering rhythm with repeated darting deliveries, because the fly works over the ground making many short casts.

entries.closingLine: Because the season is short, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Bilby

waveform.description: A busy even digging rhythm through the night with a clean fall before dawn — many small excavations rather than one.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from many small repeated excavations, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Bird-of-paradise

waveform.description: Repeated display bouts of consistent height across the day, separated by short recoveries — attendance rather than a single performance.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on repeated daily performance at a fixed location, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Bulldog Bat
entries.archetype: Hunting a Ripple, Not a Fish

modes.label: Flying low over water • Reading the surface • Raking with the feet

waveform.description: A repeating low pass with sudden drops to the water.

entries.closingLine: This is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Fairy Armadillo

waveform.description: A low, steady line with tiny undulations, showing continuous, modest activity kept under a protective layer rather than big exposed swings.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole system is built for staying buried, buffered and conservative rather than making large, exposed bursts, it operates as a low-frequency, shelter-anchored system.

entries.name: Greater Flamingo

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying pumping rhythm held for hours at a time.

entries.closingLine: Continuous rhythmic pumping in hostile water makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Glider

waveform.description: A long quiet baseline with one shallow excursion — most of the night is slow feeding, interrupted by brief glides.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal earns little and therefore spends carefully, moving mostly by falling, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Grison

waveform.description: Sustained high-rate pursuit with no break.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: continuous, insistent and expensive to run.

entries.name: Greater Hedgehog Tenrec
entries.archetype: Spiny Generalist That Lets Its Temperature Fall

waveform.description: Active night foraging through the warm season dropping into a flat torpid trough in the cool season.

entries.closingLine: Because it switches seasonally between active nightly foraging and extended torpor, the system is a phase-change system.

entries.name: Greater Honeyguide

waveform.description: A series of guiding bursts leading to the nest, followed by a long quiet period of waiting and feeding.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: active, conspicuous guiding and quiet waiting for the opened comb.

entries.name: Greater Kudu

waveform.description: A quiet selective browsing rhythm with no urgency anywhere in it.

entries.closingLine: Continuous selective browsing makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Greater Mouse-deer
entries.archetype: Drumming the Ground With the Hooves

waveform.description: A still line broken by a rapid repeated drumming sequence.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: near-total stillness and a short percussive signal.

entries.name: Greater Painted-snipe

waveform.description: Gentle, even ripples at a mid-level of activity, showing repeated, cautious foraging passes along the wetland edge.

entries.closingLine: This makes them a mid-frequency system: not built for rare dramatic bursts or heavy long-term storage, but for ongoing, rhythmic, cautious use of a specific habitat band where food, shelter and risk are continuously balanced.

entries.name: Greater Prairie-Chicken

waveform.description: Long low stretches of covered living with evenly spaced, moderate peaks for repeated lek display sessions.

entries.closingLine: The species needs both modes: the low, concealed rhythm to survive most days, and the regular, place-bound lek ritual to secure mates and territory, so its system is best understood as bimodal with a low baseline and a coordinated mid-frequency display mode.

entries.name: Greater Rhea

waveform.description: A steady sustained rhythm: continuous guarding rather than intermittent effort.

entries.closingLine: That makes the rhea a mid-frequency system: steady, coordinated and organised around continuous protection of a shared investment.

entries.name: Greater Roadrunner

waveform.description: Repeated chase events at a working pace with recovery between them.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and repeatable, built around sustained ground pursuit paid for with energy saved elsewhere.

entries.name: Greater Sage-Grouse

waveform.description: A mostly low, steady line for sheltered foraging with a moderate, rounded rise and fall representing the seasonal, rhythmic lek display period.

entries.closingLine: Because their lives alternate between a dominant low-exposure, cover-hugging routine and a recurring, structured display phase on open ground, the system is best read as bimodal: a low-frequency shelter–forage mode paired with a mid-frequency, rhythmic arena mode.

entries.name: Greater Siren

waveform.description: Continuous aquatic working, a long sealed hold, then resumption.

entries.closingLine: That makes it an adaptive system: one body running either continuous aquatic foraging or a sealed, near-suspended hold, depending on whether the water is there.

entries.name: Greater Weever

modes.label: Lying buried in sand with only the eyes and the first dorsal fin exposed • Raising black venomous spines when disturbed • Injecting through grooved spines into whatever presses down on it

waveform.description: A long buried line broken by isolated sharp events, because nothing happens until contact and then everything does.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Greek Tortoise

modes.label: Digging a nest and laying eggs in it • Having the temperature during a middle window of incubation determine whether each embryo develops as male or female • Producing clutches skewed by the weather that season

waveform.description: A very slow even line with a single small rise, because everything about this animal happens across months and years.

entries.closingLine: Since generations take decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Green Anaconda

waveform.description: An almost unbroken resting line with one slow disturbance in it.

entries.closingLine: Very low expenditure and infrequent enormous intake make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Green Anole

modes.label: Shifting between green and brown over minutes • Responding to temperature, stress and social state • Not matching the surface it sits on

waveform.description: A slow smooth drift between two levels with no abrupt transitions, because the change is gradual and driven from inside.

entries.closingLine: Since shifts occur over minutes, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Green Basilisk

waveform.description: Mostly steady mid-level activity along the stream edge, punctuated by brief sharp spikes representing sudden waterline sprints when danger appears.

entries.closingLine: The system therefore has two essential modes—a poised, mid-frequency patrol state that keeps them near the waterline, and a high-frequency, seconds-long sprint that only activates on threat—making this a bimodal pattern built around rare but decisive waterline bursts.

entries.name: Green Chafer Beetle

modes.label: Adults feeding on the foliage of a very wide range of unrelated plant families rather than on any particular host • Mandibles and digestion general enough to handle whatever leaf is available • Populations therefore unaffected by the absence of any single plant, because something suitable is always present

waveform.description: A single nightly feeding period, because the adults are active after dark and rest through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Green Huntsman Spider

waveform.description: A long low flat line of stillness with one sharp narrow spike for the rapid strike, then a return to low-level waiting.

entries.closingLine: That combination of camouflaged waiting and sudden attack makes this a bimodal system with a low-frequency baseline and a defining high-frequency strike mode.

entries.name: Green Iguana

waveform.description: A slow rise from a cold floor to a working plateau and back down.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an unproductive warming phase and a working phase that depends entirely on it.

entries.name: Green Jay

waveform.description: A consistent mid-level group rhythm with no extended quiet.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, continuously coordinated group activity rather than bursts.

entries.name: Green June Beetle
entries.archetype: Two Years Spent Eating Rotted Matter Underground

modes.label: Living as a grub in decaying soil organic matter • Crawling on its back • Emerging briefly as an adult

waveform.description: A very long even stretch ending in a single brief peak, because years of buried feeding precede a short adult period.

entries.closingLine: Since a generation takes a year or more, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Green Lacewing

waveform.description: An even searching rhythm that gives way to short, very sharp feeding spikes.

entries.closingLine: That division makes this a bimodal system: a steady mid-frequency search-and-placement stage feeding a short high-frequency consumption stage.

entries.name: Green Lynx Spider

waveform.description: Sudden leaps through the hunting season, flattening into the long guard over the egg sac.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-change system: an active leaping hunter that becomes a stationary guard.

entries.name: Green Mamba

modes.label: Climbing • Searching foliage • Extending across a gap

waveform.description: A steady daytime rhythm of climbing and searching.

entries.closingLine: Steady diurnal searching of the canopy makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Green Milkweed Locust

waveform.description: A gently rising line showing slow, continuous accumulation of defensive capacity from ongoing feeding.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is built around slow, ongoing intake and storage of plant toxins as a durable, always-on defense, this is a low-frequency, reserve-heavy operating pattern.

entries.name: Green Moray

waveform.description: Long flat low activity with a single narrow dip-and-rise curve representing a brief ambush strike from a mostly hidden, patient position.

entries.closingLine: Because their whole build and daily rhythm center on staying tucked into structure and using brief ambush bursts rather than continuous roaming, the green moray is best understood as a single, low-frequency system built around patient, place-based strikes.

entries.name: Green Peach Aphid

modes.label: Females producing live daughters without mating, each daughter genetically identical to the mother • Those daughters already containing their own developing embryos at the moment they are born • Three generations therefore present inside one animal, so the population grows faster than the generation time alone would allow

waveform.description: A rapid oscillation with a rising trend, because generations turn over quickly and the total keeps climbing.

entries.closingLine: Because generations turn over in days, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Green Peafowl

modes.label: A train of elongated upper tail coverts raised into a fan with rows of iridescent eyespots • The shorter tail feathers behind it vibrated rapidly so the whole train rattles and shimmers • The vibration producing infrasound below human hearing that the female can detect at a distance

waveform.description: A fast shivering oscillation, because the display is a sustained vibration rather than a static pose.

entries.closingLine: Because the vibration runs several times a second, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Green Planthopper

waveform.description: A long, still baseline broken by sudden spikes of jumping or flight.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: motionless leaf-like feeding and instant escape.

entries.name: Green Sea Turtle

waveform.description: A very long shallow rhythm — a life whose repeating unit is measured in years, not days.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts patient low-grade intake into an extremely long life cycle, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Green Tree Python

modes.label: Saddled on a branch • Waiting • Striking downward

waveform.description: An extremely quiet trace: a coiled snake moving almost never.

entries.closingLine: Motionless ambush makes this a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Green-blotched Moth

modes.label: Adults flying into orchards at night to pierce ripening fruit and leaving before dawn • Larvae developing not on the crop but on Menispermaceae vines in surrounding forest and scrub • The breeding population therefore sitting entirely outside the orchard, where no crop treatment reaches it

waveform.description: A single nightly incursion and withdrawal, because the adults arrive after dark and leave before morning.

entries.closingLine: Because generations run seasonally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Green-cheeked Conure

modes.label: Roosting communally inside a tree cavity every night • Pressing together in contact with several other birds • Maintaining those relationships by allopreening through the day

waveform.description: Daytime activity alternating with a long quiet plateau, because the birds are either active as a group or packed together asleep.

entries.closingLine: Since social contact is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Green-winged Cicada

modes.label: A pair of ribbed membranes on the abdomen buckled inward by muscle and springing back elastically • Each buckle producing a sharp click, repeated hundreds of times a second • The largely hollow abdomen behind them acting as a resonating chamber that amplifies the result into a continuous shrill

waveform.description: An extremely rapid regular oscillation, because the mechanism cycles hundreds of times every second.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is hundreds per second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Green-winged Macaw
entries.archetype: Slow Life History Built on a Pair Bond

modes.label: Holding one mate for decades • Raising one or two chicks at long intervals • Depending on a cliff or hollow that cannot be built

waveform.description: A long flat line broken by rare narrow peaks, because reproduction is an occasional event against decades of adult life.

entries.closingLine: Since a generation takes decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Greenbottle Blow Fly

modes.label: Detecting the volatiles • Arriving within minutes • Larvae done in days

waveform.description: A fast repeating spike train with almost no floor, because everything about this animal is a race against something rotting.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole strategy is speed against a vanishing resource, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Greenland Shark

modes.label: Swimming at under a metre a second in near-freezing water • Growing about a centimetre a year • Not breeding until past a century old

waveform.description: A nearly flat line with almost no variation across its whole length, because nothing in this animal changes quickly enough to register.

entries.closingLine: Since a generation takes a century, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Grevy's Zebra

modes.label: Males holding large territories containing water • Females moving freely across them • Mating decided by where the water is rather than by herding

waveform.description: Long level stretches with occasional raised sections, because a territory is held continuously and contested only occasionally.

entries.closingLine: Since territories are held across seasons, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Grey Crowned Crane

waveform.description: A continual social rhythm of rises and returns, never seasonal.

entries.closingLine: Continuous social signalling alongside steady foraging makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Grey Field Slug

waveform.description: A low, mostly flat line with shallow dips representing brief, careful excursions from a stable moist refuge.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole animal is built around staying within a safe moisture envelope and only venturing out in low-risk windows, the grey field slug is a strongly low-frequency system centered on sheltered, moisture-led retreat.

entries.name: Grey Seal

waveform.description: A steady loading rhythm followed by a long low spending plateau.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long steady accumulation and a short total expenditure.

entries.name: Grey-crowned Babbler

modes.label: Retaining grown offspring in the group rather than dispersing them • Sharing nest building, feeding and defence across all members • Recruiting the same helpers into the next season

waveform.description: A long even line with a modest sustained rise, because the group's work is continuous and the breeding season is a raised phase rather than a spike.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle turns over annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Greylag Goose

waveform.description: A steady mid-level waveform with gentle repeating undulations, showing ongoing coordinated activity without extreme peaks or lows.

entries.closingLine: This creates a mid-frequency system built on rhythmic, repeated group movement and communication: coordinated, route-led activity rather than rare bursts or deep reserve use, so Greylag Goose is classified as a SINGLE, MID-frequency pattern.

entries.name: Grizzly Bear

waveform.description: A rising active season of uneven peaks dropping into a flat winter.

entries.closingLine: A long active circuit funding a deep shutdown makes this a bimodal system, mid-frequency in season and low-frequency in the ground.

entries.name: Groundhog

modes.label: Feeding almost continuously through summer • Converting grass and crops into fat • Digging and maintaining a burrow system alone
Sealed in a winter chamber below the frost line • Body temperature falling to a few degrees above freezing • Heart rate dropping to a handful of beats a minute

waveform.description: Active variation giving way to a long flat depressed line, because the animal genuinely alternates between two physiological states.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two physiologies, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Grovesnail

waveform.description: A higher-activity plateau that sinks into a lower, flatter level, showing the shift from exposed foraging to sealed retreat.

entries.closingLine: Because the snail’s survival depends on switching between an exposed, moderate-paced foraging state and a sealed, low-output refuge state, this is a bimodal system anchored by a low-frequency retreat mode and a mid-frequency activity mode.

entries.name: Guanaco

waveform.description: A steady grazing and watching rhythm across open ground.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, sustainable and continuously watched.

entries.name: Guianan Cock-of-the-rock
entries.archetype: A Few Males Take Almost Everything

modes.label: Clearing a court • Displaying on the ground • Mostly failing

waveform.description: Repeated bursts of display returning to the same baseline.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daily display and feeding makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Guinea Pig

modes.label: Grazing in a group • Calling constantly • Young running the first day

waveform.description: An even close-spaced rhythm with nothing sharp in it, the trace of an animal that never accelerates and never stops.

entries.closingLine: Because the grazing and the calling run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Guira Cuckoo
entries.archetype: One Nest, Several Mothers, Eggs Thrown Out

waveform.description: A busy uneven group rhythm with constant activity.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuously social, continuously contested.

entries.name: Guppy

modes.label: Carrying male colour patterns that vary with local predation • Maturing earlier and smaller where predators are abundant • Producing measurably different populations within a handful of generations

waveform.description: A rapid varied pattern whose excursions differ from one to the next, because individuals and populations differ continuously.

entries.closingLine: Since generations turn over in weeks, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Hackberry Emperor

modes.label: Ignoring flowers almost entirely • Feeding on sap runs, rotting fruit, dung, carrion and the sweat of animals including people • Extracting sodium and nitrogen that a nectar diet cannot supply

waveform.description: A busy repeated rhythm of similar events, because the butterfly moves constantly between scattered feeding sources.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding visits recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Hairy Frogfish
entries.archetype: A Wriggling Worm Lure Over a Huge Gape

waveform.description: A low line of lure-twitching with one explosive strike spike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long stationary luring and a sudden suction strike.

entries.name: Hamadryas Baboon

waveform.description: A steady mid-level oscillation showing ongoing, rhythmic adjustments that keep the troop coordinated without extreme spikes.

entries.closingLine: This produces a strongly mid-frequency system: continuous, rhythmic troop-ordering activity that keeps signals, rank and movement clear enough to prevent chaos.

entries.name: Hamilton's Frog

waveform.description: An almost motionless line — one of the least active vertebrates it is possible to build.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal moves rarely and produces very few young, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Hammerkop
entries.archetype: A Nest Far Larger Than the Bird

waveform.description: A modest baseline rising into a long sustained construction period.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an ordinary feeding baseline and a vastly disproportionate construction effort.

entries.name: Happy-face Spider

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line with gentle undulation, showing a constant, low-cost signal that is always present and occasionally noticed.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system: the signal is continuously present and ready, but its impact depends on intermittent moments of visual contact rather than rare deep reserves or rapid bursts.

entries.name: Harbor Porpoise

waveform.description: A fast unbroken working rhythm with no gap anywhere in it.

entries.closingLine: Unbroken low-drama foraging makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Harbor Seal

waveform.description: A smooth tidal rise and fall between working and resting levels.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a working phase and a resting phase, alternating on an external schedule.

entries.name: Hard-lipped Barb

waveform.description: Even, low-amplitude oscillations showing continuous, rhythmic scraping passes over surfaces rather than long waits or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: This creates a mid-frequency operating pattern: not about deep reserves or single big strikes, but about ongoing, coordinated movement and repeated, moderate-effort scrapes that turn a broad, thinly coated surface into a reliable flow of nutrition.

entries.name: Harlequin Beetle

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line with gentle, regular undulations, representing continuous, moderate activity as the beetle repeatedly extends and repositions its long reach.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a mid-frequency system built on rhythmic, leveraged extension across surfaces.

entries.name: Harlequin Duck

waveform.description: Continuous rough working with no smooth stretch anywhere in it.

entries.closingLine: Continuous work inside turbulence makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Harlequin Filefish
entries.archetype: Coral-Polyp Picker That Smells of Coral

waveform.description: A still night inside the coral, a long steady day of polyp-picking, then stillness again.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady daytime polyp-picking and a still night hidden inside the same coral.

entries.name: Harlequin Tuskfish

waveform.description: A steady midline with small repeating dips for routine motion and modest, evenly spaced peaks for precise feeding strikes, showing ongoing, controlled activity rather than long waits or frantic bursts.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency operating pattern: a conspicuous body moving through the reef with ongoing, measured effort and frequent, precise applications of force.

entries.name: Harnessed Moth

modes.label: A pair of ridged structures on the thorax buckled rapidly to produce trains of ultrasonic clicks • Those clicks emitted in response to a bat's own calls, at the moment the bat is closing in • The returning echoes disrupted so the bat's final approach is misjudged and the attack is broken off

waveform.description: A very fast burst rhythm, because the clicks are produced in rapid trains during the seconds of an attack.

entries.closingLine: Because the clicks run at very high rates, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Harp Sponge

waveform.description: An almost flat line with small rises as drifting prey is snagged.

entries.closingLine: It is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Harpy Eagle

waveform.description: Long flat perching with two very tall narrow spikes — almost all the energy of a week is spent in a few seconds.
