entries.closingLine: Because it cannot function without both the long wait and the brief strike, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Harris's Hawk

modes.label: Stacked perching • Leapfrogging • Watching one another

waveform.description: An even patrol rhythm that lifts into one long sustained block rather than a spike, because the chase is relayed and lasts.

entries.closingLine: Because a continuous coordinated formation funds a rare and disproportionately expensive pursuit, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Harvestman

waveform.description: A low, slow, almost featureless trace with very little variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, cheap and built on distance and sacrifice rather than on defence.

entries.name: Hawaiian Crow
entries.archetype: Sticks and Fruit in an Island Forest

waveform.description: A steady foraging line with slower dips for deliberate tool-assisted extraction.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: broad forest foraging and a slower, deliberate tool-using mode.

entries.name: Hawksbill Sea Turtle

waveform.description: An even working rhythm — probe, tear, move on — repeated across the reef through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding runs as a steady continuous search rather than in bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Hazel Dormouse

waveform.description: Long low stretches of minimal activity (hibernation) separated by moderate, rounded rises of foraging when conditions are seasonally and locally favorable.

entries.closingLine: Because survival depends on this deliberate seasonal and daily switch between deep rest and measured activity, the hazel dormouse is a bimodal low–mid frequency system.

entries.name: Hazel Leaf-roller Weevil

waveform.description: Even mid-height waves showing a repeated cycle of effortful leaf-rolling followed by short recovery, rather than long dormancy or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a mid-frequency system built on rhythmic, repeated construction rather than extreme hoarding or single explosive events.

entries.name: Head Louse

modes.label: Each leg ending in a curved claw that closes against a thumb-like spur on the tibia • The gap between them matching the diameter of a human head hair almost exactly • The insect gripping individual shafts so firmly that combing, washing and scratching do not dislodge it

waveform.description: A steady unvarying rhythm, because the animal feeds and moves at short regular intervals without episodes.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding recurs every few hours, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Hecale Longwing

modes.label: Trap-lining the same flowers • Kneading pollen into a drop • Living for months

waveform.description: A slow even glide with no sharp movement, because this is a butterfly that never needs to hurry and lives long enough not to.

entries.closingLine: Since the circuit repeats at one unhurried daily tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Hellbender

waveform.description: A flat line broken by nothing at all — the animal's entire strategy is to remain where it is.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is built on remaining still in a specific place, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Helmeted Curassow
entries.archetype: A Casque Above a Very Low Voice

waveform.description: Slow, deep pulses spaced far apart across a quiet baseline.

entries.closingLine: Slow-moving, low-density and slow-breeding, it is a low-frequency system throughout.

entries.name: Helmeted Guineafowl

waveform.description: A busy continuous ground rhythm with constant noise.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, sociable ground-covering with continuous collective vigilance.

entries.name: Helmeted Hornbill

waveform.description: A steady canopy rhythm punctuated by two sharp collisions — the jousts are brief events in an otherwise even day.

entries.closingLine: Because the day runs as a steady canopy cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Hercules Beetle
entries.archetype: Two Years of Wood, One Horn

waveform.description: A long flat accumulation, then short violent contests.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long, cheap, hidden accumulation and the short expensive contest it exists to pay for.

entries.name: Hermann's Tortoise

waveform.description: A gently undulating low line showing small, regular rises and falls in activity as the tortoise follows sun and shelter without sharp bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole system is built around slow, conservative, thermally gated movement instead of bursts or distinct alternative modes, Hermann's tortoise is a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Hermit Crab

modes.label: Crabs gathering around a newly available shell that is too large for any of them • Lining up by size from largest to smallest beside it • Every crab swapping simultaneously the moment the largest moves in, so one shell rehouses the whole line

waveform.description: A flat line broken by a sudden cluster of activity, because nothing happens until a shell appears and then everything does at once.

entries.closingLine: Because shells appear rarely, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Herring Gull
entries.archetype: A Red Spot That Releases Food

modes.label: Carrying a red spot on the lower mandible • Having it pecked by chicks that respond to the mark rather than the parent • Regurgitating food in response to the pecking

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying repetition, because begging and feeding are short exchanges repeated constantly through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since exchanges recur within seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Hieroglyphic Cicada

modes.label: Males aggregating in the same trees and calling at the same time rather than spacing out • Overlapping calls merging into a continuous wall of sound with no clear origin • Any individual made harder to locate because the acoustic field cannot be resolved into sources

waveform.description: A dense continuous high-rate oscillation, because many overlapping sources merge into one unbroken sound.

entries.closingLine: Because the call cycles hundreds of times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Highfin Dragonfish

waveform.description: Long low stretches of quiet cruising punctuated by short, sharp spikes of barbel flash and strike activity.

entries.closingLine: That architecture — long passive sensing phases powered by the barbel, broken by quick, localized attack bursts — makes this a bimodal system combining a low-frequency surveillance mode with a high-frequency capture mode.

entries.name: Himalayan Goral

waveform.description: Two broad activity humps at either end of the day with a settled trough between them — a shape set by light and temperature, not by events.

entries.closingLine: Because it runs a regular, repeated daily cycle at moderate cost rather than storing or bursting, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Himalayan Monal

modes.label: Working alpine slopes with a short heavy decurved bill • Digging through soil and snow for tubers, rhizomes and insects • Occupying ground above the treeline where surface food is scarce

waveform.description: A steady even line with modest occasional rises, because digging is patient continuous work rather than a series of events.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Himalayan Snowcock
entries.archetype: Walk Up the Slope, Glide Down

waveform.description: A steady walking line with one sharp spike where the covey launches and glides downhill.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: slow uphill feeding punctuated by fast downhill escapes.

entries.name: Himalayan Tahr

waveform.description: One long shallow rise through the growing season and an equally slow decline through winter — a single annual breath.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole architecture stores in a brief window and draws down patiently across a long one, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Hirola

waveform.description: A steady grazing rhythm with regular small interruptions — each one a stop to mark rather than to feed.

entries.closingLine: Because grazing and marking run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Hispaniolan Solenodon

waveform.description: A persistent series of small probing efforts through the night, each one shallow, none of them a burst.

entries.closingLine: Because value is extracted by steady methodical probing across hours rather than by reserves or bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Hoary Marmot
entries.archetype: A Short Summer Paid For With Long Sleep

waveform.description: Months of flat hibernation broken by one short, busy summer.

entries.closingLine: This is a PHASE_CHANGE system: a MID summer phase of feeding and vigilance and a long LOW phase of hibernation.

entries.name: Hoatzin
entries.archetype: A Crop That Displaced the Flight Muscle

modes.label: Eating leaves • Fermenting in the throat • Barely able to fly

waveform.description: An almost static rhythm of eating, sitting and digesting.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Hoff Crab
entries.archetype: Bacteria Farmer on the Vent Gradient

waveform.description: A flat, near-constant line of sitting in the vent flow, with no day or night.

entries.closingLine: Because it spends its life sitting in one thin zone of the vent gradient, the system is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Hog Badger

waveform.description: A dogged forward-working rhythm without pauses or spikes.

entries.closingLine: Continuous undifferentiated working of the substrate makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Hog Deer

waveform.description: Two feeding periods at the cool ends of the day on a steady baseline — a grassland routine with no spikes.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on steady grazing inside continuous cover, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Honduran White Bat

waveform.description: A long sheltered baseline with a few short feeding excursions — a life lived mostly inside something the animal made.

entries.closingLine: Because a very small energy budget is protected by built shelter rather than by activity, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Honey Badger

waveform.description: Long low baseline interrupted by a sharp defensive spike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it bimodal: armor first, explosive response second.

entries.name: Honey Possum

waveform.description: Steady nightly feeding interrupted by a dip into torpor when conditions turn cold.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady nightly flower feeding and short energy-saving shutdowns.

entries.name: Honeypot Ant

waveform.description: A gently undulating low line, showing slow filling and gradual drawdown of a shared reserve rather than sharp spikes of activity.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is built around dense reserves, slow turnover and careful communal withdrawal, this is a strongly low-frequency, living-pantry system.

entries.name: Hooded Seal
entries.archetype: A Nose Inflated Into a Signal

waveform.description: A long steady line of deep foraging with one short, very high spike during the breeding haul-out.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: a long low-frequency foraging mode and a short, explosive breeding and display mode.

entries.name: Hooded Vulture

waveform.description: A long searching glide with brief arrivals folded into it.

entries.closingLine: Continuous soaring and social feeding makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Hoolock Gibbon

waveform.description: A dense burst of calling early on, then a long steady day — the territory is settled in the first hour and travelled afterwards.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on a daily call and steady travel, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Hoopoe

waveform.description: A steady probing rhythm across open ground.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, methodical probing across open ground.

entries.name: Horned Grebe
entries.archetype: Legs at the Back, Feathers in the Stomach

waveform.description: A regular diving rhythm alternating between surface and depth.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady repeated diving with nothing held back for land.

entries.name: Horned Nerite Snail

modes.label: Adults living and breeding in fresh water well upstream, laying egg capsules on rocks • Hatched larvae carried downstream and out to sea, where they develop in the plankton for weeks • Settled juveniles returning to the river mouth and then climbing upstream over months, sometimes in enormous aggregations

waveform.description: A long round-trip cycle, because the population moves down and then back up over the course of a year.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Horned Puffin
entries.archetype: Backward Spines Holding a Row of Fish

waveform.description: A frantic flying rhythm alternating with a steadier underwater working rate.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: expensive marginal flight and efficient wing-powered diving.

entries.name: Horned Screamer

modes.label: Grazing marsh plants • Calling across water • Standing on floating mats

waveform.description: A slow grazing rhythm with occasional loud calls through it.

entries.closingLine: Slow, grazing and conservative throughout, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Horned Sungem
entries.archetype: Iridescent Tufts on a Hovering Engine

waveform.description: Short intense feeding bouts separated by longer flat spells of perching.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: bursts of hovering feeding and still perching between them.

entries.name: Horse Fly

waveform.description: A long low larval phase in wet ground, then a short adult summer of repeated sharp pursuit spikes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-change system: slow larval life in wet ground and a brief, persistent adult pursuit.

entries.name: Horseshoe Crab

waveform.description: A long flat benthic year with two narrow spawning excursions — the events are rare and tightly timed.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on low continuous activity punctuated by a tightly timed annual event, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Hottentot Teal

modes.label: Rows of fine comb-like lamellae along the inside edges of the bill • Water drawn in at the tip and pumped out at the sides by the tongue • Small invertebrates, seeds and plankton retained on the lamellae while the water passes through

waveform.description: A rapid continuous small-amplitude rhythm, because the bill pumps steadily without pause while feeding.

entries.closingLine: Because pumping is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: House Centipede

modes.label: Running down prey • Throwing legs over it • Detaching a leg if grabbed

waveform.description: A dense violent oscillation with almost no floor, because this animal is either running or not operating.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole body plan is arranged around speed and reaction, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: House Cricket

modes.label: Rubbing wings • Calling all night • Slowing as it cools

waveform.description: A dense even pulse train whose spacing widens slightly toward the end, because the rate itself tracks the falling temperature.

entries.closingLine: Because the calling and feeding run continuously through the dark at a steady tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: House Crow

modes.label: Working human waste • Nesting in any fork • Riding vessels to new coasts

waveform.description: An opportunistic uneven rhythm where no two peaks match, because each is a different scrap being worked.

entries.closingLine: Since the scavenging runs continuously through daylight, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: House Finch

modes.label: Feeding on seeds, buds and fruit • Depositing dietary carotenoids into growing feathers at the moult • Wearing a colour that reports what was available

waveform.description: A working baseline with periodic deeper excursions, because feeding is continuous and the moult is an occasional heavy demand.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding and moult cycles repeat, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: House Fly

modes.label: Regurgitating fluid onto solid food • Dissolving it outside the body • Sponging the liquid up through channelled mouthparts

waveform.description: An extremely dense run of brief identical events, because the animal feeds and moves in very short repeated bouts all day.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding bouts recur constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: House Mouse

modes.label: Whiskers on the skirting • Running the edge • Crossing only when it must

waveform.description: A close regular tick along one level with two isolated tall spikes, because the open crossings are rare and everything else is edge.

entries.closingLine: Because the sweeping and the running are continuous through the active hours, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: House Sparrow

modes.label: Feeding on spilled grain • Nesting in a building cavity • Roosting as a flock

waveform.description: A busy sociable chatter of similar peaks, because the flock feeds and squabbles continuously through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the feeding and social activity run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: House Wren

modes.label: Packing several cavities with sticks • Offering the set to a female to choose from • Denying the same holes to every other bird

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying sequence of identical efforts, because the bird repeats the same filling work across many sites.

entries.closingLine: Since building is repeated through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Household Casebearer Moth

modes.label: A flattened silk case built by the larva and covered in sand grains, dust, hair and fibre from wherever it lives • The larva living permanently inside it, extending the head and front legs to move and feeding on wool, hair and debris • Both ends left open so the animal can turn within the case and emerge from either, without ever leaving it

waveform.description: A very slow steady rhythm, because the animal moves and feeds gradually over months without episodes.

entries.closingLine: Because development runs across months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Hoverfly

modes.label: Wearing black and yellow bands resembling a wasp or bee • Being an unconvincing copy by any measurement anyone applies • Being avoided anyway by birds that will not risk finding out

waveform.description: A rapid fine oscillation without larger structure, because the animal hovers and darts continuously all day.

entries.closingLine: Since hovering and visits recur constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Human

modes.label: Food heated before eating, breaking down starches and denaturing proteins outside the gut • More energy released per mouthful and far less chewing and digestion required • A shorter gut and a larger brain becoming affordable on the same total energy budget

waveform.description: A long slow accumulation and settling, because the change operates across generations rather than days.

entries.closingLine: Because the change runs across generations, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Humboldt Penguin

modes.label: Diving the cold band • Returning to the same burrow • Dumping heat through bare skin

waveform.description: A regular diving rhythm of similar efforts, because the bird works the same water on the same schedule every day it can.

entries.closingLine: Because the diving and returning repeat at one steady daily tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Hummingbird Clearwing
entries.archetype: A Stationary Hover on Clear Wings

waveform.description: Rapid repeated peaks as the moth darts from flower to flower.

entries.closingLine: Because the adult system is organised around fast hover-feeding visits, it is a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Hummingbird Hawk-Moth

waveform.description: A dense unbroken sawtooth: extremely rapid cycles with no pause anywhere in the trace.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: rapid, expensive and dependent on constant refuelling.

entries.name: Humpback Anglerfish

waveform.description: An almost dead-flat line broken by two extremely narrow spikes — weeks of nothing and a fraction of a second of everything.

entries.closingLine: Because both the long wait and the total gulp are essential, it is bimodal.

entries.name: Humpback Turretfish

waveform.description: A steady, unchanging rhythm of slow, fin-driven searching.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a single-mode system: slow, armoured, fin-driven foraging.

entries.name: Humpback Whale
entries.archetype: A Song That Changes and Spreads

waveform.description: An active feeding rhythm giving way to a long low singing season.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: cooperative polar feeding and a tropical season of fasting and shared song.

entries.name: Humphead Parrotfish

waveform.description: A relentless even bite rhythm — the same action thousands of times a day with no pause and no peak.

entries.closingLine: Because the biting and grinding run continuously all day at an even rate, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Huntsman Spider

modes.label: Waiting flat against a vertical surface • Running sideways on laterigrade legs • Seizing prey directly with no web involved

waveform.description: Long stillness broken by extremely brief maximal events, because the animal waits motionless and then moves at full speed without any build-up.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes happen in a fraction of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Hyacinth Macaw

waveform.description: Steady repeated cracking bouts through the day — work that is mechanical and constant rather than episodic.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts repeated mechanical work into a steady return, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Iberian Lynx

waveform.description: A regular hunting rhythm with modest peaks — a kill is a routine daily event rather than a rare one.

entries.closingLine: Because hunting runs as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ibisbill

waveform.description: A fine regular probing rhythm — many identical small actions with no event large enough to stand out.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from many small identical probes repeated for hours, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ili Pika

waveform.description: One short raised season and a long flat one — the shape of a year in which almost all the work happens in a few weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because neither state can be removed without the animal failing, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Impala

waveform.description: An even feeding rhythm erupting into scattered overlapping peaks.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady mixed feeding and a brief co-ordinated scatter.

entries.name: Imperial Fruit-sucking Moth

modes.label: A large larva resting stretched along a stem, brown and mottled, resembling a dead twig or a strip of bark
On disturbance the larva rears and contracts the front segments, expanding a pair of enormous eyespots and a row of white marks that read as a face with teeth

waveform.description: A long flat line broken by violent sudden episodes, because the display is instantaneous and everything else is stillness.

entries.closingLine: So it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Inca Tern

modes.label: Working the Humboldt current • Feeding • Carrying a measurable ornament

waveform.description: A steady coastal foraging rhythm with dips to the water.

entries.closingLine: This is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Indian Earthworm

modes.label: Soil swallowed at depth, ground with grit in the gizzard and passed through a gut that adds mucus, enzymes and microbes • The processed material voided as casts on the surface rather than where it was taken from • Many tonnes per hectare per year moved upward this way, so the whole profile is turned over from below without anything being dug

waveform.description: A slow steady progression without episodes, because the process runs continuously and never stops or peaks.

entries.closingLine: Because the process runs continuously over years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Indian Muntjac

waveform.description: A quiet browsing line rising into a short contested passage.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: solitary quiet browsing and a brief close-quarters contest.

entries.name: Indian Peafowl

waveform.description: Repeated display events raised out of an ordinary ground-feeding baseline.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: a steady foraging rhythm carrying a costly seasonal signal.

entries.name: Indian Pied Myna

modes.label: Hundreds of birds converging on the same trees at dusk from feeding areas across a wide radius • Birds that fed poorly following birds that fed well when the roost disperses at dawn • Information about where food is spreading through the roost without anything being deliberately communicated

waveform.description: A daily rhythm with one strong convergence, because the flock scatters through the day and gathers sharply at dusk.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Indian Rhinoceros

modes.label: Carrying enlarged lower incisors that grow into tusks • Slashing with them in serious fights between males • Using the horn for digging and display rather than for combat

waveform.description: A long slow line with one broad deep excursion, because a heavy solitary animal's year contains few events but they are serious.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Indian Rock Python
entries.archetype: A Cold Animal Making Its Own Heat

modes.label: Coiled on the clutch • Shivering • Weeks without feeding
Strike • Coil • Release when it stops

waveform.description: Long flat waiting, one raised brooding plateau, two brief spikes.

entries.closingLine: That is a bimodal system of long costly waiting and a very brief kill.

entries.name: Indian Star Tortoise

waveform.description: A long low year with one broad seasonal lift — activity arrives with the rain and settles again.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is slow and seasonally bounded, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Indo-Pacific Horseshoe Crab

modes.label: Circulating amebocytes in copper-based blue blood • Having those cells clot instantly around bacterial endotoxin • Sealing an infection into a gel before it can spread through an open circulatory system

waveform.description: A very slow even line with a small disturbance, because a long-lived bottom-walking animal does almost nothing quickly.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Indo-Pacific Tarpon

modes.label: Gulping air at the surface • Passing it into a lung-like swim bladder • Holding position in water too poor for gills

waveform.description: Flat stretches interrupted by regular sharp rises, because the fish holds steady between deliberate trips to the surface.

entries.closingLine: Since surfacing recurs through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Indochinese Box Turtle

waveform.description: A quiet steady line — a slow animal whose main capability requires no movement worth plotting.

entries.closingLine: Because nothing about the animal happens quickly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Indochinese Tiger
entries.archetype: An Intact Forest With Nothing In It

modes.label: Holding a huge territory • One large kill • Days at the carcass

waveform.description: Long quiet intervals punctuated by rare large kills.

entries.closingLine: Large infrequent kills and long quiet intervals make this a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Indonesian Blue-tongued Skink

modes.label: Moving slowly • Holding the bluff • Opening everything at once

waveform.description: A slow flat line with two small nicks in it, because the display is over before it registers as a change of state.

entries.closingLine: Because everything else about the animal is slow and continuous, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Indri

waveform.description: A dense chorus early, a long quiet middle and a shorter answering burst — the day is bracketed by song.

entries.closingLine: Because the singing and moving run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Indus River Dolphin

waveform.description: A steady close-spaced rhythm — the animal is scanning and moving continuously with no pauses worth plotting.

entries.closingLine: Because scanning and swimming run continuously, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Io Moth

waveform.description: A flat resting floor cut by three identical vertical flashes — a display with no build-up, no gradient and no follow-through.

entries.closingLine: Because a near-zero resting state is paired with an instantaneous full-commitment display, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Iridescent Shark

modes.label: Moving with the shoal • Reading the rising water • Running upstream

waveform.description: A rolling mid-level line that drifts steadily upward across the frame, because the whole movement has a direction as well as a rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because the movement is continuous, collective and sustained over weeks, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Iris Lorikeet

modes.label: A total world range confined to Timor and Wetar and nothing beyond • Dependence on remnant eucalypt and monsoon forest that occurs only in parts of that island • No possibility of movement to any other population because none exists

waveform.description: A steady rhythm with a slow downward drift, because ordinary life continues while the total keeps declining.

entries.closingLine: Because the pressures run across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Isabella Tiger Moth

modes.label: An active larva feeding, growing and moulting through the warm months in the ordinary way
A larva under leaf litter with glycerol and related compounds flooding its tissues, ice forming outside the cells and the animal frozen solid for months at temperatures far below zero

waveform.description: An active varying rhythm flattening into an entirely level line, because the second state has no activity of any kind.

entries.closingLine: These are not degrees of the same state; one is a metabolising animal and the other is a frozen object with its chemistry suspended, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Island Fox
entries.archetype: A Dwarfed Canid Awake by Day

waveform.description: A steady rhythm through day and night with peaks at dawn and dusk.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a steady, omnivorous routine spread across day and night, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Jabiru

waveform.description: A deliberate walking pace with a snap folded into each few steps.

entries.closingLine: Continuous deliberate wading makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Jackdaw

waveform.description: A steady social rhythm that continues unchanged whatever the surroundings are made of.

entries.closingLine: That makes the jackdaw a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and social, whose adaptability comes from a requirement loose enough to be met by new materials.

entries.name: Jackson's Chameleon

modes.label: Shifting pigment cells and reflective crystal layers within seconds • Producing high-contrast display colours during rival encounters and courtship • Returning to muted greens when no other chameleon is present

waveform.description: A quiet baseline with repeated bright display episodes, because the colour changes when another animal appears.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Jaguar

waveform.description: Long quiet approach lines cut by two narrow full-height strikes — no chase phase on either side of them.

entries.closingLine: Because a patient concealed approach exists to deliver one uncontested crushing commitment, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Jaguarundi
entries.archetype: Taking the Shift Nobody Else Works

modes.label: Hunting in daylight • Moving low through cover • Avoiding the night crowd

waveform.description: Activity concentrated in the middle of the day.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daytime activity makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Jambu Fruit Dove

modes.label: A wide flexible gape that swallows fruit whole rather than pecking pieces from it • Seeds passing through the gut intact and being voided in flight far from the parent tree • Fruits above the gape width taken by nothing at all, so which trees are dispersed depends on a measurement of the bird

waveform.description: A quiet even rhythm, because the bird moves slowly and feeds steadily through the canopy.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs seasonally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Japanese Beetle

modes.label: Grubs feeding on grass roots for most of a year • Adults emerging and skeletonising leaves • Damaged foliage and feeding beetles drawing in still more

waveform.description: A long quiet line rising into one accelerating hump and falling away, because damage builds on itself within a single short adult season.

entries.closingLine: Since a generation takes a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Japanese Bush Warbler
entries.archetype: A Loud Song From a Bird That Stays Hidden

modes.label: Singing a long carrying whistle from dense cover • Holding territory by sound alone • Never showing itself

waveform.description: Long quiet intervals punctuated by tall narrow spikes, because a drawn-in breath precedes each sudden carrying whistle.

entries.closingLine: Since bouts of song repeat through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Japanese Macaque

modes.label: A young animal inventing a way of handling food • Kin and playmates copying it first • The practice becoming standard in a troop and passing to the next generation

waveform.description: A working rhythm whose baseline steadily climbs across the whole span, because each adoption raises the level from which the next begins.

entries.closingLine: Since interactions recur continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Japanese Marten
entries.archetype: Seasonal Menu Switching on Agile Limbs

waveform.description: Steady roaming and foraging broken by short, fast bursts of climbing and pursuit.

entries.closingLine: That gives a bimodal system of wide-ranging MID foraging punctuated by HIGH pursuit.

entries.name: Japanese Quail

modes.label: Hatching precocial and feeding within a day • Reaching sexual maturity at about six weeks • Laying almost daily thereafter

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying sequence maintained throughout, because everything in this animal's life happens quickly and repeatedly.

entries.closingLine: Since laying and development recur within days, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Japanese Rice Fish

modes.label: A mouth opening upward rather than forward, set on a head flattened along the top • Eyes placed high on the skull with an unobstructed view of the underside of the surface film • Feeding on what is trapped in or resting on the top few millimetres, taken continuously through the day

waveform.description: A close-packed shallow rhythm that never stops and never rises far, because the feeding is a continuous series of very small takes.

entries.closingLine: Because the taking is a continuous series of very small events through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Japanese Sea Nettle

modes.label: A tiny polyp attached to hard substrate on the seabed, budding slowly and persisting for years as a stable colony
Strobilation, in which each polyp stacks and releases dozens of juvenile medusae into the water within days, producing a bloom that appears suddenly along the coast

waveform.description: A completely flat benthic line that breaks into a rapid oscillating band, because the two stages are different systems rather than different levels.

entries.closingLine: The two stages are not versions of one another but separate architectures, benthic and attached against pelagic and drifting, connected by a threshold, so it operates as a phase-change system.

entries.name: Japanese Serow

modes.label: Small range • Scent-marked • Walked for years

waveform.description: An unusually flat trace: the same ground, walked again and again.

entries.closingLine: Sedentary, solitary and slow-breeding, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Japanese Spider Crab

modes.label: Walking slowly across deep soft bottom • Reaching food without moving the body • Carrying a shell far too small to shelter the legs

waveform.description: A long even line with a few shallow rises, because the animal moves slowly and almost nothing about its routine varies.

entries.closingLine: Since moults are years apart, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Java Mouse-deer

waveform.description: A rapid, even stitch of small movements and small meals — many low peaks, none of them large.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal runs on frequent small returns and continuous cautious movement rather than on stored fat or explosive escape, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Javan Ferret-Badger

modes.label: A long mobile flexible snout pushed into leaf litter and soft soil ahead of the body • Prey located by scent at close range and then worked out with the snout and forefeet together • Earthworms, grubs and soil invertebrates taken from a substrate that gives no visual information at all

waveform.description: A single nocturnal foraging period, because the animal works after dark and shelters through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because foraging is nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Javan Munia

waveform.description: A busy flocking line that settles into a quieter nesting phase and back.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: flock feeding on seeds and paired nest-building.

entries.name: Javan Myna

modes.label: Approaching the new • Working food courts • Roosting in thousands

waveform.description: A quick opportunistic rhythm with uneven peaks, because each one is a different situation being investigated.

entries.closingLine: Because the investigating and feeding run continuously through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Javan Pond Heron

modes.label: Walking the bund • Standing over shallow water • Striking often

waveform.description: A patient repeating rhythm of small dips, because the strikes are frequent and none of them is large.

entries.closingLine: Because the stalking and striking run together through every workable stage of the cycle, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Javan Rhinoceros

waveform.description: A quiet unhurried line — a large animal in a hot forest, doing as little as the heat allows.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Javan Rusa Deer

modes.label: A stag in rut thrashing its antlers through vegetation and gathering grass, vines and foliage into them • That material carried and displayed on the antlers during contests and courtship, making the rack appear substantially larger • Rivals and females assessing the whole loaded structure rather than the bone alone

waveform.description: A single seasonal rise and fall, because the whole display period is concentrated into the rut.

entries.closingLine: Because the rut is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Javan Slow Loris

waveform.description: A quiet unvarying line — deliberate slow movement through the canopy with almost nothing sudden in it.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs slowly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Javan Surili

waveform.description: Even, repeating mid-height arcs showing regular bouts of canopy movement linked by short pauses, reflecting a continuous but not explosive travel rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole system is built around ongoing, connected canopy travel rather than long stillness or sudden explosive bursts, its operating rhythm is a single, coordinated mid-frequency mode.

entries.name: Javanese Grasshopper

modes.label: Muscle in the hind femur contracting slowly against a locked joint rather than extending the leg • Elastic protein in a thickened band storing that energy while the joint is held closed • The catch released so the whole store discharges in a few thousandths of a second

waveform.description: A quiet baseline broken by extremely sharp discharges, because the jump is instantaneous and everything between is still.

entries.closingLine: Because the release takes milliseconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Jerboa

waveform.description: A rapid series of tall, irregular bounds with no settled rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Short, volatile and explosive, this is a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Jewel Beetle

waveform.description: A gently undulating mid-level line showing repeated, moderate shifts in visibility and activity as the beetle alternates between stillness on bark and short feeding movements.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system built around rhythmic, posture-led use of metallic armor as a visibility filter rather than either pure stillness or explosive bursts.

entries.name: John Dory

modes.label: Turning to face prey so only a thin edge is presented • Easing forward with fin movements alone • Shooting a protrusible jaw tube forward at the last moment

waveform.description: A slow steady approach that steepens into a single narrow spike, because the stalk is long and the strike is instantaneous.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Joro Spider

waveform.description: A long anchored line broken by a short dispersal event.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long anchored adult life and one brief airborne event.

entries.name: Jumping Spider

modes.label: Scanning with a pair of large forward eyes on a long tube • Moving the retina behind a fixed lens to sweep the image • Stalking and jumping only once the target is identified

waveform.description: Small continuous scanning movements punctuated by occasional deep spikes, because the animal watches constantly and jumps rarely.

entries.closingLine: Since scans and jumps recur constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: June Beetle

modes.label: Larvae living in soil for two to three years feeding on grass and crop roots • Damage appearing above ground as wilting and dieback with no visible cause • Adults emerging in a synchronised flush for a few weeks to feed on foliage and mate

waveform.description: A long low stretch broken by one sharp emergence, because almost the entire life is spent underground.

entries.closingLine: Because development runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Kagu

waveform.description: Long still pauses punctuated by single downward strikes — listening occupies far more of the day than probing.

entries.closingLine: Because the day is a steady repeated cycle of listening and probing, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Kakapo

waveform.description: Years near the floor with one raised section — a breeding season that arrives only when a tree decides it does.

entries.closingLine: Because the two states are both essential and the animal cannot function in only one, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Kakarratul

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing steady, hidden activity under a constant cover of sand without sharp bursts.

entries.closingLine: All of this makes Kakarratul a low-frequency system: dense, hidden, and committed to slow, subsurface movement that almost never breaks cover.

entries.name: Kea

waveform.description: Ordinary foraging interrupted by bursts of intense multi-part activity — investigation that looks like play and is priced like work.

entries.closingLine: Because context genuinely selects between a routine operating state and an investigative one, this is an adaptive system.

entries.name: Keel-billed Toucan
entries.archetype: A Bill Used on Each Other

waveform.description: A busy sociable rhythm across the canopy.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steadily active and continuously social.

entries.name: Kemp's Ridley Sea Turtle
entries.archetype: Daylight Mass Landing on One Coast

waveform.description: A long steady foraging line broken by a few sharp spikes of synchronized nesting.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: dispersed bottom foraging and brief synchronized nesting.

entries.name: Kenya Tree Coral

modes.label: Growing as a branched upright colony that continues to extend at the tips • Constricting at the base of a branch until it detaches and drifts away • That fragment settling on nearby substrate and establishing as a genetically identical new colony

waveform.description: A repeating cycle of growth and release, because branches build and drop on a continuing rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Kiang
entries.archetype: Thin Blood, Not Thick, at Altitude

modes.label: Grazing at five thousand metres • Travelling far • Breathing half the oxygen

waveform.description: A sustained travelling and grazing rhythm across open ground.

entries.closingLine: Sustained daily travel makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Killdeer

modes.label: Slipping off the nest before the predator sees it • Dragging a wing and calling loudly at a distance from the eggs • Recovering and flying once the pursuer has followed far enough

waveform.description: A calm line rising into a sustained shaped event and returning, because the display builds, holds and then ends deliberately.

entries.closingLine: Since displays recur through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: King Bird-of-paradise

waveform.description: A mid-level baseline with two narrow, high peaks representing brief, intense display bouts rising from steady perching and foraging.

entries.closingLine: That creates a bimodal rhythm: a mid-frequency life of steady perch-to-perch feeding and vigilance, punctuated by short, high-frequency bursts of royal display where all that control is spent in seconds.

entries.name: King Cobra

waveform.description: A sustained searching rhythm with modest rises where a trail is followed and closed — effort spread across the hunt rather than concentrated in a strike.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on sustained searching and deliberate engagement rather than on waiting or exploding, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: King Eider

modes.label: Diving deep • Swallowing molluscs whole • Grinding them apart

waveform.description: A repeating cycle of deep dives and surface recovery.

entries.closingLine: Repeated daily diving makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: King of Saxony Bird-of-paradise
entries.archetype: Two Enamel-Flagged Plumes on Bare Shafts

waveform.description: Steady foraging interrupted by repeated spikes of calling and plume display.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: routine canopy foraging and bouts of calling and display.

entries.name: King Penguin
entries.archetype: Diving to Where the Layer Sits

waveform.description: Repeated deep dives, then a long flat stretch of fasting.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: repeated deep foraging and long periods of paying out reserves without input.

entries.name: King Vulture

modes.label: Soaring above canopy • Following smaller vultures down • Tearing the hide open

waveform.description: Long soaring searches with descents onto found carcasses.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Kinkajou
entries.archetype: A Carnivore With a Tongue for Flowers

waveform.description: A steady nocturnal canopy rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, continuous canopy foraging.

entries.name: Kipunji

waveform.description: A regular call-and-move rhythm — the group announces itself repeatedly through the day as it travels.

entries.closingLine: Because calling and travelling run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Kirk's Dik-dik
entries.archetype: A Nose That Works as a Radiator

waveform.description: A careful low browsing rhythm with small steady variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: small, careful and built entirely around not spending water.

entries.name: Kiwi

waveform.description: A steady repeating probe-and-withdraw pattern — the night is one action repeated several hundred times.

entries.closingLine: Because probing runs as a steady repeated cycle all night, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Klipspringer

waveform.description: Very little movement across a small territory of rock.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: little movement, a small range, and safety bought from terrain rather than speed.

entries.name: Knobbed Hornbill

modes.label: Large fruits swallowed whole that almost nothing else on the island can handle • Seeds held in the gut and regurgitated or voided intact after a long flight • Distances of several kilometres covered between feeding and roosting, so seeds arrive far outside the parent tree's shadow

waveform.description: A daily pattern of long commutes, because the bird travels between feeding and roosting sites twice a day.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily and seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Koala

waveform.description: A low, flat rhythm with brief small lifts: long rest broken only by quiet feeding.

entries.closingLine: That makes the koala a strongly low-frequency system: narrow, economical and organised around processing rather than pursuit.

entries.name: Kodkod

waveform.description: A quiet repeating search rhythm with many small attempts in it.

entries.closingLine: Continuous secretive searching through dense cover makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Koi

modes.label: Rooting through the bottom • Growing all summer • Taking food from the hand
Motionless near the bottom • Not feeding at all • Metabolism at a fraction

waveform.description: A summer of movement lifted out of a long flat winter floor, because the cold state registers almost nothing.

entries.closingLine: Since a warm growing season and a cold non-feeding suppression are both obligatory and chemically different, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Komodo Dragon

waveform.description: A long low waiting floor, one vertical strike, and a slightly lower trail afterwards where the animal follows what it bit.

entries.closingLine: Because near-zero waiting supports one brief committed strike with a delayed result, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Koran Angelfish

modes.label: Dark blue with concentric white and pale arcs • Tiny and confined to a crevice or a small territory • Unrecognisable as the adult species
Olive-brown with fine blue speckling and blue-edged fins • Large, ranging over a reef • Holding and defending a territory as a pair

waveform.description: One level held, a single transition, and a different level held afterwards, because the change happens once and never reverses.

entries.closingLine: The pattern shift is therefore a change of social identity as much as of appearance, and because it happens once and irreversibly it operates as a phase-change system.

entries.name: Korean Rat Snake

modes.label: Pressing the edges of the belly scales against bark or masonry • Using the angle where the flat underside meets the flank as a purchase • Climbing vertical surfaces in a series of concertina pushes

waveform.description: A steady repeating rhythm of moderate excursions, because climbing is a series of similar pushes rather than a continuous glide.

entries.closingLine: Since climbing movements repeat continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Kori Bustard
entries.archetype: Sitting at the Ceiling of Flight

modes.label: Walking all day • Taking what appears • Flying only if forced

waveform.description: A slow, even walking rhythm across the whole day.

entries.closingLine: Slow and conservative throughout, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Kowari

waveform.description: A brisk even hunting rhythm through the night — many small captures rather than one large effort.

entries.closingLine: Because hunting is a steady repeated nightly cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Kuhl's Pipistrelle Bat

modes.label: Flying circuits around a lamp where insects have accumulated • Calling continuously and steepening the call rate as a target closes • Taking prey every few seconds in a concentration nothing natural supplies

waveform.description: A rapid pulse train that tightens abruptly at intervals, because the call rate accelerates into a buzz each time prey is closed on.

entries.closingLine: Since calls recur many times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Labyrinth Funnel Weaver

waveform.description: Long flat waiting broken by two very narrow spikes — the dash is over in a fraction of a second.

entries.closingLine: Because it needs both the long wait and the instant response, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Lace Monitor

modes.label: Flicking a deeply forked tongue to sample the air and ground • Delivering each tip to a separate opening in the roof of the mouth • Comparing the two readings to get a direction as well as a strength

waveform.description: A rapid even rhythm sustained throughout, because the tongue flicks continuously while the animal is searching.

entries.closingLine: Since flicks recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Lady Amherst's Pheasant
entries.archetype: Ground Scratcher Hiding a Courtship Cape

waveform.description: A long, level line of concealed foraging interrupted by a single sharp display.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long periods of concealed ground foraging and short bursts of lateral display.

entries.name: Ladybird Beetle

waveform.description: A mostly mid-level, gently undulating line with one sharp, narrow dip upward (high activity) in the middle, then a return to the steadier baseline, representing routine control punctuated by intense responses to outbreaks.

entries.closingLine: That combination of ongoing patrolling and focused surges makes the family a bimodal system with a mid-frequency baseline and a high-frequency outbreak response.

entries.name: Ladybird Spider

waveform.description: A long low baseline of hidden, burrowed life with a single sharp, narrow rise representing a brief, vivid surface display, then a return to concealment.

entries.closingLine: This makes the species a bimodal system: a predominantly low-frequency, burrowed state punctuated by short, high-frequency bursts of vivid activity for reproduction.

entries.name: Lake Oku Clawed Frog

waveform.description: An almost featureless line — a small aquatic animal in a small closed body of water with no seasons to speak of.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs slowly in a stable environment, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Lanternfly

modes.label: Driving a stylet bundle through bark into the phloem • Taking sap under the tree's own pressure • Voiding the excess sugar as honeydew

waveform.description: An almost unvarying line across the whole span, because the insect feeds continuously from a source that does not fluctuate.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Lappet-faced Vulture

waveform.description: Long flat searching with two short high plateaus — the feeding bouts are brief but intense rather than instantaneous.

entries.closingLine: Because it needs both the long unproductive search and the brief dominant feeding bout, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Lar Gibbon

modes.label: Hanging from one arm with a hook-shaped hand and a ball-and-socket wrist that lets the body rotate freely beneath it • Swinging forward under gravity and releasing at the top of the arc • Reaching the next branch with almost no muscular work because the body is falling rather than being pushed

waveform.description: A pure regular swing repeated without variation, because each arc is mechanically identical to the last.

entries.closingLine: Because the motion is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Large Flying Fox

modes.label: Feeding on fruit and nectar at one site then flying tens of kilometres to a distant roost • Carrying seeds and pollen in the gut and on the fur across that whole distance • Depositing them into forest patches no other animal connects

waveform.description: A strong nightly excursion repeated with a flat day between, because the whole system is one long flight out and back.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is nightly and colonial, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Large-billed Crow

waveform.description: A busy daytime foraging plateau between two quiet communal-roost nights.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: versatile daytime foraging and nightly communal roosting.

entries.name: Largehead Hairtail

waveform.description: Even, rolling oscillations around a mid level, representing continuous ribbonlike undulation without extreme bursts or long stillness.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is built around ongoing, rhythmic movement that the water “reads” as part of its own flow rather than as a discrete object, this is a mid-frequency swimmer: coordinated, repeatable, and tuned to continuous operation rather than extremes of stillness or explosive bursts.

entries.name: Largetooth Sawfish

waveform.description: A quiet unvarying trace — years spent in one stretch of river with very little happening at all.

entries.closingLine: Because everything in those years runs very slowly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Laughing Kookaburra

waveform.description: Loud grouped bursts at regular intervals with quiet stretches between them.

entries.closingLine: That makes the kookaburra a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and coordinated, where a group signal does work no individual could do alone.

entries.name: Laysan Albatross

waveform.description: Long flat stretches of wind-powered soaring, interrupted by busier spells at the colony.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: wind-powered foraging and a slow, bonded colony life.

entries.name: Leaf Beetle

waveform.description: Gentle, regular mid-height undulations showing repeated daytime bouts of plant-level feeding and hiding pauses, without extreme spikes or long flat reserves.

entries.closingLine: This creates a mid-frequency system built on rhythmic, plant-tuned foraging and constant attention to fine-grained details on the leaf surface.

entries.name: Leaf Scorpionfish

waveform.description: Long flat low-activity line of still camouflage, a single sharp spike for the strike, then a quick return to quiet stillness.

entries.closingLine: Because their whole body and behavior are built around long stretches of low, camouflaged waiting punctuated by brief, explosive strikes that immediately drop back to stillness, the leaf scorpionfish is a bimodal low–high frequency system.

entries.name: Leaf Sheep Sea Slug

waveform.description: A low, nearly flat line of continuous slow grazing on one alga.

entries.closingLine: The whole system is a single slow mode: sitting on the food, draining it, and borrowing its colour.

entries.name: Leaf-eating Slug

modes.label: A flattened shell-less body moving under litter and soil surface at night in humid conditions • A radula rasping through the soft stems of germinating seedlings at or just below ground level • The seedling severed and dying, so the damage is total for that plant rather than partial, and a field can fail before anything is visible above ground

waveform.description: A single nocturnal feeding period, because the animal works after dark in humid conditions and hides by day.

entries.closingLine: Because activity is nightly, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Leafcutter Ant

waveform.description: Even, repeating mid-amplitude ripples showing continuous, rhythmic traffic along the same paths rather than long dormancy or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: That makes the leafcutter ant a mid-frequency system: continuous, coordinated activity that turns repetition into durable structure.

entries.name: Leafy Seadragon

waveform.description: A gentle sway with no propulsive rhythm visible — the movement is made to look like water, not like an animal.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system substitutes a structural disguise for speed or defence, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Least Bittern
entries.archetype: Swaying in Time With the Reeds

modes.label: Straddling stems • Bill up • Rocking with the wind

waveform.description: A gentle continuous sway with no sudden movement in it.

entries.closingLine: Almost entirely stationary except for that sway, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Least Weasel
entries.archetype: Narrow Body Built to Follow Voles Underground

waveform.description: Sharp hunting bursts repeated day and night, each followed by a short rest.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: HIGH hunting bursts separated by LOW recovery.

entries.name: Leatherback Sea Turtle

waveform.description: Two clearly separated operating levels with a visible switch between them — the same animal running at a different setting depending on the water it is in.

entries.closingLine: This is not a seasonal coat or a growth stage but an active reconfiguration of the same system to the context it is in, which is why it is an adaptive system.

entries.name: Leopard Cat

modes.label: A small wild cat drawn into early farming villages by the rodents that grain stores attract • Remains from Chinese Neolithic sites showing the species living commensally alongside people thousands of years ago • The relationship ending there, with no domestication, so the cats stayed wild while the same process elsewhere produced the domestic cat

waveform.description: A nocturnal cycle without any long-term change, because the animal's pattern has stayed the same throughout.

entries.closingLine: Because the pattern runs nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Leopard Gecko
entries.archetype: Eyelids, No Toe Pads, Fat in the Tail

waveform.description: A low economical line with small steady variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: economical, ground-bound and built around storage.

entries.name: Leopard Lacewing

modes.label: Larvae feeding on passion vines whose tissues carry cyanogenic compounds • Those compounds sequestered rather than excreted and retained through pupation into the adult • Bright orange and black wings advertising the retained toxicity to anything that has tasted one before

waveform.description: A steady unhurried rhythm, because the butterfly flies slowly and openly rather than evading anything.

entries.closingLine: Because the accumulation runs across the life cycle, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Leopard Seal

waveform.description: A mid-level patrol baseline with repeated sharp downward spikes for brief, intense hunting bursts along the ice edge.

entries.closingLine: This combination of sustained patrolling around productive edges and brief, high-intensity attacks makes the leopard seal a bimodal system built on a mid-frequency search rhythm punctuated by high-frequency strikes.

entries.name: Leopard Shark

modes.label: Hovering over soft sediment and applying suction to extract buried prey • Taking the exposed siphons of clams and the tails of innkeeper worms rather than the whole animal • Returning to the same flats as those parts regenerate

waveform.description: A steady repeated rhythm of feeding passes, because the shark works the same ground over and over.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is repeated, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Leopard Slug

modes.label: Circling and following a partner's slime trail for hours • Lowering together on a single mucus thread • Exchanging sperm through entwined everted organs

waveform.description: A long slow approach rising to a single suspended peak and subsiding, because everything builds toward one prolonged event.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a season, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Leopard Tortoise

waveform.description: A shallow unvarying pace that never rises and never stops.

entries.closingLine: Armour, fermentation and unhurried travel make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Leopoldi Stingray

modes.label: Settling under sand • Breathing through the top • Trapping under the disc

waveform.description: An almost unbroken low line, the trace of an animal whose normal state is being indistinguishable from the riverbed.

entries.closingLine: Because everything is slow, benthic and continuous, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Lesser Adjutant Stork
entries.archetype: Limited by Trees, Not by Water

modes.label: Striding shallows • Taking what appears • Nesting very high

waveform.description: A slow deliberate wading rhythm with few sudden events.

entries.closingLine: Slow and deliberate, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Lesser Banded Hornet

modes.label: A guard detecting a threat near the nest and releasing alarm pheromone from the sting apparatus • That chemical settling on the intruder itself rather than dispersing generally • Every hornet arriving afterwards directing its attack at whatever carries the mark rather than searching for a threat

waveform.description: A busy baseline with an abrupt violent spike, because ordinary traffic continues until an alarm converts it instantly.

entries.closingLine: Because the response unfolds in seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Lesser Bird-of-paradise

waveform.description: Long low stretches of preparation with brief, sharp peaks where the bird executes concentrated courtship displays.

entries.closingLine: Because the bird’s biology is built around long periods of hidden preparation punctuated by short, high-intensity, highly organized performances, it operates as a bimodal system with a low-frequency maintenance mode and a high-frequency display mode.

entries.name: Lesser Grison

waveform.description: An active mid-level rhythm with no long pauses.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: persistently active across every kind of ground rather than fast on any one.

entries.name: Lesser Hedgehog Tenrec

modes.label: Searching leaf litter • Curling up • Shutting down for months

waveform.description: Active stretches separated by long flat periods of shutdown.

entries.closingLine: Slow, conservative and reserve-based, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Lesser Kudu

waveform.description: Two feeding periods bracketing the heat with a quiet middle — a routine set by temperature and by when it is safe to move.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on continuous listening and short cautious feeding movements, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Lesser Mouse-deer

waveform.description: A quiet foraging line broken by a brief freeze and a sharp escape burst.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: secretive foraging along forest paths and explosive escape into cover.

entries.name: Lesser Sandeel

modes.label: Shoaling in open water over sandbanks by day • Driving headfirst into coarse sand with a pointed snout and elongated body • Spending nights and whole winter months buried in the sediment

waveform.description: Activity alternating with long flat depressed stretches, because the animal is either in open water or inside the seabed.

entries.closingLine: Since emergence recurs daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Lesser Whistling Duck

modes.label: Male and female indistinguishable in plumage, with no display difference between them • Both birds incubating in turn rather than the female alone • Both escorting and defending the ducklings for months after hatching

waveform.description: A steady alternating rhythm, because two birds exchange duties continuously rather than one carrying it.

entries.closingLine: Because the alternation is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Lichen Katydid
entries.archetype: Pale Branching Outline Matched to Lichen

waveform.description: A flat pale daytime line rising into night activity and calling.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: daytime lichen masquerade and night activity.

entries.name: Lilac-breasted Roller

waveform.description: A still perched line broken by a steep rolling descent.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long still watch and a brief, steep, highly visible commitment.

entries.name: Limpkin

modes.label: A long bill whose tip curves slightly to the right and whose mandibles leave a gap along their length rather than closing flush • That curve matching the right-handed spiral of an apple snail shell, so the tip follows the whorl inward • The muscle holding the snail into its shell cut and the body drawn out whole, leaving the shell undamaged and the bird able to take another immediately

waveform.description: A steady deliberate rhythm, because the bird works methodically through snails one after another.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is steady, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Lion-tailed Macaque

waveform.description: A regular fill-and-move rhythm — each cycle is a visit to a tree and a retreat to process what was taken.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding runs as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Lionfish

waveform.description: A slow unhurried approach line ending in one very sharp strike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an unhurried protected cruise and a brief engulfing event.

entries.name: Little Auk
entries.archetype: A Throat Pouch Full of Copepods

waveform.description: Bursts of short provisioning trips separated by a long, slower self-feeding trip.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: rapid provisioning trips and longer restorative trips.

entries.name: Little Barrier Giant Weta

waveform.description: A very slow browsing rhythm with no urgency anywhere in it.

entries.closingLine: Slow heavy browsing makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Little Blue Heron

modes.label: A juvenile in entirely white plumage, indistinguishable at distance from a snowy egret, foraging within egret flocks and tolerated by them
An adult in slate blue plumage, excluded from egret flocks and foraging alone in shallow water with slow deliberate movements

waveform.description: An active social rhythm giving way to a slow solitary one, because the bird changes from a flock member to a lone hunter.

entries.closingLine: The two states are different systems: one social and dependent on being mistaken for something else, the other solitary and dependent on acquired skill, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Little Dragonfish

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing slow, cautious bouts of movement separated by long periods close to the seafloor.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a low-frequency system: dense, conservative, and organized around careful seafloor walking instead of rapid bursts or continuous cruising.

entries.name: Little Egret

waveform.description: Frequent short dashes and strikes, repeated at an active working pace.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: active, rhythmic and built on repeatedly manufacturing short-lived advantages rather than on patience.

entries.name: Little Owl

modes.label: Watching from a low perch in open farmland at dusk and by day • Dropping onto the ground and then running after prey on long legs • Taking beetles, earthworms and insects as well as small mammals

waveform.description: A watchful rhythm broken by regular short drops, because the bird perches and then goes to the ground repeatedly.

entries.closingLine: Since hunting drops recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Little Wood-Satyr

modes.label: Resting with wings closed and small ringed eyespots along the outer margin • Having birds strike at those spots rather than at the body • Flying off with a notched wing and an intact thorax

waveform.description: A quiet line with small brief disturbances, because the animal flies weakly and the attacks it survives are minor events.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Llama

waveform.description: A low steady line: the same modest output held over long distances.

entries.closingLine: That makes the llama a low-frequency system: economical, sure-footed and built for sustained effort on very little input.

entries.name: Loggerhead Sea Turtle

waveform.description: One enormous slow swell across the whole frame, rising and settling again — a rhythm whose period is years, not hours.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is built on cheap movement, deep patience and a horizon measured in decades, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Loggerhead Shrike
entries.archetype: A Thorn Standing In for Talons

waveform.description: Long flat stretches of perched scanning broken by sharp drops onto prey and a brief handling phase.

entries.closingLine: That produces a bimodal system: long low-frequency spells of scanning from perches, punctuated by fast, violent strikes and the handling that follows.

entries.name: Long-eared Hedgehog

waveform.description: Active foraging at night, with a long burrow rest through the day.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a sheltered daytime burrow and night-time foraging.

entries.name: Long-eared Jerboa
entries.archetype: Ears Tuned to Insects in the Dark

waveform.description: Long quiet daytime burrow periods with a burst of fast, erratic night foraging.

entries.closingLine: The biology of this species is poorly studied, but the pattern is clear: a bimodal system of long sheltered rest and short, fast, sound-guided hunting.

entries.name: Long-eared Owl
entries.archetype: Wings Quiet Enough to Hear Past

waveform.description: Slow quartering flight at almost no acoustic or energetic cost.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, cheap, patient flight built around detecting something very quiet.

entries.name: Long-jawed Orb Weaver
entries.archetype: Stretched Flat Beside an Open-Hub Orb

waveform.description: Daily bouts of web building and trapping between long, flat resting spells.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: renewed trapping and stick-like rest.

entries.name: Long-legged Fly

modes.label: A visual system detecting the approach of a looming object in a few thousandths of a second • Take-off initiated before the image has been fully resolved, using a coarse early signal rather than a complete one • The fly airborne within about five milliseconds of the stimulus, faster than any deliberate response could be assembled

waveform.description: A jittery baseline with instantaneous vertical departures, because the escape is faster than anything else the animal does.

entries.closingLine: Because the response is measured in milliseconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Long-legged Fly

waveform.description: Repeated sharp spikes returning quickly to a light perch baseline, showing rapid bursts of motion separated by very short pauses.

entries.closingLine: This makes them a high-frequency system: fast, reactive, and built around many quick aerial maneuvers in a tight space.

entries.name: Long-legged Spiny Lobster

modes.label: Sheltering by day in a crevice or cave used repeatedly rather than occupied once • Walking out at night on long slender legs to forage across distances a short-legged animal could not cover • Returning to the same shelter before dawn rather than sheltering wherever it ends up

waveform.description: A single broad nightly excursion with a flat day either side, because the whole pattern is one outward and return trip.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Long-nosed Bandicoot

waveform.description: A quiet hidden day followed by a jagged night of repeated small digs.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: daytime concealment in a covered nest and nocturnal searching and digging for buried food.

entries.name: Long-nosed Potoroo

waveform.description: A dense run of short digging pulses through the night, each one small, none of them dominant.

entries.closingLine: Because value arrives in many modest, regularly spaced returns rather than in reserves or bursts, this is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Long-spined Porcupinefish

modes.label: Drifting slowly • Crushing shells • Swelling if seized

waveform.description: A slow low drift interrupted twice by short lifts, because the inflation is brief and cannot be held.

entries.closingLine: Because everything else runs slowly, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Long-spined Sea Urchin

modes.label: Grazing the rock • Sensing shadow • Swinging the spines toward it

waveform.description: A very shallow slow undulation, the trace of an animal whose fastest movement is a spine turning.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at the pace of scraping rock, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Long-tailed Chinchilla

waveform.description: Activity concentrated at each end of the day with a quiet middle — the shape of a crepuscular animal's timetable.
