entries.closingLine: Because the cycle of feeding, grooming and sheltering runs steadily each day, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Long-tailed Macaque

modes.label: Working whatever the site offers • Copying what pays • Testing the boundary

waveform.description: An uneven opportunistic rhythm where no two peaks match, because each is a different opening being taken.

entries.closingLine: Because the foraging and copying run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Long-tailed Manakin

waveform.description: A mostly mid-level, gently undulating line for ongoing practice, with one sharp narrow dip-and-peak burst representing a brief, intense coordinated display.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a bimodal system with a rhythmic mid-frequency base and a triggered high-frequency show mode.

entries.name: Long-tailed Widowbird
entries.archetype: A Seasonal Tail Grown for the Grassland Air

waveform.description: A steady flocking season giving way to a breeding season of repeated display flights.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-change system: a flocking non-breeding season and a display-driven breeding season.

entries.name: Long-wattled Umbrellabird

waveform.description: Repeated deep pulses at an even spacing — a display that works by repetition rather than by any single effort.

entries.closingLine: Because the display and the fruit-eating between it run on a steady daily rhythm, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Longhorn Cowfish

modes.label: Holding the trunk completely rigid inside a fused bony carapace • Sculling with fins alone in a hovering, precise way • Blowing jets of water into sand to uncover prey

waveform.description: A very regular low-amplitude pattern with no sharp features, because the animal moves slowly and never accelerates.

entries.closingLine: Since fin strokes recur continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Longhorned Orbweaver

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing mostly steady, passive operation with minor variation as conditions change.

entries.closingLine: Because this system relies on continuous, low-effort presence rather than bursts of movement, it operates as a single, low-frequency pattern of passive, always-on deterrence.

entries.name: Longnose Gar
entries.archetype: A Swim Bladder Used as a Lung

waveform.description: A drifting still line broken by one lateral sweep.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: near-motionless drifting and one lateral sweep.

entries.name: Longspine Snipefish

modes.label: A long tubular snout with a tiny toothless mouth at the end • The fish hanging head-down over the bottom and drawing individual prey items in by suction • Small crustaceans taken one at a time from between sand grains and among invertebrates where a wide mouth cannot reach

waveform.description: A rapid repeating rhythm of small suctions, because the fish takes one tiny item at a time continuously.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Lord Howe Island Stick Insect
entries.archetype: Night Feeder, Day Cluster in the Hollow

waveform.description: A long still daytime shelter phase rising into a steady night of leaf feeding.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: communal daytime sheltering and nocturnal feeding.

entries.name: Lord Howe Woodhen
entries.archetype: A Flightless Rail Probing the Litter

waveform.description: A steady walking rhythm through the day with calling peaks early and late.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a steady daily round of foraging on the ground, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Louse
entries.archetype: A Whole Life Held to One Host

waveform.description: A steady resident line on the host, broken by one brief spike when hosts touch and lice cross over.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady resident life on the host and brief transfers during contact.

entries.name: Lowland Anoa

waveform.description: A steady modest rhythm — browsing and moving through forest at an unvarying pace.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding and moving run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Lowland Streaked Tenrec

waveform.description: A fast pulse train running continuously under ordinary foraging.

entries.closingLine: Continuous foraging with continuous signalling makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Lumpfish

waveform.description: Water moving hard against a body that barely shifts at all.

entries.closingLine: Low power output, high persistence and a strategy of holding rather than moving make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Luna Moth

waveform.description: A short intense run of flight that fades as the store is used up.

entries.closingLine: A fixed store, a short window and no intake make this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Luzon Garden Spider

modes.label: A large female sitting at the hub of a web she built and maintains, feeding, growing and producing eggs
A male a small fraction of her mass, barely feeding, wandering in search of females and often not surviving the mating

waveform.description: A calm large-scale rhythm interrupted by small rapid episodes, because the two sexes operate at entirely different scales.

entries.closingLine: The asymmetry is not a curiosity of size but two entirely different solutions to what an individual of each sex should spend its life doing, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Lycaenid Butterfly

modes.label: Secreting sugar and amino acids from a gland on the abdomen • Attracting ants that feed on it and stay • Being defended by those ants against wasps and predators for the whole larval period

waveform.description: A long even line with a single modest rise, because the relationship runs continuously and quietly through the larval stage.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs once a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Macaroni Penguin

waveform.description: An active foraging rhythm alternating with a crowded colonial phase.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long distant foraging and a crowded, deliberately reduced breeding phase.

entries.name: Madagascar Day Gecko
entries.archetype: Sticking by Direction, Not by Glue

modes.label: Running up glass • Holding • Peeling off in one direction

waveform.description: A quick daytime rhythm of running, stopping and basking.

entries.closingLine: This is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Madagascar Ground Boa

waveform.description: A long flat floor, then a sharp strike that decays over several steps — the constriction takes minutes rather than an instant.

entries.closingLine: Because near-zero waiting alternates with a brief total physical commitment, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Madagascar Hognose Snake

waveform.description: Repeated digging efforts of similar size through the day — work done in many modest pushes rather than one.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts steady mechanical work into a stream of modest finds, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Madagascar Pochard

waveform.description: A regular dive-and-surface rhythm — repeated shallow descents through the day rather than any sustained effort.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding runs as a steady repeated daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Magellanic Penguin
entries.archetype: Wing-Driven Diver Returning to a Dug Burrow

waveform.description: Alternating stretches of burrow guarding and active foraging trips at sea.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: wing-driven foraging trips and patient burrow attendance.

entries.name: Magnetic Termite
entries.archetype: Flat Mound Turned Edge-On to Noon

waveform.description: Dry-season pulses of harvesting drop into a long, quiet wet season inside the mound, then resume.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-change system: dry-season harvesting and wet-season life inside the mound.

entries.name: Magnificent Bird-of-paradise

waveform.description: A long low baseline of ordinary activity, a single sharp high crest for the aligned display, then a return to low-level activity.

entries.closingLine: Because this system relies on a sharp shift from low-key, economical living to short, intense, fully aligned performance whenever the opportunity arises, it is best described as a bimodal pattern with a low baseline and a triggered high-frequency display mode.

entries.name: Magnificent Frigatebird
entries.archetype: A Seabird That Cannot Touch the Sea

waveform.description: A low continuous soaring rhythm that never reaches the ground.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: almost costless, continuous and with no fallback.

entries.name: Magnificent Riflebird

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line for routine canopy activity with one sharp, narrow dip upward (higher activity) representing the concentrated display burst before returning to the regular rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because routine canopy movement and concentrated performance are both structurally necessary and distinct operating modes, the riflebird is best understood as a bimodal system with a mid-frequency baseline and a high-frequency display burst built around its velvet stage.

entries.name: Magnificent Sea Anemone

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing a fixed base of activity with small, continuous fluctuations as tentacles pulse and partners move around a stable anchor point.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole biology is built around staying rooted, spending slowly, and sustaining a shared refuge over years, this is a single-mode, low-frequency system.

entries.name: Magpie Goose

modes.label: Wading • Digging • Always able to leave

waveform.description: A steady working rhythm that is never interrupted by a moult.

entries.closingLine: Continuous unhurried foraging makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Mahi-mahi
entries.archetype: Live Fast, Under the Floating Debris

waveform.description: Sustained high-rate output with no low interval.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: fast-growing, fast-living and continuously active.

entries.name: Mainland Serow

waveform.description: Two working periods at the cool ends of the day over a steady baseline — the profile of an animal that walks the same ground repeatedly.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts repeated movement over known ground into steady returns, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Malachite Butterfly

modes.label: Working rotting fruit • Probing dung and carrion • Rarely visiting a flower

waveform.description: An unhurried gliding wave with long shallow arcs, because a butterfly working fallen fruit has nowhere it needs to be quickly.

entries.closingLine: Since that action repeats at one unhurried tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Malachite Kingfisher

waveform.description: A gently swaying perched line broken by short sharp drops.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a compensating perched watch and a very short committed drop.

entries.name: Malagasy Giant Rat
entries.archetype: A Pair-Held Burrow in Sandy Forest

waveform.description: Quiet daylight underground, a modest night-time foraging rise, then retreat.

entries.closingLine: Because it rests on patient, burrow-centred life and slow breeding, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Malayan Box Turtle

modes.label: A hinge across the plastron allowing both lobes to be drawn up against the carapace • The shell closing completely, with no opening left at either end once the head and limbs are inside • A defence that is total against a predator and useless against a hand, so the animal simply shuts and is picked up

waveform.description: A very flat line with occasional closures, because the animal moves slowly and shuts when disturbed.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Malayan Horned Frog

modes.label: Sitting in litter • Waiting • One short lunge

waveform.description: Almost no movement at all across long stretches of the night.

entries.closingLine: Sitting motionless for hours makes this a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Malayan Porcupine

modes.label: A cluster of short hollow open-ended quills on the tail, distinct from the long solid defensive spines • Those tail quills vibrated rapidly to produce a loud dry rattle when the animal is threatened • The warning delivered first, with the animal turning, stamping and reversing into the threat only if the rattle does not work

waveform.description: A single nightly activity period, because the animal forages after dark and rests through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Malayan Tapir

waveform.description: A quiet trace with small evenly spaced lifts — a night of slow browsing rather than any concentrated effort.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs quietly and slowly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Malayan Tiger

waveform.description: A low steady line — long distances covered slowly, with a kill only every several days.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs slowly across a wide area, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Malaysian Field Rat

modes.label: Populations in oil palm plantations rising wherever predators are absent, on a food supply that never stops • Barn owls provided with nest boxes establishing at high density in the same plantations • Each owl pair taking a sustained toll that holds the rat population below the level at which damage matters

waveform.description: A rising population line progressively pushed down, because the predator pressure builds while the food supply does not change.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over seasons, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Malaysian Forest Scorpion

modes.label: Compounds in the outer layer of the cuticle absorbing ultraviolet light and re-emitting it as visible blue-green • That fluorescence present in every scorpion examined and appearing only after the cuticle has fully hardened following a moult • The function still unresolved after decades, with proposals including light detection through the whole body surface, protection from ultraviolet damage and prey attraction, none of them established

waveform.description: A single nocturnal activity period, because the animal emerges from its burrow after dark and returns before light.

entries.closingLine: Because activity is nightly, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mallard

modes.label: Pumping water through the bill • Straining seeds and invertebrates on comb-like lamellae • Upending to reach the bottom in shallow water

waveform.description: A fine, rapid, low-amplitude oscillation with no large features, because the bill works at a fast steady rate the whole time.

entries.closingLine: Since the bill cycles many times a second, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Malleefowl

waveform.description: A gently oscillating mid-level line, showing regular small corrections around a stable target rather than long waits or sharp bursts.

entries.closingLine: That makes the system a mid-frequency pattern: continuous, cyclical corrections around a target rather than extremes of stillness or sudden expenditure.

entries.name: Manatee

waveform.description: A very low unvarying line with no peaks anywhere along it.

entries.closingLine: Very low output and constant grazing make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mandarin Duck
entries.archetype: A Sail Raised From a Single Feather

waveform.description: A plain low line rising into a display season and falling back.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a short ornamented season and a long plain one.

entries.name: Mandarinfish
entries.archetype: Blue Made From Pigment, Not Structure

waveform.description: A slow deliberate reef-bottom rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, conspicuous and chemically protected.

entries.name: Mandrill

waveform.description: A steady mid band carrying the colour signal, broken once by a single very tall spike where a challenge is actually fought.

entries.closingLine: Because a continuous public signal handles almost everything while a rare violent settlement stands behind it, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Maned Sloth

waveform.description: A nearly flat line — intake, movement and output all proceed at the same very low rate.

entries.closingLine: Because intake, processing and movement all run at the same very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Maned Wolf

waveform.description: A long evening of walking with regular modest pounces — repeated small commitments rather than one decisive event.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on continuous walking search with many modest returns, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Mangrove Crab

waveform.description: A low, steady line with small undulations, showing a stable, continuously maintained defensive base with only minor routine fluctuations.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: anchored, shelter-centric, and built around the quiet stability of a mud fortress in a restless environment.

entries.name: Mangrove Horseshoe Crab

modes.label: Accumulating tetrodotoxin and saxitoxin from bacteria and diet in mangrove sediment • Concentrating those toxins in the eggs and in some tissues • Producing a clutch that poisons anything eating it rather than one that is merely hidden

waveform.description: A slow shallow swell, because toxin accumulates and is committed to eggs over a long seasonal cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because reproduction is seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mangrove Monitor

waveform.description: A steady searching rhythm along a tidal margin.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steadily active along a boundary and dispersed by accident.

entries.name: Mangrove Snake
entries.archetype: Fangs at the Back, So Hold On

modes.label: Climbing after dark • Seizing • Chewing the venom in

waveform.description: Slow deliberate climbing with rare deliberate captures.

entries.closingLine: Slow and deliberate, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mangshan Pit Viper

waveform.description: An almost dead-flat line with two extremely narrow spikes — days of stillness and a strike measured in milliseconds.

entries.closingLine: Because it needs both the long sensing wait and the instant aimed strike, it is bimodal.

entries.name: Manta Ray

waveform.description: A slow regular wingbeat rhythm with no spikes — the same motion for travel and for feeding.

entries.closingLine: Because scale is carried by continuous low-intensity intake, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mantidfly
entries.archetype: Mantis Arms, Wasp Colours, Spider Nursery

waveform.description: A long hidden larval floor rising into an active adult phase.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long concealed parasitic stage and an active disguised adult one.

entries.name: Mantled Howler Monkey

waveform.description: A settled low line lifted by two collective bouts of calling.

entries.closingLine: Slow digestion and a cheap broadcast make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Manx Shearwater
entries.archetype: Shearing the Wave Tops on Stiff Wings

waveform.description: A steady rise and fall like banking flight between wave crests and troughs.

entries.closingLine: Because the system rests on low-cost sustained flight, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Map Butterfly

modes.label: A spring form emerging from overwintered pupae, orange with black markings, flying in April and May
A summer form emerging from pupae formed in long days, black with a white band and looking like a different species entirely

waveform.description: Two distinct episodes of different height and shape, because the two generations are genuinely different insects.

entries.closingLine: The two forms are separated by a threshold rather than by a gradient, so it operates as a phase-change system.

entries.name: Marabou Stork

waveform.description: A flat unhurried line: a bird that spends most of the day doing very little.

entries.closingLine: That makes the marabou a low-frequency system: slow, cheap to run and built to accept what everything else has already passed over.

entries.name: Marbled Cat
entries.archetype: Long Tail Balancing a Canopy Hunter

waveform.description: Steady activity through the day and dusk, easing off into the night.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, cautious hunting through the forest layers.

entries.name: Marbled Godwit

waveform.description: An even walking cadence with a probe at every step.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: a repeated walk-and-probe cycle whose returns come entirely from what the tip can reach and read.

entries.name: Marbled Newt
entries.archetype: Each Egg Folded Into a Leaf

waveform.description: A long quiet terrestrial stretch and an active aquatic season.

entries.closingLine: That makes it an adaptive system: a single animal running a slow terrestrial state and an active aquatic one, switching between them as conditions allow.

entries.name: Marbled Orbweaver

waveform.description: A low, gently rippling line showing long, steady, low-output vigilance with tiny fluctuations as the web stays under tension.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a single-mode, low-frequency system: a patient, tension-held listening state that quietly converts time into opportunities.

entries.name: Marbled Salamander
entries.archetype: Laying in a Pond That Is Not There Yet

waveform.description: A long still guarding line rising into an early active larval phase.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a long still terrestrial wait and an early aquatic advantage.

entries.name: Marco Polo Sheep
entries.archetype: Wide-Flaring Horns Crossing the High Pamir

waveform.description: Steady ranging over high ground, broken by a sustained flight run.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: wide-ranging grazing and long-distance flight.

entries.name: Margay

waveform.description: Frequent climbing and hunting movements of similar magnitude — a night spent working three dimensions rather than two.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts continuous three-dimensional movement into steady returns, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Marginated Tortoise
entries.archetype: Flared Shell on a Two-Season Year

waveform.description: A buried winter line rising into a long active season with a summer dip.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an active season of basking and grazing and a long winter dormancy.

entries.name: Marine Iguana

waveform.description: Two working excursions separated by long flat recovery — the dives are bounded by something other than appetite.

entries.closingLine: Because two different operating states alternate under a hard physical threshold, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Markhor

waveform.description: Two long working periods at the cool ends of the day — a routine set by heat and by where the safe ground is.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on a steady daily routine with regular structured contests, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Marmalade Hoverfly

waveform.description: A long seasonal swell of arrival, presence and departure.

entries.closingLine: Sustained long-range movement and constant flower work make this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Marsh Deer

waveform.description: A slow deliberate wading rhythm through soft ground.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, deliberate movement made possible by the foot rather than by strength.

entries.name: Marsh Frog

waveform.description: A quiet daytime line breaking into dense repeated calling.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a quiet waiting baseline and an intense collective broadcast.

entries.name: Marsh Mongoose

waveform.description: A steady searching rhythm along a water margin.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, tactile and confined to a boundary.

entries.name: Marsh Tit

modes.label: Holding one territory with the same mate for life • Knowing every cache site and cavity within it • Refusing to leave even in the hardest winter

waveform.description: A remarkably even line across the whole span, because the bird does the same thing in the same place all year.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Martial Eagle

waveform.description: A high soaring band broken by one steep descent that overshoots below the line — the dive ends lower than it began.

entries.closingLine: Because a very cheap high search funds rare committed strikes, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Marvellous Spatuletail

waveform.description: A mostly steady mid-level line with one sharp, narrow spike for a brief, intense courtship display before returning to baseline activity.

entries.closingLine: Because its life alternates between a steady operational rhythm that funds the ornament and short, expensive bursts of controlled display, the system is best understood as bimodal with a mid-frequency baseline and high-frequency display mode.

entries.name: Mary River Turtle

waveform.description: A near-flat line — an animal that can remain in one state for days at a time without interruption.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Masked Owl
entries.archetype: One Ear Higher Than the Other

modes.label: Drop • Talons into cover • Back to the perch

waveform.description: Long flat listening stretches broken by very brief strikes.

entries.closingLine: That is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Masked Water Tyrant

waveform.description: Even, medium-height ripples: repeated short excursions from a stable level representing regular forays out and back.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole system is built around these repeated mid-length cycles rather than long stillness or extreme bursts, the Masked Water Tyrant operates as a single, mid-frequency pattern.

entries.name: Mata Mata

waveform.description: A long motionless floor and one vertical event — the strike has no approach and no follow-through.

entries.closingLine: Because near-total stillness supports one instantaneous capture, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Matschie's Tree Kangaroo

waveform.description: A quiet low trace with almost no variation — a leaf diet leaves no room for peaks.

entries.closingLine: Because intake and movement both run slowly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: May Beetle

modes.label: Underground • Chewing roots • Counting out the years
Emerging together • Flying at dusk • Six weeks and done

waveform.description: A long dead-flat floor ending in one square block of activity, because the emergence is a plateau with vertical walls rather than a peak.

entries.closingLine: Because years of hidden low-cost accumulation are discharged into one brief synchronised flight, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Meadow Froghopper

waveform.description: Long low baseline of sheltered, minimal activity with a single sharp spike representing a rapid jump, then a quick return to low output.

entries.closingLine: The system therefore runs on a low-frequency shelter-and-feed mode anchored in foam or stillness, punctuated by high-frequency bursts of jump power when timing and danger demand it, making this a bimodal low-and-high system.

entries.name: Meadow Vole

waveform.description: A low baseline with repeated moderate rises, showing long sheltered periods punctuated by regular, coordinated foraging runs along the runway network.

entries.closingLine: This creates a bimodal pattern: a low-frequency, burrow-centered reserve mode anchored in cover and stores, and a mid-frequency, runway-based operating mode that repeats short, timed movements rather than continuous roaming.

entries.name: Mealworm Beetle

modes.label: Larvae chewing polystyrene and passing it into the gut • Gut bacteria depolymerising the long carbon chains rather than the insect itself digesting them • Part of the carbon leaving as carbon dioxide and part incorporated into the larva, with the rest excreted as altered fragments

waveform.description: A slow shallow progression, because the process is gradual and continuous rather than event-driven.

entries.closingLine: Because the process runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Medicinal Leech

modes.label: Attaching with a rear sucker and cutting a Y-shaped incision with three jaws • Secreting hirudin and anaesthetic into the wound • Taking several times its own weight and digesting it over months

waveform.description: A very long flat line broken by one broad event, because a single meal supports the animal for months afterwards.

entries.closingLine: Since feeds are months apart, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mediterranean Feather Star

waveform.description: A mostly low line punctuated by several moderate, rounded waves, showing long anchored periods with repeated bouts of filtering and gentle repositioning.

entries.closingLine: Because its structure supports a clear alternation between low-expenditure anchoring and repeated moderate-effort feeding and repositioning, the Mediterranean feather star operates as a bimodal system with a low baseline and a mid-frequency active mode.

entries.name: Mediterranean House Gecko

modes.label: Holding the wall • Watching the light • Short dashes

waveform.description: A dead-level hold broken by brief identical upward flicks, because the animal alternates between gripping and one short dash.

entries.closingLine: Because that rhythm is continuous and cheap through the dark hours, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Medium Ground Finch

waveform.description: A wet-season burst of breeding and easy foraging, then a slow, lean dry-season trough.

entries.closingLine: Because the system switches between easy wet-season breeding and a lean, selective dry season, it is a phase-change system.

entries.name: Meerkat

waveform.description: An even repeating group rhythm with regular handovers.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, continuous and shared by rotation.

entries.name: Melipona Stingless Bee

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line showing continuous colony activity, with two sharp, narrow dips-and-peaks representing brief, intense resin sealing responses layered onto the stable background.

entries.closingLine: The result is a multimodal operating pattern: a rhythmic foraging-and-building core, long-lived resin architecture that persists across seasons, and fast local bursts of resin use that reconfigure access when needed.

entries.name: Merriam's Kangaroo Rat

waveform.description: Steady night foraging broken by sharp leaps away from predators.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady nocturnal harvesting and brief explosive escapes.

entries.name: Mexican Beaded Lizard

modes.label: Sheltered • Fasting • Most of the year

waveform.description: A long flat trough with one raised section — months of nothing and a short season of activity.

entries.closingLine: Because it runs a long dormant state and a short foraging one and needs both, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Mexican Mole Lizard
entries.archetype: Forelimbs Only, Head First Through Soil

waveform.description: Near-surface activity in the morning and evening with a deep, inactive dip through the heat of the day.

entries.closingLine: That yields a bimodal system of near-surface foraging and deeper inactivity.

entries.name: Mexican Paper Wasp

modes.label: Running an open-comb colony through the wet season • Foraging, building and rearing brood on a single comb • Holding rank through dominance interactions among the foundresses

Abandoning the nest entirely as the dry season begins • Flying to traditional aggregation sites, often at different elevations • Clustering there in large numbers of future queens until conditions return

waveform.description: Active colony life alternating with a long flat depressed stretch, because the wasps genuinely leave and stop being a colony.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two states, making this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Middle East Blind Mole-rat

waveform.description: Bouts of tunnel digging rising out of periods of rest in the deep nest.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: productive tunnelling and long rest in the deep nest.

entries.name: Migratory Locust

waveform.description: A stable baseline that changes sharply after a density threshold.

entries.closingLine: This is best understood as a phase-change system: the important event is the threshold where the rules of the whole system change.

entries.name: Military Macaw

modes.label: A bird able to preen every feather on its body with its own bill except those on its head and neck • Partners working through each other's head feathers, removing parasites and realigning barbs that cannot be reached alone • The exchange repeated daily, so the only part of the plumage that cannot be self-maintained is maintained by someone else

waveform.description: A regular daily rhythm, because the exchange happens repeatedly and reliably between the same birds.

entries.closingLine: Because the exchange is daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Milk Snake

modes.label: Moving at night • Wearing a warning it cannot back • Constricting what it finds

waveform.description: A slow even nocturnal rhythm with small regular variation, because nothing this animal does is abrupt.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs slowly and nocturnally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mimic Octopus

waveform.description: A shifting exploratory line repeatedly interrupted by sharp changes of state.

entries.closingLine: That makes it an adaptive system: one body selecting between operating states as the situation changes.

entries.name: Mint Moth

modes.label: Flying in sunshine • Spinning a mint leaf shut • Feeding inside it

waveform.description: A quick light flutter of small even peaks, because the animal is tiny and works in short sunlit bursts between rests.

entries.closingLine: Because the feeding and flying run at one quick, light, repeated tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: minute pirate bug

waveform.description: Long flat low-activity stretches broken by brief, sharp spikes representing sudden ambush strikes and rapid return to stillness.

entries.closingLine: The system is built around a low-frequency waiting and stalking baseline punctuated by high-frequency, high-intensity ambush events, so the minute pirate bug is best described as a bimodal low–high ambush-strike system.

entries.name: Mirror Spider

waveform.description: A mostly low, flat line for the spider’s blended state, with a brief sharp rise and fall representing rapid shifts in mirror patch expansion when attention needs to be managed.

entries.closingLine: Because its core architecture supports two context-tuned visual modes rather than one fixed camouflage, this is an adaptive system with a low baseline and a fast, attention-managing shift.

entries.name: Mississippi Kite

waveform.description: A smooth continuous soaring rhythm with no descents.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: continuous, economical and entirely aerial.

entries.name: Mistle Thrush

modes.label: Claiming a single heavily fruiting holly, yew or mistletoe clump in autumn • Driving off every other bird that approaches it for months • Living off it into spring

waveform.description: A persistent pattern of similar strong events, because the bird is repeatedly driving off intruders throughout the season.

entries.closingLine: Since intrusions recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Mitred Parakeet

modes.label: Individual birds escaping or being released from the pet trade over decades in cities far outside the native range • Enough of them accumulating in one area to find each other, pair and breed • Self-sustaining urban flocks forming from an accumulation of separate accidents rather than from any single introduction

waveform.description: A slow accumulation levelling off, because the population builds gradually from separate arrivals and then stabilises.

entries.closingLine: Because the accumulation runs over decades, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Mohol Bushbaby

waveform.description: A mostly even mid-level line of activity punctuated by a few sharp, narrow dips upward representing brief high-frequency leap or escape bursts within steady nocturnal scanning travel.

entries.closingLine: Because the bushbaby’s body is built around a regular nocturnal sensing route with occasional explosive leaps for capture or escape, its operating pattern is best described as a bimodal system with a mid-frequency scanning mode and a high-frequency triggerable burst mode.

entries.name: Mojave Desert Tortoise

waveform.description: A mostly low, flat line with a few small, rounded dips upward representing brief, modest activity pulses separated by long, quiet sheltered periods.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is built around conserving energy and water through long, low-output periods anchored by burrows, this is a single, strongly low-frequency operating pattern.

entries.name: Mole Viper

modes.label: Moving through burrows • Hooking the head sideways • One fang out

waveform.description: A quiet subsurface rhythm almost never visible above ground.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Monarch Butterfly
entries.archetype: A Clock Kept in the Antennae

modes.label: Summer generations • Breed • Die in weeks
Autumn generation • Reproduction switched off • Months of travel

waveform.description: Several short sharp generations, then one long flat one.

entries.closingLine: That is a bimodal system of fast breeding generations and one long-lived migratory one.

entries.name: Mongolian Gerbil

waveform.description: A low baseline with small, rounded rises showing brief, timed surface activity between long sheltered periods.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system leans on storage, shelter and careful timing rather than continuous output, the Mongolian gerbil is a low-frequency, burrowed-reserve system.

entries.name: Monito del Monte
entries.archetype: Fruit Carrier Banking Fat in Its Tail

waveform.description: Active nightly climbing through the warm season, then a deep flat trough of winter hibernation.

entries.closingLine: Because the system switches seasonally between active nightly foraging and hibernation funded by stored fat, it is a phase-change system.

entries.name: Monkey-tailed Skink

waveform.description: An almost unvarying low trace — the animal holds on and feeds rather than moving between states.

entries.closingLine: Because intake and movement both proceed slowly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Monkfish

modes.label: Lying buried and motionless for long periods • Twitching a modified first dorsal ray as a lure • Opening the mouth so fast that water and prey are pulled in together

waveform.description: A long motionless line broken by two extremely brief full-depth events, because almost nothing happens and then everything does in milliseconds.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes are days apart, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Monocled Cobra

waveform.description: A steady hunting rhythm lifted where the body rises and spreads.

entries.closingLine: Continuous hunting across a working landscape makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Monte Iberia Eleuth

waveform.description: A shallow steady line — a very small animal making very small movements within a very small area.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at a very low rate within a very small space, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Montezuma Oropendola

waveform.description: A gently undulating mid-level line for steady colony life with a single sharp dip-and-peak in the middle representing a brief, intense display burst at the canopy edge.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a bimodal system: a mid-frequency colony engine that continuously operates the hanging structure, and a high-frequency edge-display burst that rides on top of it.

entries.name: Moon Jellyfish

waveform.description: A small, even, endlessly repeating pulse riding a flat baseline.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: it adds a small amount of work to a flow that is already doing most of the job.

entries.name: Moon Rat

waveform.description: A slow low nocturnal line with small steady variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, unhurried and defended by smell.

entries.name: Moorish Idol

waveform.description: Fine, near-continuous picking with almost no rest.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: constant low-yield grazing through an unusually narrow feeding apparatus.

entries.name: Moose
entries.archetype: Legs Long Enough for the Snow

waveform.description: A slow browsing line rising into a sustained feeding phase and settling.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: deliberate terrestrial browsing and a distinct aquatic feeding phase.

entries.name: Moray Eel
entries.archetype: A Second Set of Jaws in the Throat

waveform.description: A still anchored line broken by one two-stage strike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: prolonged anchored stillness and a rare two-stage mechanical strike.

entries.name: Mosquito

waveform.description: A dense sawtooth signature representing rapid repeated sampling and response.

entries.closingLine: That makes the mosquito a high-frequency system: reactive, agile and built around repeated micro-opportunities.

entries.name: Moss Mimic Stick Insect
entries.archetype: Ragged Lobes That Read as Moss

waveform.description: A long flat line of daytime stillness rising gently into a slow night of feeding.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long motionless daytime masquerade and slow nocturnal feeding.

entries.name: Mossy Frog

waveform.description: An almost unbroken low line — an animal whose main activity is being indistinguishable from stone.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system substitutes structural resemblance for speed, defence or activity, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mossy Leaf-tailed Gecko
entries.archetype: Skin Fringes That Erase the Shadow

waveform.description: A flat daytime line pressed to the bark rising into a night of hunting.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: flattened daytime concealment and night hunting.

entries.name: Mottled Duck

modes.label: A dabbling duck that does not migrate, spending its entire life within one coastal marsh system • Every requirement for the whole year, including moult, breeding and winter feeding, met inside that one area • Nothing about the population buffered by movement, so a change to that marsh affects the birds immediately and completely rather than being escaped

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm through the year, because nothing about the animal's life is seasonal in location.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual and local, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mouflon

waveform.description: Steady herd grazing with rare, brief clashes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady social grazing in which an honest signal keeps the price of rank low.

entries.name: Mound-building Termite

modes.label: Gathering plant material • Feeding it to a fungus comb inside the mound • Eating the fungus and the partly digested substrate

waveform.description: A long steady line with one dramatic excursion, because the colony runs continuously and releases its reproductives all at once.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging and comb turnover run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Mountain Beaver
entries.archetype: A Kidney That Cannot Save Water

modes.label: Burrowing in wet soil • Cutting vegetation • Drinking constantly

waveform.description: A steady unremarkable rhythm of cutting and hauling.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mountain Goat

waveform.description: An extremely measured pace with nothing hurried anywhere in it.

entries.closingLine: Careful low-expenditure movement on poor alpine forage makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mountain Gorilla
entries.archetype: A Family Held Together by One Silverback

waveform.description: A slow, level line of feeding and resting broken by one sharp display.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: slow feeding and resting, and short, rare displays.

entries.name: Mountain Hare
entries.archetype: Coat Turning White Ahead of the Snow

waveform.description: A long quiet rest in the form rising into a night of feeding.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: still daytime rest in the form and nocturnal feeding.

entries.name: Mountain Nyala

waveform.description: A regular alternation with modest amplitude — the animal shifts between feeding and cover repeatedly rather than dramatically.

entries.closingLine: Because the shifting runs as a steady repeated cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Mountain Reedbuck
entries.archetype: Grazing the Slope With the Escape Uphill

waveform.description: A steady grazing line with short, sharp flight spikes when disturbed.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: steady hillside grazing and brief, explosive flight.

entries.name: Mountain Tapir

waveform.description: A steady browsing rhythm — an animal moving between forest and open ground at an unvarying pace.

entries.closingLine: Because browsing and moving run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Mountain Zebra

waveform.description: Two long grazing plateaus joined by a midday trough, with the steady grade of an animal that walks up and down all day.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal converts steady walking and continuous grazing into a living on marginal ground, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Mourning Cloak

modes.label: Emerging in midsummer and feeding on tree sap and rotting fruit rather than nectar • Entering dormancy in a cavity before autumn • Reappearing in early spring, mating and dying after nearly a year on the wing

waveform.description: Long flat depressed stretches with two separated active periods, because the same individuals fly in spring and again in late summer.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mourning Dove

modes.label: Gathering seed • Making milk • Starting again

waveform.description: A gentle rolling wave of even amplitude, unhurried and without any sharp event in it.

entries.closingLine: Because that rhythm is continuous across a long season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Mud Dauber

modes.label: Collecting mud in pellets and shaping it into tubular cells on a sheltered surface • Hunting spiders, paralysing them with a sting that preserves rather than kills • Packing several into each cell with one egg and sealing it before starting the next

waveform.description: A regular alternation between building and provisioning trips, because the two activities cycle continuously.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs seasonally, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mudpuppy
entries.archetype: A Door That Cannot Be Reopened

modes.label: Walking the bottom • Breathing through feathered gills • Active all winter

waveform.description: A flat unchanging trace: a body that never switches state.

entries.closingLine: Slow and unchanging throughout, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mudskipper

waveform.description: A steady working rhythm with regular returns to recharge.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuous work punctuated by regular recharging.

entries.name: Mugger Crocodile

waveform.description: A long flat low-activity line for extended waiting, followed by one sharp peak for the ambush strike and a quick drop back toward lower activity.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a bimodal system: a dominant low-frequency waiting mode structurally paired with a necessary high-frequency ambush burst.

entries.name: Mule Deer

modes.label: Pushing off with all four legs together in a stiff-legged bound • Covering broken rock, brush and slope in a series of high arcs rather than a run • Changing direction completely on landing because each bound starts from a standstill

waveform.description: A regular series of identical arcs, because each bound is a repetition of exactly the same launch and landing.

entries.closingLine: Because escape events recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Multicolored Asian Lady Beetle

modes.label: Hunting colonies • Breeding fast • Bleeding when seized

waveform.description: A busy unbroken feeding rhythm, quick and even, with no pause long enough to read as rest.

entries.closingLine: Because the year of consequence is one continuous rhythm of finding, eating and breeding at speed, this operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Muscovy Duck

waveform.description: A low steady line: an unhurried bird that spends little and rests high.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: quiet, economical and organised around removing risk by choosing where to rest rather than by escaping.

entries.name: Musk Ox
entries.archetype: A Stance That Works on Wolves Only

modes.label: Grazing tundra • Closing into a ring • Standing absolutely still

waveform.description: A slow conservative rhythm with a single defensive event.

entries.closingLine: Slow and conservative, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Mute Swan

waveform.description: A slow wide swell with no sharp edges at all, the trace of a heavy body moving deliberately and continuously.

entries.closingLine: Because the feeding is continuous, unhurried and repeated for many hours a day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Nacunda Nighthawk
entries.archetype: A Gape Wider Than the Bill

waveform.description: An even continuous sweep through the insect layer.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: a repeated low-cost sweep whose return depends on volume rather than on any single capture.

entries.name: Naked Mole-rat

waveform.description: Three separate levels held simultaneously — a colony running at one rate for breeding, another for work and a third for waiting.

entries.closingLine: Because the system operates at three distinct rates simultaneously rather than switching between them, it is a multimodal system.

entries.name: Namaqua Sandgrouse

waveform.description: Long low stretches of settled activity on the ground, with two moderate, rounded commuting peaks representing regular water-carrying flights before returning to a low, stable baseline.

entries.closingLine: The result is a bimodal rhythm: a low-frequency, ground-based, conservative living mode anchored around chicks and seed patches, coupled with a mid-frequency, timed shuttle mode that regularly extends care far beyond the comfort zone of local resources.

entries.name: Napoleon Wrasse

waveform.description: A rising trace rather than a repeating one, because the animal's role changes as it grows rather than cycling.

entries.closingLine: Because life on the reef runs as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Narrow-bordered Bee Hawkmoth
entries.archetype: A Bumblebee Disguise Built on Scabious

waveform.description: A long low larval phase followed by a short burst of fast adult flight.

entries.closingLine: The switch from a leaf-bound larva to a fast, bee-like adult makes it a phase-change system.

entries.name: Narwhal

waveform.description: Deep sustained excursions with brief returns to the top — a rhythm whose long axis is vertical rather than horizontal.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs on stored capacity spent slowly in a place with no margin for error, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Nene

waveform.description: An even walking and grazing rhythm — a goose that has given up the water's cycle for the ground's.

entries.closingLine: Because walking and grazing run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Neotropic Cormorant

waveform.description: A brisk repeating rhythm of short dives with brief surface intervals.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: frequent, mobile and worked in company rather than alone.

entries.name: New Caledonian Crow

modes.label: Selecting a twig or a Pandanus leaf • Working it into a hooked or barbed tool away from the food • Carrying the finished tool to the prey and keeping it afterwards

waveform.description: A structured build-up to a peak repeated at intervals, because each episode is a sequence of preparation steps ending in use.

entries.closingLine: Since tool episodes recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: New Zealand Bellbird

waveform.description: Evenly spaced sharp peaks rising from a steady baseline, representing regular ringing calls separated by short intervals of foraging and movement.

entries.closingLine: Because its survival pattern is a repeating cycle of calling, feeding and returning to favored perches rather than long waits or explosive bursts, the bellbird is best understood as a mid-frequency system built on rhythmic, projected use of place.

entries.name: New Zealand Fur Seal

modes.label: Carrying a dense underfur beneath coarse guard hairs • Trapping a layer of air against the skin that the water never reaches • Grooming constantly to keep that layer intact and diving on it

waveform.description: A steady alternating rhythm, because the animal cycles constantly between diving and hauling out.

entries.closingLine: Since dives and haul-outs recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Nicobar Pigeon

waveform.description: Two flying commutes lifting clear of a long feeding plateau — a day with a shape set by water crossings, not by hunting.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on a repeated daily circuit and continuous mechanical processing, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Niger Triggerfish

modes.label: Reversing into a crevice tail first when threatened • Raising the heavy first dorsal spine and locking it upright with a smaller second spine wedged behind its base • Becoming impossible to extract because the spine bears against the rock rather than against muscle

waveform.description: An active feeding rhythm with occasional sharp withdrawals, because the fish forages in the current and bolts for cover.

entries.closingLine: Because withdrawals recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Night Parrot

waveform.description: Long stretches of low, flat activity for concealment with modest, smooth rises representing quiet nocturnal foraging that never spike into open, high-exposure bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is built to keep exposure rare and tightly controlled, with only modest pulses of movement around a very secure base, the Night Parrot is best understood as a bimodal low–mid frequency operator.

entries.name: Nile Lechwe

waveform.description: A trough while the water is high and a raised section as it falls — the year follows the flood rather than the sun.

entries.closingLine: Because the two flood states are both essential, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Nile Monitor

waveform.description: An active searching rhythm dropping into a long submerged low and returning.

entries.closingLine: That makes it an adaptive system: the operating state is chosen to suit the situation rather than fixed by anatomy.

entries.name: Nile Tilapia

waveform.description: A growth rhythm alternating with a compressed low state.

entries.closingLine: That makes it an adaptive system: the strategy is set by the conditions rather than by the species.

entries.name: Nilgai
entries.archetype: Sloped Back, Long Legs, Dry Country

waveform.description: An unhurried low line with slow regular movement.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: unhurried, tolerant and undemanding.

entries.name: Nilgiri Tahr

waveform.description: A steady daily rhythm of grazing and moving between rock faces, with no rare peak and no long dormancy.

entries.closingLine: Because grazing and retreating run as a steady daily cycle rather than in bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Nine-banded Armadillo
entries.archetype: Banded Shell Over a Low Engine

waveform.description: A low steady line with small even variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, armoured and economical rather than reactive.

entries.name: North American Beaver

waveform.description: A steady working rhythm of repeated small construction, never fast, never stopping.

entries.closingLine: That makes the beaver a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, repetitive and defined by continuous construction rather than any burst of speed or strength.

entries.name: North American Raccoon

waveform.description: A continuous investigating rhythm: many small manipulations rather than decisive events.

entries.closingLine: That makes the raccoon a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, continuous and built on many small acts of manipulation.

entries.name: North American River Otter

waveform.description: A gently undulating mid-level line showing ongoing play and practice, with one sharp dip-and-rise spike representing brief bursts of intense hunting or escape activity.

entries.closingLine: Because their biology supports a continuous, playful mid-level activity pattern that regularly converts into short high-intensity chases and escapes, the river otter operates as a bimodal system with a rhythmic MID practice mode and a triggered HIGH execution mode.

entries.name: Northern Bald Ibis

waveform.description: A steady colonial rhythm with one broad seasonal lift — the migration raised above an otherwise even year.

entries.closingLine: Because the annual cycle runs steadily, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Northern Basket Star

waveform.description: A low flat baseline for daytime shelter, rising into a moderate, steady plateau at night when the arms are unfurled to feed, then dropping back to low.

entries.closingLine: Because its biology is built around a protected, low-output shelter state and a recurring, current-dependent feeding state, the basket star operates as a bimodal system with a low-frequency refuge mode and a mid-frequency, night-basket harvesting mode.

entries.name: Northern Bobwhite

modes.label: A covey of a dozen or so birds settling on the ground together at dusk • Arranging themselves in a tight circle with tails inward and heads facing outward • Every direction covered by a watching bird while the bodies press together to conserve heat

waveform.description: A daily cycle converging to a settled low period, because the covey disperses to feed and reassembles at night.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Northern Cardinal

waveform.description: Paired call and answer repeating steadily: two voices alternating on one line.

entries.closingLine: That makes the cardinal a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, continuous and organised around maintaining one relationship rather than competing for a new one each year.

entries.name: Northern Collared Lemming
entries.archetype: White Coat and Double Claws for Winter

waveform.description: Steady winter activity under the snow, then a sharp, busy summer on the surface.

entries.closingLine: The seasonal switch makes it a phase-change system.

entries.name: Northern Elephant Seal

waveform.description: Repeated sharp dive spikes during an active foraging phase, followed by a flatter, lower-activity haul-out plateau.

entries.closingLine: Because these two contrasting operating states are both essential and tightly tied to the annual cycle, this is a bimodal system: a low-frequency fasting phase anchored to beaches and a high-frequency diving phase offshore.

entries.name: Northern Flatid Planthopper
entries.archetype: Sidling Round to the Far Side

waveform.description: A long, quiet feeding line with a modest rise where it slides round the twig.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: still feeding and sidling evasion.

entries.name: Northern Flicker

modes.label: Hopping on open ground • Driving the bill into soil • Withdrawing a loaded tongue

waveform.description: Long flat hops broken by deep single probes, because each strike drives the whole bill into the ground rather than flicking at the surface.

entries.closingLine: Since that action repeats steadily through daylight, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Northern Fulmar
entries.archetype: Stiff Wings Working the Wind Gradient

waveform.description: A low regular rise and fall with no powered effort.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: economical, patient and dependent on the wind rather than on muscle.

entries.name: Northern Gannet

waveform.description: A high searching line dropping into a near-vertical entry.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: wide efficient searching and a committed high-speed entry that continues into pursuit.

entries.name: Northern Hairy-nosed Wombat

waveform.description: An almost flat trace — a body whose whole design is to change as little as possible.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Northern Hawk Owl
entries.archetype: From the Very Top of the Spruce

waveform.description: A long watchful line broken by extended committed glides.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: extended high watching and long committed glides.

entries.name: Northern Jacana
entries.archetype: Long Toes Turning Lily Pads Into Ground

waveform.description: A steady walking-and-picking rhythm with a long, quieter phase of care on the nest.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady surface foraging and a slow, male-run care phase.

entries.name: Northern Lapwing
entries.archetype: Broad Wings Beating the Air Audibly

waveform.description: A still ground line breaking into a tumbling aerial sequence.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: motionless concealment and a loud aerial assertion.

entries.name: Northern Luzon Giant Cloud Rat
entries.archetype: Slow Heavy Leaf-Eater Climbing by Night

waveform.description: Active at night, still in a hollow or vine tangle through the day.

entries.closingLine: Its steady, unhurried, night-time routine makes it a SINGLE LOW system.

entries.name: Northern Mockingbird

waveform.description: Groups of repeated phrases, each group a different shape from the one before.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and continuous, where output is a steadily growing library delivered in repeated bursts.

entries.name: Northern Pig-tailed Macaque

waveform.description: A steady social rhythm repeated through every day of the group's life.

entries.closingLine: That makes the macaque a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, repeated and coordination-led.

entries.name: Northern Pike

modes.label: Holding motionless among weed with fins barely moving • Curving the body into an S with the tail cocked • Straightening it in a fraction of a second to arrive at the prey

waveform.description: A motionless baseline broken by extremely narrow full-depth strikes, because nothing happens and then everything does at once.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes occur in a fraction of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Northern Shoveler

waveform.description: A fine continuous rhythm: the same small pumping action repeated without pause.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and steady, converting volume into calories rather than capturing anything individually.

entries.name: Northern Snakehead

modes.label: A suprabranchial chamber above the gills acting as a lung and requiring air from the surface • Surviving out of water for days while the skin and that chamber stay moist • Wriggling across wet ground between water bodies rather than being confined to one

waveform.description: A steady rhythm of surfacing and submerging, because the fish must return to the surface continuously to breathe.

entries.closingLine: Because surfacing is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Northern Stargazer

waveform.description: A long flat low line for buried waiting with a single sharp narrow spike for the ambush strike, then immediate return to low activity.

entries.closingLine: That makes its system a clear bimodal pattern: a dominant low-frequency conceal-and-wait phase, punctuated by brief, high-frequency strike bursts when opportunity enters the narrow kill zone.

entries.name: Northern Tamandua
entries.archetype: A Stomach That Does the Chewing

modes.label: Opening a nest • Collecting with the tongue • Grinding in the gut

waveform.description: A rapid cycle of short nest visits through the night.

entries.closingLine: This is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Norway Lobster

modes.label: Leaving the burrow to forage when light at the seabed falls to a narrow band • Walking over mud taking worms and carrion • Returning before the light changes again
Remaining inside a deep mud burrow • Irrigating it with the pleopods • Neither feeding nor visible to anything above

waveform.description: Two clearly held levels alternating on a regular cycle, because the animal is either out or entirely inside with nothing between.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, out and in are two different states with different exposure, physiology and availability, making this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Nubian Ibex

waveform.description: Steady browsing across slopes, broken by sharp spikes of cliff escape.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady browsing near water and sudden climbs to safety.

entries.name: Numbat

waveform.description: A rapid steady rhythm — many small identical actions repeated through the whole of the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole day is one action repeated at a steady rate, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Nurse Shark
entries.archetype: A Shark That Can Stop Swimming

waveform.description: A very low still line with minimal variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: economical, stationary and built around extraction rather than pursuit.

entries.name: Nutmeg Mannikin

waveform.description: Evenly spaced moderate peaks representing repeated daily flock foraging bouts with regular return to lower activity.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system: not a single long wait or one explosive burst, but steady, repeated cycles of collective seed gathering across the day and season.

entries.name: Nyala

modes.label: A male at around twice the female mass, slate grey to dark brown, shaggy-coated with a long dorsal crest and spiral horns
A female with no horns, bright chestnut coat and clear white body stripes, less than half the male's weight

waveform.description: A tall coarse rhythm giving way to a small tight one, because the two sexes run their lives at completely different scales.

entries.closingLine: The two sexes occupy the same riverine woodland in southern Africa and feed on much the same browse, but they are solving different problems with different bodies, and the architecture rather than the behaviour is what differs, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Oarfish

waveform.description: A fine continuous ripple of constant amplitude — the fin's wave passing along the body, over and over.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs continuously at a very low output, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ocean Quahog

waveform.description: A low, level line of slow filtering that drops further during periods of valve closure.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: continuous slow filtering punctuated by metabolic shutdown.

entries.name: Ocean Sunfish

waveform.description: A repeating descent and return that never settles at either end.

entries.closingLine: Continuous drifting, diving and feeding makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Oceanic Whitetip Shark

waveform.description: A long even line with almost no variation — an animal that never stops and never hurries.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs continuously at very low cost rather than in bursts, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ocellated Antbird

waveform.description: Even, moderate spikes above a steady line, showing repeated, coordinated foraging bursts as the bird tracks an army ant swarm.

entries.closingLine: Because their whole feeding system is built around this ongoing, coordinated following of another species’ movement rather than long fasting or singular explosive strikes, the ocellated antbird is best understood as a mid-frequency system with rhythmic, repeatable engagement.

entries.name: Ocellated Lizard

waveform.description: Warm-up periods alternating with brisk working excursions.

entries.closingLine: Repeated foraging trips from cover make this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ocelot

waveform.description: A patient, repeating patrol rhythm through the night.

entries.closingLine: Steady nightly patrolling of a held territory makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Oertzen's Lizard

waveform.description: A mostly low, flat line with modest, rounded rises representing repeated moderate foraging excursions between longer sheltered periods.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a bimodal system with a dominant low-frequency refuge mode anchored by rock structure, and a moderate, repeatable excursion mode for feeding and maintenance.

entries.name: Ogre-faced Spider

waveform.description: A long flat wait broken by one extremely narrow, very tall spike.

entries.closingLine: That makes the spider a bimodal system: an extremely cheap prepared state and a brief, total commitment.

entries.name: Oilbird

waveform.description: A staccato clicking section giving way to a smooth sustained one — two different senses running in two different places.

entries.closingLine: Because both are essential and both are distinct, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Okapi

waveform.description: A quiet, barely varying trace — the animal's whole strategy is to produce as little signal as possible.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on stillness, solitude and minimal signal, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Oleander Hawk-moth

modes.label: Larvae feeding on oleander, whose tissues carry cardiac glycosides that stop a vertebrate heart • Those compounds tolerated rather than avoided, through target-site changes and rapid excretion • A food plant left almost untouched by other insects, available in quantity wherever it grows

waveform.description: A single seasonal cycle of growth and pupation, because the larva develops once through a generation.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is generational, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Olingo

modes.label: Crossing branches • Feeding on fruit • Returning before light

waveform.description: A quick, repeating branch-to-branch rhythm through the night.

entries.closingLine: Continuous nightly foraging across connected canopy makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Olinguito
entries.archetype: Woolly Fig-Eater of the Cloud Canopy

waveform.description: Night-time canopy feeding on either side of a long, still daytime rest.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: nocturnal fruit-feeding in the canopy and daytime rest in dense foliage.

entries.name: Olive Baboon

modes.label: Trying it • Being watched • Copied by the troop

waveform.description: A varied uneven rhythm in which the peaks differ from one another, because each is a different thing being tried.

entries.closingLine: Because testing and copying run continuously through every foraging day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Olive Ridley Sea Turtle

waveform.description: A long dispersed low line with one enormous concentrated event.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long dispersal and one overwhelming synchronised event.

entries.name: Olive-backed Sunbird

modes.label: A pendulous nest of fibre, grass and cobweb built around a single attachment point with a side entrance and a small porch • That attachment made to a twig, a wire, a washing line, a hanging basket or a light fitting without distinction • The nest swinging freely, so nothing can climb to it and the structure itself is what makes the site secure rather than where it is

waveform.description: A single seasonal build and occupation, because the nest is constructed and used once through the cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Olm

waveform.description: An extremely low baseline with one modest raised section — a life in which feeding is the exception.

entries.closingLine: Because it runs a years-long fasting state and a brief feeding one and needs both, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Onager

waveform.description: Two long grazing periods with travel between them — a rhythm set by distance to water rather than by hunger.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on continuous ranging within a physiological cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Oncilla

waveform.description: Many modest peaks of similar height through the night — no single capture dominates the trace.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from many repeated modest captures rather than from storage or a decisive kill, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Opah
entries.archetype: A Heat Exchanger Inside the Gills

modes.label: Flapping the pectoral fins continuously • Generating heat • Keeping it in

waveform.description: A continuous unbroken beat of the pectoral fins.

entries.closingLine: This is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Orange Moth

modes.label: Carrying a coat of translucent gelatinous spines • Shedding them on contact • Leaving an attacker with jaws stuck together

waveform.description: A long even line broken by two brief raised sections, because the defence is passive almost all the time and only acts on contact.

entries.closingLine: Since a generation turns over across months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Orange Oakleaf Butterfly
entries.archetype: A Hooked Wing Folded Into a Leaf

waveform.description: Long still perches broken by short bursts of flashing flight that end abruptly.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long motionless masquerade and short bursts of flashing flight.

entries.name: Orange Roughy

waveform.description: A low, slow baseline lifted briefly each year by dense seasonal aggregations.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: slow deepwater living and predictable seasonal aggregation.

entries.name: Orange Sea Pen

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing continuous anchored presence with small variations as currents and feeding conditions change.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a low-frequency system defined by durable attachment, patient suspension-feeding and minimal, timing-based movement.

entries.name: Orange Sulphur

waveform.description: Even, repeating peaks representing regular wing flashes produced by continuous flight wingbeats.

entries.closingLine: Because the signaling is built into regular movement and relies on ongoing, rhythmic activity rather than rare bursts or deep reserves, this is a mid-frequency system driven by repeated, coordinated visual pulses.

entries.name: Orange-headed Thrush

modes.label: A bird working shaded forest floor by picking up leaves in the bill and flicking them aside • Invertebrates sheltering beneath that litter exposed by the movement rather than being searched for visually • Each flick revealing a small patch, so the forager processes the floor leaf by leaf rather than scanning it

waveform.description: A steady methodical rhythm, because the bird works the floor one flick at a time without pause.

entries.closingLine: Because the work is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Orb-weaver Spider

modes.label: Taking down the damaged web at the end of its working period and swallowing the silk • Recovering most of the protein and amino acids from it within a few hours • Spinning a complete new orb from that recycled material before the next hunting period

waveform.description: A sharp construction burst followed by a long quiet watch, repeated once per cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Orca
entries.archetype: Knowledge Held by the Oldest Female

waveform.description: A steady coordinated group rhythm sustained across generations.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuously coordinated and built on transmitted knowledge.

entries.name: Orchid Bee
entries.archetype: A Perfume Collected Over a Lifetime

waveform.description: Dense continuous collecting activity across a long range.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: continuous wide-ranging collection in service of one accumulated signal.

entries.name: Orchid Mantis

modes.label: Posed on vegetation • Waiting • Striking within reach

waveform.description: An almost motionless trace with barely perceptible variation.

entries.closingLine: A motionless ambush predator that waits for prey to arrive is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ord's Kangaroo Rat
entries.archetype: Cheek Pouches Filled for the Burrow

waveform.description: Active foraging nights settling into long quiet periods underground.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: active nightly gathering and extended sheltering on stored seed.

entries.name: Oribi
entries.archetype: Short Grass to Eat, Tall Grass to Hide

waveform.description: A steady grazing line interrupted by one explosive flush and stotting bound.
