entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: steady selective grazing and an explosive escape.

entries.name: Oriental Dwarf Kingfisher

modes.label: Perching low on a branch above shaded forest floor rather than above water • Watching leaf litter for spiders, mantises, geckos and small frogs • Dropping onto them directly, with no dive, no refraction to correct and no water involved

waveform.description: A long motionless watching line with abrupt drops, because the bird sits still and strikes without warning.

entries.closingLine: Because strikes are infrequent, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Oriental Fire-bellied Toad

waveform.description: A quiet cryptic line broken only where the underside comes up.

entries.closingLine: Small, cheap to run and long-lived for its size, this is a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Oriental Garden Lizard

modes.label: An ordinary brown or olive lizard basking, feeding and moving inconspicuously through vegetation
A breeding male with the head and throat flushed bright crimson, holding an elevated position and head-bobbing at rivals

waveform.description: A quiet even rhythm broken by tall display episodes, because the animal switches between concealment and advertisement.

entries.closingLine: Because the display runs seasonally against a continuous background, it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Oriental Honey Buzzard

waveform.description: A steady mid-level waveform with small, regular undulations showing repeated, focused foraging actions rather than long dormancy or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: This makes it a mid-frequency system: not built for single huge bursts or deep torpor, but for ongoing, repeatable, specialized nest-raiding using anatomical "tools" that turn a dangerous resource into a reliable food source.

entries.name: Oriental Latrine Fly

modes.label: Adults locating a body within minutes by volatile compounds released as decomposition begins • Laying eggs in a narrow window before other species dominate • Larvae developing at a rate set by temperature, so their stage gives an elapsed time

waveform.description: One sharp early surge followed by a long decline, because the fly dominates the first phase and then gives way.

entries.closingLine: Because generations are rapid, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Oriental Longheaded Grasshopper

modes.label: A head drawn out into a long cone with the antennae flattened into blades and the eyes elongated along it • The whole body narrow and extended, so the outline is a line rather than the blocky shape of a grasshopper • The animal aligning itself along a grass blade and holding that orientation, so both the shape and the direction match the vegetation

waveform.description: A very still line with small adjustments, because the animal holds an alignment and moves rarely.

entries.closingLine: Because the alignment is held continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Oriental Magpie-Robin
entries.archetype: A Song That Holds the Garden

waveform.description: A varied sustained vocal rhythm across the day's edges.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, sustained and carried entirely by signal.

entries.name: Oriental Pied Hornbill

waveform.description: A long series of identical delivery events at a steady interval.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, sustained and defined by continuous provisioning rather than by any burst of effort.

entries.name: Oriental White-eye

modes.label: Small parties moving through canopy and joined by drongos, minivets, babblers, woodpeckers and flycatchers • Each species foraging at a different height and in a different manner, so competition stays low while numbers stay high • Many more eyes watching for raptors, and insects flushed by one species taken by another

waveform.description: A continuous busy rhythm, because the flock moves and forages constantly through the canopy.

entries.closingLine: Because foraging is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Orinoco Mata Mata Turtle

modes.label: Sitting motionless on the bottom with a flattened fringed head that reads as leaf litter • Expanding the throat explosively when a fish comes within range • Drawing prey in on the inrush of water rather than by any pursuit

waveform.description: A flat line broken by two very sharp narrow spikes, because nothing happens at all until the strike, which is nearly instantaneous.

entries.closingLine: Because the capture is rare and the animal is otherwise still, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ornate Box Turtle
entries.archetype: A Life That Assumes Adults Never Die

modes.label: Foraging slowly • Closing the shell • Repeating for decades

waveform.description: A near-flat trace stretched across several human decades.

entries.closingLine: Slow, conservative and reserve-based throughout, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ornate Ghost Pipefish

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing long periods of near-still, low-output drifting with only small adjustments.

entries.closingLine: Because their whole system is built around low-movement hovering, precise camouflage, and patient, place-bound feeding, the ornate ghost pipefish is a low-frequency animal whose survival depends on quiet continuity rather than bursts.

entries.name: Ornate Horned Frog

waveform.description: A buried flat line broken twice by something that occupies no time.

entries.closingLine: A near-zero baseline paying for a strike with no duration makes this a bimodal system, low-frequency in the ground and high-frequency at the mouth.

entries.name: Ornate Spiny Lobster

modes.label: Growing on shallow reef and seagrass in the Torres Strait • Migrating hundreds of kilometres to spawning grounds in the Gulf of Papua • Spawning there and dying rather than returning

waveform.description: A steady line rising into broad sustained events, because the migration is a prolonged movement rather than a moment.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ornate Spiny-tailed Lizard

modes.label: A diet of desert plants carrying far more potassium and sodium salts than the body can use • Nasal glands actively concentrating those salts and excreting them as crystals • Crusts of salt accumulating around the nostrils and being sneezed away, so water is not spent flushing them through the kidney

waveform.description: A single daily arc of emergence and retreat, because activity follows the sun and returns to the burrow.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Oscar Fish

modes.label: Moving gravel with the mouth • Clearing a flat surface • Guarding it as a pair

waveform.description: A deliberate working rhythm of even efforts, because moving substrate by the mouthful is repetitive rather than dramatic.

entries.closingLine: Since that operation runs at a steady tempo, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Osprey

waveform.description: A steady searching flight broken by a deep committed plunge.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: patient wide searching and a rare total commitment.

entries.name: Ostrich

waveform.description: A long even stride rhythm that holds the same shape across the whole trace.

entries.closingLine: That makes the ostrich a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, sustained and organised around covering ground efficiently rather than exploding into a short chase.

entries.name: Ovenbird

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing steady, modest activity centered on one stable shelter site.

entries.closingLine: This makes the Ovenbird a low-frequency system: slow to shift home base, conservative with movement, and organized around a durable, place-bound dome that turns a small patch of habitat into a lasting refuge.

entries.name: Owl Butterfly
entries.archetype: An Eye Placed Far From the Body

waveform.description: A slow gentle rhythm with no sharp events.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, unhurried and protected by a mark rather than by movement.

entries.name: Owlet Moth

modes.label: A simple ear on each side of the thorax with very few sensory cells, tuned to ultrasound • A distant bat call producing steady firing that turns the moth away • A close call producing saturated firing that collapses the flight into a spiral or a drop

waveform.description: A quick irregular flight line broken by violent instantaneous collapses, because evasion is abrupt and total.

entries.closingLine: Because the response is near-instantaneous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Paca
entries.archetype: A Resonating Chamber in the Cheek

waveform.description: A quiet nocturnal line with small steady variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: quiet, solitary and economical.

entries.name: Pacarana

waveform.description: A shallow unvarying rhythm — an animal that never accelerates and never stops for long.

entries.closingLine: Because everything is arranged around low expenditure, careful handling and slow turnover, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pachyrhynchus Weevil

modes.label: A cuticle so heavily sclerotised that lizards attempting to eat one cannot crush it and abandon the attempt • Patterned scales containing photonic crystals, producing bright metallic spots visible from a distance • Predators learning to associate those spots with an insect that cannot be processed, and several unrelated beetles converging on the same pattern

waveform.description: A very flat unhurried line, because a beetle that cannot be eaten has no reason to move quickly.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pacific Black Duck

modes.label: Waiting through dry years without breeding • Responding to flooding within weeks • Raising broods while the water and its invertebrates last

waveform.description: A long flat stretch broken by one broad rise, because years can pass with nothing happening and then everything happens at once.

entries.closingLine: Since breeding events are years apart, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pacific Hagfish

waveform.description: Long, low, steady activity with a single sharp upward spike and quick return, representing slow scavenging punctuated by brief slime escape bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because the hagfish’s whole system is built around a calm, thrifty baseline punctuated by rare but extreme slime-and-knot escape bursts, it operates as a bimodal low-plus-high frequency system.

entries.name: Pacific Herring
entries.archetype: School That Turns the Bay White

waveform.description: A steady schooling baseline broken by one tall, brief spawning peak each year.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: synchronised schooling and a brief mass spawning.

entries.name: Pacific Mole Crab

waveform.description: Even, repeating ripples showing the crab’s steady, wave-synchronized cycles of brief exposure and filtering followed by re-burial.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system built around rhythmic, repeated engagement with each wave cycle rather than long fasting or single explosive bursts.

entries.name: Pacific Parrotlet

waveform.description: A busy foraging baseline broken by abrupt spikes as the flock flushes into cover.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady flock foraging and sudden flight into cover.

entries.name: Pacific Sea Nettle

modes.label: Slow rhythmic pulsing of the bell that moves the animal forward rather than chasing anything • Long tentacles and frilled oral arms trailing far behind, forming a wide curtain through the water • Anything that touches the curtain stung by nematocysts and passed forward to the mouth

waveform.description: A slow regular pulse repeated without variation, because propulsion and feeding are the same continuous rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because the pulsing is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pacific Spiny Lumpsucker

waveform.description: A steady, low, nearly flat line showing continuous holding with only tiny fluctuations as currents push around a stable anchor.

entries.closingLine: This architecture makes it a low-frequency system: it is built to stay put and endure flow, not to cycle rapidly or sprint for long distances.

entries.name: Paddyfield Warbler

modes.label: Climbing reed stems rather than perching on branches • Foraging up and down a vertical world • Singing from inside the stand

waveform.description: Rapid alternation between two levels, because the bird is continually working up and down the stems rather than settling.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging bouts repeat through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pagoda Cup Coral

modes.label: Growing as broad horizontal plates rather than branches or mounds • Stacking successive plates in offset tiers as the colony expands • Presenting maximum surface to a dim overhead light while letting sediment slide off the sloping edges

waveform.description: A slow steady climb without oscillation, because the colony only accumulates and never cycles.

entries.closingLine: Because growth accumulates over years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Painted Bunting
entries.archetype: A Stop Halfway to Change Feathers

waveform.description: An active rhythm interrupted by a flat, quiet stretch in the middle.

entries.closingLine: Continuous seasonal work makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Painted Frogfish
entries.archetype: The Rod Held Still Above the Mouth

waveform.description: A long flat line of stillness broken by rare, near-instantaneous strikes.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: long, low-frequency waiting and a rare, explosive strike.

entries.name: Painted Stork

waveform.description: Identical snap events at irregular but frequent intervals over a flat wading baseline — a rhythm set by contact, not by decision.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from many identical low-cost contacts repeated through the day, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Painted Turtle

modes.label: Hauled onto a log • Warming to working temperature • Feeding in the shallows
Under the ice • No oxygen at all • Dissolving its own shell to survive it

waveform.description: A working season lifted out of a long dead-flat floor, because the winter state produces no activity of any kind to register.

entries.closingLine: Because both are indispensable and neither is a quieter version of the other, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Pajama Cardinalfish

waveform.description: A gentle, even ripple showing a calm, repeating mid-level activity pattern without sharp spikes or long flat pauses.

entries.closingLine: Because their whole system is built around a rhythmic, ongoing pattern of moderate activity and conspicuous but calm presence, this is a single mid-frequency system driven by patterned, steady behavior rather than bursts or deep reserves.

entries.name: Pale Beauty Moth

modes.label: Wings of pale translucent green-white scaled thinly enough that the surface beneath shows faintly through them • The moth resting flat against lichen-covered bark rather than holding the wings up • No clear boundary between the insect and the substrate, so the outline a searching bird looks for does not exist

waveform.description: An almost perfectly level line, because the moth rests without moving for the whole of the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the posture is held all day, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pale-billed Flowerpecker

modes.label: Mistletoe berries swallowed whole and passed through a shortened gut that bypasses the gizzard entirely • The seed voided within minutes, still coated in the sticky viscin the fruit carries • The bird wiping its vent along the branch it is perched on to remove that seed, which glues it to bark where mistletoe can germinate

waveform.description: A very rapid rhythm with no pauses, because the whole process from swallowing to depositing takes minutes.

entries.closingLine: Because the passage takes minutes, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Pallas's Cat

waveform.description: A long flat hold with one short, shallow commitment near the end — the cat's whole hunt is waiting, then a few metres.

entries.closingLine: Because this animal earns its living by holding still, keeping its own heat in and spending energy only at the last moment, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Palm Cockatoo
entries.archetype: A Drumstick Made for the Purpose

waveform.description: A slow feeding line broken by a regular rhythmic passage.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a slow feeding baseline and a deliberate rhythmic display.

entries.name: Palm Flatid Planthopper
entries.archetype: Underside of the Frond, Day and Night

waveform.description: A flat, unbroken line of settled feeding on the frond.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a single-mode system: constant, settled feeding on the frond underside.

entries.name: Palm Warbler

waveform.description: A fine unbroken rhythm: small movements repeating with almost no pause.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, continuous and productive through coverage rather than through any single catch.

entries.name: Panamanian Golden Frog

waveform.description: A regular repeating signal rhythm — the gesture is made over and over because a single one is easily missed.

entries.closingLine: Because signalling and foraging run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pancake Tortoise

waveform.description: A low line with brief foraging excursions — an animal that is rarely far from the crevice it lives in.

entries.closingLine: Because a low-cost body relies on the structure of the landscape rather than on its own, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Panda Ant

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line with small ripples, showing continuous conspicuous signaling with modest fluctuations in activity.

entries.closingLine: This makes the panda ant a mid-frequency system built around constant visible warning backed by durable defenses.

entries.name: Panther Chameleon

waveform.description: A shifting baseline with one sharp precision event, representing context adaptation plus a ballistic strike.

entries.closingLine: That makes the chameleon adaptive, with a shifting mid-frequency baseline and brief high-frequency precision actions.

entries.name: Pantropical Jumping Spider

modes.label: Hind legs with flexor muscles but no extensor muscles at the crucial joints • Body fluid driven into the legs by rapid contraction of the abdomen, straightening them hydraulically • A jump many times the body length produced with no extensor muscle at all, and a silk dragline paid out as a safety line

waveform.description: A careful stalking baseline broken by instantaneous jumps, because the approach is slow and the leap is not.

entries.closingLine: Because the jump is measured in milliseconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Pantry Moth

modes.label: Hatching from eggs laid on or near stored food • Boring through plastic film, paper and thin card to reach it or to leave • Webbing the food together with silk as they feed

waveform.description: A rapid even rhythm sustained throughout, because generations follow one another continuously in a heated building.

entries.closingLine: Since generations turn over in weeks, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Paper Nautilus
entries.archetype: A Secreted Cradle That Holds Air

waveform.description: A gentle, even swell: an animal hovering and drifting rather than working.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: passive, buoyant drifting organised around a portable brood chamber.

entries.name: Paper Wasp

modes.label: Several females founding a nest together • Establishing rank through repeated dominance encounters • The top female laying while the others forage and build

waveform.description: A continual back-and-forth without settling, because rank is maintained through repeated interaction rather than fixed once.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Paradise Flying Snake

waveform.description: A climbing and descending pattern with a wave running through it.

entries.closingLine: Continuous canopy movement makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Paradise Riflebird

waveform.description: A mostly low, steady line of background activity with one narrow, tall spike showing a brief, intense display performance before returning to baseline.

entries.closingLine: The biology is therefore built around a bimodal rhythm: long stretches of controlled, low-profile foraging and resting, punctuated by short, high-intensity, precision-timed performances that must land perfectly to succeed.

entries.name: Paradise Tanager
entries.archetype: Nucleus of the Moving Canopy Flock

waveform.description: A steady, rippling line of social foraging as the flock moves from tree to tree.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady social foraging through the canopy.

entries.name: Paradoxical Frog

waveform.description: A rise through the larval period and a settling afterwards — the largest values in this animal's life come before the end, not at it.

entries.closingLine: Because the system banks growth slowly in one long stage rather than spending in bursts, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Parasitic Wasp

modes.label: Tapping and listening along a surface to detect a host concealed inside wood or plant tissue • Locating it by vibration, chemical trace and the response of the substrate • Drilling through with a hair-thin ovipositor and laying an egg directly on or in the hidden host

waveform.description: A long searching baseline with one deliberate committed episode, because location takes far longer than the act itself.

entries.closingLine: Because each act takes a long search, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Parma Wallaby

waveform.description: Two narrow activity windows at either end of the night with a flat middle — a day defined by two short openings.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal runs a repeated short foraging cycle governed by light rather than by hunger, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Patagonian Hog-nosed Skunk

waveform.description: Low steady rooting with one brief defensive escalation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow durable groundwork protected by a signal that costs nothing to repeat.

entries.name: Patagonian Mara

waveform.description: A paired grazing rhythm with one animal always at the higher line.

entries.closingLine: Continuous grazing with continuous watching makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Patas Monkey
entries.archetype: A Primate Built Like a Dog

waveform.description: A quiet dispersed rhythm broken by a short explosive run.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: quiet dispersed foraging and a short explosive run.

entries.name: Pea Aphid

waveform.description: Numbers climb steeply through summer on clonal births, then collapse into a flat overwintering egg phase.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-changing system: summer clonal multiplication and a seasonal sexual switch.

entries.name: Peach-faced Lovebird
entries.archetype: Daily Water Run, Borrowed Weaver Chamber

waveform.description: A busy day of flock feeding and drinking between quiet nights in the nest chamber.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: daily flock movement to feed and drink and sheltered pair nesting.

entries.name: Peacock Butterfly

modes.label: Sitting closed with wings that look like dead leaf • Snapping them open to present four large eyespots • Rubbing the wing bases together to produce an audible hiss

waveform.description: A flat concealed line broken by sharp discrete displays, because nothing happens until the animal is found and then everything does at once.

entries.closingLine: Since disturbances recur unpredictably through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Peacock Fly
entries.archetype: Wings Fanned Over the Back on Bark

waveform.description: A steady line of bark patrol broken by sharp spikes of wing display.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady bark patrol and short bouts of display.

entries.name: Peacock Katydid

waveform.description: A long flat line of leaf disguise interrupted by one sudden spike of display.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long masquerade and a brief startle.

entries.name: Peacock Mantis Shrimp
entries.archetype: A Spring-Loaded Club Behind the Latch

waveform.description: A long, quiet watching line broken by one near-instantaneous strike spike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long watchful sheltering and an extremely brief strike.

entries.name: Peacock Spider
entries.archetype: A Dance Sent Through the Leaf

modes.label: Raising the fan • Waving the legs • Drumming the substrate

waveform.description: A rapid drumming rhythm of very short intense bursts.

entries.closingLine: Fast, brief and short-horizon, this is a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Peacock Tarantula

waveform.description: A long low, flat line for cryptic stillness, a single sharp spike for a rapid warning display, then a return to low baseline.

entries.closingLine: Because its biology is built around a quiet, cryptic default with a distinct, high-intensity warning display when boundaries are crossed, the system is best understood as bimodal: a low-frequency concealment mode and a high-frequency threat-flare mode.

entries.name: Peanut-headed Lanternfly

waveform.description: Calm baseline with one sharp, narrow peak representing a brief, intense startle display followed by a return to low activity.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system built around brief startle pulses that create just enough confusion for escape.

entries.name: Pearl Oysters

modes.label: Detecting material lodged between the mantle and the shell • Depositing successive layers of aragonite tablets and protein over it • Producing a smooth interior where an irritant would otherwise wound the mantle

waveform.description: An almost unvarying line across the span, because deposition is continuous and extremely slow.

entries.closingLine: Since deposition is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pelican Eel

waveform.description: A long flat low-activity line with one sharp narrow spike representing a sudden mouth expansion, then a quick return to low-level drifting.

entries.closingLine: This architecture creates two essential operating modes: long, low-expenditure waiting and rare, explosive expansion when opportunity and safety overlap, so the pelican eel is best described as a bimodal system with a low baseline and a high-frequency strike.

entries.name: Pere David's Deer
entries.archetype: A Species Rebuilt From Eighteen Animals

waveform.description: A slow wading rhythm with a recovery rising from a very low floor.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a wetland-adapted animal and a population rebuilt through an extreme bottleneck.

entries.name: Peregrine Falcon

waveform.description: A high patient line dropping into one extremely steep descent.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: patient positioning and a single irreversible drop.

entries.name: Perentie
entries.archetype: A Forked Tongue Reading in Stereo

waveform.description: Steady wide-ranging search with occasional closing bursts.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady wide-ranging search over scattered food, guided by the difference between two sensors.

entries.name: Periwinkle

modes.label: A horny plate on the foot that fits the shell aperture exactly • The animal withdrawing at low tide and pulling that plate closed behind it • A sealed chamber of seawater retained inside while the rock around it dries, heats and freezes

waveform.description: A tidal rhythm of activity and closure repeated twice a day without variation.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is tidal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Persian Leopard

waveform.description: Long still watching cut by an attack that covers very little ground.

entries.closingLine: Long motionless watching paying for a very short rush makes this a bimodal system, low-frequency on the ledge and high-frequency at the end.

entries.name: Pesquet's Parrot

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line with slight undulation, showing consistent, specialized activity rather than bursts or deep lulls.

entries.closingLine: Because its appearance, anatomy and feeding are all tuned around a single, clear niche and signal, its operating rhythm is a steady, mid-frequency specialization rather than a slow reserve strategy or a rapid burst system.

entries.name: Peters's Jumping Spider

modes.label: Two large forward-facing eyes with fixed lenses and a long tube behind each one, ending in a narrow retina • That retina moved by muscles, swept sideways and rotated behind the stationary lens rather than the whole eye turning • A high-resolution image built up by scanning a small acute region across the scene, so an animal a centimetre long resolves detail comparable to a much larger vertebrate

waveform.description: A rapid scanning rhythm, because the retina sweeps continuously while the animal examines something.

entries.closingLine: Because the scanning is continuous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Philippine Bulbul

modes.label: A generalist frugivore taking fruit from a very wide range of trees rather than specialising on any • Occupying secondary growth, plantation edge and regenerating clearings as readily as closed forest • Depositing seeds of pioneer and forest trees into cleared ground, so the bird that benefits from disturbance also reverses it

waveform.description: A steady untroubled rhythm, because the bird moves and feeds continuously without strong seasonal pattern.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Philippine Crocodile

waveform.description: A quiet unvarying line — a small ambush predator in a small stretch of water.

entries.closingLine: Because everything about the animal runs slowly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Philippine Eagle

waveform.description: An uneven rhythm with occasional deeper drops — coordinated attempts interleaved with ordinary movement.

entries.closingLine: Because hunting runs as a steady coordinated daily activity, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Philippine Sailfin Lizard

waveform.description: A steady riverside rhythm interrupted by sharp escapes — the drops into water are the only fast events.

entries.closingLine: Because the daily pattern of basking, feeding and escaping repeats steadily, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Philippine Tarsier

waveform.description: A held motionless line broken twice by a launch and a landing.

entries.closingLine: Long motionless watching between occasional leaps makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Picasso Bug

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line with tiny ripples, representing a continuous, always-on visual warning signal with minor variation as the insect moves.

entries.closingLine: That makes this a single, mid-frequency system: a continuous, always-available warning display rather than a slow reserve or a short explosive burst.

entries.name: Picasso Moth

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line showing a constant, always-on visual signal rather than bursts or deep lulls.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system: the signal is neither a rare, conserved burst nor a frantic flicker, but a steady, always-available display encoded into the moth’s structure.

entries.name: Pichi Armadillo
entries.archetype: Armour Wedged in a Winter Burrow

waveform.description: An active foraging season sinks into a long flat winter shutdown and rises again in spring.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-change system: seasonal foraging and winter shutdown.

entries.name: Pied Avocet

waveform.description: A regular side-to-side sweeping rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: a steady rhythmic sweep processing volume rather than selecting targets.

entries.name: Pied Butcherbird

modes.label: Watching from a bare branch • Dropping on prey • Wedging it into a fork

waveform.description: Long flat watches broken by short identical drops, because the hunt is a wait followed by one committed fall.

entries.closingLine: Since watching and singing run together through daylight, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pied Crow

modes.label: Building on pylons, poles and planted trees • Feeding along road verges • Spreading wherever both appear together

waveform.description: A regular baseline with evenly spaced peaks, because the bird works a landscape whose resources are arranged in a line.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging turns over daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pied Cuckoo

modes.label: Eggs laid in babbler nests that closely match the hosts' own in colour and size • The cuckoo chick hatching earlier and growing faster but leaving the host chicks alive in the nest • Out-begging its nestmates with a louder call and a wider gape so it takes most of what arrives

waveform.description: A single seasonal rise and fall, because the whole parasitic episode runs once through a breeding cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pied Fantail

modes.label: Moving restlessly through foliage with the tail fanned and swung • Startling insects into flight with the flash of black and white • Taking them in the air before they can settle again

waveform.description: A very rapid continuous pattern with no settled moments, because the bird is in constant motion the whole time it is awake.

entries.closingLine: Since the movement is continuous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Pied Kingfisher

waveform.description: Dense continuous high-rate work with no low plateau.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: continuous expensive effort with no economical setting.

entries.name: Pied Paddy Skimmer

modes.label: Broad opaque dark patches of pigment laid into otherwise transparent wing membrane • Those patches held out and displayed during territorial encounters over water • Rivals assessing the patches directly, so disputes over perching sites are settled by display rather than by collision

waveform.description: A busy repeating rhythm of patrols and encounters, because the insect holds a territory and meets rivals constantly.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pig-nosed Turtle

waveform.description: A steady even oscillation — flipper strokes and surfacing repeat at a constant rhythm rather than in bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because both the swimming and the breathing run as a continuous steady rhythm, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pika

waveform.description: A frantic repeating harvest rhythm that thins toward the end.

entries.closingLine: Continuous urgent harvesting makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pileated Woodpecker

waveform.description: Bursts of rapid identical blows separated by short pauses.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, repetitive and defined by opening access rather than by speed.

entries.name: Pill Millipede

waveform.description: A low, steady line with a slight dip, representing mostly inactive, tightly protected periods with minimal fluctuation in activity.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is built around a single, low-activity, armor-first response that trades motion for security, the pill millipede is a clear low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pin-tailed Whydah

waveform.description: A mid-level baseline showing steady dependence on host care, punctuated by sharp, brief spikes representing intense male display bursts to secure those foster nests.

entries.closingLine: The result is a bimodal system: a steady, host-embedded dependence mode that carries most of the life-history load, plus a high-frequency display-and-mating mode that briefly spikes to secure access to those borrowed nests.

entries.name: Pine Marten

waveform.description: An active climbing rhythm moving continuously between levels.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuously active and acting through recognition as much as through capture.

entries.name: Pinecone Fish

waveform.description: A steady low band lifting slightly through the dark hours — activity that never rises far above the resting line.

entries.closingLine: Because a low-cost body borrows both its weapon and its light, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pink Fairy Armadillo

waveform.description: A shallow steady rhythm below the baseline — digging is continuous and slow rather than intermittent.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal moves slowly through sand and rarely surfaces, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pink Pigeon

waveform.description: A low line with small regular lifts — each one an intervention rather than a change in the bird's own capacity.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs on a slow supported cycle, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pink See-through Fantasia
entries.archetype: Mud Eater That Lifts Off to Move

waveform.description: A long flat line of seabed feeding interrupted by one slow lift into the water and back.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: slow sediment feeding on the seabed and swimming relocation through the water above it.

entries.name: Pink-necked Green Pigeon

modes.label: Fruit swallowed whole and passed into a heavily muscled gizzard containing grit • Seeds ground and crushed there rather than passed intact through the gut • The bird taking the nutrition in the seed itself, so it removes the seeds it consumes instead of dispersing them

waveform.description: A quiet even feeding rhythm, because the bird works steadily through fruiting canopy without episodes.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is steady, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pink-spotted Hawkmoth

modes.label: Resting head-up along a grass blade or stem • Carrying a long conical head and slanted face that continues the line of the stem • Moving slowly and turning to keep the narrow profile toward an observer

waveform.description: A very flat slow line with a single small disturbance, because the animal is motionless for long periods and moves deliberately.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pinyon Jay
entries.archetype: A Flock Timed to the Cone Crop

waveform.description: A sharp autumn harvest peak followed by a long, lower season of recovering caches.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an intense harvest-and-cache season followed by a long period of patient recovery.

entries.name: Piping Plover

waveform.description: Quiet foraging broken by occasional sharp episodes — each one a distraction display rather than a feeding event.

entries.closingLine: Because foraging and vigilance run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pit-trapping Antlion
entries.archetype: A Pit Dug to the Angle of Collapse

waveform.description: An almost featureless low line.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: near-zero expenditure with the environment doing the work.

entries.name: Plains Vizcacha
entries.archetype: A Mound Other Species Move Into

waveform.description: A steady communal rhythm sustained over long periods.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady collective construction rather than any individual behaviour.

entries.name: Plains Zebra

waveform.description: A steady grazing rhythm sustained across the day.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady grazing protected by a pattern and a group rather than by any behaviour.

entries.name: Planarian

waveform.description: Mostly low, steady activity with occasional slow repair arcs rising and returning to baseline after injury events.

entries.closingLine: This makes the planarian a low-frequency system: slow, durable, pattern-led regeneration that repeatedly turns damage into another beginning.

entries.name: Plantain Squirrel

modes.label: A squirrel feeding at large night-opening flowers including durian, reaching in for nectar and soft tissue • Pollen picked up on the face and forelimbs and carried to the next flower on the same or a nearby tree • Fruit set in trees whose flowers are too large and too robust for insects and which open at the wrong time for birds

waveform.description: A steady daily rhythm with a nocturnal extension, because the animal forages through the day and at flowering trees into the night.

entries.closingLine: Because visits are daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Plate-billed Mountain Toucan
entries.archetype: Light Bill Carrying Seeds Across Cloud Forest

waveform.description: Steady fruit foraging through the day, easing at midday and towards dusk.

entries.closingLine: Its foraging runs at a steady daily rhythm, making it a SINGLE MID system.

entries.name: Platypus

modes.label: Eyes shut • Sweeping the bill • Reading two signals at once

waveform.description: A repeating cycle of short dives and surface intervals.

entries.closingLine: This is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ploughshare Tortoise

waveform.description: A very low line with one modest seasonal lift — contests happen rarely and slowly, and nothing else does much at all.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Plumbeous Ibis
entries.archetype: A Bill That Reads by Touch

modes.label: Probing soft ground and shallow water • Detecting prey by touch rather than sight • Closing on contact without seeing what was taken

waveform.description: A persistent even series of identical probes, because the bird works the substrate at a steady rhythm rather than in bursts.

entries.closingLine: Since probes repeat continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Plume Moth

waveform.description: A slow light line with very small variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: delicate, economical and defended by resemblance.

entries.name: Pointed Snail

modes.label: Ground surface temperatures in summer pasture rising far above what a snail can survive • The animal climbing a grass stem or fence post and sealing itself to it with dried mucus • The temperature at that height substantially lower than at the ground, so the snail waits out the season above the heat rather than beneath it

waveform.description: A long seasonal excursion, because the animal climbs once and stays there through the whole dry period.

entries.closingLine: Because the aestivation runs across a season, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Polar Bear

waveform.description: A low, nearly flat waveform representing long periods of conserved output.

entries.closingLine: That makes the polar bear a strongly low-frequency system: dense, patient, reserve-heavy and optimized for scarcity.

entries.name: Polyphemus Moth

waveform.description: A still line broken by one abrupt display.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: total stillness and one abrupt display.

entries.name: Pompeii Worm
entries.archetype: Gills in the Cool, Tail in the Heat

waveform.description: A near-flat line: one fixed position held continuously across the gradient, with only small shifts inside the tube.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: one position held continuously across a gradient.

entries.name: Pond Slider

waveform.description: Gentle rises and falls from a low baseline, showing calm basking plateaus punctuated by moderate activity arcs before returning to a warm reset.

entries.closingLine: Because the turtle’s whole design ties these two modes together and it depends on returning to warmth before the next swim, the pond slider is best understood as a bimodal low–mid frequency system.

entries.name: Pool Frog
entries.archetype: A Genome Thrown Away Each Generation

modes.label: Calling from the pond • Breeding • Supplying a hybrid that cannot supply itself

waveform.description: A dense chorus rhythm through the breeding season.

entries.closingLine: Seasonal breeding and steady feeding make this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Popeyed Scorpionfish
entries.archetype: Weed That Rocks With the Swell

waveform.description: A quiet swaying baseline broken by a single sudden strike.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: long motionless or slowly swaying rest and a brief, explosive strike.

entries.name: Porcupinefish
entries.archetype: Spines That Only Stand Up When Needed

waveform.description: A smooth low line rising abruptly into a short held peak.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an ordinary streamlined state and a rare, dramatic, self-arming one.

entries.name: Portuguese Dogfish
entries.archetype: An Oil-Filled Liver for Neutral Depth

waveform.description: A slow, nearly level line of deep-sea cruising with rare feeding peaks.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a single low-frequency system: slow, buoyant cruising and opportunistic feeding in the deep.

entries.name: Portuguese Man o' War
entries.archetype: Four Kinds of Animal in One Body

waveform.description: A low passive line moved by something outside itself.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: passive, divided and moved by forces outside itself.

entries.name: Postman Butterfly

modes.label: Wearing another species' pattern • Both being genuinely toxic • Sharing the cost of teaching

waveform.description: An unhurried even glide, matched to a relative rather than distinguished from it, because the biology genuinely is shared.

entries.closingLine: Since the flower circuit repeats daily across a long life, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pot-bellied Seahorse

modes.label: The female depositing eggs into a sealed pouch on the male's abdomen • Pouch tissue growing a dense capillary bed around the embedded eggs and regulating salinity, oxygen and nutrients inside • The male carrying the brood for weeks and then expelling fully formed young by muscular contraction

waveform.description: A long sustained raised period, because the whole brood is carried continuously for weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Potato Leafhopper

modes.label: Probing leaf veins with piercing mouthparts • Injecting saliva that plugs the phloem • Feeding while the leaf beyond the puncture starves

waveform.description: A very rapid shallow repetition across the whole span, because feeding probes are continuous and individually tiny.

entries.closingLine: Since probes recur constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Potter Wasp

modes.label: Building a clay pot the size of a small marble • Suspending a single egg from the ceiling on a fine filament before any food goes in • Packing paralysed caterpillars beneath it and sealing the lid

waveform.description: A repeated sequence of similar effortful cycles, because each cell is built, stocked and sealed the same way.

entries.closingLine: Since cells are completed within days, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Potto

waveform.description: An extremely even line with no acceleration anywhere along it.

entries.closingLine: Minimal expenditure and continuous contact make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Powder Blue Isopod

modes.label: Secreting a fine waxy bloom across the whole cuticle surface • Reducing water loss through that layer in air other isopods cannot tolerate • Renewing the coating after each moult as the old cuticle is shed

waveform.description: A brisk even oscillation, because this is a fast-moving active isopod rather than a slow one.

entries.closingLine: Because the maintenance is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Powder Blue Tang

modes.label: Holding a defined patch of reef and grazing it repeatedly • Driving off other herbivores that enter • Cropping the turf short enough to keep it growing rather than letting it mature

waveform.description: A working grazing rhythm punctuated by sharper events, because feeding is continuous and intruders are driven off repeatedly.

entries.closingLine: Since grazing and defence are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Prairie Dog
entries.archetype: An Alarm Call That Describes the Predator

waveform.description: A steady colonial rhythm with continuous calling.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuous grazing under continuous, informative vocal coverage.

entries.name: Prairie Vole

waveform.description: Even, medium-height oscillations showing repeated short trips out from the nest and back, with no long flat waits or extreme bursts.

entries.closingLine: This creates a mid-frequency system: a steady, rhythmic pattern of shared activity centred on a fixed nest, with continuous practical care rather than rare big efforts or deep long-term storage.

entries.name: Praying Mantis

modes.label: Two large forward-facing eyes with overlapping fields on a head that swivels freely • Comparing the two images to extract distance rather than judging it from motion or size • Striking only once the prey is inside the fixed reach of the forelegs

waveform.description: A long motionless line with extremely brief strikes, because the animal holds still and then moves in milliseconds.

entries.closingLine: Because strikes are brief and occasional, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Prevost's Squirrel

modes.label: Populations separated by the large rivers and straits of Sundaland • Each isolated block diverging in coat colour into sharply distinct regional forms • Dozens of named subspecies across Borneo, Sumatra and the peninsula differing mainly in how the black, white and chestnut are arranged

waveform.description: A stepped drifting line, because each isolated population moves independently rather than as one connected system.

entries.closingLine: Because divergence runs over evolutionary time, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Proboscis Monkey

waveform.description: Regular deep calls punctuating a steady feeding rhythm — the sound marks the day rather than interrupting it.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding and calling run as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Pronghorn
entries.archetype: Built for a Predator That Is Gone

waveform.description: Sustained high-rate output held without dropping.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: sustained, expensive and built for a pressure that has gone.

entries.name: Psychedelic Frogfish

waveform.description: Long flat low-activity periods with occasional sharp, narrow spikes representing sudden ambush strikes before dropping back to stillness.

entries.closingLine: That combination of extended hidden waiting and rare explosive strikes makes this a bimodal low–high system.

entries.name: Pufferfish
entries.archetype: A Stomach That Becomes a Balloon

waveform.description: A slow low line rising sharply into a held plateau and dropping back.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: slow precise movement and a rare, dramatic, physically limiting transformation.

entries.name: Puku

waveform.description: A grazing rhythm with the head coming up on a constant beat.

entries.closingLine: Continuous grazing with continuous watching makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Purple Finch

waveform.description: A repeated working rhythm: the same modest force applied over and over.

entries.closingLine: That makes the finch a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and repeatable, where output comes from accurate repetition rather than from any large effort.

entries.name: Purple Frog

waveform.description: An almost unbroken trough with a single very narrow raised section — one fortnight out of a year.

entries.closingLine: Because it runs a year-long buried state and a fortnight-long surface one, it is bimodal.

entries.name: Purple Gallinule

waveform.description: A careful even pace with no step larger than the last.

entries.closingLine: Continuous, considered movement over an unstable surface makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Purple-crowned Fairywren
entries.archetype: Waiting in Line Along the River

waveform.description: A steady cooperative rhythm through the day along a narrow strip of cover.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, cooperative work within a saturated strip of habitat.

entries.name: Pygmy Hippopotamus

waveform.description: A quiet unhurried rhythm — a solitary animal moving through forest at night and resting by day.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs slowly and continuously, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pygmy Marmoset

waveform.description: A patient repeating round of visits with nothing sharp in it.

entries.closingLine: Very low intake from a maintained resource makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pygmy Seahorse

waveform.description: A flat line with barely perceptible movement — a fish whose entire strategy is to be indistinguishable from the thing it sits on.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal replaces activity with an exact structural match to one object, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pygmy Slow Loris

waveform.description: A deep flat trough and a raised active section — the same animal running at two different settings across the year.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal is not the same system in both halves of the year and needs both, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Pygmy Three-toed Sloth

waveform.description: An almost unbroken low line — the system rarely departs from its baseline at all.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal has solved a small island by becoming a smaller animal that spends almost nothing, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pyramid Sea Butterfly

waveform.description: Even, low-amplitude ripples representing steady, rhythmic fluttering to maintain position and feed.

entries.closingLine: That makes the Pyramid Sea Butterfly a mid-frequency system built around ongoing, rhythmic, network-like movement through the water column.

entries.name: Pyrenean Brook Newt

waveform.description: A held line with only slight tremor — the profile of an animal whose main activity is not being moved.

entries.closingLine: Because persistence in a demanding niche replaces speed and turnover, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Pyrenean Desman

waveform.description: Gentle, even ripples around a midline, showing a steady pattern of repeated aquatic foraging passes along the stream.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole system is built around this steady, touch-led tracking of hidden pathways in moving water, the Pyrenean Desman is best understood as a single, mid-frequency foraging engine.

entries.name: Quenda

waveform.description: Small repeated diggings at an even nightly rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: small repeated disturbances whose value accumulates in the soil rather than in the animal.

entries.name: Quokka

modes.label: Browsing at dusk • Resting in scrub • Not running away

waveform.description: A quiet browsing rhythm with no sharp escape events.

entries.closingLine: Slow, nocturnal and conservative, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Raccoon Dog

waveform.description: An active rhythm through the warm months dropping to a long flat winter trough and returning.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a broad active earning phase and a low dormant spending phase.

entries.name: Racket-tailed Roller

modes.label: Climbing steeply and then diving with the wings half closed • Rolling and tumbling through the descent so the flight is barely controlled • Pulling out close to the ground while calling, with the elongated tail rackets streaming behind

waveform.description: A flat line broken by violent tumbling excursions, because the display is a sequence of abrupt uncontrolled-looking movements.

entries.closingLine: Because displays are seasonal, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Radiated Tortoise

waveform.description: A line that barely rises across its whole length — output accumulating over decades rather than within a season.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Raggiana Bird-of-paradise

waveform.description: A mostly mid-level line with one sharp, narrow dip upward (higher activity) showing a brief, intense display phase rising out of a steady rhythmic baseline.

entries.closingLine: That makes the Raggiana Bird-of-paradise a bimodal system: a mid-frequency, site-faithful rhythm that supports a high-frequency, disciplined display burst.

entries.name: Rail-babbler

waveform.description: An even, unbroken line of steady walking and foraging on the forest floor.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a single-mode system: steady, secretive foraging on foot across the forest floor.

entries.name: Rainbow Bee-eater

waveform.description: A regular catch-and-process rhythm repeated all day.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: a steady repeating cycle in which every item has to be handled before it can be used.

entries.name: Rainbow Crab

modes.label: Living in deep burrows inland, breathing air through modified gill chambers kept moist • Carrying eggs until they are ready and then migrating to the shore to release larvae into seawater • The larvae developing entirely in the sea before returning as juveniles to colonise land again

waveform.description: A flat resident line with one pronounced migratory episode, because the year is ordinary except for the run to the sea.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Rainbow Lorikeet

modes.label: A tongue tipped with erectile papillae that rise into a brush when extended • Sweeping nectar and pollen out of flowers rather than crushing seed • Moving between flowering trees as different species come into bloom across the year

waveform.description: A rapid repeating rhythm, because the bird works flower after flower in quick succession all day.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Rainbow Runner
entries.archetype: A School That Reads as One Surface

waveform.description: Dense fast output sustained without pause.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: continuously fast and collectively protected.

entries.name: Rainbow Scarab
entries.archetype: Tunnels That Pack Dung Into Brood Balls

waveform.description: Quiet in cool months, steady tunnelling and burying through the warm season.

entries.closingLine: It is a SINGLE MID system of steady seasonal work.

entries.name: Rainbow Stag Beetle
entries.archetype: Years in Rotting Wood, Weeks of Jaws

waveform.description: A long, slowly rising larval line ending in a short burst of adult contests.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-change system: a long larval stage and a short, contest-driven adult stage.

entries.name: Rainbow Trout

modes.label: Holding the seam • Reading the drift • Taking and returning

waveform.description: A fine rapid serration riding on one flat hold line, because the interceptions are frequent and small and the station never moves.

entries.closingLine: Because a continuously held position is worked by a constant fine rhythm of interceptions, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Rainbowfish
entries.archetype: Flashing Colours in a Sunlit School

waveform.description: Steady schooling with brief, bright spikes of male display.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: coordinated schooling with brief bursts of display.

entries.name: Rakali

modes.label: Swimming the margin • Carrying prey ashore • Dissecting it precisely

waveform.description: A repeating cycle of entering the water and returning to the bank.

entries.closingLine: Continuous nightly hunting makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ram’s Horn Squid
entries.archetype: Gas Chambers in a Coiled Inner Shell

waveform.description: A low, gentle wave: near-weightless hovering with one rise and fall each day.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: near-weightless hovering and a regular daily vertical migration.

entries.name: Ray

modes.label: Lying flat under sand with only the eyes and two openings on the upper surface exposed • Drawing clean water in through those spiracles behind the eyes rather than through the mouth below • Passing it over the gills and out beneath, so respiration continues without disturbing the sand or the disguise

waveform.description: An extremely flat and even line, because a buried ray does almost nothing at all for long periods.

entries.closingLine: Because a buried ray is nearly motionless, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Razorbill
entries.archetype: The Same Wing in Two Fluids

waveform.description: A rapid flight rhythm giving way to a deep sustained dive.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: marginal costly flight and deep sustained wing-powered diving.

entries.name: Razorfish

modes.label: Holding the body vertical with the snout pointing at the seabed • Hovering in synchronised groups between the spines of a sea urchin • Moving as a unit while keeping the same orientation

waveform.description: A very steady shallow rhythm, because the fish hovers and adjusts constantly without ever moving quickly.

entries.closingLine: Since adjustments are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Admiral

modes.label: Drawing a nettle leaf over itself and stitching the edges with silk • Feeding on the inside of that closed tent while hidden • Abandoning it and building a larger one at each successive stage

waveform.description: A stepped rhythm of build and outgrow, because each instar repeats the same construction at a larger size.

entries.closingLine: Because construction repeats through the stages, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Ant

modes.label: Releasing volatile alarm compounds from head glands on contact • Drawing nestmates toward the source within seconds • Stinging or spraying acid once they arrive

waveform.description: Flat stretches broken by abrupt spikes that decay quickly, because the alarm signal is volatile and fades almost as fast as it appears.

entries.closingLine: Since the signal rises and decays within seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Assassin Bug

waveform.description: A very slow low line with minimal variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, adhesive and protected by advertisement.

entries.name: Red Bird-of-paradise

waveform.description: Even, repeating mid-height pulses representing regular returns to a display perch for ritualized courtship performances.

entries.closingLine: This makes the species a mid-frequency system: a rhythmic, site-centered performer whose biology is built around sustained, repeated ritual presence rather than single dramatic peaks or deep-conservation lows.

entries.name: Red Crossbill

waveform.description: Even, repeating mid-height pulses showing regular bouts of focused cone-opening activity separated by brief resets.

entries.closingLine: Because their whole system is built around repeated, precise use of a specialized tool in regular foraging cycles, the red crossbill is a mid-frequency system with rhythmic, targeted activity rather than long dormancy or explosive bursts.

entries.name: Red Deer
entries.archetype: A Roar That Declares Body Size

waveform.description: An even grazing rhythm broken by a sustained deep contest.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: separate herd grazing and a short, exhausting, largely acoustic contest.

entries.name: Red Fox

waveform.description: A quiet patrolling rhythm interrupted by one narrow committed spike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a cheap, flexible search mode punctuated by short decisive strikes.

entries.name: Red Handfish
entries.archetype: Hand-Fins Walking a Tiny Reef Patch

waveform.description: A nearly flat line of slow walking and resting on the reef floor.

entries.closingLine: Because it is built on slow bottom walking in one small place, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Hartebeest

waveform.description: An unchanging long-striding rhythm that could continue indefinitely.

entries.closingLine: Sustained repeatable output rather than any burst makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Harvester Ant

waveform.description: Even, medium-height peaks showing repeated daily foraging trips out and back to the nest with steady effort.

entries.closingLine: The result is a mid-frequency system built on coordinated, repeatable work: not a single big burst, but steady, rhythmic collection that fills the granary before the ground turns empty.

entries.name: Red Imported Fire Ant

modes.label: A single queen founding alone • Workers killing any additional queen • Territories defended against neighbouring colonies
Dozens or hundreds of queens in one network • No aggression between neighbouring nests • Spread by budding rather than flight

waveform.description: Two clearly separated levels held for long stretches, because a colony is in one social form or the other and does not sit between them.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two colony architectures, making this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Red Junglefowl

modes.label: Producing different alarm calls for aerial and ground predators • Calling far more when a hen is within earshot • Staying silent when alone or when only a rival male is present

waveform.description: A working baseline broken by alarm events of differing depth, because the response varies with who is present.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Kangaroo

waveform.description: An even bouncing rhythm where each cycle looks like the one before it.

entries.closingLine: That makes the kangaroo a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, repeatable and efficient precisely because the pace does not change.

entries.name: Red Kite

modes.label: Riding lift • Scanning • Dropping on whatever appeared

waveform.description: Long easy soaring with occasional drops to the ground.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daylight searching makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Lady Beetle

modes.label: Pores at the leg joints from which the beetle can release droplets of its own haemolymph on demand • That fluid carrying bitter alkaloids that ants, birds and lizards reject immediately, and staining what it touches • The beetle recovering afterwards, so the defence costs fluid and alkaloid rather than the animal itself

waveform.description: A steady foraging rhythm with occasional discharges, because the beetle hunts continuously and bleeds only when handled.

entries.closingLine: Because discharges are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Lory

modes.label: A liquid nectar diet with very little bulk and almost no fibre • A short simple gut with rapid transit that extracts sugars and passes the rest through within an hour or two • No capacity to store a meal, so the bird must feed for much of the day and cannot go long without

waveform.description: A very rapid repeating rhythm, because feeding and processing cycle many times through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle repeats many times a day, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Palm Weevil

modes.label: Adults boring into the crown of a palm and laying eggs inside the soft tissue at the growing point • Larvae tunnelling through that tissue in numbers, hollowing the crown while the fronds above remain green • The tree only showing symptoms when the crown collapses, by which point it is already dead and has been producing weevils for months

waveform.description: A slow internal build with no external sign, because everything happens inside the tree over months.

entries.closingLine: Because development runs over months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Panda

waveform.description: A shallow steady rhythm near the baseline — long feeding bouts and long rests, with nothing sharp between them.

entries.closingLine: Because intake is poor and everything is slowed to match, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Paper Wasp

modes.label: Chewing wood fibre into paper • Building a single uncovered comb on a stalk • Defending it with bodies rather than with a wall

waveform.description: A steady moderate rhythm without extremes, because the colony works continuously at one modest scale.

entries.closingLine: Since the colony cycle runs through a season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red River Hog
entries.archetype: A Snout Disc Driven by the Neck

waveform.description: A steady digging rhythm sustained across a foraging group.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady collective excavation.

entries.name: Red Salamander

waveform.description: A slow low line with minimal variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, unarmed and defended by a resemblance rather than by anything it produces.

entries.name: Red Sea Urchin

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing steady, modest activity and expenditure sustained over a very long span.

entries.closingLine: Because nearly everything in this system favors durability, low daily output and very long time horizons rather than bursts or switching states, the Red Sea Urchin is a strongly low-frequency system built for patient survival across centuries.

entries.name: Red Slender Loris

waveform.description: Long stretches of low, steady activity punctuated by a single sharp, narrow spike representing a rapid reach or strike after extended cautious movement.

entries.closingLine: That makes the Red Slender Loris a bimodal system: a dominant low-frequency creeping mode structurally paired with essential high-frequency snatch movements.

entries.name: Red Slug

modes.label: A mucus that behaves as a solid glue when undisturbed and as a liquid when sheared by the foot • Waves of muscular contraction passing along the foot, liquefying the mucus locally under each moving section • The rest of the animal held firmly in place by the same mucus while those sections advance, so it can climb vertical surfaces without sliding

waveform.description: A regular wave rhythm, because waves of contraction pass along the foot continuously while the animal moves.

entries.closingLine: Because the waves pass continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Squirrel
entries.archetype: Caches Found by Smell, Not Memory

waveform.description: An intense autumn burst settling into a long low winter line.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a short intense storing phase and a long retrieving one.

entries.name: Red Swamp Crayfish

modes.label: Carrying the oomycete Aphanomyces astaci in its cuticle while remaining healthy • Shedding spores continuously into any water it occupies • Killing native European crayfish that have no resistance while itself persisting and spreading

waveform.description: A steady relentless advance without episodes, because the spread is continuous rather than event-driven.

entries.closingLine: Because the spread runs across seasons, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Tegu

modes.label: Basking first • Ranging wide • Eating almost anything

waveform.description: A long flat floor with a single raised working season lifted out of it, because the year has two settings and no gradual middle.

entries.closingLine: Because conditions select between two genuinely different operating states, this is an adaptive system.

entries.name: Red Triangle Slug
entries.archetype: A Radula Rasping the Film on Bark

waveform.description: Dry-weather flat stretches alternating with rises of grazing after rain.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: wet-weather grazing and dry-weather withdrawal.

entries.name: Red Wolf

waveform.description: A line drifting slowly downward — a decline measured in genetic composition rather than in deaths.

entries.closingLine: Because everything about the process runs slowly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red Zebra Cichlid

modes.label: The female taking her eggs into her mouth immediately after laying • The male displaying yellow egg-shaped spots on his anal fin • The female nipping at those false eggs and taking in sperm, fertilising the clutch already in her mouth

waveform.description: A flat line with one raised breeding episode, because the whole sequence happens once in a cycle of weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-backed Fairywren

waveform.description: A mostly mid-level, gently undulating line for routine cover-tied activity, with one sharp, narrow spike showing a brief display burst before returning to the previous rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That pattern makes the Red-backed Fairywren a bimodal system: a mid-frequency, habitat-matching routine with essential high-frequency flashes of color and display.

entries.name: Red-backed Poison Frog

waveform.description: An unvarying low line with small regular movements — an animal with no reason to hurry and nothing to hide from.

entries.closingLine: Because a chemical defence removes the need for speed or concealment, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-bearded Bee-eater

waveform.description: Long low, flat stretches of stillness punctuated by brief, sharp spikes representing rapid intercept flights.

entries.closingLine: This architecture—long periods of low-cost monitoring punctuated by brief, high-intensity intercepts—means it structurally depends on both a low-frequency watch state and a high-frequency strike state, making it a bimodal low–high system.

entries.name: Red-bellied Pacu

modes.label: Rows of broad flat molar-like teeth strikingly similar to human molars • Fruit and hard nuts falling into flooded forest during the annual high water • The fish cracking those seeds, digesting some and voiding others intact far from the parent tree

waveform.description: A single broad annual swell, because the whole feeding pattern follows the rise and fall of the river.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-bellied Piranha
entries.archetype: A Jaw Beyond Its Body Size

waveform.description: A steady shoaling and foraging rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady grouped foraging with an extreme cutting tool.

entries.name: Red-bellied Titi
entries.archetype: The Infant Attaches to the Father

modes.label: Duetting at dawn • Sitting tails twined • The father carrying

waveform.description: A quiet stable rhythm with a duet at the start of the day.

entries.closingLine: Small, quiet and stable over years, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-billed Oxpecker
entries.archetype: Riding and Feeding on Living Hosts

waveform.description: A steady line of foraging on hosts with one sharp spike of alarm.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady foraging over the bodies of large mammals and sudden alarm flights.

entries.name: Red-billed Tropicbird
entries.archetype: A Seabird Related to No Seabird

modes.label: Soaring far offshore • Plunging • Shuffling back to a ledge

waveform.description: Long ocean gliding punctuated by steep plunges.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daily ocean foraging makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-breasted Goose

waveform.description: A quiet summer of sheltered nesting, then winter days of dawn-to-dusk flock commuting.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a daily winter commute in dense flocks and sheltered tundra nesting.

entries.name: Red-breasted Nuthatch

modes.label: Conifer resin collected and carried in the bill, sometimes on a flake of bark used as an applicator • Smeared in a ring around the outside and inside of the nest hole entrance • The bird flying straight in without touching the sides, while anything that lands on the rim is caught

waveform.description: A seasonal build and decline, because the resin is applied repeatedly through the nesting period and then stops.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-breasted Parakeet

modes.label: Contact calls learned from surrounding birds rather than inherited • Populations in different parts of the range converging on distinct call structures • A bird's calls identifying where it came from and whether it belongs to the local flock

waveform.description: A varied rhythm that differs from place to place, because the material is learned rather than fixed.

entries.closingLine: Because dialect change runs across generations, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-capped Manakin
entries.archetype: Wing Muscle Faster Than a Hummingbird's

waveform.description: A quiet feeding line broken by an extremely rapid display sequence.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an ordinary feeding baseline and an extremely fast display.

entries.name: Red-crested Pochard

waveform.description: An unhurried mixed feeding rhythm alternating shallow and deeper.

entries.closingLine: Steady mixed feeding on open water makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-crowned Crane

waveform.description: Paired call bursts at either end of the day with long steady foraging between — the bond is renewed twice daily.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on repeated coordinated display and steady foraging, it is a mid-frequency system.
