entries.name: Red-eared Slider

modes.label: Hauling out onto logs, banks and rocks to raise body temperature above the water • Occupying the best basking sites earlier, longer and more aggressively than native turtles • Forcing residents into cooler or more exposed places where digestion and egg development slow

waveform.description: A strong daily cycle of hauling out and returning, because the whole pattern is driven by the movement of the sun.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-eyed Crocodile Skink
entries.archetype: One Egg, and a Mother Guarding It

modes.label: Hidden in damp litter • Squeaking when seized • Sitting with one egg

waveform.description: A very quiet trace: a small animal that mostly hides.

entries.closingLine: Slow, hidden and low-output, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-fan Parrot
entries.archetype: Hidden Ruff Raised in an Instant

waveform.description: A steady canopy rhythm interrupted by one sudden spike when the fan is raised.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: quiet productive foraging and a rare, abrupt display.

entries.name: Red-footed Cannibalfly

waveform.description: A still perched line broken by a short violent interception.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: motionless watching and one violent committed interception.

entries.name: Red-footed Tortoise

waveform.description: A very slow steady line with small variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: unhurried, economical and effective over long timescales.

entries.name: Red-kneed Tarantula
entries.archetype: Barbed Hairs Kicked Into Your Face

modes.label: Sitting at the burrow • Raising the front • Flicking hairs off the abdomen

waveform.description: A near-motionless trace across a life measured in decades.

entries.closingLine: Slow, long-lived and almost motionless, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-knobbed Coot

waveform.description: A patrolling rhythm with sharp confrontations raised out of it.

entries.closingLine: Continuous feeding and patrolling makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-legged Honeycreeper

waveform.description: A regular mid-level rhythm of repeated short visits.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: a steady repeated rhythm of many small gains across a wide area.

entries.name: Red-legged Seriema
entries.archetype: A Duet That Spaces the Grassland

waveform.description: Dawn calling either side of a long day of walking.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady ground-level hunting inside a territory maintained acoustically rather than by patrol.

entries.name: Red-lipped Batfish

waveform.description: A barely moving line with a few small shuffles and one extension.

entries.closingLine: Almost no movement and long waits make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-necked Phalarope
entries.archetype: Spinning Up Prey, Leaving Males to Incubate

waveform.description: A busy spinning rhythm, a long quiet incubation phase, then a return to feeding.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: rapid surface feeding and a slow, male-run incubation phase.

entries.name: Red-necked Wallaby

waveform.description: A gently undulating mid-level line showing steady, rhythmic activity with small buffered fluctuations rather than sharp spikes or long flat lows.

entries.closingLine: This creates a buffered, ongoing rhythm of foraging, resting and care, where a modest reserve of reproductive and energetic capacity is always held back for the next joey rather than spent all at once, making the wallaby a mid-frequency, rhythm-and-buffer system.

entries.name: Red-shanked Douc

waveform.description: A shallow rhythm near the baseline — short feeding bouts separated by long periods of digestion.

entries.closingLine: Because intake and processing both run slowly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-sided Garter Snake

waveform.description: A long cold floor rising into a short active season and falling back.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: extreme concentration at a fixed point and wide dispersal afterwards.

entries.name: Red-spotted Guard Crab

waveform.description: Even, modest oscillations showing a steady pattern of cautious outings from cover and returns, without long dormancy or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: This creates a mid-frequency system built on repeated, measured patrols around a fixed home rather than long stillness or all-or-nothing lunges.

entries.name: Red-spotted Purple

modes.label: Dark iridescent blue wings with no white band • Resembling the toxic pipevine swallowtail • Occurring where that model is common
A bold white band across both wings • No resemblance to any toxic species • Occurring north of where the model lives

waveform.description: Two separated stable levels joined by a single transition, because the two forms meet only in a narrow band of country.

entries.closingLine: The two defences also work on different timescales, the mimicry depending on a season of predator learning where the banded form acts within one encounter, which makes this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Red-tailed Black Shark

modes.label: Holding a territory around a cave, root or rock on the stream bed • Attacking intruders in proportion to how closely they resemble itself • Ignoring fish of different shape and habit that use other parts of the water

waveform.description: A calm baseline interrupted by regular sharp confrontations, because the fish patrols quietly and charges intruders.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-tailed Hawk

waveform.description: A long cheap scan followed by one narrow committed drop.

entries.closingLine: That makes the hawk a bimodal system: an extremely cheap elevated search state and a brief decisive descent.

entries.name: Red-tailed Tinfoil Barb

modes.label: Flanks covered in guanine-crystal scales that reflect light almost like a mirror • Hundreds of fish shoaling and turning together so the reflections flash and shift constantly • A predator unable to hold a single target because the visual field is broken into moving points of light

waveform.description: A rapid coordinated rhythm, because the whole shoal turns and flashes continuously.

entries.closingLine: Because turning is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-tailed Tropicbird

waveform.description: A mostly steady mid-level line of cruising flight with a single sharp dip-and-rise spike for the plunge or evasive burst before returning to stable distance-holding.

entries.closingLine: The system therefore runs on a mid-frequency baseline of sustained line-holding flight punctuated by short, structurally important high-frequency bursts for plunges and escapes, making it a bimodal pattern.

entries.name: Red-veined Darter

modes.label: Arriving in spring from further south • Breeding immediately in warm shallow water • Producing adults from those eggs within about two months, which then breed again or move on

waveform.description: A working rhythm with two distinct raised events, because the summer contains two separate emergences.

entries.closingLine: Since emergences and breeding recur within a season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Red-vented Bulbul

waveform.description: Even, repeating mid-height ripples showing steady, small bursts of activity as the bird moves between many modest food patches through the day.

entries.closingLine: The result is a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, networked foraging across many small urban opportunities, with no separate high-burst or deep-reserve operating mode.

entries.name: Red-winged Blackbird

waveform.description: A mid-level, gently undulating line for routine song-display punctuated by brief sharp dips upward representing sudden high-intensity warning flashes.

entries.closingLine: This split between ongoing broadcast and triggered escalation makes the Red-winged Blackbird a bimodal system, with a mid-frequency signaling baseline and a high-frequency warning-and-confrontation mode layered on top.

entries.name: Redclaw Crayfish

modes.label: Carrying eggs beneath the tail • Hatching young already formed • Releasing juveniles straight into the burrow

waveform.description: Broad low plateaus separated by raised sections, because brooding periods interrupt an otherwise even routine.

entries.closingLine: Since brooding cycles repeat within a season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Redwing

modes.label: Flying through the night over unlit country • Giving a thin high seep call repeatedly • Keeping a loose flock together by sound alone

waveform.description: A regular unvarying pulse maintained across the whole span, because the call is repeated steadily through hours of flight.

entries.closingLine: Since calls recur through the night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Reef Manta Ray
entries.archetype: Open-Mouthed Filter Wings and Cleaning Stops

waveform.description: Bouts of plankton feeding separated by slower, hovering visits to cleaning stations.

entries.closingLine: Because the system alternates between active feeding and slow, site-faithful cleaning visits, it is bimodal.

entries.name: Reef Stonefish

waveform.description: A long flat low line of stillness with a single sharp, narrow spike representing the brief, contact-triggered strike and venom discharge before returning to rest.

entries.closingLine: The system is built on long, low-expenditure stillness punctuated by very brief, contact-triggered bursts, so it operates as a bimodal pattern with a dominant low-frequency waiting mode and a sharp high-frequency response mode.

entries.name: Reeves's Muntjac

waveform.description: A quiet line broken by a long series of repeated calls.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a hidden solitary baseline and a persistent vocal response.

entries.name: Regent Bowerbird

waveform.description: Daily building strokes accumulating through the season with regular small setbacks — construction that has to be redone as often as it is added to.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts steady daily construction into reproductive standing, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Reindeer

waveform.description: A long unvarying travelling rhythm held across whole seasons.

entries.closingLine: Sustained long-distance movement makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Remora

waveform.description: A flat low line: almost no work done by the animal itself.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: economical, patient and built around riding rather than producing movement.

entries.name: Resplendent Quetzal

waveform.description: Short hovering sallies repeated through the day at an even rate — each one is a single fruit taken and returned with.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding runs as a steady sequence of short sallies rather than long pursuits or rare strikes, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Reticulated Python
entries.archetype: A Heat Image Built From Lip Pits

waveform.description: A motionless line broken by one very fast strike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: prolonged thermally-guided waiting and a very fast strike.

entries.name: Reticulated River Stingray

modes.label: Settled on sand • Net pattern breaking the edge • Feeling for worms

waveform.description: A long shallow drift with no events in it, the trace of an animal whose main activity is not being seen.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs slowly across a river bottom, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Rhinoceros
entries.archetype: Bulk Forage Behind a Keratin Horn

waveform.description: A long, heavy feeding line interrupted by one brief, sharp charge.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: slow bulk feeding and brief defensive charges.

entries.name: Rhinoceros Hornbill

waveform.description: Repeated delivery runs of almost identical shape — a schedule rather than a hunt, held for months without variation.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system depends on a repeated dependable circuit rather than reserves or bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Rhinoceros Iguana

waveform.description: A slow shallow rhythm — long basking, occasional feeding, nothing that resembles a burst.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs slowly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Rhinoceros Rat Snake

waveform.description: A slow shallow undulation that never leaves the low band — movement at the speed of a branch in wind.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal spends almost nothing and earns its living by being mistaken for vegetation, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Rhinoceros Viper

waveform.description: A long motionless floor with one vertical strike — the same architecture as its drier-forest relatives, in wetter ground.

entries.closingLine: Because near-zero waiting supports one overwhelming commitment, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Ribbon Eel

waveform.description: A continuous gentle sway with small, quick notches where a snap occurs — the body never leaves its low band.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal spends almost nothing on locomotion and earns its food by waiting in place with a very small maintenance bill, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ribbon-tailed Astrapia

waveform.description: A mostly low, steady line showing careful everyday movement with one sharp dip-and-rise spike representing a short, intense display burst.

entries.closingLine: That combination of burdened conservation in daily life and explosive show during mating makes this a bimodal system with a low baseline and a high-frequency display mode.

entries.name: Rice Grasshopper

modes.label: Life spent on rice stems standing in water rather than on dry ground • The insect swimming when it falls in and climbing back onto a stem rather than drowning • Eggs laid in the raised bunds and drier margins above the waterline, so the vulnerable stage is never submerged

waveform.description: A steady active rhythm, because the insect feeds, climbs and moves continuously through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because activity is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Rifleman
entries.archetype: Spiralling Up Every Trunk All Day

waveform.description: A continuous saw-tooth of short climbs and drops through the whole foraging day.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: a steady, repetitive working rhythm with no slow or explosive phase.

entries.name: Ring-billed Gull

modes.label: Working whatever is briefly abundant • Learning where and when it appears • Moving on when it stops

waveform.description: Irregular spikes of different heights against a common baseline, because each opportunity is a different size and arrives unpredictably.

entries.closingLine: Since opportunities turn over within days, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ring-necked Dove

modes.label: Putting the bill into water and drawing continuously • Emptying a puddle in seconds without straightening up • Leaving the water almost immediately

waveform.description: A calm baseline broken by short flat-bottomed dips, because drinking is a brief continuous act rather than a series of movements.

entries.closingLine: Since drinking and feeding recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ring-tailed Lemur

waveform.description: A steady troop rhythm with a raised start — the day opens with sunning and settles into coordinated foraging.

entries.closingLine: Because troop coherence is maintained by continuous signalling and repeated daily routine, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ring-tailed Vontsira
entries.archetype: A Generalist on Floor, Trunk and Stream

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line of daytime foraging with small peaks.

entries.closingLine: Because it is built around steady opportunistic foraging, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Ringed Seal
entries.archetype: A Snow Room Above the Hole

modes.label: Scraping holes open • Diving • Hollowing a chamber in a drift

waveform.description: A patient repeating cycle of dive, surface and scrape.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ringtail
entries.archetype: Hind Feet That Turn Right Round

waveform.description: An agile climbing rhythm moving constantly between levels.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuously active in three dimensions rather than fast in one.

entries.name: Rivoli's Hummingbird

waveform.description: A front section of dense, small-amplitude oscillations showing intense hovering activity, followed by a long, gentle descent into a flat low line representing extended sheltered rest.

entries.closingLine: The system therefore depends on a high-frequency hover-and-dart mode coupled to a contrasting low-frequency resting mode that keeps the engine from burning out, making it a bimodal pattern built around explosive precision sustained by deep stillness.

entries.name: Roadside Hawk

modes.label: Perching on exposed posts, wires and low branches along the boundary of forest and open ground • Watching the cleared side while remaining in cover on the wooded side • Dropping short distances onto lizards, large insects and small vertebrates crossing that boundary

waveform.description: A steady repeating rhythm of perch, watch and short drop, sustained through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because hunting is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Roan Antelope
entries.archetype: Ruined by Making the Land Better

modes.label: Grazing tall poor grass • Watching • Living at low density

waveform.description: A steady grazing and scanning rhythm across the day.

entries.closingLine: Steady grazing and vigilance makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Robust Ghost Pipefish
entries.archetype: A Drifting Leaf with a Pipette Snout

waveform.description: A still, hovering line with brief dips for each snap at prey.

entries.closingLine: Because it is built on stillness, disguise and brief ambush strikes, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Rock Cavy

waveform.description: Long stretches of steady, low-level activity near shelter with a brief sharp spike representing a sudden, coordinated dash into rock crevices when alarm is raised.

entries.closingLine: Because their survival depends on spending most of their time in a cautious, shelter-anchored state and occasionally converting that into a rapid collective dash, the rock cavy operates as a bimodal system with a low-frequency watch-and-feed mode and a high-frequency alarm-and-retreat mode.

entries.name: Rock Hyrax

waveform.description: A long low warming phase with short raised feeding bouts.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long passive warming and brief guarded feeding.

entries.name: Rock Ptarmigan

waveform.description: A gently undulating, low-amplitude line showing slow, continuous adjustment rather than sharp bursts or swings.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system: a dense, patient, season-locked cycle that spends energy on infrequent, whole-body updates rather than constant rapid adjustments.

entries.name: Roe Deer

waveform.description: A steady year with a long flattened section in the middle — the months when development is paused rather than absent.

entries.closingLine: Because the annual cycle runs steadily, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Roloway Monkey

waveform.description: A continuous social rhythm across the day — many small exchanges rather than any single event.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on constant low-cost signalling and steady daily foraging, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Rook

waveform.description: A steady collective rhythm: the colony's day repeated without individual variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes the rook a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, networked and dependent on numbers doing what one bird cannot.

entries.name: Roosterfish

waveform.description: Patrolling broken repeatedly by very steep committed runs.

entries.closingLine: Short violent pursuits in shallow broken water make this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Rose-ringed Parakeet

modes.label: Feeding out in small parties • Returning to one roost • Following whoever fed well

waveform.description: A busy daytime rhythm with two taller convergences in it, because the flock assembles twice a day and disperses between.

entries.closingLine: Since the feeding and the assembling repeat on one daily cycle, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Roseate Spoonbill

waveform.description: A steady side-to-side sweep with a snap cut into each pass.

entries.closingLine: Continuous rhythmic sweeping makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Roseate Tern

waveform.description: Repeated dips below the working line — each plunge is a fall rather than a burst, and the recovery is the expensive part.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from many repeated modest dives, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Rosy Maple Moth

waveform.description: A single rise to a sustained peak followed by a decline with no recovery.

entries.closingLine: That makes the adult a high-frequency system: short-horizon, fully committed and spending a fixed store as fast as it usefully can.

entries.name: Rosy Tetra

modes.label: Holding spacing • Matching heading • Turning with the neighbour

waveform.description: An identical repeating ripple with no variation whatever, because every part of the system is doing the same thing as its neighbour.

entries.closingLine: Because the matching is continuous and never pauses, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Rough Keyhole Limpet

waveform.description: A mostly low, steady line with two shallow, regular dips for feeding excursions, showing a stable grip with small repeated forays before returning to the same hold.

entries.closingLine: Because its feeding, safety and movement are all organized around this repeated grip-and-return cycle rather than continuous roaming or bursts, its whole biology expresses a low-frequency system built on stable anchoring and rhythmic reuse of the same hold.

entries.name: Rove Beetle

modes.label: A bacterial symbiont living inside the beetle producing pederin, a compound the insect has no genes to synthesise • That toxin held in the body fluid, so crushing the beetle releases it onto skin • Blistering dermatitis developing hours later at the site, from a beetle that never bit or stung anything

waveform.description: A quiet line with occasional releases, because the beetle is unremarkable until it is crushed.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are sporadic, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Royal Antelope

waveform.description: Small frequent feeding movements with a low ceiling — an animal that never does anything large.

entries.closingLine: Because a small body takes many small meals and relies on stillness between them, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Royal Flycatcher

waveform.description: Long, low stretches of quiet activity punctuated by short, tall spikes for sudden crest displays when conditions justify the risk.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is built around long periods of low-key, camouflaged operation punctuated by rare, high-intensity visual bursts, the Royal Flycatcher is best understood as a bimodal system with a low baseline and a high-frequency display mode.

entries.name: Ruby-throated Hummingbird

waveform.description: Dense rapid daytime peaks dropping to a long flat nocturnal floor.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an extremely expensive daytime mode and a near-shutdown at night.

entries.name: Ruddy Daggerwing

modes.label: Long thin tails projecting from the hindwings that resemble antennae • Dark lines on the closed underside converging towards those tails as if towards a head • A strike directed at that end removing a piece of wing while the butterfly leaves in the opposite direction

waveform.description: A quiet resting line with a single sharp interruption, because the butterfly sits still and is attacked occasionally.

entries.closingLine: Because attacks are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Ruddy Darter

waveform.description: Evenly spaced peaks rising from a stable midline, showing repeated short bursts of activity from a consistent perch baseline.

entries.closingLine: This creates a mid-frequency operating pattern: rhythmic, repeatable cycles of moderate expenditure anchored by a recurring perch.

entries.name: Ruddy Ground Dove

waveform.description: A flat low trace: almost nothing about the bird's output varies.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: quiet, economical and dependent on not being detected at all.

entries.name: Ruddy Shelduck

waveform.description: A steady coordinated rhythm shared between two birds.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, coordinated and paired.

entries.name: Ruff

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line of routine activity with a single sharp high spike representing a concentrated lek display phase, then a return to the baseline.

entries.closingLine: Because the species depends on both the ongoing wet-meadow routine and the concentrated arena-display bouts, with a clear rise in tempo when the lek is active, the Ruff operates as a bimodal system with a mid-frequency baseline and a high-frequency display mode.

entries.name: Ruffed Grouse

waveform.description: Accelerating pulses building to a peak, separated by long silences.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and repeated, built around a signal that reaches through cover the bird never leaves.

entries.name: Rufous Elephant Shrew

waveform.description: Long stretches of steady low-level activity punctuated by brief, sharp spikes representing rapid runway sprints when moving between cover or escaping predators.

entries.closingLine: This makes their system bimodal: a dominant low-frequency mode of route maintenance and cautious foraging, and a high-frequency mode of explosive, pathway-bound sprinting when danger or movement demands it.

entries.name: Rufous Hornero

modes.label: Mud and dung carried beakful by beakful and built up in courses that are allowed to dry between them • A domed chamber formed with a side entrance and an internal wall creating a curved passage • The nest baking hard in the sun into a rigid shell that lasts years and is used by many other species afterwards

waveform.description: A long seasonal build and decline, because the nest takes weeks of accumulation and is then simply occupied.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Rufous Potoo

waveform.description: A long, flat day roost followed by brief, sharp feeding sallies after dusk.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: prolonged daytime stillness and short, fast nocturnal sallies.

entries.name: Rufous-bellied Thrush

modes.label: A diet dominated by earthworms and soil invertebrates taken from the surface layer of the ground • Those animals accessible only when the soil is moist enough to be soft and for worms to come near the surface • Breeding therefore timed to the rains, because a brood requires a rate of delivery that only wet ground can supply

waveform.description: A single seasonal peak tied to the rains, because the whole breeding effort falls inside the wet period.

entries.closingLine: Because breeding is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Rufous-sided Crake

waveform.description: A steady, finely textured line of concealed foraging within marsh cover.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a single-mode system: steady, concealed foraging within dense marsh vegetation.

entries.name: Rufous-tailed Jacamar
entries.archetype: A Predator That Learns the Pattern

waveform.description: A repeated sally-and-return rhythm from a fixed perch.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: repeated attempts from a fixed perch, progressively refined.

entries.name: Rugose Hermit Crab

modes.label: A shell occupied on land, where its full weight must be carried rather than supported by water • The interior worn away and remodelled by the crab so the walls become thinner and the internal volume larger • A shell that is lighter to carry and roomier to grow in than the same shell would be for a marine crab

waveform.description: A nightly activity period, because the crab forages after dark and shelters through the heat of the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the remodelling runs over months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Russian Desman

waveform.description: Even, moderate undulations representing steady bouts of underwater snout-scanning and brief returns to the surface or bank.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system: a rhythmic cycle of steady, information-led searching and retreat, built around continuous tactile sampling rather than rare deep reserves or explosive attacks.

entries.name: Russian Tortoise

modes.label: Three months up • Feeding hard • Nine months down

waveform.description: A long flat floor with one shallow raised block near the start, because even the active months are slow ones.

entries.closingLine: Because everything the animal does is slow, compressed and metered against a very short season, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Rusty-spotted Cat

waveform.description: Dense repeated spikes with no rest between them — a night of many small hunts rather than one decisive event.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal's whole existence is a rapid repeating cycle of hunting and eating, it is a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Sable Antelope
entries.archetype: Kneeling to Sweep Behind the Shoulder

modes.label: Grazing • Watching • Dropping to the knees and sweeping

waveform.description: A steady grazing rhythm with one sharp defensive event in it.

entries.closingLine: Steady grazing with rare violent events makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Sac Spider
entries.archetype: Nightly Rounds From a Silk Pocket

waveform.description: Quiet daytime in the sac, rising to steady roaming through the night.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: nightly roaming for food and daytime retreat into silk.

entries.name: Sacred Ibis

waveform.description: A steady sequence of identical probes at walking pace.

entries.closingLine: That makes the ibis a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and repetitive, gathering information by contact rather than at a distance.

entries.name: Sacred Kingfisher
entries.archetype: Flying Head-First at a Termite Mound

waveform.description: A watchful perched line broken by a series of repeated impacts.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a patient perched watch and a violent repeated construction phase.

entries.name: Saddle-billed Stork
entries.archetype: A Stork That Will Not Flock

modes.label: Walking a wetland alone • Striking • Holding a very large territory

waveform.description: A slow measured wading rhythm with occasional strikes.

entries.closingLine: Solitary and unhurried, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sahara Desert Ant

modes.label: An outbound search path of hundreds of metres, winding and doubling back across featureless ground • Direction taken continuously from the polarisation pattern of the sky and distance from the number of steps taken • Those two quantities combined into a running estimate of the straight line home, so the return is made directly rather than by retracing

waveform.description: A rapid searching rhythm with one direct return, because the outbound path is erratic and the homeward one is not.

entries.closingLine: Because the updating runs with every step, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Sahara Spiny-tailed Lizard

modes.label: Emerging dark, almost black, in the cold morning to absorb solar radiation quickly • Lightening through the day to yellow, orange or red as body temperature rises • Reflecting rather than absorbing once the target temperature is reached

waveform.description: A smooth daily arc, because the colour tracks body temperature continuously from dawn to dusk.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Saiga Antelope

waveform.description: One raised summer section and one lowered winter section, with the transition visible between them rather than abrupt.

entries.closingLine: Because the same system is reconfigured by context rather than running one way, it is an adaptive system.

entries.name: Sailfin Tang

modes.label: Swimming with the enormous dorsal and anal fins folded flat against the body • Erecting both simultaneously when threatened or challenged, roughly doubling the apparent body depth • Turning side-on so the expanded outline faces the other animal directly

waveform.description: A calm line with repeated sharp expansions, because the display snaps on and off rather than building.

entries.closingLine: Because displays recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Saimaa Ringed Seal

modes.label: Open water • Diving • Rest of the year

waveform.description: A steady active level dropping into a quiet winter trough and returning — the lair months run at a different rate.

entries.closingLine: Because the lair winter and the open-water year are both essential and run at different rates, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Sally Lightfoot Crab
entries.archetype: Ten Legs on Wet Vertical Rock

waveform.description: Dense rapid movement with no pause.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: continuously fast and continuously adhering.

entries.name: Salmon Shark

waveform.description: Continuous warm-bodied cruising punctuated by fast pursuits where prey gathers.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: continuous warm-bodied cruising and fast pursuit at prey concentrations.

entries.name: Salmon-crested Cockatoo
entries.archetype: A Signal That Changes In A Second

modes.label: Decades of pairing • Slow breeding • Instant signalling

waveform.description: A very slow underlying life with brief flicks of signal on top.

entries.closingLine: Everything about the system is low-frequency except the one channel that had to be fast.

entries.name: Saltwater Crocodile

modes.label: Floating • Waiting out the wrong tide • Riding the right one

waveform.description: A long flat floor rising gradually into one enormous spike and settling slowly afterwards, because the approach is a slow gather and the release is not.

entries.closingLine: Because an overwhelmingly cheap waiting state exists to fund rare and enormous releases of power, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Sambar Deer

modes.label: Detecting a stalking predator by scent, sound or sight while browsing alone • Giving a loud repeated metallic bell call that carries far through dense forest • Other deer, langurs and peafowl responding to that call as reliable information

waveform.description: A flat line broken by a short cluster of repeated calls, because the alarm is delivered as an insistent burst and then stops.

entries.closingLine: Because alarms are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sand Cat

waveform.description: A steady sequence of modest hunting events through the night with a clean drop before dawn.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from many modest captures repeated nightly, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Sand Goby

modes.label: Excavating sand from beneath a bivalve shell to make a chamber • Attracting a female to lay on its underside • Fanning the clutch with the pectoral fins continuously until it hatches

waveform.description: A rapid shallow oscillation maintained without a break, because the fanning continues for days without stopping.

entries.closingLine: Since fin beats repeat continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Sanderling

waveform.description: Rapid oscillation with each wave, a flat high-tide roost, then rapid oscillation again as the tide falls.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: rapid, rhythmic wave-edge feeding and tidal rests.

entries.name: Sandhill Crane

waveform.description: A gently undulating mid-level rhythm of coordinated movement with a single sharp dip-and-peak spike showing brief high-intensity rally and evasive action.

entries.closingLine: This makes the crane a bimodal system: a primarily mid-frequency, coordinated passage engine with a distinct high-frequency rally-and-evade mode layered on top.

entries.name: Saola

waveform.description: A quiet unvarying rhythm — a solitary animal moving slowly through wet forest and doing very little that shows.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal is slow, solitary and undemonstrative, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sarcastic Fringehead

waveform.description: A settled line in a hole, raised twice by something arriving at the rim.

entries.closingLine: A fixed shelter and minimal expenditure make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sargassum Fish

waveform.description: A mostly low, gently wavering line for passive drifting with a single small lift at the end for the brief ambush strike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system built around passive blending and rare, tightly-local ambushes rather than continuous movement.

entries.name: Sarus Crane

waveform.description: Paired call bursts — two voices answering inside one display — separated by long even stretches of wetland feeding.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on a repeated coordinated performance and continuous shared foraging rather than on reserves or bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Satanic Leaf-tailed Gecko

waveform.description: An almost unbroken flat line — the animal's entire daytime strategy is the absence of any change at all.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal spends almost all its time doing nothing at all, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Satin Bowerbird

waveform.description: A steady maintaining rhythm sustained over months.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuous curation rather than any single performance.

entries.name: Satin Flycatcher

waveform.description: A mid-level baseline with repeated sharp narrow spikes, showing periods of perch-based readiness punctuated by brief, high-intensity sallies and quick returns.

entries.closingLine: This dependence on a steady scanning perch state plus a repeated, very short, high-agility strike-and-return state makes the Satin Flycatcher a bimodal system with a mid-frequency baseline and high-frequency bursts.

entries.name: Savannah Monitor

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing long periods of protected, low-output refuge with small fluctuations for surface forays.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is built to withdraw into a durable, low-expenditure space and emerge only for limited tasks, it operates as a single, low-frequency refuge-centered pattern.

entries.name: Scalloped Hammerhead

waveform.description: A calm circling section giving way to a faster searching one — day and night are different animals.

entries.closingLine: Because both the schooling day and the solitary hunting night are essential, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Scaly-foot Snail

modes.label: Fed by bacteria • Enormous heart running • Plating itself in iron sulphide

waveform.description: A steady unvarying pulse, the trace of an animal whose largest organ is a heart that never changes rate.

entries.closingLine: Because the circulation and chemosynthesis run continuously at one unvarying rate, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Scarlet Cleaner Shrimp

waveform.description: A gently oscillating mid-level line showing steady, repeated activity around a stable cleaning station rather than long dormancy or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: Activity follows a repeatable day–crevice–night shelter rhythm tied to the station, so the system is structured as a rhythmic mid-frequency service loop rather than a slow reserve store or a short explosive burst.

entries.name: Scarlet Ibis

waveform.description: A repeating dip-and-lift rhythm with no variation in depth or pace.

entries.closingLine: Steady repeated probing makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Scarlet Macaw
entries.archetype: Bound to a Few Clay Banks

modes.label: Cracking hard seeds • Flying long routes • Gathering at a riverbank

waveform.description: A daily rhythm of long flights out and back to fixed points.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daily flying and feeding makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Scarlet Skimmer
entries.archetype: Pointing the Abdomen at the Sun

waveform.description: An active patrolling rhythm dropping into a still midday pause.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: active contested patrolling and a still thermal posture.

entries.name: Scarlet-rumped Cacique
entries.archetype: A Voice Assembled From Other Birds

waveform.description: A busy varied vocal rhythm sustained across a colony.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuously vocal, social and built on what has been picked up from elsewhere.

entries.name: Scimitar-horned Oryx

modes.label: Allowing body temperature to rise through the day rather than sweating it away • Cooling arterial blood to the brain through a network in the nasal passages • Shedding the stored heat at night when the desert cools

waveform.description: A slow smooth rise and fall across the span, because the whole system is a single daily cycle of storing heat and releasing it.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is daily and generations are slow, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Scrawled Filefish

waveform.description: Gentle, even undulations showing repeated bouts of reef-blended movement and stillness rather than long dormancy or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system built on ongoing, terrain-matched adjustment: steady cycles of blend, probe, feed and pause, all written to the local reef pattern rather than to a single big burst or deep reserve.

entries.name: Screaming Hairy Armadillo
entries.archetype: A Scream From Under the Shell

waveform.description: A steady foraging line with one sharp spike where it screams and bolts for cover.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady scent-led foraging and brief, noisy escapes.

entries.name: Sea Angel

waveform.description: A mostly low, gently wavy line representing continuous drift, with one narrow high dip for a brief, intense predatory strike before returning to low activity.

entries.closingLine: This makes the system bimodal: a dominant low-frequency, current-led drift that preserves invisibility and energy, punctuated by short high-frequency capture bursts that are only triggered when a target is close enough to justify breaking the calm.

entries.name: Sea Bunny Nudibranch
entries.archetype: A Furred Back Tasting for Sponge

waveform.description: A low, even line of continuous slow crawling and grazing.

entries.closingLine: The system is a single slow mode of scent-guided crawling and grazing.

entries.name: Sea Butterfly

waveform.description: Even, low-amplitude undulations representing steady wing-beat swimming and gentle vertical drifting in the water column.

entries.closingLine: This makes the sea butterfly a mid-frequency system: it runs on ongoing, rhythmic activity that tracks a moving environment rather than on heavy reserves or explosive bursts.

entries.name: Sea Gooseberry

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing continuous, soft movement with small variations rather than spikes.

entries.closingLine: This makes the sea gooseberry a low-frequency system: soft, continuous expenditure that lets movement, light and capture all ride on the same calm rhythm.

entries.name: Sea Krait
entries.archetype: Coming Ashore to Find a Drink

modes.label: Hunting eels in crevices • Hauling out • Drinking fresh water

waveform.description: A steady alternation between reef water and island shore.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sea Lamprey

waveform.description: A long low, flat segment for buried larval life, then a modest, steadier rise for the attached, host-riding adult stage.

entries.closingLine: That makes the lamprey a bimodal system built on low-frequency, sediment-anchored larval endurance and a steadier mid-frequency adult pattern of attachment and host-riding.

entries.name: Sea Otter
entries.archetype: No Blubber, So Nothing Is Skipped

waveform.description: A relentless repeating cycle of dives with no long rests.

entries.closingLine: High, relentless and short-horizon, this is a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Sea Pig

modes.label: Walking on inflated tube feet • Reading the mud chemically • Facing into the current

waveform.description: A barely perceptible drift across the whole span, because nothing this animal does registers as an event.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at the rate food falls, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Secretarybird

waveform.description: An even walking band with two needle-thin strikes — the strike is so short it has no width on the trace.

entries.closingLine: Because sustained walking search supports a rare, extremely brief application of force, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Sedge Warbler

modes.label: Feeding almost exclusively on plum-reed aphids at autumn reedbeds • Nearly doubling body weight in a fortnight • Flying the whole distance to sub-Saharan Africa without stopping

waveform.description: A working rhythm that descends into a deep sustained excursion and recovers, because the fuelling period is a prolonged departure from normal life.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Sedge Wren

waveform.description: Dense repeated attempts, each begun and ended quickly.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: fast, cheap, repeated attempts wherever conditions are briefly right.

entries.name: Seed Bug

modes.label: Fallen seed accumulating on the ground and persisting for months or years as a dormant bank • Stylets inserted through the seed coat and enzymes injected to liquefy the contents • The insect drawing out the liquefied endosperm, so a hard dry package becomes drinkable

waveform.description: A steady low-amplitude rhythm, because the food supply persists and feeding continues without seasonal peaks.

entries.closingLine: Because the supply is persistent, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sei Whale

waveform.description: A long, even band of skimming with occasional sharp spikes where it lunges on fish or krill.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady surface skimming and occasional engulfing lunges.

entries.name: Semaphore Crab

waveform.description: Evenly spaced, moderate spikes above a stable baseline, representing repeated bouts of claw signaling around a steady territorial position.

entries.closingLine: That makes the semaphore crab a single, mid-frequency system built around steady, repeated signaling rather than rare deep reserves or brief explosive bursts.

entries.name: Semi-slug

modes.label: A thin shell reduced to a small plate over the back, far too small for the animal to withdraw into • Neither the protection of a snail nor the full flexibility of a slug, but the ability to climb and squeeze into spaces a shelled snail could not • The animal therefore living on vegetation above ground rather than under cover, which is where it meets both the rats and the people that matter

waveform.description: A single nocturnal activity period, because the animal climbs and feeds after dark and shelters by day.

entries.closingLine: Because activity is nightly, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Senegal Bichir

waveform.description: A slow bottom rhythm lifted twice by a trip to the surface.

entries.closingLine: Low output, high durability and a long life make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Senegal Bushbaby

waveform.description: A repeating pattern of settled pauses and fully committed jumps.

entries.closingLine: Repeated committed movement along a remembered network makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Serval
entries.archetype: Only Attacking What Is Already Located

modes.label: Standing in grass • Rotating the ears • One vertical pounce

waveform.description: Long listening pauses cut by high vertical pounces.

entries.closingLine: Continuous patrolling and listening makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Seven-spot Ladybird

modes.label: Finding a colony • Laying into it • Larvae clearing it

waveform.description: A brisk working rhythm with slightly rising peaks, because a larva's appetite grows through every instar.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a continuous cycle of finding colonies and converting them, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Seventeen-year Cicada
entries.archetype: Emergence Timed to Outnumber Every Predator

waveform.description: Years of flat underground feeding, then one tall, brief emergence spike before the cycle resets.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-changing system: a long buried phase and a single explosive emergence.

entries.name: Seychelles Magpie Robin
entries.archetype: One-Egg Clutch, Territory Held by Song

waveform.description: A steady daily rhythm with morning and late-afternoon peaks.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a steady daily round of ground foraging within a fixed territory, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Shield & Stink Bug

modes.label: Brilliant metallic colour produced by layered structure in the cuticle rather than by pigment • Glands on the thorax releasing a strongly repellent mixture of aldehydes when the insect is handled • The colour functioning as an advertisement of that chemistry rather than as decoration or camouflage

waveform.description: A quiet feeding line with occasional discharges, because the insect sits and feeds and only rarely releases.

entries.closingLine: Because discharges are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Shingleback Skink

waveform.description: An unhurried plodding pace that never changes across a season.

entries.closingLine: Slow armoured persistence makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Shoebill

waveform.description: An extremely flat standing line with one vertical collapse — the whole bird commits at once rather than extending a neck.

entries.closingLine: Because near-total stillness supports one total commitment, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Shore Crab

modes.label: Moving between full seawater, estuary and rockpool within a tide • Actively pumping salts across the gills to hold internal concentration • Feeding on whatever the change of water exposes

waveform.description: A regular tidal rhythm of moderate excursions, because activity follows the water rather than the clock.

entries.closingLine: Since tidal movements recur twice a day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Short-beaked Echidna

modes.label: Nosing damp soil • Reading faint fields • Digging straight down

waveform.description: A single slow shallow undulation across the whole frame, as close to nothing as a working animal produces.

entries.closingLine: Because every process here is slow, cheap and measured in months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Short-billed Dowitcher
entries.archetype: A Bill Tip That Opens Underground

waveform.description: A rapid regular vertical rhythm with no variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, rhythmic and tactile.

entries.name: Short-eared Owl
entries.archetype: Breeding Sized to the Vole Year

waveform.description: A working breeding rhythm alternating with a long nomadic low.

entries.closingLine: That makes it an adaptive system: the breeding state is set by the food supply rather than by the calendar.

entries.name: Short-finned Pilot Whale
entries.archetype: Deep Squid Sprints From a Bonded Pod

waveform.description: Quiet surface rest by day, deep diving bouts by night.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: LOW cohesive surface rest and HIGH deep sprint dives.

entries.name: Shortfin Mako

waveform.description: Repeated full-height bursts with a high floor between them — a system that lives near its maximum rather than visiting it.

entries.closingLine: Because the architecture is built and paid for at a high rate all the time, it is a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Siamang

waveform.description: One tall call each morning followed by a day of gentle canopy travel, repeated without variation.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on a repeated daily broadcast and a coordinated route rather than on reserves or bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Siamese Algae Eater

modes.label: Working the surface • Rasping the film • Moving to the next stone

waveform.description: A close repetitive rasp of near-identical strokes, because the work is thousands of small identical passes.

entries.closingLine: Because that rasping is repetitive, unhurried and effectively constant, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Siamese Crocodile

waveform.description: A low year with one broad raised section — the nesting season sustained across months rather than concentrated.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs on a long seasonal cycle, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Siamese Fighting Fish

modes.label: Breathing at the surface • Flaring the gill covers • Tending a raft of bubbles

waveform.description: A working rhythm with three taller lifts in it, because the display is repeated whenever a boundary is tested.

entries.closingLine: Because the breathing, guarding and displaying run continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Siberian Crane

waveform.description: A steady baseline lifting twice a year — two long migrations bracketing the seasons at either end.

entries.closingLine: Because the annual cycle runs steadily with two long movements, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Siberian Ibex
entries.archetype: Summer Meadows, Winter on Wind-Scoured Rock

waveform.description: A long low winter line rising into a summer grazing plateau and falling back.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-change system: a summer of alpine grazing and a winter of endurance on wind-cleared rock.

entries.name: Siberian Musk Deer

waveform.description: A shallow steady rhythm low on the trace — a small animal eating poor food at an unvarying rate.

entries.closingLine: Because intake is poor and the pace is unvarying, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Siberian Sturgeon

modes.label: Completing the entire life cycle within one river system rather than running to the sea • Migrating long distances upstream and downstream inside the same catchment • Depending on that river's gravels, depth and flow for every stage from egg to adult

waveform.description: A broad slow cycle within a single range, because the fish moves long distances but always within the same water.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle spans years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sidewinder
entries.archetype: Two Points of Contact With Hot Sand

waveform.description: A buried still line rising into a brief lateral progression.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: prolonged buried waiting and a brief, entirely lateral progression.

entries.name: Signature Spider

modes.label: Bands of dense white silk laid in a zigzag across the centre of an otherwise near-invisible orb web • That structure varying between individuals, days and conditions rather than being fixed • Several competing explanations supported in different studies, with no single function established across all cases

waveform.description: A quiet variable rhythm without a fixed pattern, because the structure itself is built inconsistently.

entries.closingLine: Because the web is rebuilt over days, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sika Deer

waveform.description: A long still line rising modestly and settling again.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: prolonged concealment and a quiet, deliberate withdrawal.

entries.name: Silky Anteater

waveform.description: A shallow, unhurried undulation that never leaves the low band — small nightly effort, no peaks.

entries.closingLine: Because every part of the body is arranged to hold on and spend as little as possible, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Silky Carpenter Ant

modes.label: Workers emerging across a continuous range of sizes from small to very large within one colony • Small individuals handling brood, nest work and tasks requiring fine manipulation • Large individuals with disproportionately enlarged heads and jaws handling defence, cutting and carrying, so the same colony covers jobs needing opposite body sizes

waveform.description: A continuous busy rhythm, because many individuals are working simultaneously at different tasks.

entries.closingLine: Because the colony works continuously, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Silver Argiope

waveform.description: A long, still waiting line broken by sharp spikes of attack or web-shaking.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long waiting at the hub and explosive wrapping or shaking.

entries.name: Silver Arowana
entries.archetype: Leaving the Water to Take the Branch

waveform.description: A surface-level cruising line broken by a steep upward launch.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: surface cruising and a brief committed launch out of the water entirely.

entries.name: Silver Dollar Fish

modes.label: Broad flat teeth adapted for shearing leaves rather than flesh • Shoaling in numbers through flooded forest and vegetated river margins • Feeding on submerged plants, fallen leaves and fruit taken directly from the water column

waveform.description: A brisk even oscillation, because a shoaling fish moves and feeds continuously without pauses or peaks.

entries.closingLine: Because shoaling is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Silver Pheasant

modes.label: Walking forest floor and displaying on the ground rather than in the air • Carrying upperparts of white feathers each ruled with fine black lines • Producing a pattern that reads as bright white from a distance and as fine detail up close

waveform.description: A quiet line broken by broad moderate rises, because displays are occasional and sustained rather than sudden.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Silverfish

waveform.description: A mostly low, steady line with a small nightly bump, showing long quiet persistence with modest, repeatable activity pulses.

entries.closingLine: Because their whole life strategy is to keep a low profile while quietly repeating the same crack-to-food-to-crack pattern across seasons, this is a single-mode, low-frequency system built on hidden persistence rather than bursts or phase shifts.

entries.name: Silvery Gibbon

waveform.description: A rising sequence of call phrases at dawn, a long quiet working day, and a shorter answering bout — the day is bracketed by song.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs on a repeated daily broadcast and a steady canopy circuit, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Silvery Lutung
entries.archetype: An Orange Baby Everyone Wants to Hold

modes.label: Browsing leaves • Sitting to ferment • Passing the infant around

waveform.description: A slow leaf-eater's rhythm of feed, sit and digest.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sitatunga
entries.archetype: A Hoof That Cannot Leave the Swamp

modes.label: Wading papyrus • Browsing • Sinking to the nostrils

waveform.description: A slow, careful trace with almost nothing sudden in it.

entries.closingLine: Quiet, careful and largely stationary, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Six-spotted Tiger Beetle

waveform.description: Repeated sharp drops to high activity (sprints) separated by quick returns to a mid-level baseline (pause and re-aim), showing a staccato chase rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole hunting system depends on alternating blinding speed with brief mid-frequency resets, this beetle is a bimodal system built from a high-frequency burst mode interlocked with a mid-frequency pause-and-aim mode.

entries.name: Skeleton Panda Sea Squirt
entries.archetype: One Body Plan, Budded Many Times

waveform.description: A steady filtering line that edges slowly higher as the colony adds new zooids.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: slow colonial growth by budding and continuous filter pumping.

entries.name: Skeleton Shrimp
entries.archetype: A Stick Body Anchored by Hind Claws

waveform.description: An almost flat, anchored line broken by one brief contest between males.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: long anchored feeding and brief male competition.

entries.name: Skipper Butterfly
entries.archetype: Darting Sorties From a Sunlit Perch

waveform.description: Sharp flight bursts separated by still, sunlit perching intervals.

entries.closingLine: The adult system is bimodal: bursts of rapid, frequently corrected flight separated by still, watchful perching.

entries.name: Slender Sea Spider

waveform.description: A low, gently wavering line showing continuous but quiet, small-scale movement rather than bursts.

entries.closingLine: This architecture produces a low-frequency system: continuous, cautious, low-amplitude activity built for persistence and minimal disturbance rather than fast bursts or large excursions.

entries.name: Slender Skimmer

waveform.description: Rapid repeated attack peaks with almost no gap between them.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: fast, reactive and organised around many brief precise events.

entries.name: Sloane's Viperfish

waveform.description: Long, low baseline of stillness with a single narrow, tall spike showing a brief needle-like strike before returning to quiet.

entries.closingLine: This pattern of extended low-activity waiting punctuated by very short, intense attacks makes the viperfish a bimodal system with a dominant low-frequency ambush mode and a defining high-frequency strike mode.

entries.name: Sloth Bear

waveform.description: Repeated working bouts of similar size through the night — many mounds opened rather than one large event.

entries.closingLine: Because value is assembled from many repeated extraction bouts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Small Branded Swift

modes.label: Short narrow wings carrying a thick heavily muscled body, giving very high wing loading for a butterfly • Wingbeats fast enough to blur, with no capacity to glide or soar at all • Flight that is extremely fast and abruptly directional, darting between perches rather than flapping across open ground

waveform.description: An extremely fast unbroken beat, because the insect cannot glide and must beat continuously to stay airborne.

entries.closingLine: Because the beat is continuous, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Small Buttonquail

waveform.description: Even mid-level undulations showing a repeated, moderate-intensity cycle of hidden movement and foraging under cover.

entries.closingLine: This makes them a mid-frequency system: a continuous, repeatable operating loop that turns one piece of ground into many roles without leaving the grass.

entries.name: Small Cabbage White

modes.label: Feeding on brassica leaves that release mustard oils when damaged • Redirecting that reaction in the gut with a nitrile-specifier protein • Excreting harmless nitriles instead of the toxic isothiocyanates

waveform.description: A rapid unvarying repetition, because generations follow one another continuously through the season.

entries.closingLine: Since generations turn over in weeks, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Small Indian Civet
entries.archetype: A Gland That Writes on the Landscape

waveform.description: A steady nocturnal patrolling and marking rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady patrolling and continuous chemical marking.

entries.name: Smalltooth Sawfish

waveform.description: Long flat waiting broken by two very narrow spikes — the slash is a fraction of a second in a day of stillness.

entries.closingLine: Because it needs both the long sensing wait and the instant slash, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Smew
entries.archetype: Backward Serrations on a Thin Bill

waveform.description: A repeating cycle of surface and depth with no pause between.

entries.closingLine: Repeated diving through the day makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Smooth Ground Beetle

modes.label: Carrying elytra fused into a single rigid shell with no wings beneath • Walking everywhere it goes • Being unable to cross a road, a field or a clearing that a flying beetle would not notice

waveform.description: A long slow unvarying line with one small rise, because everything this animal does happens at walking pace.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Smooth Newt
entries.archetype: A Crest Grown Only for the Pond

waveform.description: A low terrestrial line rising into a spring aquatic peak and falling back.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a short built-up aquatic phase and a long plain terrestrial one.

entries.name: Smooth-coated Otter

waveform.description: Dense continuous coordinated activity.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: continuously active and continuously coordinated.

entries.name: Snail

modes.label: Drawing a chitinous ribbon carrying thousands of teeth across a surface • Wearing the front rows away as it works • Growing replacements continuously from the back so the working edge is always new

waveform.description: A rapid even rasping rhythm sustained without variation, because the ribbon is drawn back and forth continuously while feeding.

entries.closingLine: Since rasping repeats many times a minute, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Snakefly
entries.archetype: A Lengthened Prothorax That Lifts the Head

waveform.description: A long, low larval line under bark followed by a brief adult hunting phase.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-change system: a long hidden larval stage and a brief adult one.

entries.name: Snout Moth

modes.label: Labial palps projecting forward from the head into a long pointed snout • Wings held in a triangular tent whose outline resembles a curled dead leaf • The projecting snout continuing that outline as the leaf stalk, so the most animal-like part of the head becomes the least

waveform.description: An almost perfectly level line, because the moth rests motionless in one posture through the whole day.

entries.closingLine: Because the posture is held for long periods, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Snow Bunting

waveform.description: Gentle mid-level undulations for repeated ground foraging, interrupted by a single sharp high spike representing a sudden flush to escape or relocate.

entries.closingLine: The system depends on both the steady ground circuit and these rapid flares of activity, making the Snow Bunting a bimodal animal with a rhythmic mid-frequency baseline and a triggered high-frequency escape mode.

entries.name: Snow Goose

waveform.description: A long repeating travel rhythm of legs and staging stops.

entries.closingLine: That makes the snow goose a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, collective and dependent on a route that is taught rather than found.

entries.name: Snow Leopard

waveform.description: Days of flat movement punctuated by two very narrow spikes — a kill every week or two, and nothing in between.

entries.closingLine: Because it needs both the long invisible approach and the brief committed strike, it is bimodal.

entries.name: Snow Partridge
entries.archetype: Barred Plumage Matching Scree and Snow

waveform.description: Steady slow foraging with one sharp flush and glide downhill.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: slow cryptic foraging and explosive downhill escape.

entries.name: Snow Petrel
entries.archetype: A Seabird Bound to the Pack Ice

waveform.description: Steady foraging among the pack ice with regular returns to the nest.

entries.closingLine: Because it is built on steady foraging among the ice, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Snowshoe Hare

waveform.description: A mostly mid-level, gently undulating line for regular seasonal and daily adjustment, punctuated by a tight cluster of sharp spikes representing brief escape bursts when predators appear.

entries.closingLine: This makes the snowshoe hare a bimodal system, with a primary mid-frequency pattern of ongoing seasonal and daily adjustment backed by brief high-frequency escape bursts.

entries.name: Snowy Egret

waveform.description: A working rhythm of stir and strike repeated at a constant pace.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and repeatable, built around producing many small detectable events rather than searching for rare visible ones.

entries.name: Snowy Owl

modes.label: Scanning tundra • Following the rodent cycle • Breeding somewhere new

waveform.description: A boom-and-bust rhythm tracking a rodent cycle.

entries.closingLine: This is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Snowy Plover
entries.archetype: An Exposed Scrape Hidden by Colour

waveform.description: A long still line of incubation broken by a stretch of short run-and-stop foraging bursts.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: still, cryptic incubation and run-and-stop foraging.

entries.name: Snowy Sheathbill

waveform.description: Frequent small opportunistic grabs at an even pace — many tiny returns and no event large enough to dominate the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on many small interceptions repeated continuously rather than on reserves or bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Snubnose Pompano

modes.label: Regulating internal salt balance across water from nearly fresh to full seawater • Continuing to grow rather than merely surviving across that whole range • Occupying estuaries, lagoons and open coast without a physiological transition

waveform.description: A steady moderate oscillation, because the fish is continuously compensating for water that keeps changing around it.

entries.closingLine: Because compensation is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Sociable Weaver

waveform.description: A steady mid-level oscillation showing regular, repeated communal activity around a stable shared nest.

entries.closingLine: That makes Sociable Weaver a mid-frequency system: its defining pattern is ongoing, rhythmic, cooperative work anchored to a fixed home rather than rare deep reserves or explosive bursts.

entries.name: Sockeye Salmon
entries.archetype: Plankton Grazer That Spends Itself in Red

waveform.description: A long steady line of feeding that climbs to a sharp spawning peak and then falls away.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is years of steady feeding ended by one intense, terminal return, it is a phase-change system.

entries.name: Socorro Dove
entries.archetype: A Ground Dove With No Cats to Fear

waveform.description: A steady unhurried foraging line with no sharp escape events.

entries.closingLine: Because the system was a steady daily round of ground foraging, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Song Sparrow

modes.label: Learning several song types as a young bird • Matching the type a neighbour just sang • Escalating or retreating on the basis of the match

waveform.description: Repeated bouts of similar height with small differences between them, because the bird cycles through a set of song types rather than repeating one.

entries.closingLine: Since exchanges occur within seconds, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Sooty Shearwater
entries.archetype: A Figure of Eight Around an Ocean

waveform.description: A continuous low-cost travelling rhythm with no rest phase.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: continuous, economical travel with almost nothing spent on propulsion.

entries.name: Sooty-headed Bulbul

waveform.description: A steady unremarkable rhythm that continues whatever the season is doing.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, rhythmic and reliable because it is never committed to a single resource.

entries.name: South American Coati

waveform.description: A steady searching rhythm sustained through the day.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, wide and continuously searching rather than waiting.

entries.name: South American Tapir

modes.label: Swallowing whole fruits and large seeds no smaller animal can take • Walking kilometres through forest before voiding them • Depositing them in dung far from the parent tree

waveform.description: A long slow even line with a small rise, because the animal moves steadily and nothing about its routine is abrupt.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Southeastern Five-lined Skink
entries.archetype: A Tail Meant to Be Struck

modes.label: Carrying a vivid blue tail as a juvenile that draws the eye away from the head • Shedding it at a fracture plane when it is seized • Leaving it writhing for minutes while the animal leaves

waveform.description: A line broken by a sharp event after which it settles at a different level, because the loss is real and the recovery is partial.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern African Porcupine

waveform.description: A slow flat baseline, a warning step, then one sharp committed reversal.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a cheap unhurried baseline holding one brief, expensive and deliberately advertised defence.

entries.name: Southern Alligator Lizard
entries.archetype: A Fold of Skin Along Each Side

waveform.description: A steady searching rhythm through confined spaces.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steadily active in confined spaces with protection that does not cost mobility.

entries.name: Southern Black Widow

waveform.description: A near-flat line with two small disturbances from something else's struggle.

entries.closingLine: Minimal expenditure and a durable structure make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Brown Bandicoot

waveform.description: A low, flat baseline of shelter punctuated by a band of moderate, regular undulations representing repeated foraging digs before returning to cover.

entries.closingLine: This combination of sheltered downtime and repeated, careful digging makes them a bimodal system with a low-frequency hiding mode and a mid-frequency, rhythmic foraging mode.

entries.name: Southern Cassowary

waveform.description: Two steady foraging periods across the day, with no sharp events anywhere — the trace of an animal that walks and eats.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is a steady daily conversion of fruit into dispersal, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Elephant Seal

waveform.description: A sharp descending curve from high activity into a long, low plateau, showing an intense foraging phase that quickly gives way to an extended fasting period on shore.

entries.closingLine: That creates a bimodal rhythm: a high-frequency intake engine at depth, followed by a strongly low-frequency fasting state that dominates the cycle and defines Deep Fasting.

entries.name: Southern Flying Squirrel

waveform.description: A mostly even mid-level glide rhythm with a few sharp downward spikes representing sudden high-frequency escape launches when threats appear.

entries.closingLine: This makes its system bimodal: a mid-frequency, rhythmic nocturnal glide-commute that can flip into brief high-frequency escape launches when danger compresses time and distance.

entries.name: Southern Ground Hornbill

waveform.description: One broad shallow rise across several years and then a long flat stretch — a cycle measured in years, not seasons.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole reproductive system runs on a multi-year cycle, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Hairy-nosed Wombat

waveform.description: A long underground baseline with shallow night-time grazing excursions — almost nothing happens above the line.

entries.closingLine: Because a very low-cost body is protected by a durable built structure, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Lapwing

modes.label: Feeding in the open • Screaming at anything approaching • Dragging a wing away from the nest

waveform.description: A working rhythm cut by three sharp lifts, because the display is deployed repeatedly rather than held.

entries.closingLine: Because that vigilance and feeding run together through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Lechwe
entries.archetype: Hooves Made for Bounding Through Water

waveform.description: A bounding rhythm of repeated leaps through resistance.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuously active in a medium that is itself the defence.

entries.name: Southern Marsupial Mole

waveform.description: A steady line of sand-swimming with only small variations.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is steady, continuous sand-swimming, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Mole Cricket

modes.label: A male calling from a burrow shaped to project his song across a field • That song used by females to find him and by a parasitoid fly with an ear built to locate it • The fly depositing larvae on or near the cricket, which burrow in and consume it, so the signal that brings mates brings the parasite on the same channel

waveform.description: A sustained regular call, because the male sings continuously from the burrow for long periods.

entries.closingLine: Because the call runs at high rates, it operates as a high-frequency system.
