entries.name: Southern Mountain Viscacha

waveform.description: Long flat stretches of low activity on the rocks, punctuated by brief, sharp spikes of movement when the viscacha dashes or jumps.

entries.closingLine: Because their lives alternate between extended, shared basking-watch phases and sudden escape or repositioning bursts, their system is best described as bimodal: a low-frequency stone-slope stillness anchored by rocks, with a high-frequency dash mode that activates only when needed.

entries.name: Southern Platyfish

modes.label: A pigment-cell gene in the platyfish held in check by a suppressor elsewhere in its own genome • Crossing with a swordtail bringing the gene in without that suppressor • The unrestrained gene driving pigment cells into malignant melanoma in the hybrid offspring

waveform.description: A flat line disturbed by one developing excursion, because the effect only appears when two genomes are combined.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is generational, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Pudu

waveform.description: Small frequent feeding movements at an even tempo — an animal that eats little and often and never travels far.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on steady small intake inside a protected network rather than on storage or speed, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Right Whale
entries.archetype: Skim Far Away, Calve in Calm Bays

waveform.description: A quiet nursery season in coastal bays followed by a long period of slow skim-feeding.

entries.closingLine: Because the system alternates between steady feeding and a calm, reserve-funded nursery season, it is bimodal.

entries.name: Southern Rockhopper Penguin

waveform.description: A repeating jump-and-land pattern that climbs across the trace — each hop is identical, and the height accumulates.

entries.closingLine: Because that commute is a steady repeated cycle rather than a single effort, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Screamer

waveform.description: A steady grazing pace punctuated by calls that lift clear of it.

entries.closingLine: Steady grazing with constant watching makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Tamandua

waveform.description: Many identical short raids strung along a night with gaps between.

entries.closingLine: Many short repeated raids make this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Southern Three-banded Armadillo
entries.archetype: A Shell With Room to Close

waveform.description: A low walking line rising abruptly into a held closed state.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an unhurried ordinary gait and a single complete transformation.

entries.name: Southern Toad

modes.label: Sitting still when approached • Secreting a milky toxin from glands behind the eyes • Relying on the attacker releasing it rather than on escape

waveform.description: A long unbroken flat line with a single abrupt spike, because nothing happens until contact and then everything does.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur through active periods, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spanish Dancer

modes.label: Grazing sponge • Storing toxin • Laying ribbons

waveform.description: A slow grazing rhythm, with the famous swim happening almost never.

entries.closingLine: Slow, continuous, low-output grazing makes it a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Spanish Ribbed Newt
entries.archetype: Pushing Its Own Ribs Through Its Skin

waveform.description: A slow featureless line broken by one extreme event.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a wholly unremarkable baseline and one extreme defensive act.

entries.name: Spanish Shawl Nudibranch

waveform.description: A gently undulating midline showing steady, ongoing movement with small rhythmic variations rather than long waits or sharp bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because its survival depends on this ongoing, graceful drift through food-rich habitat with a constant, conspicuous warning, the Spanish Shawl Nudibranch is a mid-frequency system built around rhythmic, continuous operation rather than extremes of stillness or explosive bursts.

entries.name: Speckled Padloper Tortoise
entries.archetype: Small Enough for the Rock Crevice

waveform.description: Long flat spells of shelter broken by short foraging bouts when the weather is mild.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long spells sheltered in rock crevices and brief foraging bouts when the weather allows.

entries.name: Spectacled Bear

waveform.description: A slow steady line with gentle variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, powerful and built to use poor material.

entries.name: Spectacled Caiman

waveform.description: Long flat low-activity line of waiting, interrupted by a single sharp spike for the ambush strike, then a return to low output.

entries.closingLine: That combination of long, low-cost waiting anchored by rare, explosive capture attempts makes this a bimodal system with a dominant low-frequency surveillance mode and a short high-frequency ambush mode.

entries.name: Spectacled Owl

modes.label: Drop • Grab • Back to the branch

waveform.description: Long flat stretches of waiting cut by very brief vertical strikes.

entries.closingLine: Long motionless watches with rare brief drops make this a bimodal system of low-frequency waiting and high-frequency strikes.

entries.name: Spectral Tarsier

waveform.description: Long motionless scanning broken by two vertical launches — the transition between the two states has no intermediate stage.

entries.closingLine: Because motionless scanning alternates with a committed ballistic capture, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Sperm Whale

waveform.description: A long, low, barely varying trace: steady work far below the surface between short recharges.

entries.closingLine: That makes the sperm whale a strongly low-frequency system: dense, patient and built around a reserve carried away from resupply.

entries.name: Spider Monkey

modes.label: A long prehensile tail with a hairless friction pad on the underside of the tip • Ridged skin on that pad forming patterns like fingerprints and densely supplied with touch receptors • Hanging, bridging and feeding with the tail supporting the whole body weight while both hands work

waveform.description: A continuous flowing rhythm with no pauses, because the animal is always in contact with several supports at once.

entries.closingLine: Because movement is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spinifex Hopping Mouse
entries.archetype: Vertical Pop-Holes to a Shared Nest

waveform.description: A long flat day underground, then a bounding stretch of night foraging.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: nocturnal hopping foraging and a shared, deep daytime refuge.

entries.name: Spinner Dolphin
entries.archetype: Rotating on the Long Axis in Mid-Air

waveform.description: An active nocturnal rhythm alternating with a shallow daytime lull.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a shallow resting phase and a deep active one.

entries.name: Spiny Devil Katydid
entries.archetype: An Ear on the Leg Listening for Bats

modes.label: Singing after dark • Falling silent • Spines if found

waveform.description: Bursts of song with abrupt silences cut into them.

entries.closingLine: Nightly calling and feeding makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spiny Flower Mantis

waveform.description: A long flat low-activity line representing still, attractive waiting, with one sharp spike for the rapid ambush strike before returning to stillness.

entries.closingLine: Because its architecture depends on long, low-expenditure waiting powered by passive visual luring, punctuated by short, high-speed strikes when a narrow spatial trigger is met, the mantis operates as a bimodal system with a dominant low-frequency lure phase and a high-frequency ambush phase.

entries.name: Spiny Hill Turtle
entries.archetype: A Spiked Rim That Wears Down With Age

waveform.description: A low line with gentle morning and evening rises, mostly spent still and hidden.

entries.closingLine: The system is a single low-frequency mode of slow, concealed progress.

entries.name: Spiny Leaf Insect

waveform.description: A very low, almost flat line with tiny ripples, showing long periods of stillness with only slight, slow adjustments.

entries.closingLine: This makes it a low-frequency system: energy and motion are minimized, posture and camouflage are maintained continuously, and survival comes from patient matching to the surrounding foliage rather than bursts of activity.

entries.name: Spiny Softshell Turtle

waveform.description: Long flat low-activity stretches of burial punctuated by brief, sharp high spikes for sudden escape or strike, then a quick return to stillness.

entries.closingLine: Because both the patient concealment and the rapid sprint are structurally necessary to survive with a soft shell in exposed waters, this is a bimodal system with a low baseline and a defining high-frequency burst mode.

entries.name: Spinybacked Orbweaver

modes.label: Rebuilding an orb web daily across an open gap • Adding conspicuous tufts of white silk along the anchor lines • Sitting in the hub behind a hard spined abdomen

waveform.description: A steady repetitive pattern of comparable effort, because the web is rebuilt and maintained on the same cycle continually.

entries.closingLine: Since web maintenance is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Splendid Fairywren

waveform.description: A seasonal rise into display condition and a return to a plain baseline.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and social, with a signal that is switched on seasonally rather than carried all year.

entries.name: Splendid Garden Eel

waveform.description: Gentle repeating waves from a fixed baseline, representing a rooted body with regular cycles of extension to feed and retraction to safety.

entries.closingLine: That anchored, rhythmic watch-and-feed pattern makes them a mid-frequency system built on rooted awareness.

entries.name: Splendid Toadfish

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line with small repeating pulses, showing ongoing low-range activity with periodic close-up reveals rather than long dormancy or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: That rhythm of staying put, working a small patch and revealing its brilliance only at short range is a mid-frequency pattern.

entries.name: Spoon-billed Sandpiper

modes.label: Sweeping • Tidal • Most of the year

waveform.description: A steady tidal rhythm interrupted by a dense compressed section — the Arctic weeks run at a different rate entirely.

entries.closingLine: Because the tidal feeding and the compressed Arctic breeding are both essential and run at different rates, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Spottail Mantis Shrimp

modes.label: Waiting at a burrow mouth in soft mud • Unfolding barbed raptorial appendages in milliseconds • Impaling soft prey and withdrawing underground

waveform.description: A flat line broken by extremely narrow full-depth spikes, because the strike is over before anything else has time to change.

entries.closingLine: Since strikes happen in thousandths of a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Barb

modes.label: Occupying streams, ditches, rice fields and rivers across a vast area of Southeast Asia • Showing considerable variation in form and markings between populations • Having genetic work reveal that the name covers several distinct lineages rather than one fish

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm with modest variation, because a small stream barb's day is continuous and unremarkable.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Cuscus
entries.archetype: A Tail That Works as a Fifth Hand

waveform.description: A very slow steady line with almost no variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, anchored and matched to a very low energy income.

entries.name: Spotted Dove

modes.label: Producing crop milk in both sexes • Feeding chicks on it regardless of season • Breeding through most of the year

waveform.description: A gentle, even undulation with no sharp features, because the system runs continuously at a low amplitude.

entries.closingLine: Since nesting attempts repeat within weeks, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Eagle Ray

waveform.description: A mostly low, smooth line for extended gliding with a clustered section of moderate waves representing periods of active foraging when conditions align.

entries.closingLine: The system depends on long stretches of efficient glide punctuated by coordinated, moderate-intensity feeding sequences rather than constant effort or explosive sprints, which makes this a bimodal low-and-mid frequency animal.

entries.name: Spotted Gar

modes.label: Diamond-shaped ganoid scales locked to one another by peg-and-socket joints • A hard enamel-like ganoine surface over a bone base across the whole body • A rigid casing that resists bite and puncture while allowing only limited flexion

waveform.description: A long flat line with two sudden strikes, because the fish hangs motionless and then lunges sideways.

entries.closingLine: Because strikes are infrequent, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Garden Eel

modes.label: Holding the tail in a mucus-lined burrow • Extending the body into the current and picking plankton • Withdrawing entirely when anything approaches

waveform.description: A gently varying raised level that drops flat at intervals, because the animal is either up in the current or entirely gone.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding picks recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Handfish
entries.archetype: Walking Fish Needing Upright Egg Stalks

waveform.description: A flat line of slow bottom walking, lifting slightly through the egg-guarding season.

entries.closingLine: Because it is built on slow walking and long, stationary egg guarding, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Hyena

waveform.description: A long tireless working rhythm that neither peaks nor stops.

entries.closingLine: Continuous travel, hunting and processing makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Jellyfish

waveform.description: A pure regular pulse with identical peaks and no interruption anywhere, because the bell has no other rhythm to switch into.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal runs one uninterrupted pulse that is simultaneously its propulsion and its feeding, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Lanternfish
entries.archetype: Twilight Commuter with a Lit Belly

waveform.description: Deep, flat daytime water, a climb at dusk, a night near the surface and a descent at dawn.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: deep daytime waiting and a night-time feeding climb.

entries.name: Spotted Lanternfly

waveform.description: A long, low, steady line of camouflage and feeding with a single sharp, narrow spike representing a brief flash-and-jump startle event when danger approaches.

entries.closingLine: This makes the system bimodal: a dominant low-frequency mode of quiet, cryptic feeding on host plants, and a brief high-frequency mode of conspicuous wing-flash and escape that only activates under acute threat.

entries.name: Spotted Linsang

waveform.description: A quiet careful nocturnal line with minimal variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: light, quiet and almost entirely undetected.

entries.name: Spotted Nutcracker
entries.archetype: A Mountain of Seeds Mapped in Memory

waveform.description: A strong autumn caching rise followed by a long, slow winter of recovery.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: an autumn harvesting mode and a long, slower recovery mode.

entries.name: Spotted Ratfish
entries.archetype: Wing-Finned Shell Crusher of the Mud

waveform.description: A slow, even line of flapping glides across the seabed.

entries.closingLine: Because it is built on slow gliding and crushing, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Salamander

waveform.description: A year-long flat line broken by one extremely narrow spike.

entries.closingLine: Fifty weeks of almost nothing and one night of everything make this a bimodal system, a low-frequency buried life punctuated by a high-frequency run.

entries.name: Spotted Sharpnose Puffer

modes.label: Feeding across reef on invertebrates and algae • Accumulating tetrodotoxin produced by bacteria and passed along the food chain • Carrying it in the skin and organs and inflating when threatened

waveform.description: A calm line rising into sustained raised events, because inflation is held for as long as the threat is present.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Trunkfish
entries.archetype: A Rigid Bony Box That Sculls Slowly

waveform.description: A low, even line of slow sculling and probing with no sharp bursts.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is built on slow sculling and probing, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Turtle

waveform.description: A shallow seasonal arc — activity lifts a little in spring and settles again, without ever rising far above the baseline.

entries.closingLine: Since activity is concentrated into part of the year and otherwise dormant, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Spotted Wobbegong

waveform.description: Long flat low-activity line for seafloor waiting, with a single sharp narrow spike for the ambush strike and a quick return to stillness.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system with a dominant low-frequency camouflage mode and a structurally critical high-frequency strike mode.

entries.name: Spotted Wood Owl

waveform.description: A long motionless watch broken by one narrow drop that settles quickly.

entries.closingLine: That makes the owl a bimodal system: a very cheap listening state and one brief committed descent.

entries.name: Spotted-tailed Quoll

waveform.description: A sustained hunting rhythm with regular moderate peaks — several kills a week rather than one large event.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from repeated moderate kills across a wide nightly circuit, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Springbok

waveform.description: An even grazing rhythm breaking into a short series of tall stiff peaks.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady herd grazing and a short deliberately expensive declaration.

entries.name: Springhare

waveform.description: Regular bounding through a night with returns folded into it.

entries.closingLine: Repeated nightly loops make this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Squirrel Monkey
entries.archetype: A Large Troop Kept Together by Sound

waveform.description: Dense continuous activity with no quiet interval.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: fast, noisy and continuously coordinated.

entries.name: Squirrelfish

waveform.description: A low daytime floor rising into a sustained night-time level.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a hidden inactive day and an active low-light night.

entries.name: Sri Lanka Frogmouth

waveform.description: A long daylight flatline, then a cluster of very small night-time excursions that barely lift off the baseline.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal earns its living by spending almost nothing and committing only at arm's length, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sri Lankan Elephant

modes.label: Calls produced with a substantial part of their energy below the range of human hearing • Those low frequencies travelling far further than higher ones because long wavelengths pass around vegetation instead of being absorbed • Groups several kilometres apart coordinating movement, so animals that cannot see each other stay in contact across a landscape

waveform.description: A very slow deep rhythm, because the signals are long-wavelength and the exchanges unfold over minutes.

entries.closingLine: Because exchanges unfold over minutes, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: St Mark's Fly

modes.label: Larvae developing through autumn and winter in soil and leaf litter and all reaching maturity together • Adults emerging within a narrow window in late April in numbers large enough to be conspicuous • Males hanging in swarms with legs dangling, the whole population mating and dying within a fortnight

waveform.description: A long flat absence with one sharp spike, because the whole adult population appears and disappears within days.

entries.closingLine: Because the emergence is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Stag Beetle

waveform.description: Repeated bouts of the same shape — grapple, heave, break off — separated by ordinary evenings at the sap run.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on repeated moderate contests at a steady tempo rather than on reserves or explosive strikes, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Stalk-eyed Fly

modes.label: Eyes and antennae carried at the ends of long lateral stalks projecting from the head • Newly emerged flies pumping air through those stalks to inflate them to full length while the cuticle is soft • Males facing one another and comparing spans directly, the shorter withdrawing without a fight

waveform.description: A calm line with repeated confrontations, because encounters occur regularly and resolve quickly.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters recur, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Standardwing Bird-of-paradise

waveform.description: A baseline of rest punctuated by a series of rapid, narrow peaks representing tightly timed display frames during an active courtship bout.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is built around fast, highly choreographed display bursts rather than slow endurance or steady cycling, this is a high-frequency performance mechanism.

entries.name: Star-nosed Mole

waveform.description: Dense, repeated sharp peaks representing continuous high-frequency tactile sampling bursts as the mole sweeps its star-shaped nose.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole body plan, habitat choice, and foraging rhythm are built around nonstop, very fast tactile sampling instead of slow surveying, the star-nosed mole is a high-frequency system driven by rapid contact-led bursts of activity.

entries.name: Stars and Stripes Pufferfish

modes.label: Four teeth fused into a heavy beak, two above and two below • Continuous growth of that beak throughout life • Crushing molluscs, urchins and coral so that the beak is worn back as fast as it grows

waveform.description: A flat line with deliberate isolated bites, because the fish moves slowly and feeds in discrete crushing events.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding events are discrete, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Steenbok

waveform.description: A motionless line broken by a short erratic burst.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: concealment maintained in two senses at once, and a violent short escape.

entries.name: Steller's Sea Eagle

waveform.description: A perched baseline with regular short swoops — many modest efforts rather than one sustained pursuit.

entries.closingLine: Because value comes from repeated modest efforts around a seasonal resource, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Steppe Eagle

waveform.description: A low soaring rhythm covering distance without effort.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: economical, wide-ranging and opportunistic.

entries.name: Sterlet Sturgeon

modes.label: Reaching sexual maturity in three to five years rather than the fifteen or twenty typical of the family • Staying small at around a metre instead of growing for decades • Completing generations fast enough to restock a river within a human working lifetime

waveform.description: A gentle rise and slow settling, because the life history is compressed but still measured in years.

entries.closingLine: Because generations still run over years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Stick Insect

modes.label: Holding a twig-like posture for hours • Swaying slightly as if in wind • Feeding only in darkness

waveform.description: Long flat stretches with a single shallow raised section, because almost the entire cycle is stillness broken by a slow night of feeding.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle turns over across a season, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Stick Mantis

modes.label: An extremely elongated body with leaf-like flanges and irregular projections breaking the outline • The insect rocking gently from side to side while stationary rather than holding perfectly still • That movement matching what surrounding vegetation does in moving air, so stillness in a moving background would be the thing that stood out

waveform.description: A gentle continuous sway with small amplitude, because the insect is always moving slightly and never abruptly.

entries.closingLine: Because the sway is continuous, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Stick Mimic Assassin Bug

modes.label: The bug entering a spider's web on thread-thin legs and plucking the silk with its forelegs • Those vibrations reproducing the pattern a trapped insect makes, which is the signal the spider is built to respond to • The spider approaching its own trap expecting prey and being seized, so the predator is brought to the hunter rather than stalked

waveform.description: A patterned vibratory rhythm ending in a single strike, because the luring is sustained and the capture is instant.

entries.closingLine: Because the plucking runs at high rates, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Stilt Bug

modes.label: Extremely long slender legs holding the body well clear of the leaf surface • Only the small tips of the feet in contact at any moment, and those moved deliberately and slowly • Progress across sticky glandular hairs that trap and kill insects with ordinary leg contact

waveform.description: A slow careful even rhythm, because the animal moves deliberately and never hurries.

entries.closingLine: Because the movement is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Stoat

waveform.description: Dense unbroken high-rate activity with no extended rest.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: constant, unbanked and unable to pause.

entries.name: Stoplight Loosejaw

waveform.description: Short, repeated spikes rising sharply from a low baseline, representing brief, high-intensity hunting bursts using private illumination in the dark.

entries.closingLine: That combination of covert sensing and rapid, low-drag attack makes this a high-frequency system built around brief, stealthy opportunities in an otherwise quiet environment.

entries.name: Straw-headed Bulbul

modes.label: A loud rich bubbling song delivered from riverside vegetation and audible at a distance • That song prized above almost any other in the Southeast Asian songbird trade and in competitions • Trappers locating and taking birds by the song itself, so the trait that defines the species is what removes it

waveform.description: A normal rhythm drifting steadily downward, because ordinary behaviour continues while the population falls.

entries.closingLine: Because the decline runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Strawberry Hermit Crab

waveform.description: A quiet daytime line, then a sustained rise of night-time foraging along the beach.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: daytime shelter and nocturnal scavenging.

entries.name: Strawberry Poison Dart Frog
entries.archetype: Honesty Bought From Mites and Ants

modes.label: Calling • Eating tiny arthropods • Carrying tadpoles

waveform.description: A busy daily rhythm of calling, feeding and tending young.

entries.closingLine: Constant daytime calling, feeding and tadpole care makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Streaked Gurnard

modes.label: The lowest three pectoral fin rays on each side detached and free-moving • Those rays used to walk over the bottom and to probe the sediment • Chemoreceptors on them detecting buried prey by taste before anything is seen

waveform.description: A steady exploratory rhythm, because the fish works methodically across the bottom without pause.

entries.closingLine: Because searching is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Striated Caracara
entries.archetype: A Falcon That Forages on Foot

waveform.description: A steady day of walking and scavenging, broken by short spikes of investigation.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a steady daily round of ground foraging, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Striped Albatross

modes.label: Developing in the wet season with broader dark markings • Flying in cooler cloudier conditions • Producing the form that most descriptions treat as typical
Developing in the dry season with reduced dark markings and paler wings • Flying in hot bright conditions • Being taken repeatedly for a different species

waveform.description: Two separated levels with transitions between them twice, because the forms alternate with the seasons rather than switching once.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two developmental states, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Striped Blister Beetle

modes.label: Feeding openly on foliage in conspicuous stripes • Releasing haemolymph from leg joints when seized • Delivering cantharidin that blisters the skin of whatever grasped it

waveform.description: A quiet line broken by isolated sharp events, because the defence is discharged only on contact.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs annually, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Striped Hyena

modes.label: Ranging at night • Carrying bones home • Cracking them open

waveform.description: A long quiet nightly ranging pattern over great distances.

entries.closingLine: Solitary, wide-ranging and slow, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Striped Skunk

waveform.description: A slow flat baseline, a small warning step, then one sharp discharge.

entries.closingLine: That makes the skunk a bimodal system: a cheap unhurried baseline holding one costly, deliberately advertised response.

entries.name: Striped Snakehead

modes.label: An active fish in standing water, breathing air at the surface, hunting and guarding young in the wet season
A fish buried in the mud of a dried pool, metabolism suppressed, held in a moist chamber and surviving months without water

waveform.description: An active varying rhythm dropping to a flat suppressed line, because the animal moves between two different physiological states.

entries.closingLine: The two states are distinct architectures, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Stump-tailed Macaque
entries.archetype: Troop on Foot on the Forest Floor

waveform.description: A daylong plateau of ground foraging between two quiet nights huddled in trees.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: ground foraging by day and huddled roosting at night.

entries.name: Sturgeon

modes.label: Cruising just above the bed with a flattened snout lowered • Detecting buried prey with barbels and electroreceptors • Protruding a toothless tube-like mouth downward to suck it out

waveform.description: A long slow even line with almost no features, because a large bottom-feeding fish moves and feeds at one steady unhurried rate.

entries.closingLine: Since generations run in decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sugar Glider

modes.label: Launching from a high trunk with limbs spread • Gliding on a membrane stretched between fifth finger and ankle • Steering by altering the tension and landing head-up on the next trunk

waveform.description: A repeated pattern of sharp launches followed by controlled descents, because each movement between trees is one glide with a definite shape.

entries.closingLine: Since glides recur through the night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Sulcata Tortoise

waveform.description: One seasonal rise where the rains allow activity, settling back into a long underground floor for the rest of the year.

entries.closingLine: Because a very low-cost body waits out the hard season inside a structure it built, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sulphur-crested Cockatoo

waveform.description: A steady social rhythm that lifts as a copied behaviour spreads through the group.

entries.closingLine: That makes the cockatoo a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, networked and defined by how fast information moves between birds.

entries.name: Sumatran Bamboo Rat

modes.label: Cutting tunnel with the incisors • Reaching rhizomes from below • Pulling the culm down

waveform.description: A slow steady working rhythm with no peaks, because progress is measured in centimetres of tunnel rather than in events.

entries.closingLine: Because everything proceeds slowly and without interruption, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sumatran Orangutan

waveform.description: A quiet rhythm of long feeding bouts — a large animal on a poor diet, working carefully rather than quickly.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding and learning both run slowly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sumatran Rhinoceros

waveform.description: A quiet line with small even lifts — a large animal browsing steadily and doing very little else.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs very slowly, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sumatran Tiger

waveform.description: Long flat approach broken by two very narrow spikes — the attack is a fraction of the hunt.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal needs both the long invisible approach and the brief total commitment, it is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Sun Bear

waveform.description: Repeated opening-and-extracting bouts through the night — steady work rather than any single decisive event.

entries.closingLine: Because returns come from many repeated extraction bouts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Sun Conure

waveform.description: Dense bursts of collective noise at movement times with quieter feeding stretches between — a day punctuated by the flock deciding to go.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on continuous group coordination and repeated movement between patches, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Sunbeam Snake

waveform.description: A slow subsurface movement with nothing rising above the ground line.

entries.closingLine: Slow subsurface movement, occasional ambush and a long life make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sunbittern

waveform.description: A narrow low line opening abruptly into a held broad state.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a narrow concealed baseline and one abrupt change of apparent size.

entries.name: Sunda Clouded Leopard

waveform.description: Mostly low, steady activity along the canopy with a single sharp dip representing a fast, committed arboreal pounce before returning to quiet movement.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole system is organized around long stretches of quiet, energy-sparing arboreal stealth punctuated by short, acrobatic bursts, the Sunda clouded leopard is best understood as a bimodal low–high frequency hunter.

entries.name: Sunda Colugo

waveform.description: Even, rolling undulations showing a repeating pattern of launch, glide and landing across the night.

entries.closingLine: This makes the colugo a mid-frequency system built around rhythmic, linked transitions through the canopy using its full-span membrane as a living sail.

entries.name: Sunda Pangolin

waveform.description: A quiet repeating rhythm of insertions and withdrawals through the night, with nothing sharp in it.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs slowly through the night, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sunda Scops Owl

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing quiet, continuous low-intensity signalling rather than loud bursts.

entries.closingLine: This combination of enhanced reception and modest, targeted output makes it a low-frequency communication system: soft, efficient signalling in the dark rather than high-powered broadcast.

entries.name: Sunda Slow Loris

waveform.description: Long, low, nearly flat activity representing quiet, deliberate movement, interrupted by a short cluster of sharp peaks for a rare venomous defensive burst.

entries.closingLine: That makes the slow loris a bimodal system: predominantly low-frequency stealth and conservation, with a structurally important high-frequency venom burst for close-quarters defense.

entries.name: Sundas Pit Viper

modes.label: A membrane-lined pit between eye and nostril on each side of the head • Detecting temperature differences of a fraction of a degree across that membrane • Overlaying the thermal image on the visual one so a warm body is located in total darkness

waveform.description: A low irregular baseline of scanning with occasional sharp strikes, because the snake searches continuously and strikes rarely.

entries.closingLine: Because scanning is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Suni

modes.label: Browsing in thicket • Standing frozen • One short bolt

waveform.description: An extremely quiet trace with almost nothing happening in it.

entries.closingLine: Feeding quietly inside cover and moving very little makes this a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Sunset Moth

waveform.description: A continuous daytime flight rhythm — regular, sustained and without the peaks a night-flying moth would show.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on continuous daytime activity backed by a permanent structural signal, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Superb Bird-of-paradise

waveform.description: An ordinary baseline broken by one dense cluster of maximum-amplitude activity — the display is not a peak but a different regime entirely.

entries.closingLine: Because a plain low-cost baseline alternates with a brief regime the whole plumage exists to produce, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Superb Fairywren

waveform.description: Even mid-height ripples showing repeated bouts of activity and signaling threaded through shelter, without extreme peaks or long flat lows.

entries.closingLine: That makes the Superb Fairywren a single mid-frequency system: its whole biology is tuned to continuous, coordinated social signaling threaded through protective cover.

entries.name: Superb Fruit Dove
entries.archetype: Swallowing Fruit Whole, Passing Seeds Intact

waveform.description: Probable feeding peaks in early morning and late afternoon, as in many canopy frugivores, with a quieter middle of the day.

entries.closingLine: The result is a single, steady mid-frequency foraging rhythm, probably concentrated, as in many canopy frugivores, in the cooler morning and late-afternoon hours.

entries.name: Superb Lyrebird

waveform.description: A repeating delivery whose swings widen as the stored repertoire grows.

entries.closingLine: Collection, storage and replay run continuously through the year, which makes this a mid-frequency system built on accumulation rather than on any single performance.

entries.name: Superb Starling
entries.archetype: Many Pairs, Many Helpers, One Nest Tree

waveform.description: A steady line of group foraging and chick-feeding punctuated by bursts of mobbing.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady cooperative foraging and breeding, with bursts of collective defence.

entries.name: Surinam Horned Frog
entries.archetype: Bite Force Out of All Proportion

modes.label: Buried in litter • Waiting • One enormous bite

waveform.description: Long flat stillness broken only by events too brief to draw.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Surinam Toad
entries.archetype: Skin Grown Up Around Each Egg

modes.label: Somersaulting in the clasp • Eggs pressed into the back • Months of waiting

waveform.description: An almost motionless trace across months of brooding.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Swallow-tailed Kite

modes.label: Soaring • Snatching from the canopy • Drinking on the wing

waveform.description: Continuous buoyant flight with no returns to the ground.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daylight flight and feeding makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Swamp Harrier
entries.archetype: Slow Flight Below the Reed Line

waveform.description: A slow rocking search rhythm held close to one level.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: sustained low-cost searching in which surprise comes from the flight path rather than from any burst.

entries.name: Swift Fox

modes.label: Burrows occupied and maintained throughout the year rather than only for raising young • Multiple entrances and several dens within a home range, used and switched constantly • The animal retreating underground from coyotes, raptors, heat and cold alike, on ground with no cover of any kind

waveform.description: A single nocturnal excursion each day, because the animal is below ground for most of every cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Swinhoe's Pheasant
entries.archetype: Iridescence Aimed at a Light Gap

waveform.description: Quiet forest-floor foraging with brief aimed flashes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady ground foraging carrying a signal that is aimed rather than simply worn.

entries.name: Sword-billed Hummingbird
entries.archetype: A Bill Too Long to Preen With

modes.label: Hovering at deep flowers • Perching bill upward • Grooming with the feet

waveform.description: A rapid repeating rhythm of hovering visits and brief perches.

entries.closingLine: Fast and short-horizon, this is a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Swordfish

waveform.description: Level cruising torn open by strikes that reach the top of the frame.

entries.closingLine: Short committed attacks between long cruising makes this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Tadpole Shrimp

modes.label: Hatching within a day of a pool filling • Growing to full size in two or three weeks • Feeding on everything in the pool and laying before the water goes
Lying in dry sediment as a desiccated cyst • Withstanding years or decades without water • Requiring drying and rewetting before hatching at all

waveform.description: Long flat depressed stretches interrupted by short violent bursts, because almost all of the time nothing is alive and then everything happens at once.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two different states, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Tailless Whip Scorpion

waveform.description: An almost motionless line with slow feeler sweeps written into it.

entries.closingLine: Almost nothing is spent between meals, which makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tailless Whip Spider

waveform.description: A slow exploratory line with small continuous variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, continuous and built on a remembered map rather than on a sense of direction.

entries.name: Takahe

waveform.description: A fast unvarying rhythm — one small action repeated continuously through the whole of the day.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is a fast steady repeated cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Takhi

waveform.description: Two long grazing periods with movement between them — a steady band rhythm with no sharp events.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on continuous grazing and coordinated movement, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Takin

waveform.description: One long seasonal rise and fall — the animal's year has a single shape, driven by altitude rather than by days.

entries.closingLine: Because the system depends on structural investment and slow seasonal movement rather than on bursts, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tamaraw
entries.archetype: Dwarf Buffalo Grazing by Night on One Island

waveform.description: Grazing at night and twilight, resting hidden through the day.

entries.closingLine: A slow grazing routine at night makes it a SINGLE LOW system.

entries.name: Tapanuli Orangutan

waveform.description: A quiet unvarying line — a slow ape in a small forest, with nothing about the system that runs fast.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tarantula

waveform.description: Long flat stretches of waiting broken by rare, abrupt strikes.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: long, sensitive stillness with rare, decisive attacks.

entries.name: Tarantula Hawk Wasp

waveform.description: Long searching flights broken by encounters that go entirely one way.

entries.closingLine: One decisive act inside a short adult life makes this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Tarpon
entries.archetype: Surface Rolls for a Second Oxygen Supply

waveform.description: Steady cruising with regular breathing rolls and sharp feeding bursts.

entries.closingLine: It is bimodal: steady cruising punctuated by air breaths, and explosive feeding strikes.

entries.name: Tasmanian Devil

waveform.description: A long night-shaped ramp of travel with irregular working peaks wherever a carcass is found, then a fall back to rest.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on sustained ranging and continuous processing capacity, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Tasmanian Pademelon
entries.archetype: Edge Grazing with Cover at Its Back

waveform.description: A long quiet day in cover rising into steady grazing through dusk and night.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: daytime concealment in cover and dusk-to-night grazing at the edge.

entries.name: Tasselled Wobbegong

waveform.description: A line lying flat against the bottom broken by two instant gapes.

entries.closingLine: A near-free hold and an instant engulfment make this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Tawny Frogmouth
entries.archetype: Holding the Pose of a Broken Branch

waveform.description: A completely still daytime line rising into a moderate night level.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: total daytime stillness and moderate nocturnal activity.

entries.name: Tawny Owl

waveform.description: A flat economical line: an animal that works a small area it already knows.

entries.closingLine: That makes the tawny owl a low-frequency system: economical, resident and dependent on accumulated local knowledge rather than on searching.

entries.name: Tayra

waveform.description: Dense continuous activity across levels with no rest interval.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: restless, exploratory and continuously active.

entries.name: Tench

modes.label: Living in warm shallow water thick with vegetation • Tolerating dissolved oxygen levels that kill other fish • Burying into soft mud and remaining there when conditions become impossible

waveform.description: A slow steady line with small occasional excursions, because a fish in still warm water does everything at a deliberate pace.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tenkile

waveform.description: A low steady line with a slight upward drift — a population recovering slowly from very few animals.

entries.closingLine: Because everything about the system runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tent Tortoise

waveform.description: A very low intermittent line with brief periods of activity in it.

entries.closingLine: Minimal expenditure and minimal output make this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tent-making Bat

waveform.description: A low baseline with evenly spaced medium peaks, showing long sheltered roosting punctuated by regular foraging and tent-maintenance bouts.

entries.closingLine: Because their biology depends on both a conservative, shelter-centered resting state and a recurring cycle of movement and roost maintenance, the tent-making bat expresses a bimodal system with a low-frequency core and a mid-frequency working rhythm.

entries.name: Tentacled Snake
entries.archetype: Aiming Where the Fish Will Flee

modes.label: Held in a J • Twitching the body • Striking before the fish moves

waveform.description: Almost complete stillness in water, held for hours.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Termite

modes.label: Building a porous chimney and surface channels • Letting the sun heat one side and cool the other • Driving air through the nest with no muscular effort at all

waveform.description: A smooth symmetrical oscillation about a fixed centre, because the whole system breathes in and out on a daily cycle.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle turns over daily, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Texas Horned Lizard

waveform.description: A long, low flat line of quiet defense with a single sharp, brief spike representing the rapid inflation and blood-squirting burst, then a return to low-profile stillness.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal’s whole system is built around long periods of inexpensive, passive warning backed by a short, intense deterrent burst, it operates as a bimodal low-plus-high frequency system.

entries.name: Texas Tortoise

modes.label: Pushing a shallow depression under dense thorn scrub • Using vegetation rather than depth for shelter • Depending on that scrub for shade, humidity and concealment

waveform.description: A very flat slow line with a single small rise, because a small tortoise in scrub does almost nothing quickly.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Texas Unicorn Mantis
entries.archetype: A Horned Silhouette Waiting on a Stem

waveform.description: Long flat waiting punctuated by near-instant strikes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long stationary waiting and a very fast strike.

entries.name: Thick-billed Murre
entries.archetype: Wings That Row Deep for Arctic Cod

waveform.description: Ledge-bound rest punctuated by bouts of repeated deep dives.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: deep wing-propelled foraging and ledge-bound incubation.

entries.name: Thorny Devil
entries.archetype: Damp Sand Pressed to the Belly

modes.label: Walking slowly • Eating ants • Filling the skin channels

waveform.description: A very flat trace built from thousands of tiny identical gains.

entries.closingLine: Small repeated gains throughout make this a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Thorny Oyster

modes.label: Cemented to rock • Growing spines outward • Letting sponges cover them

waveform.description: A near-flat line with two shallow rises in it, because the only rhythm a cemented filter feeder has is the tide passing over it.

entries.closingLine: Because the filtering and growing proceed at one unvarying slow rate, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Thorny Stick Insect
entries.archetype: Thorned Hind Legs That Close Like Pliers

waveform.description: A low sheltered line with a slow night rise and a rare sharp defensive spike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: sheltered, slow nocturnal life and a sudden defensive clamp.

entries.name: Threadfin Acara

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line with repeated shallow notches, showing ongoing activity punctuated by localized spikes of defense at the entrance.

entries.closingLine: Because their biology centers on a defended entrance with regular, coordinated tending rather than extreme stillness or explosive bursts, Threadfin Acaras operate as a mid-frequency, gateway-led system.

entries.name: Three-spined Stickleback

waveform.description: A rapid unbroken rhythm — the fanning that oxygenates the eggs continues almost without pause for days.

entries.closingLine: Because building and fanning run as a fast steady cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Three-spot Gourami

modes.label: Trailing two long thread-like pelvic rays ahead and beside the body • Touching surfaces and objects it cannot see • Building a bubble nest at the surface and guarding it

waveform.description: A continuous gentle exploratory rhythm with no strong events, because the feelers are in motion almost all the time.

entries.closingLine: Since the filaments move constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Three-toed Sloth

waveform.description: A flat low anchor representing minimal variation and minimal expenditure.

entries.closingLine: This is a strongly low-frequency strategy: minimal burn, low variation and extreme economy of motion.

entries.name: Thresher Shark

waveform.description: A circling band interrupted by two full-height strokes that overshoot below the line afterwards — the recoil is part of the event.

entries.closingLine: Because a sustained herding phase exists to enable one extreme movement, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Tibetan Fox

waveform.description: A patient low line with small steady variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: patient, narrow and dependent on one prey species entirely.

entries.name: Tick

waveform.description: A flat, low line showing long periods of steady, minimal activity while the tick waits for rare but sufficient contact.

entries.closingLine: This makes ticks a strongly low-frequency system: they commit almost all structure to patient, low-expenditure waiting tuned to recurring host traffic, then exploit contact when it arrives rather than generating it.

entries.name: Tiger Barb

modes.label: Maintaining a constant order of chasing and nipping within the group • Spreading that aggression across many individuals when the shoal is large • Concentrating it destructively on one or two when it is small

waveform.description: A dense continuous pattern of similar small events, because the interactions are constant, minor and never stop.

entries.closingLine: Since interactions recur every few seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Tiger Moth

modes.label: Feeding as a larva on fig leaves that bleed latex when cut • Tolerating and storing the compounds in that latex • Advertising the result with orange, black and white warning colours as an adult

waveform.description: A quiet even line with a single modest rise, because the animal's year is one slow larval period and a brief adult stage.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tiger Salamander

waveform.description: A long quiet subterranean line broken by a raised band of surface activity.

entries.closingLine: Because the surroundings select which state runs, rather than the animal cycling through a fixed sequence, this is an adaptive system swinging between a low-frequency underground hold and a mid-frequency aquatic phase.

entries.name: Tiger Shark

waveform.description: Long steady cruising interrupted by occasional decisive takes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuous unhurried patrol in which the range of usable food, not the hunting, is what does the work.

entries.name: Tiger Wolf Spider

modes.label: Held still • Legs on the ground • Eyes open to the dark

waveform.description: A long quiet floor broken by one needle-thin spike and nothing else, because the whole night reduces to a single committed movement.

entries.closingLine: Because a long cheap listening state exists in order to fund one very short and very expensive movement, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Timneh Parrot
entries.archetype: Dawn Dispersal From a Shared Roost

waveform.description: A day of steady canopy foraging, a noisy peak at the roost and a quiet night.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: daytime canopy foraging and a noisy communal roost.

entries.name: Titicaca Water Frog

waveform.description: A small continuous oscillation — the bobbing that keeps water moving never really stops.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Toadstool Leather Coral

modes.label: Withdrawing the polyps and developing a waxy film across the whole surface of the cap • Holding that state for days while algae and settling larvae accumulate on the film • Sloughing the entire layer off and reopening, leaving a clean surface beneath

waveform.description: A slow accumulation followed by an abrupt return, because fouling builds up and is then discarded at once.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tobacco Grasshopper

modes.label: Hovering in front of a flower after dark • Uncoiling a proboscis longer than the body into a deep corolla • Taking nectar no shorter-tongued insect can reach

waveform.description: A rapid fine oscillation maintained throughout, because hovering requires continuous wingbeats and the visits follow one another.

entries.closingLine: Since wingbeats and visits recur constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Toco Toucan
entries.archetype: A Bill That Is Mostly Air

waveform.description: A steady reaching rhythm of repeated stretches.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady reaching in which one structure serves several purposes at once.

entries.name: Tokay Gecko
entries.archetype: Billions of Hairs and a Shout

waveform.description: A still clinging line broken by loud repeated calling.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: silent clinging and aggressive announcement.

entries.name: Tomato Frog

waveform.description: A flat, almost featureless line — an animal that neither flees nor pursues and spends accordingly.

entries.closingLine: Because a cheap defence removes any need for speed or concealment, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tooth-billed Pigeon

waveform.description: A steady working rhythm — repeated cutting efforts on individual fruits through the day.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding runs as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Topi

waveform.description: A grazing rhythm punctuated regularly by heads coming up.

entries.closingLine: Continuous grazing joined to continuous shared watching makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Toque Macaque

modes.label: Individual monkeys identified, named and followed continuously since the late 1960s at Polonnaruwa • Births, deaths, ranks, injuries and migrations recorded for every animal across their whole lives • Patterns emerging that no short study could detect, including how rank is inherited, how droughts remove cohorts and how lineages rise and fall

waveform.description: A steady continuous rhythm with no interruption, because the record and the society both run without a break.

entries.closingLine: Because the patterns run across generations, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Trap-jaw Ant

waveform.description: Flat carrying stretches interrupted by strikes too brief to see.

entries.closingLine: Tiny windows, enormous instantaneous output and constant repetition make this a single high-frequency system.

entries.name: Trapdoor Spider

waveform.description: Very long sealed stretches broken by two extremely brief openings.

entries.closingLine: A very long almost costless occupancy paying for an extremely brief seizure makes this a bimodal system, low-frequency in the ground and high-frequency at the rim.

entries.name: Trashline Orb-weaver

modes.label: Prey husks, moulted skins, plant fragments and egg sacs fastened into a vertical line down the centre of the web • The spider sitting at the hub in the middle of that line, matched in size and colour to the debris around it • A searching predator presented with a row of similar objects, only one of which is alive

waveform.description: A very flat line with only slight variation, because the spider sits motionless at the hub for long periods.

entries.closingLine: Because the line accumulates over days, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tree Frog

modes.label: Pressing a broad toe pad against a leaf or a stem • Secreting a thin film of mucus between the pad and the surface • Holding on by the surface tension and viscosity of that film rather than by suction or glue

waveform.description: A steady holding line broken by sharp brief events, because the animal clings still and then jumps.

entries.closingLine: Since grips and jumps recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Tree Hyrax

waveform.description: A call that builds in steps to a peak and then falls away — the escalation itself is the shape, not a series of equal events.

entries.closingLine: Because the system depends on a repeated nightly broadcast and steady local foraging, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Tree Pangolin
entries.archetype: Keratin Scales and a Gripping Tail

waveform.description: Night-time foraging activity with one abrupt armoured closure.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady nocturnal insect foraging and a brief, complete armoured closure.

entries.name: Treehopper

modes.label: Sitting still on a stem with a helmet that reads as a thorn or a piece of debris • Feeding on sap through the bark • Signalling to others through vibrations in the plant itself

waveform.description: A near-flat line with small occasional disturbances, because the animal barely moves and its signalling is a subtle vibration rather than an event.

entries.closingLine: Since feeding and signalling are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Triangulate Combfoot

modes.label: Waiting in a tangle web in a corner or under furniture • Flicking sticky silk over an entangled animal from a distance using a comb of serrated bristles on the hind legs • Approaching only once the prey is wrapped and immobile

waveform.description: A still line broken by short sequences of escalating events, because the wrapping builds before the spider approaches.

entries.closingLine: Since captures recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Tricolored Heron

modes.label: Rapid running through shallow water with wings opened and half raised, rather than the motionless stalking most herons use • Fish flushed out of cover by the disturbance and taken as they break, with the bird turning and pivoting to follow them • Energy spent continuously rather than conserved, so the method depends on flushing enough fish to pay for the running

waveform.description: An energetic irregular rhythm, because the bird is constantly moving, turning and striking rather than standing still.

entries.closingLine: Because the hunting is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Trilobite Beetle

waveform.description: A low, steady line with tiny undulations, showing continuous passive defense with minimal bursts or spikes.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is built around continuous passive protection and slow, deliberate movement rather than bursts or switching modes, it is a single, low-frequency architecture.

entries.name: Tripod Fish

waveform.description: An almost unbroken flat line — an animal that has reduced its own movement to nearly nothing.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs at almost zero output, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tropical Carpenter Bee

modes.label: Boring dead wood • Provisioning each cell • Sealing behind her

waveform.description: Bursts of heavy cutting separated by flat stretches, because the bee stops to clear shavings before boring again.

entries.closingLine: Because that cycle repeats steadily through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Tropical House Gecko

modes.label: Waiting on a wall beside an artificial light after dark • Taking moths and other insects that the light has already concentrated • Occupying a food supply created by human infrastructure rather than by any habitat

waveform.description: A single nightly plateau of activity, because the whole system switches on when the lights do and off at dawn.

entries.closingLine: Because the pattern repeats nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Tropical Leatherleaf Slug

modes.label: Carrying a thick tough mantle covering the whole upper surface with no shell beneath it • Breathing through a single pore at the rear rather than a mantle cavity on the side • Burrowing into soil by day and grazing at night

waveform.description: A very slow even line with a single small rise, because everything about this animal happens at a crawl.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tropical Two-wing Flyingfish

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line for cruising near the surface, interrupted by a sharp narrow spike for the explosive break into a glide, then settling back to the prior cruising level.

entries.closingLine: This makes them a bimodal system: a mid-frequency, surface-oriented cruising state that exists mainly to keep them in launch position, and a high-frequency, short, intense escape-glide burst that turns immediate threat into forward flight and distance.

entries.name: True Oyster

modes.label: Drifting as larvae until they detect chemical cues from existing oyster shell • Cementing the left valve permanently to it • Growing into a three-dimensional structure built from generations of shells

waveform.description: A rapid shallow rhythm with no larger structure, because the animal filters continuously and never does anything else.

entries.closingLine: Since filtering is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Trumpeter Hornbill

waveform.description: A regular calling rhythm underlying continuous canopy travel.

entries.closingLine: Continuous canopy movement joined by continuous vocal contact makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Trumpeter Swan
entries.archetype: A Windpipe Coiled in the Breastbone

waveform.description: A heavy slow line with large-scale gentle movement.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, heavy and reliant on scale rather than on speed.

entries.name: Tuatara

waveform.description: A line that barely moves at all — the slowest vertebrate rhythm it is possible to plot.

entries.closingLine: Because every rate in the animal is extremely low, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Tufted Capuchin

waveform.description: Steady group foraging from dawn to late afternoon, then settling to roost.

entries.closingLine: Its steady daylong group foraging makes it a SINGLE MID system.

entries.name: Tufted Deer

waveform.description: Two browsing periods at the cool ends of the day with a long settled middle — a routine shaped by cover and temperature.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal runs a steady browsing routine with a permanent low-cost weapon, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Tufted Gray Langur

modes.label: Each animal scanning the surroundings between bouts of feeding • Individual scanning time falling as the group gets larger • The group as a whole keeping the same total coverage with less cost to each member

waveform.description: A continuous alternation between feeding and looking up, gradually easing as the animal relaxes into the group.

entries.closingLine: Because scanning is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Tufted Puffin
entries.archetype: One Wing for Two Different Fluids

modes.label: Whirring flight • Swimming with the wings • Digging a burrow

waveform.description: A hard alternation between air above and water below.

entries.closingLine: Continuous foraging trips through the breeding season make this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Tui

waveform.description: A mid-level undulating line with several narrow sharp dips upward, showing steady chorus activity punctuated by brief high-intensity bursts for feeding, defense or escape.

entries.closingLine: This architecture—steady, repeated vocal-and-foraging loops with brief, decisive bursts—makes the tui a bimodal system with a mid-frequency chorus baseline and a high-frequency activation mode layered on top.

entries.name: Tunnelweb Spider

modes.label: Heavy forward-pointing chelicerae driven by large muscles filling the front of the body • Prey seized and crushed mechanically rather than subdued by venom alone • Snails, beetles and other hard-cased animals opened by force that a puncturing bite could not handle

waveform.description: A long still line with occasional powerful events, because the spider waits and then commits heavily.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding events are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Turbot

modes.label: Swimming upright in the plankton as a symmetrical larva • Having eyes on both sides of the head • Feeding in open water like any other fish
Lying on the bottom on the right side • Carrying both eyes on the left with a twisted skull • Ambushing from within the sediment for the rest of its life

waveform.description: One level held, a single transition, and a different level afterwards, because the change happens once and cannot reverse.

entries.closingLine: Because the change happens once and irreversibly, it operates as a phase-change system.

entries.name: Turkey Vulture

waveform.description: A long gentle rocking line: hours of searching that cost almost nothing.

entries.closingLine: That makes the turkey vulture a low-frequency system: patient, cheap to run and built around collecting what the landscape has already produced.

entries.name: Turquoise-browed Motmot

waveform.description: A slow regular side-to-side swing at a low level.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: quiet, economical and communicating rather than reacting.

entries.name: Turtle Ant

waveform.description: A mostly flat, low line for the plugged-entrance guard state with modest, regular bumps showing the colony’s periodic patrol and rotation activity around a fixed boundary.

entries.closingLine: The system therefore depends on a stable, shape-matched barrier anchored by stationary guards, supported by ongoing but moderate traffic and rotation, making turtle ants a bimodal system built on a low-frequency door-plug core with a mid-frequency operational layer around it.

entries.name: Turtle Frog

waveform.description: Long buried flat stretches, lifted by short bursts of activity on humid nights after rain.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long buried inactivity and short humid-night periods of feeding, calling and breeding.

entries.name: Twelve-wired Bird-of-paradise

waveform.description: Calm baselines broken by clusters of sharp, rapid peaks representing brief, intense tactile display bouts.

entries.closingLine: That makes the Twelve-wired Bird-of-paradise a single-mode, high-frequency system built around short, precise contact displays.

entries.name: Two-spotted Cricket

modes.label: Rubbing a file on one wing across a scraper on the other • Producing a pure carrying tone in short pulses • Hearing it through tympanal membranes on the foreleg tibia

waveform.description: Tight groups of identical pulses separated by short gaps, because the song is built from repeated chirps rather than a continuous tone.

entries.closingLine: Since chirps repeat several times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Two-spotted Spider Mite

modes.label: A generation completed in under a week in warm conditions, so a season contains many rounds of selection • Enormous populations on a single plant, so even a very rare resistance variant is present somewhere • Haplodiploid inheritance exposing every male's genes directly to selection, so resistance spreads faster than in an ordinary diploid population

waveform.description: A very rapid oscillation with a rising trend, because generations turn over in days and numbers climb through the season.

entries.closingLine: Because generations run in days, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Two-tailed Pasha

waveform.description: Even, repeating peaks returning to a stable midline, representing regular launches from a perch and returns while holding a territory.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal’s biology is built around this ongoing, rhythmic pattern of holding a perch and making repeated sorties, it operates as a mid-frequency system: coordinated, patrol-like activity anchored to a fixed observation point.

entries.name: Ugandan Kob

waveform.description: Long ordinary grazing, a short intense occupation, then recovery.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: unremarkable feeding that builds the reserve, and a short, ruinous occupation of one small piece of ground.

entries.name: Uinta Ground Squirrel
entries.archetype: A Whole Life in Four Months

waveform.description: A long deep floor with one intense compressed active period.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an intense compressed active season and a long dormant one.

entries.name: Ultramarine Lorikeet

waveform.description: Dense rapid spikes with no gaps — a bird that eats almost continuously because its fuel does not last.

entries.closingLine: Because intake is continuous and rapid, it is a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Umbrella Cockatoo

modes.label: Growing specialised down feathers that never stop growing and never moult • Having their tips disintegrate continuously into a fine keratin powder • Working that powder through the plumage while preening, where it absorbs oil and repels water

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm sustained throughout, because preening is continuous and the powder is produced without interruption.

entries.closingLine: Since preening is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Underwing Moth

modes.label: Adults nearly identical across dozens of species, separable only by fine differences in the hindwing bands • Larvae specialising tightly on particular trees, one group on oaks, another on hickories, another on willows and poplars • Populations diverging along hostplant lines rather than by geography, producing sibling species side by side in the same wood

waveform.description: A varied line with many similar excursions, because the genus repeats the same pattern across many near-identical species.

entries.closingLine: Because the divergence runs across generations, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Upland Goose

waveform.description: A shared unvarying grazing pace held by two birds at once.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daylight grazing paired with continuous watching makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Urial

waveform.description: Two grazing periods at the cool ends of the day — a steady routine with no sharp events.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal runs a repeated daily routine whose safety comes from continuous watchfulness, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Vampire Crab

modes.label: Holding a few square metres • Carrying large eggs • Hatching finished crabs

waveform.description: A small quiet rhythm of short movements, because nothing in this animal's life happens more than a few metres from where it started.

entries.closingLine: Because everything is small, local and slow, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Vampire Squid

waveform.description: An almost flat drifting line — the lowest metabolic trace of any cephalopod, with nothing that could be called an event.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal converts near-zero expenditure into survival in a layer nothing else uses, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Vaquita

waveform.description: A steady close-spaced rhythm — an animal moving and clicking continuously within a very small space.

entries.closingLine: Because the animal's life runs as a continuous steady cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Variable Hawk

modes.label: Occupying everything from sea-level desert to high Andean plateau above four thousand metres • Taking whatever prey each of those zones provides rather than specialising anywhere • Varying enormously in plumage between individuals and regions across that whole span

waveform.description: An irregular varying rhythm without a fixed pattern, because the bird works whatever conditions it finds.

entries.closingLine: Because hunting is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Varied Carpet Beetle

waveform.description: A mostly low, steady line for long concealed feeding, with a moderate rise and gentle oscillation representing the adult's periodic searching and reproduction before returning the system to another low, hidden store.

entries.closingLine: Because the system’s success depends on a brief, moderate-activity search phase that seeds very long, low-activity feeding periods inside concealed reserves, the beetle operates as a bimodal system with a low-frequency reserve mode anchored by a mid-frequency locating-and-seeding mode.

entries.name: Variegated Lizardfish

modes.label: Resting on or partly buried in sand with only the eyes exposed • Launching vertically off the bottom when a fish passes overhead • Holding the prey on inward-curving teeth that cover the jaws, palate and tongue

waveform.description: A long flat line with one sharp spike and a brief settling shoulder, because the fish is motionless, strikes once and then resettles.

entries.closingLine: Because strikes are infrequent, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Variegated Meadowhawk

modes.label: Flight timed to the passage of weather systems rather than to any fixed calendar • The insect moving with the tailwind ahead of a front rather than flying against the air • Hundreds of kilometres covered on wind energy that the dragonfly did not have to generate itself

waveform.description: A pattern of pushes and pauses rather than a steady rate, because the movement depends on when the weather arrives.

entries.closingLine: Because the pushes recur through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Veiled Chameleon

waveform.description: A smooth, even mid-level oscillation representing continuous, rhythmic motion that tracks the background rather than spiking independently.
