entries.closingLine: Because it relies on matching the pattern and timing of its environment rather than freezing or sprinting, its system is best described as a single mid-frequency mode built on coordinated, ongoing movement with the background.

entries.name: Velvet Ant

waveform.description: A near-flat walking signature with one handling event.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: durable, conservative, and built so that conflict is avoided rather than survived.

entries.name: Velvet Swimming Crab

modes.label: Swimming clear of the bottom with flattened rear legs • Reaching prey and refuges a walking crab cannot • Turning to face anything that approaches

waveform.description: A brisk repeated pattern of strong excursions, because swimming bursts are frequent and each is a definite effort.

entries.closingLine: Since swimming bursts recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Velvet Worm

waveform.description: A low, steady line showing long periods of quiet, with only tiny ripples for brief, close-range strikes that do not change the overall low-output pattern.

entries.closingLine: This close-cast, ambush style means long stretches of low activity punctuated by very small, local bursts, so the whole system is built as a low-frequency, patient, reserve-conscious hunter rather than a high-frequency chaser.

entries.name: Vendace

modes.label: Feeding on zooplankton in cold open water through the year • Moving to shallow gravel in late autumn as the lake cools • Spawning at the coldest time of year so eggs develop slowly over winter

waveform.description: A long even line with one late rise, because almost the whole year is uniform and the event falls at the end of it.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Venus Flytrap

waveform.description: A long flat baseline of inactivity followed by a sharp spike and partial return, showing extended waiting, a rapid snap event, then a slower, elevated recovery phase.

entries.closingLine: Because most of its life is spent in a low-cost, primed state and its defining action is a short, all-or-nothing closure triggered only when signals cross a threshold, this is a bimodal system with a low baseline and a high-frequency snap mode.

entries.name: Venus' Flower Basket

waveform.description: A very low, gently undulating line showing continuous, steady operation with no sharp bursts: a fixed structure bearing constant load while filtering slowly.

entries.closingLine: Because its entire life depends on a single, continuous, low-waste structural strategy—hold shape, passively filter, endure pressure over long timescales—this is a strongly low-frequency system built around precise, durable architecture.

entries.name: Verdin
entries.archetype: A Different Nest for Each Season

waveform.description: A steady construction rhythm repeated through the year.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady repeated construction as a substitute for physiology.

entries.name: Vernal Pool Fairy Shrimp

waveform.description: A long flat low line for dry egg dormancy, a sharp rise into a short active peak while water is present, then a return to low as the pool dries and only eggs remain.

entries.closingLine: The biology is built around this stark alternation between long, low-cost dormancy and a compressed, high-speed life cycle whenever water appears, so the system is best described as a bimodal pattern with a low-frequency waiting state and a high-frequency burst state.

entries.name: Verreaux's Sifaka

waveform.description: A mostly mid-level undulating line for regular arboreal travel, with one sharp, narrow spike representing a brief, intense sidelong hop burst before returning to the mid rhythm.

entries.closingLine: That combination of steady tree travel with triggered sidelong bursts makes Verreaux's sifaka a bimodal system with a mid baseline and a high-frequency escape-and-crossing mode.

entries.name: Vervet Monkey

modes.label: Giving a distinct call for leopard, eagle or snake • Producing the matching escape in everyone who hears it • Learning through infancy which call fits what

waveform.description: Long ordinary stretches punctuated by isolated very sharp events, because social life is continuous and alarms are rare and total.

entries.closingLine: Since social exchanges recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Victoria Crowned Pigeon

waveform.description: An even walking rhythm — steady progress across the floor with no bursts and no long pauses.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding runs as a steady daily walk, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Victoria's Riflebird
entries.archetype: Wing-Circle Display on a Stump Stage

waveform.description: Steady bark-probing foraging broken by short, repeated bursts of display.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady bark-probing foraging and the male's short, highly stereotyped display.

entries.name: Vicuna

waveform.description: A steady frugal grazing line with nothing spent above it.

entries.closingLine: Minimal expenditure on a capped ration makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Vinegaroon

waveform.description: A slow low line broken by one sharp directed burst.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a quiet venomless routine and a brief, aimed, chemical response.

entries.name: Violet Carpenter Bee

modes.label: Landing on the outside of a long tubular flower • Slitting the base of the corolla with the mandibles • Drinking nectar directly without entering or pollinating

waveform.description: A steady busy rhythm of similar visits, because the bee works flower after flower at a consistent pace.

entries.closingLine: Since flower visits recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Violet Sea Snail
entries.archetype: Upside-Down Drift Beneath a Mucus Float

waveform.description: An almost flat line: constant drifting and feeding with no daily cycle.

entries.closingLine: Because it never actively swims and simply drifts and feeds, it is a SINGLE LOW system.

entries.name: Violin Beetle

waveform.description: A low, gently undulating line showing steady, constrained movement with no sharp bursts, reflecting slow passage through tight spaces.

entries.closingLine: That makes its operating rhythm low-frequency: a constrained, steady system built around continuous occupation of thin spaces rather than rapid, open movement.

entries.name: Visayan Warty Pig

waveform.description: A fast even rhythm of repeated small efforts — a day is hundreds of pushes rather than any single action.

entries.closingLine: Because rooting runs as a fast steady daily rhythm, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Vogelkop Bowerbird
entries.archetype: A Built Display in Place of Plumage

waveform.description: A long, sustained building line with occasional lifts when a female visits the court.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: sustained building and maintenance and shorter bouts of courtship at the bower.

entries.name: Vulture Bee

waveform.description: A mostly low line for nest-bound conservation with repeated moderate rises and plateaus representing organized foraging and carrion processing trips.

entries.closingLine: The architecture is built around low-exposure conservation punctuated by organized, medium-tempo exploitation of a harsh but rich resource, so the vulture bee is best understood as a bimodal system with low and mid frequencies.

entries.name: Vulturine Guineafowl
entries.archetype: Stable Groups Nested Inside a Larger Society

waveform.description: Morning and late-afternoon foraging walks with a shaded midday lull and a long night roost.

entries.closingLine: That gives a bimodal system of steady collective foraging and communal rest.

entries.name: Wahnes's Parotia

waveform.description: Even mid-height oscillations showing a steady sequence of prepared, repeated display bouts on a maintained stage.

entries.closingLine: The system is not about rare explosive bursts or long fasting endurance, but about a reliable, repeatable performance cycle built on spatial control and practiced choreography, which makes it a mid-frequency, stage-disciplined display specialist.

entries.name: Wahoo

waveform.description: Sustained fast output with no low interval.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: fast, continuous and dependent on speed for both food and safety.

entries.name: Walia Ibex

waveform.description: A steady daily rhythm of grazing and moving along the rock, with no burst and no long pause.

entries.closingLine: Because grazing runs as a steady daily cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Walking Catfish

modes.label: Locking the stiff pectoral spines outward as props • Flexing the body from side to side to drive forward across wet ground • Breathing air through a branched organ above the gills the whole time

waveform.description: Ordinary activity interrupted by sustained excursions, because the overland journeys are prolonged events rather than moments.

entries.closingLine: Since journeys recur on wet nights, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Walking Leaf

modes.label: Hanging among foliage • Swaying • Dropping seed-like eggs

waveform.description: A near-motionless trace with a slow leaf-like sway in it.

entries.closingLine: Slow and low-output, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Wall Spider

modes.label: A flat star-shaped silk sheet under which the spider waits pressed against a wall • An ant touching the sheet detected instantly and the spider bolting out and running around it • Silk paid out from spinnerets held high while circling, so the ant is bound in a lengthening tether before it can turn

waveform.description: A still waiting rhythm punctuated by extremely fast circling episodes, because the attack is a burst of running.

entries.closingLine: Because the attack takes seconds, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Wallace's Flying Frog

waveform.description: Long level holds joined by smooth downward slides — every transition is a controlled descent, never a climb.

entries.closingLine: Because movement is arranged to cost as little as possible and activity is otherwise minimal, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Wallcreeper
entries.archetype: Wings Flicked to Startle Prey Out

modes.label: Clinging to rock • Flicking the wings open • Probing cracks

waveform.description: A constant fluttering pulse against a vertical surface.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daylight foraging makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Walnut Orb-weaver

modes.label: Spending the day pressed into a crevice under bark or in a fence post • Being flat enough to occupy a gap of a few millimetres • Coming out after dark to build and work an orb web nearby

waveform.description: Long hidden stretches alternating with an active period, because the animal is either sealed in a crack or out working the web.

entries.closingLine: Since web activity recurs nightly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Walrus

modes.label: Sweeping the seabed • Jetting water into sediment • Suction feeding

waveform.description: A repeating cycle of dives to the bottom and returns to the surface.

entries.closingLine: Repeated daily bottom foraging makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Wandering Albatross

waveform.description: A long shallow unbroken S-curve across the whole frame — the trace of energy taken from the wind rather than produced, on the widest arc of any bird.

entries.closingLine: Because enormous movement is funded by borrowed energy on a decade-scale clock, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Wandering Glider

modes.label: Climbing to altitude on rising air rather than flying under power • Riding monsoon wind systems across open ocean • Breeding in temporary pools that the same rains create, wherever they appear

waveform.description: A long smooth drifting line with very little structure, because the animal is carried rather than driving itself.

entries.closingLine: Since gliding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Wandering Violin Mantis

waveform.description: A long low swaying line broken by one abrupt strike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long cryptic waiting and a very brief strike.

entries.name: Wandering Whistling Duck

waveform.description: Even, moderate oscillations representing repeated contact calls and coordinated flock movements over time.

entries.closingLine: This produces a mid-frequency system: not a rare, single burst, but a steady rhythm of communication and shared movement that keeps the waterflock intact and mobile.

entries.name: Warty Frogfish

waveform.description: Long motionless floor broken by two needle-thin vertical spikes — the strike has no build-up and no follow-through.

entries.closingLine: Because a near-static low-cost baseline is paired with an explosive committed capture, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Wasp Moth

modes.label: Wing scales largely absent so the wings are transparent like a wasp's rather than opaque
A narrow waist, banded yellow and black abdomen and clubbed antennae reproducing hymenopteran proportions
Rapid darting flight, frequent landing and abdomen-curling movements copied from a wasp rather than moth-like fluttering

waveform.description: A jittery irregular rhythm at several overlapping rates, because appearance, proportion and movement each operate on different timescales.

entries.closingLine: Each element runs on its own scale, structural, proportional and behavioural, and the deception fails if any one is missing, so it operates as a multimodal system.

entries.name: Wasp Spider

modes.label: Hanging head-down at the hub • Thick zigzag band through the centre • Waiting on vibration

waveform.description: A long still line with two narrow spikes, because the animal does nothing at all between arrivals and everything in the moment of one.

entries.closingLine: Since the animal is otherwise motionless for hours, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Water Bear

waveform.description: A long flat low line for extended cryptobiotic pause, a brief sharp dip upward (higher activity) for a short active phase, then a return to the low dormant baseline.

entries.closingLine: Because the architecture is built around very long, ultra-low-activity pauses punctuated by short bursts of life and feeding, the water bear is a bimodal system with a dominant low-frequency survival mode and a secondary high-frequency active mode that must fit into narrow safe windows.

entries.name: Water Buffalo

modes.label: Grazing coarse stems • Working • Lying in water

waveform.description: A steady working rhythm with one deep flat trough dropped into the middle of it, because the day is built around the hours spent submerged.

entries.closingLine: Because the system is a steady unbroken conversion with a cooling duty built into its daily cycle, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Water Chevrotain
entries.archetype: Down Into the Stream and Along the Bottom

waveform.description: A quiet nocturnal line rising briefly and returning.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a quiet hidden baseline and a brief submerged withdrawal.

entries.name: Water Deer
entries.archetype: A Deer With a Rodent's Litter

modes.label: Grazing reedbed • Hiding fawns separately • Producing several at once

waveform.description: A steady grazing rhythm with a sharp seasonal breeding pulse.

entries.closingLine: This is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Water Monitor

waveform.description: A long unvarying working rhythm with no rest gaps cut into it.

entries.closingLine: Continuous undramatic coverage of a very long edge makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Water Rail
entries.archetype: Slim Body Through Reeds, Loud Voice From Cover

waveform.description: A steady line of concealed foraging broken by abrupt outbursts of calling.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady concealed foraging within wetland cover and sudden loud outbursts of calling and aggression.

entries.name: Water Scorpion
entries.archetype: A Snorkel Holding It in Place

waveform.description: An almost motionless line broken by one instantaneous closure.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: near-total stillness and one instantaneous closure.

entries.name: Water Strider

modes.label: Spreading weight across long legs tipped with water-repellent hair • Denting the surface film without piercing it • Rowing with the middle pair and signalling with ripples

waveform.description: A rapid even series of short strokes, because the animal moves in continual small rowing bursts across the surface.

entries.closingLine: Since strokes recur several times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Waterbuck
entries.archetype: Standing In It Rather Than Running

waveform.description: A steady grazing rhythm dropping into a long low held state.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: ordinary riverside grazing and a slow deliberate retreat into water.

entries.name: Wattled Crane
entries.archetype: Feeding at One Particular Water Depth

waveform.description: A slow deliberate wading rhythm with little variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, precise and tied to a narrow physical condition.

entries.name: Weddell Seal

waveform.description: Even, repeating peaks showing cyclical dives from a stable breathing hole and returns to the surface.

entries.closingLine: This creates a mid-frequency system built on disciplined, rhythmic cycles of dive, hunt, surface and maintain, all anchored to reliable breathing places.

entries.name: Wedge-tailed Eagle

waveform.description: A long high soaring line broken by a coordinated attack sequence.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: economical high observation and a coordinated two-bird attack.

entries.name: Weedy Seadragon

waveform.description: A soft, weed-like sway with no sharp edges anywhere — movement that is deliberately indistinguishable from the background.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system is arranged around cheap, slow, background-matched movement, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Weevil

waveform.description: A long, quiet concealed larval phase giving way to an active adult phase.

entries.closingLine: The system is a phase change between hidden larval feeding and active adult site preparation.

entries.name: Welcome Swallow

modes.label: An Australian species crossing the Tasman Sea without any human assistance and breeding in New Zealand from the 1950s • Nesting on bridges, culverts and buildings, which are structures that had not existed there before people built them • Spreading the length of both islands within a few decades on infrastructure rather than on habitat

waveform.description: A steady climb levelling off, because the population expanded rapidly and then filled the available sites.

entries.closingLine: Because the expansion ran across decades, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Wels Catfish

waveform.description: A motionless deep line broken by one enormous engulfment.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: prolonged sensory stillness and one enormous engulfment.

entries.name: West African Lungfish
entries.archetype: Sealed in Dried Mucus Until Rain

waveform.description: A long dormant flat line in the dry season rising into a wet season of feeding and breeding.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a phase-change system: a feeding and breeding season in water and a dormant season in mud.

entries.name: West African Manatee
entries.archetype: Tide-Timed Grazer Between Salt and Fresh

waveform.description: Long quiet rests broken by feeding pulses timed to the tide and river level.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: quiet submerged rest and feeding timed by tide and river level along the water’s edge.

entries.name: Western Crowned Pigeon

waveform.description: Two unhurried feeding periods across the day with nothing sharp anywhere — the pace of an animal with no need to hurry.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on steady walking, continuous modest intake and no bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Western Diamondback Rattlesnake

modes.label: Holding position and rattling at an approaching animal • Adding a segment at each shed • Striking only when the warning has failed

waveform.description: A quiet line breaking into a rapid buzz that escalates before one decisive spike, because the warning builds before anything else happens.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur through the active season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Western Gorilla

modes.label: Eating very large volumes of leaf, pith and stem • Fermenting it slowly in an enlarged hindgut • Moving short distances and resting most of the day

waveform.description: A wide, slow, barely varying curve with no sharp features at all, because the whole system operates at a deliberately low rate.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle turns over slowly, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Western Hognose Snake

waveform.description: A quiet digging line breaking into a loud display and dropping below it.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: quiet unremarkable foraging and a loud staged defence.

entries.name: Western Honey Bee

waveform.description: A repeating coordinated mid-frequency rhythm representing synchronized colony work.

entries.closingLine: That makes the honey bee a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, networked and coordination-led.

entries.name: Western Lowland Gorilla

waveform.description: Two long feeding periods with a midday rest — a day shaped by digestion rather than by any event.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system converts continuous moderate intake into size, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Western Meadowlark

modes.label: Weaving standing grass into a dome over a scrape • Entering along a concealed side runway • Singing from a post well away from it

waveform.description: A regular alternation of song bouts against a working baseline, because the bird sings in repeated bursts through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since song bouts and feeding trips repeat, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Western Yellow Wagtail

modes.label: Feeding intensively at a stopover site for days or weeks before the desert crossing • Laying down fat until body mass rises by a large fraction, far beyond any normal condition • Flying across the Sahara without landing, the entire journey funded by reserves accumulated beforehand

waveform.description: A build to a peak followed by a sharp decline, because reserves are accumulated over weeks and spent in days.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Whale Shark

waveform.description: A long shallow cruising line interrupted by one slow deep excursion — the pace of an animal whose largest movement is vertical.

entries.closingLine: Because enormous scale is supported by low-intensity continuous intake over a very long horizon, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Wheel Bug

waveform.description: A very slow low line with minimal variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, patient and chemical rather than mechanical.

entries.name: Whinchat

modes.label: Perching on a tall stem, fence wire or thistle above the sward • Dropping onto insects seen on the ground below • Returning to the same or a nearby vantage

waveform.description: A regular pattern of short identical drops from a returning baseline, because every hunt is the same brief action from a perch.

entries.closingLine: Since hunting drops recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Whirligig Beetle

waveform.description: A continuous circling rhythm held on the surface film through the day.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and continuous, built to monitor two environments without ever switching between them.

entries.name: White Bellbird

waveform.description: Long stretches of low activity punctuated by a few narrow, very tall spikes representing brief, extremely loud calls.

entries.closingLine: That combination of a quiet standby state and a defining, ultra-loud display state makes the white bellbird a bimodal system with a low baseline and a high-frequency, maximum-signal burst mode.

entries.name: White Grub

modes.label: Curled underground • Rasping roots • Fermenting it slowly

waveform.description: An almost unvarying low line with the faintest swell in it, because growth at this rate has no events.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at the pace of microbial digestion in the dark, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: White Peacock Butterfly

modes.label: Perching low on bare ground • Wings held flat and open • Holding a small patch against rivals

waveform.description: A quick low flutter with short sharp peaks, because the flights are brief sallies from a perch rather than sustained travel.

entries.closingLine: Since those run continuously through the sunlit hours, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: White Rhinoceros

waveform.description: A broad, near-continuous plateau of grazing with a shallow midday dip — no spikes anywhere in the day.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole architecture converts constant moderate intake into constant size rather than storing or bursting, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: White Seabream

modes.label: Broad chisel-like incisors at the front of the jaw for cropping and scraping • Rows of rounded molars further back for crushing • The two sets used in sequence so a single mouth both detaches and processes hard prey

waveform.description: A steady varied foraging rhythm, because the fish works along the rock taking whatever it finds.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: White Stork

waveform.description: A settled breeding rhythm falling into a long low travelling phase.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: a fixed, returned-to breeding site and a long cheap journey dictated by the air.

entries.name: White Underwing Moth

modes.label: At rest on birch, forewings closed over the body in a pattern of white, grey and black that matches the bark exactly
On being disturbed, the forewings open to expose banded black and white hindwings, the moth flies erratically and lands with the wings closed again

waveform.description: A long flat line broken by a violent burst that stops as abruptly as it began.

entries.closingLine: These are not two settings of one defence but opposite strategies, one built on never being seen and the other on being seen very clearly and then not, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: White-backed Planthopper

modes.label: Developing short useless wings when the crop is young and the density is low • Putting everything into reproduction instead of flight muscle • Building the population where it already is
Developing full wings and flight muscle when density is high or the crop is deteriorating • Leaving the field entirely • Riding weather systems hundreds of kilometres to new crops

waveform.description: Two clearly separated stable levels alternating, because an individual develops into one form or the other with nothing between.

entries.closingLine: This is an adaptive system running two states.

entries.name: White-backed Vulture

waveform.description: Long cheap searching with one convergence event — the whole day's return arrives in a single descent.

entries.closingLine: Because a very cheap search is punctuated by rare concentrated feeding, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: White-bellied Sea Eagle

waveform.description: Long level watching cut twice by a descent that goes all the way.

entries.closingLine: Long cheap watching paying for a short converted descent makes this a bimodal system, low-frequency aloft and high-frequency coming down.

entries.name: White-browed Fantail

modes.label: A broad tail spread into a fan and used to generate abrupt changes of direction in flight • Insects flushed from foliage taken in the air, with the fantail matching every turn they make • The tail providing the control surface for manoeuvres a bird with a narrow tail could not execute, so evasive prey is followed rather than pursued in a straight line

waveform.description: A rapid erratic rhythm with sharp direction changes, because the flight is all turns and no straight sections.

entries.closingLine: Because the turns come in rapid sequence, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: White-crested Laughingthrush

modes.label: A group of birds foraging together on the forest floor in loose contact • One individual beginning a loud cackling call and the others joining within a second or two • The chorus building to full volume across the whole group and stopping as abruptly, so the signal is produced by the group rather than by any individual

waveform.description: A quiet baseline broken by sudden collective bursts that build and stop abruptly.

entries.closingLine: Because choruses recur through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: White-faced Capuchin
entries.archetype: Testing the Bond by Making It Costly

waveform.description: Dense continuous manipulative activity.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a high-frequency system: continuously manipulative, continuously social.

entries.name: White-faced Saki
entries.archetype: Eating Fruit Before Anyone Else Can

modes.label: Bounding through canopy • Opening hard fruit • Destroying seeds

waveform.description: A bounding, leaping rhythm through the day with regular feeding.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daily feeding and travel makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: White-faced Whistling-duck
entries.archetype: A Flock Held Together by Whistling

waveform.description: A continuous vocal flock rhythm with no quiet interval.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuously vocal and continuously grouped.

entries.name: White-headed Fruit Dove

modes.label: A genus of fruit doves distributed across the Pacific with each island group holding its own species • Populations separated by sea crossings too long for a small canopy dove to make routinely • Each isolated group diverging in plumage and voice until it no longer recognises or interbreeds with its neighbours

waveform.description: A steady rhythm drifting apart step by step, because each isolated population moves independently of the others.

entries.closingLine: Because divergence runs across evolutionary time, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: White-headed Vulture
entries.archetype: Acid Strong Enough to Erase Disease

modes.label: Soaring alone • Arriving early • Digesting what would kill anything else

waveform.description: Long soaring searches punctuated by descents to a carcass.

entries.closingLine: Slow, wide-ranging and long-lived, this is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: White-nosed Coati

waveform.description: A persistent investigative rhythm with no long pauses.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: continuously investigative rather than reactive.

entries.name: White-rumped Shama

modes.label: A vocal organ at the junction of the two bronchi with independently controlled membranes on each side • Each side capable of producing its own note, with separate muscular control of pitch and timing • Two independent voices sounding together, so a single bird produces intervals and overlapping phrases no single larynx could make

waveform.description: A rapid intricate rhythm with overlapping components, because two independent sources are running at the same time.

entries.closingLine: Because the song runs at high rates, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: White-rumped Vulture

modes.label: Finding a carcass from the air and gathering in numbers • Stripping it within hours • Passing the material through a gut acidic enough to destroy anthrax spores, botulinum toxin and cholera

waveform.description: A long quiet line broken by intense concentrated events, because nothing happens until a carcass appears and then everything does.

entries.closingLine: Since the cycle runs across years, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: White-spotted Pufferfish

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line for routine foraging and site use, rising into a tall, narrow peak for the intense nest-building display before settling back to the baseline rhythm.

entries.closingLine: Together this makes a bimodal system: a stable, site-bound mid-frequency routine that supports a high-frequency window of elaborate sand patterning and display.

entries.name: White-tailed Deer

modes.label: Feeding with the tail held down and the white underside hidden • Raising and flaring the tail on detecting a threat • Running with it up, making an unmissable moving signal

waveform.description: A calm feeding line broken by sharp sustained alarm events, because the display is held for the whole of a flight.

entries.closingLine: Since alarm events recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: White-tailed Tropicbird
entries.archetype: Legs Too Far Back to Walk

modes.label: Soaring • Plunging • Returning to a crevice

waveform.description: Long high gliding broken by sudden vertical plunges.

entries.closingLine: Continuous daily foraging across open ocean makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: White-throated Dipper

waveform.description: Even, repeating rises and drops showing regular cycles of submerging to walk the riverbed and returning to the surface along a stable stretch of stream.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole system is built around these coordinated, repeatable foraging cycles in a specific, challenging flow, the dipper is best understood as a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, place-bound and activity-led rather than purely slow or explosively fast.

entries.name: White-throated Kingfisher

modes.label: Prey below the surface appearing displaced because light bends as it leaves the water • The bird judging the real position rather than the apparent one before committing to a dive • That correction applied from a perch at whatever angle the bird happens to be sitting at, so the offset differs on every attempt

waveform.description: A long still watching line with brief committed dives, because the bird waits motionless and then strikes.

entries.closingLine: Because dives recur, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: White-throated Needletail

waveform.description: A high fast-flight line with one low, braced rest.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: fast aerial hunting and braced rest against trees.

entries.name: Whitemargin Stargazer
entries.archetype: Upturned Mouth Hidden Beneath the Sand

waveform.description: A long flat buried line broken by two instantaneous strike spikes.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: long buried waiting and brief explosive strikes.

entries.name: Whooper Swan
entries.archetype: A Family Held Together by Trumpeting

waveform.description: A steady family feeding rhythm with two long committed migration flights.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady family feeding and a small number of long, committed flights.

entries.name: Whooping Crane

waveform.description: A low line with one broad annual lift — a long slow recovery in which each year adds a little.

entries.closingLine: Because everything runs at a very low rate, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Wild Boar

modes.label: Driving a hardened snout disc into soil and levering it upward • Exposing roots, tubers, invertebrates and fungi • Leaving turned ground that changes what grows there next

waveform.description: A persistent pattern of similar strong efforts, because rooting is repeated work at a consistent intensity.

entries.closingLine: Since rooting bouts recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Wild Turkey

modes.label: Scratching leaf litter • Heads up in rotation • Up a tree by dusk

waveform.description: A raised daytime band sitting on a flat floor at both ends, because the animal's operating day has hard edges at dawn and dusk.

entries.closingLine: Because the watching and the feeding proceed together through every daylight hour, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Wild Yak

waveform.description: A heavy, almost unvarying line — an animal whose entire method is to keep going slowly without stopping.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole system runs at a steady low output, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Willow Tit
entries.archetype: Its Own Hole in Soft Wood

modes.label: Finding a standing dead stem soft enough to work • Chipping out a cavity over days and carrying the chips away • Nesting only in a hole it made itself

waveform.description: A quiet line rising into one sustained working period and subsiding, because the excavation is days of concentrated effort once a year.

entries.closingLine: Since excavation happens once a year, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Willow Warbler

modes.label: Moulting the entire plumage after breeding in Europe • Moulting the entire plumage again on the wintering grounds in Africa • Carrying feathers that are never more than a few months old

waveform.description: A working line interrupted twice by broad sustained excursions, because the year contains two prolonged moults rather than one.

entries.closingLine: Since each moult is a months-long process within an annual cycle, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Wilson's Bird-of-paradise

waveform.description: Repeated display bouts at consistent height with maintenance between them — attendance and preparation rather than a single performance.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on steady preparation and repeated daily display, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Wilson's Phalarope

waveform.description: A steady feeding rhythm interrupted by one short, intense season of female competition.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady spin-feeding and fattening, and a short, intense season of female competition.

entries.name: Wilson's Snipe

waveform.description: Long flat low-activity line for hidden probing, with a single sharp high spike and quick return for the zigzag escape burst.

entries.closingLine: Because its whole system is built around a dominant low-frequency, camouflaged probing state with a structurally crucial high-frequency escape burst, Wilson’s Snipe operates as a bimodal low-and-high frequency system.

entries.name: Wilson's Storm Petrel
entries.archetype: Hovering on Feet That Touch the Sea

waveform.description: A busy, flickering foraging line at sea, dropping into a quiet sheltered spell at the breeding crevice.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: steady surface foraging at sea and a sheltered nocturnal breeding phase.

entries.name: Winter White Dwarf Hamster

modes.label: A grey-brown summer coat with a dark dorsal stripe, full body mass and normal nightly activity
A white winter coat, reduced body mass, suspended reproduction and daily torpor in which body temperature falls for hours

waveform.description: An active high-amplitude phase giving way to a subdued low one, because the animal changes its whole operating level.

entries.closingLine: The two states are genuinely distinct systems, so it operates as a bimodal system.

entries.name: Wire-tailed Manakin
entries.archetype: Wire Filaments Brushed in Lek Displays

waveform.description: Intense early-morning display bursts, then steady fruit sallies through the day.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: MID fruit foraging and HIGH display bouts.

entries.name: Wolf Eel

waveform.description: A settled den rhythm lifted twice where something hard is opened.

entries.closingLine: Very low output against very hard food makes this a single low-frequency system.

entries.name: Wolverine

waveform.description: A sustained high-effort trace with no rest periods and no single dominant peak — continuous travel rather than episodes.

entries.closingLine: Because the system runs on relentless continuous travel and storage rather than on bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Wonderpus Octopus
entries.archetype: A Tent Thrown Over Every Burrow

waveform.description: Long sheltered stretches in the burrow with two sustained foraging peaks around dawn and dusk.

entries.closingLine: The system is bimodal: sheltered waiting in the burrow and a sustained, methodical foraging mode at dawn and dusk.

entries.name: Wood Duck

waveform.description: A steady wetland rhythm with one sharp downward event where the brood leaves the nest.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: a steady wetland rhythm containing one decisive transition.

entries.name: Wood Frog

waveform.description: An active rhythm that drops to a long flat line at the threshold, then resumes its old rhythm after the thaw.

entries.closingLine: That makes the wood frog a phase-change system, switching from a mid-frequency active state into a near-zero frozen state when temperature crosses the line.

entries.name: Wood Stork
entries.archetype: Depending on the Water Going Down

modes.label: Wading with the bill open • Sweeping • Snapping on contact

waveform.description: A slow sweeping rhythm broken by rapid snaps.

entries.closingLine: This is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Wood Turtle
entries.archetype: Winter in the Stream, Summer in the Fields

waveform.description: A low winter line rising through a long summer plateau on land and falling back to the stream.

entries.closingLine: The system switches between an aquatic winter phase and a productive terrestrial summer phase.

entries.name: Woodlouse

modes.label: Overlapping plates on the underside of the female forming a sealed chamber • That chamber filled with fluid in which the eggs and early young develop • The whole aquatic stage carried inside the mother rather than taking place in water

waveform.description: A long flat line with one sustained raised period, because the brood is carried continuously for weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because brooding runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Woodlouse Hunter Spider

modes.label: Enormous forward-projecting fangs carried on jaws that open unusually wide • Striking a woodlouse from above and below simultaneously so the armoured plates are pinned between them • Feeding almost exclusively on a prey type nearly every other spider ignores

waveform.description: A flat nocturnal line with brief decisive strikes, because the spider hunts by encounter rather than by waiting in a web.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are occasional, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Woodpecker Finch
entries.archetype: Spine in the Beak for Hidden Larvae

waveform.description: Active foraging most of the year, easing into slower, tool-based probing in drier months.

entries.closingLine: That makes it an adaptive system: direct foraging when food is easy and patient tool use when it is hidden.

entries.name: Woolly Monkey

waveform.description: Two broad feeding periods with travel between them — a shape set by distance covered rather than by any single event.

entries.closingLine: Because the system converts continuous wide-ranging foraging into steady returns, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Woylie

waveform.description: A steady digging rhythm through the night — dozens of small excavations rather than any single effort.

entries.closingLine: Because the digging runs as a steady repeated nightly cycle, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Wreathed Hornbill

modes.label: The female entering a natural tree cavity and sealing the entrance to a narrow slit with mud, droppings and fruit pulp • Remaining sealed inside for months, moulting her flight feathers while incubating and brooding • The male passing every item of food through that slit for the whole period

waveform.description: A long sustained commitment rising and falling slowly, because the whole arrangement runs for months without interruption.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle is annual, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Wrybill

waveform.description: Even, low-amplitude ripples showing a steady sequence of probing and moving along stones rather than long stillness or explosive bursts.

entries.closingLine: That anatomy and foraging pattern produce a mid-frequency system: a repeated, coordinated search-and-probe cycle tuned to the structure of the riverbed.

entries.name: X-marked Snouted Tree Frog

waveform.description: A low sheltering baseline broken by sharp chorus spikes after rain.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: quiet sheltering and rain-triggered chorusing.

entries.name: X-ray Tetra

waveform.description: An even school rhythm: many identical small movements staying together.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: rhythmic and coordinated, where safety comes from being unresolvable rather than from speed or defence.

entries.name: Xantus's Hummingbird

waveform.description: A dense band of maximum-rate activity through daylight that collapses to a deep flat floor at dusk — two states with nothing in between.

entries.closingLine: Because a maximum-rate daytime mode alternates with a genuinely suppressed nocturnal state, this is a bimodal system.

entries.name: Xantus's Murrelet

waveform.description: An even nightly rhythm — colony visits and offshore feeding alternate on the same steady cycle rather than building to a peak.

entries.closingLine: Because colony attendance and offshore feeding alternate on a steady nightly rhythm rather than in bursts, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Xeme

modes.label: Tundra pools • Crossing the equator • Feeding at sea

waveform.description: A light continuous travelling rhythm across the year.

entries.closingLine: Continuous seasonal travel and feeding makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yacare Caiman
entries.archetype: Bone Plates as a Chemical Reserve

modes.label: Floating still • Taking small fish • Holding position

waveform.description: A very flat trace with small, frequent ripples in it.

entries.closingLine: Yacare reach some of the highest densities of any crocodilian on earth in the Pantanal, taking small fish constantly rather than rarely, which makes this a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Yam Hawk-moth

modes.label: A proboscis longer than the body, coiled when not in use and extended while the moth hovers in front of a flower • Nectar reached at the bottom of long tubular corollas that no short-tongued insect can empty • Flowers with tubes of that depth correspondingly dependent on moths of that tongue length, so each is useless to the other unless the two match

waveform.description: A single nocturnal foraging period, because the moth flies at dusk and through the night and rests by day.

entries.closingLine: Because foraging is continuous through the night, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yangtze Finless Porpoise

waveform.description: A rapid regular pulse train — the animal is emitting and listening almost continuously.

entries.closingLine: Because emitting and listening run continuously at a rapid rate, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow Anaconda

waveform.description: A submerged still line broken by one heavy strike.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: prolonged submerged waiting and a heavy committed strike.

entries.name: Yellow Boxfish
entries.archetype: Bony Box Steered by Small Fins

waveform.description: A steady daytime foraging plateau between nights resting in crevices.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a single, mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow Dung Fly

waveform.description: Even, repeating mid-level rises and falls, showing regular trips between dung patches and nearby cover without extreme peaks or long flat lows.

entries.closingLine: That makes the dung fly a mid-frequency system: a rhythmic, cue-led operator built around ongoing activity on an overlooked but regularly renewed resource.

entries.name: Yellow Mongoose

waveform.description: An even mid-level rhythm of outward trips returning to the same level.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: steady, repeated outward trips anchored to one fixed point.

entries.name: Yellow Sac Spider

modes.label: A spider that builds a silk retreat rather than a web and hunts on foliage at night • A bite that is genuinely painful and occasionally causes local reactions, delivered when the animal is pressed against skin • Necrotic lesions widely attributed to this species and repeatedly shown on investigation to have other causes, so the reputation far exceeds the evidence

waveform.description: A quiet nocturnal rhythm with no strong pattern, because the animal hunts steadily and rarely encounters anyone.

entries.closingLine: Because encounters are rare, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow Tang

modes.label: Grazing filamentous algae across Hawaiian reef all day • Being collected in enormous numbers for the marine aquarium trade • Having that trade halted by litigation rather than by biology

waveform.description: A steady even grazing rhythm with no interruptions, because the fish crops algae continuously through the day.

entries.closingLine: Since grazing is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-banded Caecilian

waveform.description: A slow unvarying rhythm in the low band — continuous small effort with no events at all.

entries.closingLine: Because everything is arranged for slow continuous work in a medium nothing else exploits, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-banded Millipede

modes.label: Dozens of leg pairs each stepping slightly later than the one in front • The resulting pattern travelling backwards along the body as a continuous visible wave • Many legs always in contact with the ground, producing steady force rather than the alternating push of a few

waveform.description: An extremely regular travelling oscillation, because the same pattern passes down the body continuously.

entries.closingLine: Because the wave repeats many times a second, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-billed Shrike

modes.label: Spread across perches • Watching different ground • Feeding each other's young

waveform.description: A steady watching rhythm of regular drops, because the group is always working and no single bird is doing anything dramatic.

entries.closingLine: Because the watching and feeding run together through daylight, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-billed Stork

waveform.description: A continuous sweeping rhythm with frequent small closures.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: a continuous sweeping search with a very fast automatic closure on contact.

entries.name: Yellow-crowned Amazon Parrot

modes.label: A vocal organ with two independently controlled sides producing sounds without lips or teeth • Neural circuitry for vocal learning that stays open through adult life rather than closing after a juvenile period • New sounds acquired and added at any age, including those of entirely different species

waveform.description: An irregular varied rhythm that never settles, because the material keeps changing rather than repeating.

entries.closingLine: Because learning and calling are continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-crowned Night Heron

modes.label: Wading slowly • Seizing • Breaking the shell

waveform.description: A deliberate walking rhythm with modest regular dips, the trace of an animal that never hurries and never stops.

entries.closingLine: Because that foraging is sustained and repeated on every workable tide, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-footed Rock-wallaby

waveform.description: Long low periods of shelter and stillness with a central run of moderate, evenly spaced peaks representing repeated precise cliff-hopping before returning to rest.

entries.closingLine: This creates a bimodal rhythm: low-frequency sheltering and recovery anchored to the rocks, and a moderate, repeatable cliff-hopping mode that trades raw speed for precise, recoverable movement along dangerous terrain.

entries.name: Yellow-footed Tortoise
entries.archetype: A Slow Gut Moving Big Seeds

modes.label: Walking the forest floor • Swallowing fruit whole • Passing seeds days later

waveform.description: An extremely slow steady trace across a very long life.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-legged Gull

modes.label: Patrolling seabird colonies rather than foraging at sea • Taking eggs, chicks and adults of smaller species • Robbing food from birds returning to feed their young

waveform.description: A persistent pattern of strong repeated events, because the bird works a colony continuously rather than searching a landscape.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging events recur constantly, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-legged Nomad Bee

waveform.description: A steady mid-level line with small, regular dips of increased activity, representing repeated, timed infiltration bouts separated by calm positioning.

entries.closingLine: This creates a rhythm of repeated, moderate bursts of targeted action rather than continuous foraging or a single giant gamble, which makes the yellow-legged nomad bee a mid-frequency, timed-opportunistic system.

entries.name: Yellow-spotted Millipede

modes.label: Coiling into a spiral when disturbed • Releasing a precursor and an enzyme from separate chambers in paired glands along the body • Producing hydrogen cyanide and benzaldehyde at the moment of contact

waveform.description: A long slow line broken by very sharp brief events, because a slow animal's defence is instantaneous when it fires.

entries.closingLine: Since encounters recur, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-spotted River Turtle

waveform.description: A long flat river year with one rounded seasonal rise — nesting is the only structure in the line.

entries.closingLine: Because a slow low-cost life is organised around one externally timed event, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-throated Marten

waveform.description: An energetic daytime rhythm of repeated rushes and re-searches.

entries.closingLine: Continuous wide-ranging search in company makes this a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellow-vented Bulbul

modes.label: A generalist frugivore taking fruit from ornamental, cultivated and weedy plants across a city as readily as from forest trees • Seeds passing through the gut intact and being voided on walls, wires, roofs and vacant ground • Introduced and invasive plants therefore dispersed continuously through the urban landscape by a native bird

waveform.description: A steady untroubled rhythm, because the bird feeds continuously across an urban landscape with no seasonal gap.

entries.closingLine: Because feeding is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellowbelly Damselfish

modes.label: Eggs laid in a sheet on a cleaned surface of coral, rock or gorgonian rather than released into the water • The male remaining with them and fanning continuously with the pectoral fins • Attacking anything that approaches and removing dead eggs until they hatch

waveform.description: A long sustained raised effort that gradually releases, because the guarding runs continuously for days.

entries.closingLine: Because the cycle repeats through the season, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellowfin Surgeonfish

modes.label: Assembling into large mixed feeding schools over the reef • Entering damselfish territories as a mass rather than as individuals • Grazing the defended algae while the resident cannot expel more than one fish at a time

waveform.description: Repeated grouped surges against a calm baseline, because the fish feed normally until a mass incursion happens.

entries.closingLine: Because incursions recur often, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Yellowjacket & Hornet

modes.label: A single mated queen founding a nest alone in spring • Workers accumulating through summer until the colony numbers thousands • Every individual working toward a colony that will not survive the winter
New queens leaving in autumn and mating • Overwintering individually in crevices and log piles • The nest, the workers and the old queen all dying

waveform.description: A steep annual build followed by a collapse to a long flat low line, because the colony grows from nothing and ends completely.

entries.closingLine: Applying the structural test, these are two different states, making it a bimodal system.

entries.name: Yellowtail Damselfish

modes.label: Feeding on plankton in the water immediately above a coral head • Staying within a body length or two of the branches at all times • Darting into them at any movement and re-emerging seconds later

waveform.description: A busy feeding rhythm punctuated by very frequent sharp retreats, because the fish is constantly darting back to cover.

entries.closingLine: Since darts recur constantly, it operates as a high-frequency system.

entries.name: Yeti Crab

waveform.description: A smooth continuous oscillation — the waving never stops, because the crop stops growing if it does.

entries.closingLine: Because the waving and grazing run continuously, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Zander

waveform.description: A low bright-hours floor with activity peaks at both ends of the day.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: an inactive bright phase and a productive low-light one.

entries.name: Zebra Danio

modes.label: A substantial portion of the heart ventricle removed and the wound sealed by a clot within hours • Surviving cardiac muscle cells losing their mature structure, dividing, and repopulating the missing tissue • The heart restored to essentially normal structure and function within two months, with little or no permanent scar

waveform.description: A sharp drop followed by a slow full recovery, because the loss is sudden and the rebuilding takes weeks.

entries.closingLine: Because the process runs over weeks, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Zebra Dove

modes.label: Walking on open ground • Barring breaking the outline • Calling from cover

waveform.description: A quiet even walking rhythm with very small variation, because nothing this bird does is abrupt enough to draw attention.

entries.closingLine: Because that routine is continuous through the day, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Zebra Duiker

waveform.description: An even foraging rhythm with regular small efforts — each one a fruit tested and opened.

entries.closingLine: Because foraging proceeds as a steady daily cycle of testing and opening fruit, it is a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Zebra Finch

waveform.description: Frequent small calls in clusters: continuous low-cost contact rather than loud song.

entries.closingLine: That makes the finch a mid-frequency system: rhythmic, social and built on continuous cheap signalling.

entries.name: Zebra Longwing

waveform.description: A slow gentle rhythm sustained without variation.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a low-frequency system: slow, durable and built on a food supply nothing else in its group uses.

entries.name: Zebra Moray Eel

modes.label: Working reef crevices by smell rather than sight • Taking crabs, urchins and molluscs instead of fish • Crushing them between flattened pebble-like teeth rather than holding them with fangs

waveform.description: A slow steady line with occasional modest events, because the animal works crevices methodically rather than striking.

entries.closingLine: Since foraging is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Zebra Shark

waveform.description: A long resting floor lifting slightly through the night — activity that never rises far above doing nothing.

entries.closingLine: Because the whole design minimises expenditure and hunts by access rather than pursuit, it is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Zebra Swallowtail

waveform.description: A quick irregular rhythm with frequent changes of direction.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a mid-frequency system: quick, restless searching bounded entirely by where one tree grows.

entries.name: Zebu

modes.label: A large loose dewlap and folded skin greatly increasing the surface area available for heat loss • A short pale reflective coat over dark pigmented skin, and a much higher density of sweat glands than temperate cattle • A lower metabolic heat production and higher tolerance of dehydration, so the animal both makes less heat and loses more of it

waveform.description: A steady even rhythm, because the animal continues grazing through heat that would stop others.

entries.closingLine: Because the regulation is continuous, it operates as a mid-frequency system.

entries.name: Zoanthid

modes.label: Colonies spreading as connected mats across reef rock and holding the space against other invertebrates • Tissues carrying palytoxin, among the most poisonous non-protein substances known • Neighbouring corals and settling larvae suppressed chemically rather than by any physical contest

waveform.description: A slow steady spread with no cycle, because the colony only advances and never retreats or resets.

entries.closingLine: Because expansion runs over months, it operates as a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Zokor

modes.label: Tunnelling toward roots • Eating below • Pushing spoil up

waveform.description: A steady unbroken grind of underground work.

entries.closingLine: This is a low-frequency system.

entries.name: Zone-tailed Hawk

waveform.description: An ordinary circling rhythm interrupted twice by a vertical drop.

entries.closingLine: Long cheap circling paying for a single unexpected drop makes this a bimodal system.

entries.name: Zorilla

waveform.description: A quiet nocturnal line broken by a short intense defensive burst.

entries.closingLine: That makes it a bimodal system: unbothered nocturnal foraging and a short escalating defence.
